On November 27, 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte of Ghent, Holland was martyred for her faith in the Lord, Jesus Christ. Prior to her passing, her husband had also been martyred for his faith. During the time of her imprisonment, she wrote several lengthy letters to her three youth-aged children. The following are abridged excerpts of these letters which can be found in full text on pages 646-651 in the Martyr’s Mirror.

Grace, peace, and mercy from God, the Father, and the Lord, Jesus Christ, to my dear children, David, Betgen, and Tanneken. This affectionate greeting, written by your mother in bonds, is a memorial of the truth to you. I hope to testify to this Truth by my words, my life, and my death, with the help of the Most High. May the wisdom of the Holy Ghost instruct and strengthen you, that you may be brought up in the ways of the Lord. Since it pleases the Lord to take me out of this world, I will leave you this memorial of my faith in the only true God, not of silver or gold for such jewels are perishable.

Receive admonition. First, I admonish you, my most beloved children, always allow yourselves to be instructed by those who fear the Lord. As long as you obey good admonition and instruction, God will be your Father and not leave you as orphans. For David says: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose –Psalm 25:12. Children, grieve not when you are corrected and do not speak in anger to those who correct you. A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke –Proverbs 13:1.

Guard your tongue. My dear children, guard your tongue, that it speak no evil. Do not practice deceit or backbiting with your lips. Paul teaches us to live peaceably with all men if it be possible. –see 1 Peter 3:10 and Romans 12:18. If you are crossly spoken to, learn to answer kindly, and you will be loved by all men. Humility and meekness are acceptable to both God and man.

Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight –Proverbs 12:22. I admonish you to beware of lying, since liars have no part in the kingdom of God. –see Revelation 21:8.

Be diligent in work and give alms. Always be diligent to do your work, wherever you be; for Paul says …that if any would not work, neither should he eat –2 Thessalonians 3:10. It is also written, be diligent to labor, that you …may have to give to him that needeth –Ephesians 4:28.

Do not turn your face away from the poor. Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard –Proverbs 21:13. Therefore, be diligent in prayer, and love the poor; for Christ also was poor for our sakes—For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich –2 Corinthians 8:9. Be therefore also merciful, even as your heavenly Father is merciful; for such shall be blessed, and shall obtain mercy. –see Matthew 5:7.

Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith –Proverbs 15:16. And, Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife –Proverbs 17:1. Choose to earn your bread by the labor of your hands, and to eat your bread with peace. Seek not to be a merchant, nor be anxious for great gain.

Be meek, merciful, and pure in heart. Learn to be meek and lowly in heart for such are blessed and shall inherit the earth. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Luke 6:36. And, Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth –Matthew 5:5. Finally, Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God –Matthew 5:8. Hence, my dear children, let no impure thoughts remain in your hearts. Engage yourselves with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs and evil thoughts will have no room. –see Ephesians 5:19.

Neither let filthiness proceed out of your mouth. You will have to give an account of all filthiness. –see Matthew 12:36-37. Always esteem yourselves as the least and be not wise in your own conceit. Allow yourselves to be instructed by your elders and always be silent when others speak. Humble yourselves, for …whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted –Matthew 23:12. For Christ who is the greatest made Himself the least for an example unto us. –see John 13:13-15.

Avoid a luxurious life. My children, do not desire the luxuries of fine food or wine. He that desires costly feasts will not become rich. Be content with the labor of your hands. Do not be a burden to anyone as long as you can obtain the things needful—…It is more blessed to give than to receive –Acts 20:35. Paul says: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Be sober and thankful as you have heard me read of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They were selected by the king of Babylon to be nourished with the same wine and meat which the king drank and ate at his table. But they chose to have pulse [vegetables] and water. They wanted to observe the law and commandments of their fathers with sobriety and thankfulness in the fear of God. In the end, they were fairer and fatter than those who ate of the king’s dainties, see Daniel chapter 1. Thus, faithfully they walked in the ways of the Lord. They made themselves acceptable to God in prayer and supplication, therefore, he did great things through them. He delivered them from the den of lions and out of the fiery furnace.

When Joseph was sold into Egypt, he desired no worldly dainties. When the Egyptian woman sought to seduce him, he feared God, and God preserved him. He pleased God in sobriety and prayer and God appointed him ruler over Egypt. –see Genesis chapters 37, 39, and 41. Take an example from this in your youth and you will please God. He will keep you from all seduction.

Oh, my lambs, you are still in your youth, yet you have a part in your Father’s kingdom. See that you keep it well and not as Esau who gave his inheritance or birthright for a mess of pottage, disregarding his father’s blessing. –see Genesis 25:30-34. But Jacob chose the better part, walking in the ways of the Lord with all righteousness.

Shun worldly living. Do not delight in the evils of the world such as lying, cheating, gambling, banqueting, playing, swearing, cursing, backbiting, hatred, and dancing, nor envy, drunkenness, excess, idolatry, covetousness, lasciviousness, vanity, filthy conversation. Though the world does not consider these things to be sin but rather calls them amusements, nevertheless, they are abominations in the eyes of the Lord. –see 1 Peter 4:3-4. If you take pleasure in these things, you sell your birthright (or the spiritual inheritance) from your Father, for a mess of pottage—namely, for a few temporal pleasures, which lead you to damnation.

Choose to suffer affliction with the children of God. From the time of Abel until now many have been afflicted and have suffered. They were rejected, despised, persecuted, and killed because they would not follow the wicked world and her false prophets.

My children, choose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God [that you may be rewarded with them], than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25. Unto such belong all the beautiful promises of God. It is written: …ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy –John 16:20. And, Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life –Revelation 2:10. Finally, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world –John 16:33.

Instructions to my son, David. David, my dear son, I commend you to the Lord. You are the oldest; learn wisdom, so that you may be a good example to your sisters. Beware of bad company and of playing in the street with bad boys. Diligently learn to read and write so that you may get understanding.

Love one another without contention or quarreling. Be kind to your sisters. Bear them up as the stronger and out of love help all you can. Assist them out of brotherly love.

Learn to obey your elders in that which is good. Be industrious so that people may love you. Exhort one another to good works, modesty, honorableness, and quietness. Always care for one another for the time has come that …iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold –Matthew 24:12.

Beware of deception. Remember, Jesus said …that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect –Matthew 24:24. Learn to diligently search the Scriptures so that you may not be deceived. Do not believe gossip but examine the matter.

Make no commotion when you are slandered but bear it for Christ’s sake. Love your enemies and pray for those who speak evil of you and afflict you. Suffer affliction rather than afflicting others. Suffer reproach rather than reproaching others. Be slandered rather than slandering others.

You must constantly see that you do not seek solely your own profit, but always care for those with whom you have dealings, whether they be young or old.

Instructions to my daughters Betgen and Tanneken, my beloved lambs, I admonish you in all these same things, that you obey the commandments of the Lord. Also, obey your elders and all who instruct you in virtue.

Be diligent to do your work, and you will be loved wherever you live. Don’t be quarrelsome, talkative, light-minded, proud, or surly of speech. Be kind, honorable, and quiet, as behooves young girls.

Pray the Lord for wisdom, and it shall be given you. Diligently learn to read and write, and take delight therein, and you will become wise. Take pleasure and sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Learn to please the Lord from your youth, as did the holy women and virgins of old. Esther also was a virgin who feared God; she was adorned with humility, was gracious, honorable, kind, and humble of heart; hence she pleased King Ahasuerus above all the other virgins. –see Esther 2:17. But even in her high estate she was not proud. Though she shone in royal apparel, she humbled her heart with fasting and prayer to the Lord, for her brethren, that they might be delivered out of the hands of their enemies. She did not esteem herself better than one of the least of her brethren.

When you have attained the years of understanding, see that you adorn yourselves with the works of the Spirit such as goodness, gentleness, meekness, humility, obedience, long suffering, righteousness, modesty, honorableness, purity, peaceableness, steadfastness, mercifulness, wisdom, diligence in good works, faith, hope and love. Love God above all that is in the world and do to your neighbor as you would have men do unto you. –see Galatians 5:22-23 and Titus 2:3-5. Remember that Jesus said: …Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets –Matthew 22:37-40.

Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints –Revelation 19:7-8. My daughters, this is the adornment of the saints; labor for such a wedding garment, so that you may enter into the marriage of the Lamb, where they …the righteous, [shall] shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father… –Matthew 13:43. May the Lord lead you as He led Israel out of Egypt, and bring you to the New Jerusalem, that we may see each other with joy in the day of the resurrection. I commend you to the Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; may He keep you to the end of your lives.

In conclusion, O my dear children, I have written this in tears, admonishing you out of love. My prayer and solicitude are constantly for your salvation. I hope and pray constantly that He, in His mercy, will preserve you, just as He preserved Joseph, Moses, and Daniel in the midst of wicked men. And He will do this if you give diligence to follow the truth.

This is my last farewell, my dear lambs. always remember each other in love; diligently learn to read and write and obey everyone in that which is good. I bid you adieu, my dear children Betgen, David and Tanneken. Adieu all my dear brethren and sisters, and friends everywhere.

Written by me, Soetgen van den Houte, your mother in bonds; written in haste (while trembling with cold), out of love for you all, amen.

Em 27 de novembro de 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte, de Ghent, Holanda, foi martirizada por sua fé no Senhor Jesus Cristo. Antes de sua morte, seu marido também havia sido martirizado por sua fé. Durante o tempo de seu aprisionamento, ela escreveu várias cartas longas para seus três filhos, ainda jovens. A seguir vão trechos abreviados dessas cartas que podem ser lidas na íntegra nas páginas 646–651 do Martyr’s Mirror.

Graça, paz e misericórdia de Deus Pai e do Senhor Jesus Cristo, aos meus queridos filhos, David, Betgen e Tanneken. Esta saudação afetuosa, escrita por vossa mãe em grilhões, é uma memória da verdade para vós. Espero testemunhar esta Verdade por minhas palavras, minha vida e minha morte, com a ajuda do Altíssimo. Que a sabedoria do Espírito Santo vos instrua e fortaleça, para que sejais criados nos caminhos do Senhor. Pois, agradando ao Senhor tirar-me deste mundo, deixarei a vós esta memória de minha fé no único Deus verdadeiro, não de prata nem de ouro, pois tais jóias são perecíveis.

Recebei admoestação. Em primeiro lugar, admoesto-vos, meus mais amados filhos, que sempre vos deixeis instruir por aqueles que temem ao Senhor. Enquanto obedecerdes a boa admoestação e instrução, Deus será vosso Pai e não vos abandonará como órfãos. Pois David diz: Quem é o homem que teme ao SENHOR? A esse ele o ensinará no caminho que deve escolher –Salmos 25:12. Filhos, não vos entristeçais quando sois corrigidos e não faleis com ira aos que vos corrigem. O filho sábio ouve a instrução de seu pai; mas o escarnecedor não atende à repreensão –Provérbios 13:1.

Guarda tua língua. Meus queridos filhos, guardai vossa língua, para que não fale mal. Não pratiquem engano nem murmuração com vossos lábios. Paulo nos ensina a viver pacificamente com todos, se possível. –ver 1 Pedro 3:10 e Romanos 12:18. Se alguém vos falar asperamente, aprendei a responder com bondade, e sereis amados por todos. Humildade e mansidão são aceitáveis tanto a Deus quanto ao homem.

Os lábios mentirosos são abominação ao SENHOR, mas os que procedem fielmente são o seu prazer –Provérbios 12:22. Admoesto-vos para que vigieis quanto à mentira, pois os mentirosos não têm parte no reino de Deus. –ver Apocalipse 21:8.

Sê diligente no trabalho e dá esmolas. Sede sempre diligentes em fazer vossa obra, onde quer que estejais; pois Paulo diz …se alguém não quiser trabalhar, também não coma –2 Tessalonicenses 3:10. Está também escrito: sede diligentes para trabalhar, para que …tenhais o que dar ao que tem necessidade –Efésios 4:28.

Não desviem o rosto do pobre. Aquele que fecha os seus ouvidos ao clamor do pobre também clamará, e não será ouvido –Provérbios 21:13. Portanto, sede diligentes em oração e amai os pobres; pois Cristo também foi pobre por amor de nós—Porque conhecestes a graça de nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo, que, sendo rico, por amor de vós se fez pobre, para que pela sua pobreza enriquecêsseis –2 Coríntios 8:9. Sede, pois, misericordiosos, assim como vosso Pai celeste é misericordioso; pois tais serão bem-aventurados e alcançarão misericórdia. –ver Mateus 5:7.

Melhor é ter pouco com o temor do SENHOR do que um grande tesouro acompanhado de inquietação –Provérbios 15:16. E, Melhor é um pedaço seco com tranquilidade do que casa cheia de festas com contenda –Provérbios 17:1. Escolhei ganhar vosso pão com o trabalho das vossas mãos e comê-lo em paz. Não procureis ser mercadores nem andeis afligidos por grande ganho.

Sede mansos, misericordiosos e puros de coração. Aprendei a ser manso e humilde de coração; pois tais são bem-aventurados e herdarão a terra. Sede, pois, misericordiosos, como também vosso Pai é misericordioso. Lucas 6:36. E, Bem-aventurados os mansos, porque herdarão a terra –Mateus 5:5. Finalmente, Bem-aventurados os limpos de coração, porque verão a Deus –Mateus 5:8. Assim, meus queridos filhos, não deixeis que pensamentos impuros permaneçam em vossos corações. Ocupai-vos com salmos, hinos e cânticos espirituais e os maus pensamentos não terão lugar. –ver Efésios 5:19.

Nem deixe que imundícia proceda de vossa boca. Devereis prestar conta de toda imundícia. –ver Mateus 12:36-37. Considerai-vos sempre os menores e não sejais sábios em vossa própria estima. Deixai-vos instruir por vossos mais velhos e estai sempre em silêncio quando outros falarem. Humilhai-vos, pois …quem a si mesmo se exaltar será humilhado; e quem a si mesmo se humilhar será exaltado –Mateus 23:12. Pois Cristo, que é o maior, fez-Se o menor como exemplo para nós. –ver João 13:13-15.

Avoid a vida luxuosa. Meus filhos, não desejeis as luxúrias de boa comida ou vinho. Aquele que deseja banquetes custosos não enriquecerá. Contentai-vos com o trabalho de vossas mãos. Não sejais fardo para ninguém enquanto puderes obter o necessário—…É mais bem-aventurado dar do que receber –Atos 20:35. Paulo diz: Tendo, pois, alimento e com que nos vestir, estejamos com isso contentes –1 Timóteo 6:8.

Sede sóbrios e agradecidos como ouvistes eu ler sobre Daniel, Sadraque, Mesaque e Abednego. Eles foram escolhidos pelo rei da Babilônia para serem nutridos com o mesmo vinho e carnes que o rei comia à sua mesa. Mas escolheram ter leguminosas [vegetais] e água. Queriam observar a lei e os mandamentos de seus pais com sobriedade e gratidão no temor de Deus. Ao fim, ficaram mais formosos e mais saudáveis que os que comeram das iguarias do rei; ver Daniel capítulo 1. Assim, andaram fielmente nos caminhos do Senhor. Tornaram-se aceitáveis a Deus em oração e súplica; por isso, ele fez grandes coisas por meio deles. Livrou-os da cova dos leões e da fornalha ardente.

Quando José foi vendido para o Egito, ele não cobiçou as iguarias mundanas. Quando a esposa do egípcio tentou seduzi-lo, temeu a Deus, e Deus o preservou. Ele agradou a Deus em sobriedade e oração e Deus o nomeou governador do Egito. –ver Gênesis capítulos 37, 39 e 41. Tomai deste exemplo na vossa mocidade e agradareis a Deus. Ele vos guardará de toda sedução.

Ó, meus cordeirinhos, ainda sois jovens, porém tendes parte no reino de vosso Pai. Vede que a conserveis bem e não como Esaú, que vendeu sua herança ou direito de primogenitura por um prato de lentilhas, desprezando a bênção de seu pai. –ver Gênesis 25:30-34. Mas Jacó escolheu a melhor parte, andando nos caminhos do Senhor com toda justiça.

Evitem a vida mundana. Não vos deleiteis nos males do mundo tais como mentir, enganar, jogar, banquetes, brincadeiras, juramentos, maldições, difamação, ódio e dança, nem inveja, embriaguez, excesso, idolatria, avareza, lascívia, vaidade, conversação imunda. Embora o mundo não considere estas coisas pecado e as chame divertimentos, contudo, são abominações aos olhos do Senhor. –ver 1 Pedro 4:3-4. Se vos agradares nessas coisas, vendeis vossa primogenitura (ou a herança espiritual) de vosso Pai por um prato de lentilhas—isto é, por alguns prazeres temporais que vos conduzem à perdição.

Escolhei sofrer aflição com os filhos de Deus. Desde o tempo de Abel até agora, muitos foram afligidos e sofreram. Foram rejeitados, desprezados, perseguidos e mortos porque não seguiam o mundo ímpio e seus falsos profetas.

Meus filhos, escolhei …antes sofrer aflição com o povo de Deus [para que possais ser recompensados com eles], do que gozar dos prazeres do pecado por um tempo –Hebreus 11:25. A tais pertencem todas as belas promessas de Deus. Está escrito: …vós chorareis e vos lamentareis, mas o mundo se alegrará; vós haveis de estar tristes, mas a vossa tristeza se converterá em alegria –João 16:20. E, Não temas nada do que hás de padecer: eis que o diabo lançará alguns de vós na prisão, para que sejais tentados; e tereis uma tribulação por dez dias; sê fiel até à morte, e dar-te-ei a coroa da vida –Apocalipse 2:10. Finalmente, Destas coisas vos tenho dito, para que em mim tenhais paz. No mundo tereis aflições; mas tende bom ânimo; eu venci o mundo –João 16:33.

Instruções ao meu filho, David. David, meu querido filho, eu vos recomendo ao Senhor. Tu és o mais velho; aprende sabedoria, para que sejas um bom exemplo para tuas irmãs. Guarda-te da má companhia e de brincar na rua com rapazes maus. Aprende diligentemente a ler e a escrever para que obtenhas entendimento.

Amai-vos uns aos outros sem contenda nem brigas. Sê bondoso com tuas irmãs. Sustentai-as como mais fortes e, por amor, ajudai tudo o que puderes. Assistí-las com amor fraternal.

Aprende a obedecer a teus mais velhos naquilo que é bom. Sê industrioso para que as pessoas te amem. Exortai-vos uns aos outros a boas obras, modéstia, honra e quietude. Cuidai sempre uns dos outros, pois chegou o tempo em que …a iniqüidade se multiplicará, e o amor de muitos esfriará –Mateus 24:12.

Guarda-te do engano. Lembra-te, Jesus disse …se isso fosse possível, enganariam até os escolhidos –Mateus 24:24. Aprende a diligentemente buscar as Escrituras para que não sejais enganados. Não creiais em boatos, mas examinai a questão.

Não crie tumulto quando for caluniado, mas suporta-o por amor de Cristo. Amai vossos inimigos e orai por aqueles que falam mal de vós e vos afligem. Sofer as aflições antes de afligir os outros. Sofrei a reprovação em vez de reprovar os outros. Sede caluniados antes de caluniares outros.

Deveis cuidar constantemente em não buscar só o vosso próprio proveito, mas zelai sempre por aqueles com quem lidais, sejam jovens ou velhos.

Instruções às minhas filhas Betgen e Tanneken, minhas queridas cordeirinhas, admoesto-vos em todas estas mesmas coisas, para que obedeçais aos mandamentos do Senhor. Obedecei também a vossos mais velhos e a todos os que vos instruem em virtude.

Sede diligentes em fazer vossa obra, e sereis amadas onde quer que vivais. Não sejais contenciosas, tagarelas, levianas, orgulhosas nem de linguagem áspera. Sede amáveis, honráveis e quietas, como convém a jovens moças.

Rogai ao Senhor por sabedoria, e ela vos será dada. Aprendei diligentemente a ler e a escrever, e alegrai-vos nisso, e vos tornareis sábias. Alegrai-vos e cantai salmos, hinos e cânticos espirituais. Aprendei a agradar ao Senhor desde a juventude, como fizeram as mulheres santas e virgens de antigamente. Ester também foi uma virgem que temia a Deus; era adornada de humildade, foi graciosa, honrada, bondosa e humilde de coração; por isso agradou ao rei Assuero acima de todas as outras virgens. –ver Ester 2:17. Mas mesmo em sua alta condição não foi orgulhosa. Embora se distinguísse em trajes reais, humilhou seu coração com jejum e oração ao Senhor, pelos seus irmãos, para que fossem livrados das mãos de seus inimigos. Não se considerou melhor do que um dos mais humildes de seus irmãos.

Quando alcançardes a idade do entendimento, vede que vos enfeiteis com as obras do Espírito, tais como bondade, mansidão, humildade, obediência, longanimidade, justiça, modéstia, honra, pureza, pacificidade, firmeza, misericórdia, sabedoria, diligência em boas obras, fé, esperança e amor. Amai a Deus acima de tudo que há no mundo e fazei ao próximo como quereis que os homens vos façam. –ver Gálatas 5:22-23 e Tito 2:3-5. Lembrai-vos que Jesus disse: …Amarás o Senhor teu Deus de todo o teu coração, de toda a tua alma e de todo o teu entendimento. Este é o primeiro e grande mandamento. E o segundo, semelhante a este, é: Amarás o teu próximo como a ti mesmo. Nesses dois mandamentos se cumprem toda a lei e os profetas –Mateus 22:37-40.

Regozijemo-nos e exultemos e demos-lhe glória; porque veio o casamento do Cordeiro, e a sua esposa já se aprontou. E foi-lhe concedido que se vestisse de linho fino, puro e resplandecente; porque o linho fino são as justiças dos santos –Apocalipse 19:7-8. Minhas filhas, este é o adorno dos santos; trabalhai por tal veste nupcial, para que possais entrar no casamento do Cordeiro, onde eles …os justos resplandecerão como o sol no reino de seu Pai… –Mateus 13:43. Que o Senhor vos conduza como conduziu Israel para fora do Egito, e vos traga à Nova Jerusalém, para que nos vejamos com alegria no dia da ressurreição. Recomendo-vos ao Senhor, o Deus de Abraão, o Deus de Isaque e o Deus de Jacó; que Ele vos guarde até o fim de vossas vidas.

Em conclusão, ó, meus queridos filhos, escrevi isto em lágrimas, admoestando-vos por amor. Minha oração e solicitude são constantemente por vossa salvação. Espero e rogo continuamente que Ele, em Sua misericórdia, vos preserve, assim como preservou José, Moisés e Daniel no meio de homens ímpios. E Ele fará isso se diligentemente seguirdes a verdade.

Esta é minha última despedida, meus queridos cordeirinhos. Lembrai-vos sempre uns dos outros em amor; aprendei diligentemente a ler e a escrever e obedecei a todos no que é bom. Despeço-me, meus queridos filhos Betgen, David e Tanneken. Adeus a todos os meus queridos irmãos e irmãs, e amigos em toda parte.

Escrito por mim, Soetgen van den Houte, vossa mãe em grilhões; escrito às pressas (tremer de frio), por amor a todos vós, amém.

Being a ruler over a group of people is marked with stress, hard decisions, and sleepless nights—certainly not a position for the mentally weak or immature. The position is difficult, be it sheriff, mayor, governor, or president. The average person does not fully mature until the age of 25, according to neuroscientific studies.1 And yet, in AD 54, a ruler was appointed who was only seventeen years old. This was no petty judge or political secretary. He was crowned ruler over one of the largest empires of the world at that time. The boy’s name was Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus—commonly called Nero. He was the fifth emperor of Rome.

Nero was not brought into power by any election or choice of his citizens. His mother, Agrippina, had married Caesar Claudius (her uncle), emperor of Rome. Claudius adopted Nero as his son. Nero would go on to marry Claudius’ daughter Octavia, his own cousin and stepsister.

On October 13, A.D. 54, Agrippina poisoned her powerful husband, and her son Nero became emperor. It was rumored that Nero and his mother had an incestuous relationship, but the new ruler was well received by his subjects and seemed eager to please them, ordering grand public buildings to be built, as well as lowering taxes and the price of food. However, it was not to last.

Nero soon killed his brother-in-law, who was fourteen, which angered his wife. At this point, the emperor was in a relationship with a freedwoman (a formerly enslaved person), so he had his wife exiled. When this sparked public outrage, he had Octavia beheaded on false charges of being unfaithful.

He then became infatuated with a woman named Poppaea Sabina, who was scheming to marry him. Sabina roused Nero to such fear and jealousy that he decided to kill his mother for fear of losing the throne. The plan was simple—while Agrippina was on a cruise ship, it would be discreetly sunk, and Nero’s mother would drown. However, this was not to be. Agrippina was a strong swimmer and escaped with her life. Undeterred, Nero dispatched his executioners to stab her to death in broad daylight. Unfortunately, things had just gotten started for the most powerful man in the empire and these bizarre and inhuman acts were only a sampling of what was to come.

Nero was given to fits of rage and became violent towards his wife in one such outburst. He kicked Sabina repeatedly until both she and her unborn child died. Nero is said to have regretted this, and he soon started a hunt for anyone who looked like Sabina, his dead wife. He finally found a slave that is said to have resembled her strongly, and they were married. The catch? The slave was a man. Nero took to dressing him in the clothing of a woman and referring to him as a lady. At this point, Nero’s slippery slope was only getting more slippery. He believed himself to be an artist—a genius, even—and gave massive public performances. If you were in attendance, you could not leave. Why? The doors were locked. Nero also dreamed of singing to his enemies and bringing them to tears for their perceived wrongdoings.

But the emperor was not content with only putting on musical performances. In A.D. 67, he entered into the Olympic Games, which was against the rules (no emperor was allowed to compete in the Games). Nevertheless, Nero entered. He introduced new competitions, such as trumpeting and acting. He entered into several and won each one. His actions caused much outrage since the Olympics were considered a sacred event and Nero had changed them.

However, Nero had an even bigger goal in mind. The chariot races were the biggest spectacle the Olympics had to offer. In them, chariot riders were allowed a team of four horses. Teams would race around a massive arena for a total of seven laps. Sometimes wheels fell off, or chariots crashed into each other. It was not uncommon for drivers to be thrown from their ride and to be trampled to death or to be dragged by their own team of horses. However, the winner would be celebrated and highly paid.

Knowing all the difficulty, danger, and stress involved, you can only imagine how the charioteers felt to see Emperor Nero roll up to the racetrack in an expensive chariot and a team consisting of not four, but ten horses. As it turns out, Nero was inexperienced and out of shape. Almost immediately, he lost control of his team and was thrown from the chariot, being seriously injured in the process. Despite never finishing the race, Nero won first place.

This incident does a good job of demonstrating Nero’s attitude toward his authority at this point in his reign. In fact, in A.D. 66, he won more than 1,800 first-place prizes for his supposed exhibits of artistry. Here was a man that could not be told “no”.

On the night of July 18, A.D. 64, a fire started in Rome’s Circus Maximus. The fire grew and spread, becoming out of control. The fire would rage for the next six days, leaving almost no part of the city untouched. It was devastating for the citizens of Rome and would go on to be the incident Nero would be most widely known for. Many ancient writers blamed Nero for starting the fire, although he was not in the city when it began. Whether or not he started the fire, Nero needed someone to blame. He chose a group of people who were despised and feared by the Romans and tortured them relentlessly. That group was known as the Christians. Tacitus, a secular Roman writer, described it as such, “Nero fastened the guilt and inflicted the most exquisite tortures on a class hated for their abominations, called Christians by the populace. Mockery of every sort was added to their deaths. Covered with the skins of beasts, they were torn by dogs and perished, or were nailed to crosses, or were doomed to the flames and burnt, to serve as nightly illumination when daylight had expired.”

Meanwhile, Nero grew even more wicked. He ruthlessly slaughtered Christian men, women, and children, and plunged ever deeper into immorality. Finally, On June 9, AD 68, Nero, the last emperor of Rome killed himself after having been declared a public enemy by the Roman Senate. He was only 31 years old.

So, here is a man corrupt in every way. His lifestyle was deeply offensive to Christianity, and his persecution was one of the most horrible in history. How would we respond to such a ruler? How did Christians respond to him?

Paul lived under Nero’s reign. He saw all the horrible things detailed above. Yet, he gave the church the following admonition: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake –Romans 13: 1-5.

These words seem impossible when we consider the situation. Yet the Word of God tells us that our governmental authorities are put in place by God Himself. What a testimony! How much more, then, are we called to respect our authorities—to not slander them; to obey them in all possible aspects; to stay away from their elections and campaigns; and yet, to yield ourselves to God and His authority as our final say?! Or, as Paul put it, Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God… –Romans 13:1.

The believers of the early church saw Nero—the murderous, bloodthirsty, corrupt emperor—as a man ordained of God. They sought to honor and respect him in his authority, while ultimately yielding to the higher authority of God. Herein, we see a potential paradox, that the earthly authorities are “ministers of God” to be honored and obeyed, yet IF the time would come wherein the believer is required by the civil authorities to disobey God, we then have a higher responsibility—…We ought to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29.

This all puts a great responsibility on our shoulders today as Christians living in an increasingly corrupt and evil society. Can we find that biblical balance between honoring our governmental leaders while still obeying God in all things? Or do we fail just like the unregenerate around us in picking apart the faults of our earthly authorities when we feel our “easy living” being trodden upon?

See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is –Ephesians 5:15-17. And Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful –1 Corinthians 4:2.

Let each one of us as committed, born-again, Bible-believing Christians walk circumspectly, redeeming the time. For we all want to be found faithful in that soon-coming day when we all will stand before the judgment seat to receive our just reward.

Kuwa mtawala juu ya kikundi cha watu kunaambatana na msongo wa mawazo, maamuzi magumu, na usingizi mdogo—hakika si nafasi kwa watu dhaifu kisaikolojia au wasiolewa kiakili. Nafasi hiyo ni ngumu, iwe sheriff, meya, gavana, au rais. Mtu wa kawaida hajakomaa kikamilifu hadi umri wa miaka 25, kulingana na tafiti za neurosayansi.1 Na hata hivyo, mwaka wa 54 BK, mtawala aliwekwa mwenye umri wa miaka kumi na saba tu. Huyu si hakimu mdogo wala katibu wa siasa. Aliteuliwa kuwa mtawala wa moja ya milki kubwa zaidi duniani wakati huo. Jina la mvulana huyo lilikuwa Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus—anayejulikana kwa kawaida kama Nero. Alikuwa mfalme wa tano wa Waroma.

Nero hakupandishwa madarakani kwa uchaguzi wala kwa hiari ya raia wake. Mama yake, Agrippina, alikuwa ameolewa na Kaisari Claudius (mjukuu wake), mfalme wa Waroma. Claudius alimchukua Nero kama mwana. Nero baadaye aliolewa na binti wa Claudius, Octavia, ambaye alikuwa binamu yake na kwa upande mmoja dada yake wa hatua.

Kufikia Oktoba 13, mwaka wa 54 BK, Agrippina alimlidha mumewe mwenye nguvu, na mwanawe Nero akawa mfalme. Kulikuwa na uvumi kwamba Nero na mama yake walikuwa na uhusiano wa kifamilia, lakini mtawala mpya alikubaliwa vizuri na watu wake na alionekana kuwa tayari kuwafurahisha, akamwagilia amri ujenzi wa majengo makubwa ya umma, pamoja na kupunguza ushuru na bei ya vyakula. Hata hivyo, hilo halikuendelea kwa muda mrefu.

Nero hivi karibuni aliua shemeji yake, ambaye alikuwa na umri wa miaka kumi na nne, jambo ambalo lilimkasirisha mkewe. Wakati huo, mfalme alikuwa katika uhusiano na mwanamke aliyeachiwa uwe esemabali (aliyehuruwa kutoka utumwa), hivyo akamtuma mke wake kutoroka nchi. Hii ilipopasua hasira za umma, aliamuru Octavia achanwe kwa madai ya uminyofu wa uongo.

Kisha alijihusisha kimapenzi na mwanamke aitwaye Poppaea Sabina, ambaye alikuwa akipanga kumwoea. Sabina alimfanya Nero kuwa na hofu na wivu kiasi kwamba akamua kuua mama yake kwa hofu ya kupoteza taji. Mpango ulikuwa rahisi—wakati Agrippina alikuwa katika meli ya kusafiria, ingenibomolewa kwa siri, na mama wa Nero angezama. Hata hivyo, hivyo hakutokea. Agrippina alikuwa mpigaji wa kuogelea hodari na alitoroka kwa kuokolewa maisha yake. Akishindwa, Nero alituma wakatemwa wake wa kuuawa wamchomee kwa visu mchana wazi. Kwa bahati mbaya, mambo yalikuwa tu yameanza kwa mtu mwenye mamlaka zaidi katika milki na matendo haya ya kustaajabisha na ya kibinadamu yalikuwa ni sampuli tu ya yatakayofuata.

Nero alimpata wimbi la hasira na akawa mkali dhidi ya mkewe katika moja ya milipuko yake. Alimpiga Sabina mara kwa mara hadi yeye na mtoto aliyejifungua walikufa. Inasemwa Nero alijuta hili, na hivi karibuni alianza kuwinda yeyote aliyekuwa na sura inayomkumbusha Sabina, mkewe aliyekufa. Hatimaye alipata mfungwa ambaye inasemwa alimfanana sana naye, na waliolewa. Tatizo? Mfungwa huyo alikuwa mwanaume. Nero alimfanyia mavazi ya mwanamke na kumtaja kama bibi. Hapo ndipo uelekeo wa Nero ulipoanza kugeuka zaidi na zaidi. Alijiamini kuwa msanii—bale kuwa geniusi—na alifanya tamasha kubwa za umma. Ikiwa ulikuwa mgeni, hakuweza kuondoka. Kwa nini? Milango ilikuwa imefungwa. Nero pia aliota kuimba kwa adui zake na kuwafanya walilie kwa sababu ya ubaya ulioonekana wao kufanya.

Lakini mfalme hakuridhika kwa kuwasilisha tu maonyesho ya muziki. Mwaka wa 67 BK, alishiriki katika Michezo ya Olimpiki, jambo lililokuwa kinyume cha sheria (hakukuwa binti yeyote wa mfalme anayeweza kushiriki katika Michezo). Hata hivyo, Nero alishiriki. Alianzisha mashindano mapya, kama kupiga tarumbeta na utendakazi. Alishiriki katika kadhaa na kushinda kila moja. Matendo yake yalileta hasira kwa kuwa Olimpiki zilizingatiwa tukio takatifu na Nero alikuwa amezibadilisha.

Hata hivyo, Nero alikuwa na lengo kubwa zaidi akilini. Mashindano ya magari ya kibanda (chariot races) yalikuwa burudani kuu Olimpiki zilizoweza kutoa. Katika mashindano hayo, wavumbuzi wa magari waliokolea waliruhusiwa kuwa na timu ya farasi wanne. Timu zingepiga mbio katika uwanja mkubwa kwa jumla ya mizunguko saba. Wakati mwingine magurudumu yalitoka, au magari yaligongana. Si jambo la kawaida kwa madereva kurushwa nje ya gari lao na kupasuliwa hadi kufa au kuvutwa na timu yao ya farasi. Hata hivyo, mshindi angeadhimishwa na kulipwa kwa kiwango kikubwa.

Ukijua wote jana changamoto, hatari, na msongo wa mawazo ulihusishwa, unaweza tu kufikiria jinsi wapanda magari walivyohisi walipomuona Mfalme Nero akifika uwanjani katika gari la gharama kubwa na timu ya farasi sio wanne, bali kumi. Kama ilivyojitokeza, Nero alikuwa hana uzoefu na alikuwa hana mazoezi. Karibu mara moja, alipoteza udhibiti wa timu yake na aliruswa kutoka kwenye gari, akajeruhiwa vibaya katika mchakato. Licha ya kutokumaliza mbio hiyo, Nero alishinda nafasi ya kwanza.

Tukio hili linaonyesha vizuri mtazamo wa Nero kuhusu mamlaka yake katika kipindi hiki cha utawala wake. Kwa kweli, mwaka wa 66 BK, alishinda zaidi ya tuzo 1,800 za nafasi ya kwanza kwa wazi kwa maonyesho yake ya ujanja wa kisanii. Huyu alikuwa mtu ambaye hakuweza kusemwa “hapana”.

Usiku wa Julai 18, mwaka wa 64 BK, moto ulianza katika Circus Maximus ya Roma. Moto ulienea na kukua, ukageuka ukawa wa nje ya udhibiti. Moto huo ulizidi kwa siku sita zifuatazo, ukiacha sehemu ndogo tu ya mji bila kuguswa. Ilikuwa ni maafa kwa raia wa Roma na itakuwa tukio ambalo Nero atajulikana kwa upana juu yake. Waandishi wengi wa kale walimlaumu Nero kwa kuwasha moto huo, ingawa hakuwa mjini wakati ulipoanza. Iwapo aliuanzisha moto au la, Nero alihitaji mtu wa kumlaumu. Alichagua kundi la watu waliokasirishwa na kuogeshwa na Waroma na kuwatendea mateso bila huruma. Kundi hilo lilijulikana kama Wakristo. Tacitus, mwandishi wa kiraia wa Roma, alielezea hivyo, “Nero akabana hatia na akawatia mateso mazito ya namna ya kupendeza kwa tabaka lililochukiwa kwa uharibifu wao, likiwa linaitwa Wakristo na umma. Kicheko cha kila aina kiliongezwa kwa vifo vyao. Wakiwa wamefunikwa ngozi za wanyama, walichyomwa na mbwa wakafa, au walikabiliwa kushikiliwa kwa mivuko, au walitolewa kwa moto na kuchomwa, kutumika kama taa za usiku wakati mwanga wa mchana ulikuwa umekwisha.”

Wakati huo huo, Nero alizidi kuwa mbaya zaidi. Aliwaua kwa ukatili wanaume, wanawake, na watoto Wakristo, na akajimwagia ndani ya ukovu zaidi ya maadili. Mwisho, tarehe 9 Juni, mwaka wa 68 BK, Nero, mfalme wa mwisho wa Roma, alijinyonga baada ya kutangazwa kuwa adui wa umma na Seneti ya Roma. Alikuwa na umri wa miaka 31 tu.

Basi, huwapo mtu aliyevurugika kwa kila upande. Mtindo wake wa maisha ulikuwa kero kubwa kwa Ukristo, na mateso yake yalikuwa mojawapo ya mabaya zaidi katika historia. Tutamlipia vipi mtawala kama huyo? Wakristo walitimiza vipi kwa mwelekeo wake?

Paulo aliishi wakati wa utawala wa Nero. Aliwona yote mabaya yaliyotajwa hapo juu. Hata hivyo, alitoa onyo zifuatazo kwa kanisa: “Kila nafsi imtii mamlakani juu yake. Kwa maana hakuna mamlaka ila ya Mungu; zile zilizopo zimetangazwa na Mungu. Kwa hivyo, ambaye anapingana na mamlaka, anapingana na utaratibu wa Mungu; na wale wanaopingana watapokea hukumu juu yao wenyewe. Kwa maana wateule si ya kuogopesha kwa vitendo vyema, bali kwa uovu. Je, basi hupaswi kuogopa mamlaka? Fanya yale yaliyo mema, na utapata sifa yake; kwa maana yeye ni mtumishi wa Mungu kwako kwa mema. Lakini ukifanya uovu, ogopa; kwa maana yeye si kubeba upanga bure; kwa kuwa yeye ni mtumishi wa Mungu, mwalipaji atenda ghadhabu kwa kufanya uovu. Hivyo basi lazima muwe wakoo, si kwa ghadhabu tu, bali pia kwa dhamiri.” —Waroma 13:1-5.

Maneno haya yanaonekana yasiyowezekana tukizingatia hali ilivyokuwa. Hata hivyo Neno la Mungu linasema kwamba mamlaka zetu za kisiasa zimewekwa na Mwenyezi Mungu mwenyewe. Ni ushuhuda gani! Je, basi si tumeitwa kuheshimu viongozi wetu—kutochafua jina lao; kuwatii katika mambo yote yanayowezekana; kukaa mbali na uchaguzi na kampeni zao; na hata hivyo, kujiweka chini ya Mwenyezi Mungu na mamlaka yake kama uamuzi wetu wa mwisho?! Au kama Paulo alivyosema, “Kila nafsi imtii mamlakani juu yake. Kwa maana hakuna mamlaka ila ya Mungu… —Waroma 13:1.”

Waumini wa kanisa la mwanzo waliiona Nero—mfalme mchukumu, mwili wa damu, aliyeharibiwa—kama mtu aliyeteuliwa na Mungu. Walitafuta kumheshimu na kumtii kwa mamlaka yake, wakati hatimaye wakijiweka chini ya mamlaka ya juu ya Mungu. Hapa, tunaona pande mbili zinazoweza kukanushwa, kwamba mamlaka ya duniani ni “watumishi wa Mungu” wanaostahili kuheshimiwa na kutiiwa, lakini IKIWA wakati utakuja ambapo muumini atatakiwa na mamlaka za kifalme kukiuka amri za Mungu, basi tuna wajibu wa juu—“Ni lazima tumtii Mungu badala ya watu”—Matendo 5:29.

Hili yote linaweka jukumu kubwa kwa mabegani mwetu leo sisi Wakristo tunaoishi katika jamii inayoongezeka kuwa ya rushwa na uovu. Je, tunaweza kupata ule uwiano wa kibiblia kati ya kuheshimu viongozi wetu wa serikali wakati bado tukimtumikia Mungu katika kila jambo? Au tunashindwa kama wasiookolewa waliotuzunguka kwa kuchambua makosa ya mamlaka ya duniani tunapohisi maisha yetu ya “urahisi” yanathibitika?

“Basi muangalieni kwa uangalifu jinsi mnavyotembea, si kama wapumbavu, bali kama wenye busara, mkitumia wakati, maana siku ni mbaya. Kwa hivyo msipoteze busara, bali mnielewe mapenzi ya Bwana.” —Waefeso 5:15-17. Na “Mtu aone kwetu kama watumishi wa Kristo, na wasimamizi wa siri za Mungu. Kwa zaidi, katika wasimamizi inahitajika mtu apatikane mwaminifu.” —1 Wakorintho 4:1-2.

Tumbe kila mmoja wetu kama Wakristo waliomwagika, waliobatizwa upya, wanaoamini Biblia, watembelee kwa tahadhari, wakichukuwa wakati. Kwa maana sote tunataka kupatikana kuwa waaminifu siku ile ya karibuni wakati sote tutasimama mbele ya kiti cha hukumu kupokea tuzo zetu za haki.

On November 27, 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte of Ghent, Holland was martyred for her faith in the Lord, Jesus Christ. Prior to her passing, her husband had also been martyred for his faith. During the time of her imprisonment, she wrote several lengthy letters to her three youth-aged children. The following are abridged excerpts of these letters which can be found in full text on pages 646-651 in the Martyr’s Mirror.

Grace, peace, and mercy from God, the Father, and the Lord, Jesus Christ, to my dear children, David, Betgen, and Tanneken. This affectionate greeting, written by your mother in bonds, is a memorial of the truth to you. I hope to testify to this Truth by my words, my life, and my death, with the help of the Most High. May the wisdom of the Holy Ghost instruct and strengthen you, that you may be brought up in the ways of the Lord. Since it pleases the Lord to take me out of this world, I will leave you this memorial of my faith in the only true God, not of silver or gold for such jewels are perishable.

Receive admonition. First, I admonish you, my most beloved children, always allow yourselves to be instructed by those who fear the Lord. As long as you obey good admonition and instruction, God will be your Father and not leave you as orphans. For David says: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose –Psalm 25:12. Children, grieve not when you are corrected and do not speak in anger to those who correct you. A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke –Proverbs 13:1.

Guard your tongue. My dear children, guard your tongue, that it speak no evil. Do not practice deceit or backbiting with your lips. Paul teaches us to live peaceably with all men if it be possible. –see 1 Peter 3:10 and Romans 12:18. If you are crossly spoken to, learn to answer kindly, and you will be loved by all men. Humility and meekness are acceptable to both God and man.

Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight –Proverbs 12:22. I admonish you to beware of lying, since liars have no part in the kingdom of God. –see Revelation 21:8.

Be diligent in work and give alms. Always be diligent to do your work, wherever you be; for Paul says …that if any would not work, neither should he eat –2 Thessalonians 3:10. It is also written, be diligent to labor, that you …may have to give to him that needeth –Ephesians 4:28.

Do not turn your face away from the poor. Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard –Proverbs 21:13. Therefore, be diligent in prayer, and love the poor; for Christ also was poor for our sakes—For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich –2 Corinthians 8:9. Be therefore also merciful, even as your heavenly Father is merciful; for such shall be blessed, and shall obtain mercy. –see Matthew 5:7.

Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith –Proverbs 15:16. And, Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife –Proverbs 17:1. Choose to earn your bread by the labor of your hands, and to eat your bread with peace. Seek not to be a merchant, nor be anxious for great gain.

Be meek, merciful, and pure in heart. Learn to be meek and lowly in heart for such are blessed and shall inherit the earth. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Luke 6:36. And, Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth –Matthew 5:5. Finally, Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God –Matthew 5:8. Hence, my dear children, let no impure thoughts remain in your hearts. Engage yourselves with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs and evil thoughts will have no room. –see Ephesians 5:19.

Neither let filthiness proceed out of your mouth. You will have to give an account of all filthiness. –see Matthew 12:36-37. Always esteem yourselves as the least and be not wise in your own conceit. Allow yourselves to be instructed by your elders and always be silent when others speak. Humble yourselves, for …whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted –Matthew 23:12. For Christ who is the greatest made Himself the least for an example unto us. –see John 13:13-15.

Avoid a luxurious life. My children, do not desire the luxuries of fine food or wine. He that desires costly feasts will not become rich. Be content with the labor of your hands. Do not be a burden to anyone as long as you can obtain the things needful—…It is more blessed to give than to receive –Acts 20:35. Paul says: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Be sober and thankful as you have heard me read of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They were selected by the king of Babylon to be nourished with the same wine and meat which the king drank and ate at his table. But they chose to have pulse [vegetables] and water. They wanted to observe the law and commandments of their fathers with sobriety and thankfulness in the fear of God. In the end, they were fairer and fatter than those who ate of the king’s dainties, see Daniel chapter 1. Thus, faithfully they walked in the ways of the Lord. They made themselves acceptable to God in prayer and supplication, therefore, he did great things through them. He delivered them from the den of lions and out of the fiery furnace.

When Joseph was sold into Egypt, he desired no worldly dainties. When the Egyptian woman sought to seduce him, he feared God, and God preserved him. He pleased God in sobriety and prayer and God appointed him ruler over Egypt. –see Genesis chapters 37, 39, and 41. Take an example from this in your youth and you will please God. He will keep you from all seduction.

Oh, my lambs, you are still in your youth, yet you have a part in your Father’s kingdom. See that you keep it well and not as Esau who gave his inheritance or birthright for a mess of pottage, disregarding his father’s blessing. –see Genesis 25:30-34. But Jacob chose the better part, walking in the ways of the Lord with all righteousness.

Shun worldly living. Do not delight in the evils of the world such as lying, cheating, gambling, banqueting, playing, swearing, cursing, backbiting, hatred, and dancing, nor envy, drunkenness, excess, idolatry, covetousness, lasciviousness, vanity, filthy conversation. Though the world does not consider these things to be sin but rather calls them amusements, nevertheless, they are abominations in the eyes of the Lord. –see 1 Peter 4:3-4. If you take pleasure in these things, you sell your birthright (or the spiritual inheritance) from your Father, for a mess of pottage—namely, for a few temporal pleasures, which lead you to damnation.

Choose to suffer affliction with the children of God. From the time of Abel until now many have been afflicted and have suffered. They were rejected, despised, persecuted, and killed because they would not follow the wicked world and her false prophets.

My children, choose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God [that you may be rewarded with them], than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25. Unto such belong all the beautiful promises of God. It is written: …ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy –John 16:20. And, Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life –Revelation 2:10. Finally, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world –John 16:33.

Instructions to my son, David. David, my dear son, I commend you to the Lord. You are the oldest; learn wisdom, so that you may be a good example to your sisters. Beware of bad company and of playing in the street with bad boys. Diligently learn to read and write so that you may get understanding.

Love one another without contention or quarreling. Be kind to your sisters. Bear them up as the stronger and out of love help all you can. Assist them out of brotherly love.

Learn to obey your elders in that which is good. Be industrious so that people may love you. Exhort one another to good works, modesty, honorableness, and quietness. Always care for one another for the time has come that …iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold –Matthew 24:12.

Beware of deception. Remember, Jesus said …that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect –Matthew 24:24. Learn to diligently search the Scriptures so that you may not be deceived. Do not believe gossip but examine the matter.

Make no commotion when you are slandered but bear it for Christ’s sake. Love your enemies and pray for those who speak evil of you and afflict you. Suffer affliction rather than afflicting others. Suffer reproach rather than reproaching others. Be slandered rather than slandering others.

You must constantly see that you do not seek solely your own profit, but always care for those with whom you have dealings, whether they be young or old.

Instructions to my daughters Betgen and Tanneken, my beloved lambs, I admonish you in all these same things, that you obey the commandments of the Lord. Also, obey your elders and all who instruct you in virtue.

Be diligent to do your work, and you will be loved wherever you live. Don’t be quarrelsome, talkative, light-minded, proud, or surly of speech. Be kind, honorable, and quiet, as behooves young girls.

Pray the Lord for wisdom, and it shall be given you. Diligently learn to read and write, and take delight therein, and you will become wise. Take pleasure and sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Learn to please the Lord from your youth, as did the holy women and virgins of old. Esther also was a virgin who feared God; she was adorned with humility, was gracious, honorable, kind, and humble of heart; hence she pleased King Ahasuerus above all the other virgins. –see Esther 2:17. But even in her high estate she was not proud. Though she shone in royal apparel, she humbled her heart with fasting and prayer to the Lord, for her brethren, that they might be delivered out of the hands of their enemies. She did not esteem herself better than one of the least of her brethren.

When you have attained the years of understanding, see that you adorn yourselves with the works of the Spirit such as goodness, gentleness, meekness, humility, obedience, long suffering, righteousness, modesty, honorableness, purity, peaceableness, steadfastness, mercifulness, wisdom, diligence in good works, faith, hope and love. Love God above all that is in the world and do to your neighbor as you would have men do unto you. –see Galatians 5:22-23 and Titus 2:3-5. Remember that Jesus said: …Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets –Matthew 22:37-40.

Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints –Revelation 19:7-8. My daughters, this is the adornment of the saints; labor for such a wedding garment, so that you may enter into the marriage of the Lamb, where they …the righteous, [shall] shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father… –Matthew 13:43. May the Lord lead you as He led Israel out of Egypt, and bring you to the New Jerusalem, that we may see each other with joy in the day of the resurrection. I commend you to the Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; may He keep you to the end of your lives.

In conclusion, O my dear children, I have written this in tears, admonishing you out of love. My prayer and solicitude are constantly for your salvation. I hope and pray constantly that He, in His mercy, will preserve you, just as He preserved Joseph, Moses, and Daniel in the midst of wicked men. And He will do this if you give diligence to follow the truth.

This is my last farewell, my dear lambs. always remember each other in love; diligently learn to read and write and obey everyone in that which is good. I bid you adieu, my dear children Betgen, David and Tanneken. Adieu all my dear brethren and sisters, and friends everywhere.

Written by me, Soetgen van den Houte, your mother in bonds; written in haste (while trembling with cold), out of love for you all, amen.

Op 27 november 1560 werd Sotegen Van Den Houte uit Gent, Holland, gemarteld voor haar geloof in de Heere Jezus Christus. Voor haar overlijden was ook haar man om zijn geloof gemarteld. Tijdens haar gevangenschap schreef zij verschillende lange brieven aan haar drie kinderen die nog jong waren. Hieronder volgen ingekorte fragmenten van deze brieven die volledig te vinden zijn op bladzijden 646–651 in de Martyr’s Mirror.

Genade, vrede en barmhartigheid van God de Vader en de Heere Jezus Christus, aan mijn dierbare kinderen, David, Betgen en Tanneken. Deze liefdevolle groet, geschreven door uw moeder in ketenen, is een gedenkteken van de waarheid voor u. Ik hoop deze Waarheid te getuigen met mijn woorden, mijn leven en mijn dood, met de hulp van de Allerhoogste. Moge de wijsheid van de Heilige Geest u onderwijzen en versterken, opdat u wordt opgevoed in de wegen des Heren. Omdat het de Heere behaagt Mij uit deze wereld weg te nemen, laat ik u dit gedenkteken na van mijn geloof in de enige ware God, niet van zilver of goud, want zulke juwelen zijn vergankelijk.

Ontvang vermaning. Eerst vermanen ik u, mijn meest geliefde kinderen, laat u altijd onderwijzen door degenen die de Heere vrezen. Zolang u goede vermaning en onderwijs gehoorzaamt, zal God uw Vader zijn en u niet als wezen achterlaten. Want David zegt: Wie is de man die de HEERE vreest? Die zal Hij onderwijzen in de weg die Hij kiezen zal –Psalmen 25:12. Kinderen, treur niet wanneer u wordt gecorrigeerd en spreek niet in toorn tot degenen die u corrigeren. Een wijs kind hoort de chastijning van zijn vader; maar spotters horen geen terechtwijzing –Spreuken 13:1.

Bewaar uw tong. Mijn lieve kinderen, bewaart uw tong, opdat zij geen kwaad spreekt. Oefent geen bedrog of lastering met uw lippen. Paulus leert ons met alle mensen zoveel mogelijk in vrede te leven. –zie 1 Petrus 3:10 en Romeinen 12:18. Als men u hard aanspreekt, leert dan vriendelijk te antwoorden, en u zult door alle mensen bemind worden. Nederigheid en zachtmoedigheid zijn aangenaam voor zowel God als mensen.

Valse lippen zijn een gruwel voor de HEERE, maar die waarheid spreken, Zijn aangenaamheid –Spreuken 12:22. Ik vermanen u om op uw hoede te zijn voor liegen, want leugenaars hebben geen deel aan het koninkrijk van God. –zie Openbaring 21:8.

Wees ijverig in werk en geef aalmoezen. Wees altijd ijverig om uw werk te doen, waar u ook zijt; want Paulus zegt: …want als iemand niet wil werken, zal hij ook niet eten –2 Thessalonicenzen 3:10. Het is ook geschreven: wees ijverig om te arbeiden, opdat u …iets overhoudt om te geven aan wie gebrek heeft –Efeziërs 4:28.

Keert uw aangezicht niet af van de armen. Wie zijn oor sluit voor het gekerm van de armen, die zal ook roepen en niet gehoord worden –Spreuken 21:13. Wees daarom ijverig in gebed en heb de armen lief; want Christus was ook arm ter wille van ons—Want gij weet de genade van onzen Heere Jezus Christus, dat Hij, hoewel Hij rijk was, om uws wille arm is geworden, opdat gij door zijn armoede rijk zoudt worden –2 Korintiërs 8:9. Weest daarom ook barmhartig, gelijk uw hemelse Vader barmhartig is; want zodanigen zullen gezegend worden en barmhartigheid verkrijgen. –zie Matteüs 5:7.

Beter is weinig met de vreze des HEEREN dan grote schatten en daardoor bevangenheid –Spreuken 15:16. En, Beter is een droge brok met stilte daarmede, dan een huis vol offers met twist –Spreuken 17:1. Kies om uw brood te verdienen door het werk van uw handen en uw brood in vrede te eten. Streef er niet naar koopman te zijn, noch bezorgd te zijn om grote winst.

Wees zachtmoedig, barmhartig en rein van hart. Leert zachtmoedig en ootmoedig van hart te zijn, want zulke zijn zalig en zullen de aarde beërven. Weest dan barmhartig, gelijk uw Vader ook barmhartig is. Lucas 6:36. En, Zalig zijn de zachtmoedigen: want zij zullen de aarde beërven –Mattheüs 5:5. Ten slotte, Zalig zijn de reinen van hart: want zij zullen God zien –Mattheüs 5:8. Dus, mijn lieve kinderen, laat geen onreine gedachten in uw harten achterblijven. Houd u bezig met psalmen, lofzangen en geestelijke liederen en kwade gedachten zullen geen plaats hebben. –zie Efeziërs 5:19.

Laat ook geen vuile gesprekken uit uw mond komen. U zult rekenschap moeten geven van alle vuile woorden. –zie Mattheüs 12:36-37. Houdt uzelf altijd voor het geringste en wees niet wijs in uw eigen ogen. Laat u door uw ouderen onderwijzen en zwijgt altijd wanneer anderen spreken. Verneder uzelf, want …wie zich zal verheffen, zal vernederd worden; en wie zich zal vernederen, zal verheven worden –Mattheüs 23:12. Want Christus, die de grootste is, maakte Zichzelf de geringste tot een voorbeeld voor ons. –zie Johannes 13:13-15.

Vermijdt een luxueus leven. Mijn kinderen, begeer niet de luxe van fijn voedsel of wijn. Wie kostbare banketten begeert, zal niet rijk worden. Wees tevreden met het werk van uw handen. Weest niemand tot last zolang u de nodige dingen zelf kunt verkrijgen—…het is zaliger te geven dan te ontvangen –Handelingen 20:35. Paulus zegt: Als wij voedsel en kleding hebben, zo zullen wij daarmee te vrede zijn –1 Timoteüs 6:8.

Wees nuchter en dankbaar zoals u hebt gehoord dat ik gelezen heb over Daniël, Sadrach, Meshach en Abednego. Zij werden uitgekozen door de koning van Babel om gevoed te worden met dezelfde wijn en spijzen als de koning aan zijn tafel dronk en at. Maar zij kozen om groenten en water te hebben. Zij wilden de wet en de geboden van hun vaderen in nuchterheid en dankbaarheid houden in de vreze Gods. In het einde waren zij frisser en ronder dan degenen die van de lekkernijen van de koning aten, zie Daniël hoofdstuk 1. Zo wandelden zij getrouw in de wegen des Heren. Zij maakten zich in gebed en smeking aan God aannemelijk; daarom deed Hij grote dingen door hen. Hij verloste hen uit de leeuwenkuil en uit het vuur van de oven.

Wanneer Jozef in Egypte verkocht werd, begeerde hij geen wereldse lekkernijen. Toen de Egyptische vrouw hem trachtte te verleiden, vreesde hij God en God bewaarde hem. Hij behaagde God in nuchterheid en gebed en God stelde hem aan als heerser over Egypte. –zie Genesis hoofdstukken 37, 39 en 41. Neem hier een voorbeeld aan in uw jeugd en u zult God behagen. Hij zal u bewaren voor alle verzoeking.

O mijn lammeren, u bent nog jong, toch hebt u deel aan het koninkrijk van uw Vader. Zorg dat u het goed bewaart en niet zoals Ezau die zijn erfdeel of geboortegrond verkocht voor een bord linzen en geen acht sloeg op de zegen van zijn vader. –zie Genesis 25:30-34. Maar Jacob koos het betere deel en wandelde in de wegen des Heren in alle gerechtigheid.

Vermijdt werelds leven. Verheugt u niet in de boosheden der wereld zoals liegen, bedriegen, gokken, buitensporige banketten, spelen, vloeken, vervloeken, lasteren, haat en dansen, noch ijver, dronkenschap, overvloed, afgoderij, hebzucht, wellust, ijdelheid, vuile conversatie. Hoewel de wereld deze dingen niet als zonde beschouwt maar veeleer als vermaak, zijn zij toch gruwelen in de ogen des Heeren. –zie 1 Petrus 4:3-4. Als u plezier schept in deze dingen, verkoopt u uw erfdeel (of de geestelijke erfenis) van uw Vader voor een bord linzen—namelijk voor een paar tijdelijke genoegens, die u naar verdoemenis leiden.

Kiest liever lijden met de kinderen van God. Van de tijd van Abel tot nu zijn velen beknot en geleden. Zij werden verworpen, veracht, vervolgd en gedood omdat zij de boze wereld en haar valse profeten niet wilden volgen.

Mijn kinderen, kiest …liever met het volk Gods te lijden [opdat u met hen vergolden wordt], dan de genieting der zonde voor een tijd –Hebreeën 11:25. Aan zodanigen toebehoren alle heerlijke beloften van God. Het is geschreven: …gij zult treuren en rouw hebben, maar de wereld zal zich verblijden; gij zult bedroefd zijn, maar uw bedroefdheid zal in blijdschap veranderen –Johannes 16:20. En, Vrees niet hetgeen gij zult lijden: zie, de duivel zal sommigen van u in de gevangenis werpen, opdat gij beproefd wordt; en gij zult tien dagen verdrukking hebben; wees getrouw tot de dood, en Ik zal u de kroon des levens geven –Openbaring 2:10. Ten slotte, Deze dingen heb Ik tot u gesproken, opdat gij in Mij vrede zou hebben. In de wereld zult gij verdrukking hebben; maar hebt goede moed, Ik heb de wereld overwonnen –Johannes 16:33.

Instructies aan mijn zoon, David. David, mijn lieve zoon, ik beveel u aan aan den Heere. U bent de oudste; leert wijsheid, opdat u een goed voorbeeld zijt voor uw zusters. Weest op uw hoede voor slecht gezelschap en voor spelen op straat met kwajongens. Leer ijverig lezen en schrijven zodat u inzicht verkrijgt.

Hebt elkander lief zonder twist of geruzie. Weest vriendelijk jegens uw zusters. Ondersteunt hen als de sterkere en helpt uit liefde zoveel als u kunt. Assisteer hen uit broederlijke liefde.

Leert uw ouderen te gehoorzamen in hetgeen goed is. Weest ijverig zodat mensen u liefhebben. Vermanen elkander tot goede werken, kuisheid, eerbaarheid en stilte. Zorg altijd voor elkander want de tijd is gekomen dat …de ongerechtigheid zal toenemen, en de liefde van velen zal verkillen –Mattheüs 24:12.

Weest op uw hoede voor bedrog. Gedenkt, Jezus zei: …dat, indien het mogelijk ware, zijzelven de uitverkorenen zouden verleiden –Mattheüs 24:24. Leert ijverig de Schriften te doorzoeken opdat u niet misleid wordt. Geloof geen roddel maar onderzoekt de zaak.

Maakt geen oproer wanneer u lasterlijk wordt behandeld maar draagt het ter wille van Christus. Hebt uw vijanden lief en bidt voor degenen die kwaad van u spreken en u benauwen. Lijdt verdrukking eerder dan anderen te verdrukken. Draagt schimp eerder dan anderen te schimpen. Weest lasterlijk genoemd eerder dan anderen te lasteren.

Ziet er voortdurend op toe dat u niet alleen uw eigen voordeel zoekt, maar zorgt altijd voor degenen met wie u omgaat, of zij nu jong of oud zijn.

Instructies aan mijn dochters Betgen en Tanneken, mijn geliefde lammeren, ik vermanen u in al deze dingen, dat u de geboden des Heeren gehoorzaamt. Gehoorzaamt ook uw ouderen en allen die u in deugd onderwijzen.

Weest ijverig om uw werk te doen, en u zult overal geliefd zijn waar u woont. Weest niet twistziek, praatziek, lichtzinnig, hoogmoedig of grof van taal. Weest vriendelijk, eerbaar en rustig, zoals het jonge meisjes betaamt.

Bidt den Heere om wijsheid en zij zal u gegeven worden. Leert ijverig lezen en schrijven en vermaakt u daarin, en u zult wijs worden. Zingt en hebt vreugde met psalmen, lofzangen en geestelijke liederen. Leert den Heere te behagen van uw jeugd af, zoals de heilige vrouwen en maagden van ouds. Esther was ook een maagd die God vreesde; zij was getooid met ootmoed, genadig, eerbaar, vriendelijk en nederig van hart; daardoor behaagde zij de koning Ahasverus boven alle andere maagden. –zie Esther 2:17. Maar zelfs in haar hoge staat was zij niet trots. Hoewel zij schitterde in koninklijke kledij, vernederde zij haar hart met vasten en gebed tot den Heere, voor haar broeders, opdat zij verlost zouden worden uit de handen hunner vijanden. Zij achtte zich niet beter dan een der geringsten van haar broeders.

Wanneer u de jaren der verstandhouding bereikt hebt, zorgt dat u uzelf tooit met de werken des Geestes zoals goedheid, zachtmoedigheid, zachtheid, ootmoed, gehoorzaamheid, lankmoedigheid, gerechtigheid, kuisheid, eerbaarheid, reinheid, vrede, standvastigheid, barmhartigheid, wijsheid, ijver in goede werken, geloof, hoop en liefde. Hebt God lief boven alles wat in de wereld is en doet uw naaste gelijk als gij wilt dat mensen u doen. –zie Galaten 5:22-23 en Titus 2:3-5. Gedenkt dat Jezus zei: …Gij zult den Heere uw God liefhebben met geheel uw hart, en met geheel uw ziel, en met geheel uw verstand. Dit is het grote en eerste gebod. Het tweede is daaraan gelijk: Gij zult uw naaste liefhebben als uzelf. Aan deze twee geboden hangen de ganse wet en de profeten –Mattheüs 22:37-40.

Laten wij ons verblijden en ons verheugen en Hem eer geven; want het huwelijk van het Lam is gekomen, en Zijn vrouw heeft zich bereid gemaakt. En haar is gegeven dat zij zich kleden zou in fijn linnen, rein en wit; want het fijn linnen is de gerechtigheid der heiligen –Openbaring 19:7-8. Mijn dochters, dit is de tooi der heiligen; arbeidt voor zo'n bruiloftskleed, opdat u moogt ingaan in het huwelijk van het Lam, waar zij …de rechtvaardigen, zullen stralen als de zon in het koninkrijk huns Vaders… –Mattheüs 13:43. Moge de Heere u leiden gelijk Hij Israël uit Egypte leidde, en u brengen tot het Nieuwe Jeruzalem, opdat wij elkander met blijdschap mogen zien op de dag der opstanding. Ik beveel u aan bij den Heere, den God van Abraham, den God van Isaak, en den God van Jakob; moge Hij u bewaren tot het einde uwer levens.

Tot slot, O mijn dierbare kinderen, ik heb dit in tranen geschreven, u uit liefde vermanend. Mijn gebed en zorg zijn voortdurend voor uw behoudenis. Ik hoop en bid voortdurend dat Hij, in Zijn barmhartigheid, u bewaren zal, zoals Hij Jozef, Mozes en Daniël bewaarde te midden van boze mensen. En Hij zal dit doen, indien u ijverig de waarheid volgt.

Dit is mijn laatste vaarwel, mijn lieve lammeren. Gedenkt altijd elkander in liefde; leert ijverig lezen en schrijven en gehoorzaamt allen in hetgeen goed is. Ik neem van u afscheid, mijn dierbare kinderen Betgen, David en Tanneken. Adieu aan al mijn dierbare broeders en zusters en vrienden overal.

Geschreven door mij, Soetgen van den Houte, uw moeder in ketenen; geschreven in haast (bevende van koude), uit liefde tot u allen, amen.
