I have enjoyed listening to, and even taking part in, discussions about the Covid shot—about why someone has, and why the other has not, received it. I venture to say we could have seven people give their viewpoint on the subject and maybe have eight different ideas.

I begin with the disclaimer that these are my thoughts, and I am quite okay with someone disagreeing. In fact, I would welcome others to share their viewpoints.

One of the things you will notice in this writing is that I don’t call the Covid shot a ‘vaccine’. Not that it doesn’t technically fit the official definition, but rather that it doesn’t function the way we have known vaccines to work. I remember when I was a lad about four years of age, I went with my mother to the health department and received a vaccination in my upper arm for smallpox. (The pock mark is still there) I remember some years later when the whole community gathered at our local public school for the sugar cube treatment which was an oral vaccination against polio. I don’t remember if I had any other vaccinations or not. My point is that these vaccinations were immunizations against a disease. We were assured that we would not get smallpox, polio, measles or whatever else we were vaccinated for. And we didn’t—not just a lesser amount or a case not as severe. We understood that we were immunized, and the fight was over.

During the current pandemic we kept hearing about the vaccination that was coming. It sounded like this was going to be the answer to this pestilence that had settled on the world. Some of us wondered if this would be like the flu shot that targets certain viruses, while it misses the other flu viruses. As the drama unfolded, we soon began to hear of variants and the need for booster shots. We now know for sure that this shot does not give an immunization for Covid 19, and hence, for clarity it is better to call it a flu shot.

I remember so well farming in the early 90’s and hearing about Roundup-Ready crops. It seemed too good to be true to be able to spray glyphosate (Roundup) over the top of the crop and take out all the weeds while doing no harm to the crop. The manufacturer did keep telling us to spray maximum rates so as to ‘kill’ every weed. Theoretically they were right, if we could have killed every weed, without missing one, we would not have had the next problem—spray-resistant weeds. We didn’t realize how fast our troublesome ‘pigweeds’ (and other weeds) in the south, would mutate and develop a resistance to glyphosate.

Sure, farmers had several good years with an easy way to keep out the weeds, but that didn’t last and now the situation is worse than it was before. Today, every farmer knows about ‘Palmer amaranth Pigweed’. You can almost ‘pour’ glyphosate on it, and still it thrives. These weeds mutated very rapidly and became resistant.

I think we have a similar scenario with the Covid shot. I’m certainly not a scientist but it does seem to me that since the shot admittedly mostly reduces symptoms instead of producing immunity, then it will most likely speed up the mutation of the Covid-19 virus. This seems like the normal ‘struggle for survival’ principle of life.

The rapid speed with which this shot came on the market is another concern. We really don’t know what all it will bring down the road nor the side effects it may cause. We don’t know how many boosters will be called for. It seems the world is the test field at the moment, and from what I’m seeing it is not working too well and many of the people who have had the shot don’t really trust it. The people who have had the virus have built an immunity that is far superior to the protection of the shot. We’ve known since childhood that when we had the flu, our body would build immunity to that strain. This is the way our Maker designed us. One of the first people I personally knew that had Covid was told they would have six months of immunity. I wondered how they figured that out so quickly. This was a new virus, and we had no experience to draw on for this virus. Also, the viruses we were familiar with gave lifetime immunity to that strain. So what science was behind this?

Hence, I think it much better to take precautions and do what we can to boost our immune system. It is an excellent time to remember we are to be stewards of the body that God gave us. It’s a good time to put a plan in place of good nutrition, exercise, and weight loss. If you are overweight, you are much more likely to be affected by this pestilence and many other illnesses. If you regularly consume sugary drinks or unhealthy foods of any kind, it is an excellent time to kick the habit and reduce your sugar consumption. If you are overweight or out of shape physically, there is no better time than now to bring your body into a condition that will be much healthier, so you will be better able to ward off this virus and many other illnesses.

My belief is that in the long run it will be safer and better to do my part and let this body build the immunities to protect itself against this virus. I realize there are those who have died after contracting this illness. I don’t belittle this fact and I am sorry for the loss of life. I do believe too that we as Christians should constantly commit our lives to God and look at the whole picture of life and its preservation through the lens of Christian ethics.

It is unprecedented that an illness with a recovery rate of somewhere around 99%, would cause such a stir, the world over. We know that if it wouldn’t be for the invention of social media there would not have been near the panic and turmoil. One of my greatest concerns is how we are being ‘conditioned’ for more to come. Who would have ever thought that a flu virus would be the instrument that ushers in a global push for something that will be the benchmark for whether we can travel, go to eating places, gather for public events and other such restrictions. It sounds strangely similar to what God says will one day be a reality—And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads: And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name –Revelation 13:16-17.

I have been almost ridiculed for even mentioning the mark of the beast. Still others think this passage is to be spiritualized and has nothing to do with the end time system of government. Still others think the bride will be raptured before this, hence nothing for us to be concerned with. I could wish one of these views would be right, then I could move along in silence hoping that all would be well.

I will hasten to say that I don’t think this is the ‘mark of the beast’, but rather I see it as another step closer to that event. I also hasten to say that this is not a writing to ridicule another belief nor is it an effort to try to pull together certain Scriptures to try to support a particular doctrinal agenda such as the idea that all believers will be raptured prior to the unfolding of end time events, thereby escaping what the Bible refers to as “great tribulation”. –See Matthew 24:21 and Revelation 7:14. It’s time we open our eyes to the ‘conditioning’ that our society is having upon us in general, and the conditioning of this shot in particular. There are all kinds of good reasons we will go ahead with it—it makes good sense, it defies science not to, I’ve even heard we can be better witnesses if we have had it, and the list goes on. All the while we are being ‘conditioned’ to do what it takes to keep rolling down our economic road.

So, my plea is that we consider where we are headed. One day God’s people will need to jump off the train of this world—Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you –2 Corinthians 6:17. Revelation 14:10-11 declares that all who take the mark will seal their destiny in hell. The next verse gives a calling for the endurance of the saints—Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus –Revelation 14:12.

There will be hard times—Read Matthew 24:4-28. Consider the famines, pestilences, and earthquakes that are promised will come. Jesus said all these are the beginnings of sorrows—literally birth pangs. He said along with this, ‘the end is not yet’. Yet we have the promise of triumph—And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death –Revelation 12:11. I say again, “One day the saints will need to jump off the economic train.”

I think now is an excellent time to evaluate our attachment, whether it is connected to this world or to our future heavenly reward. Let’s make a commitment anew to identify with our soon coming Lord and King. Also, it’s an excellent time to share the gospel of Jesus’ Kingdom with a society that is bent on going away from the Creator.

So, for now, I’m content to feel safe with the immunity in my body as God created it and I am purposing in a new way to seek the immunity from the ways of sin and evil and to be inoculated with the Holy Ghost from heaven. Will you join me in this commitment?

我很喜欢听别人就新冠疫苗展开的讨论，甚至参与其中——为何有人接种，而有人没有接种。我敢说，如果让七个人谈论这个话题，可能会出现八种不同的观点。

我先声明：以下是我的想法，如果有人不同意我完全接受。事实上，我欢迎别人分享他们的观点。

你在此文中会注意到的一点是，我不把新冠疫苗称为“疫苗”（vaccine）。并不是说它在技术上不符合官方定义，而是它并不像我们所熟知的疫苗那样起作用。我记得四岁左右时随母亲到卫生所，在上臂接受过一次天花疫苗（疤痕至今还在）。几年后，全社区会聚在当地公立学校接受那种在糖块上滴口服的脊髓灰质炎疫苗。我记不清是否还接种过别的疫苗。我的观点是：那些疫苗是对疾病的免疫接种。我们被保证不会再得天花、脊髓灰质炎、麻疹或其他接种对象的病。而且我们确实没有再得——不是症状更轻或病情不那么严重。我们明白自己是被免疫了，战斗就结束了。

在这次大流行期间，我们不断听到将有一种疫苗面世。听起来好像这将是解决降临在世界上的灾疫的答案。我们中有些人想，它是否会像流感疫苗那样，只针对某些病毒株，而对其他流感病毒无效。随着事情的发展，我们很快就听到出现变种并需要加强针的说法。现在我们已确定，这种疫苗并不能给人提供对新冠的免疫，因此，为了清楚起见，把它称为流感疫苗更为恰当。

我还清晰地记得九十年代初耕作时听说“耐草甘膦”作物的事。能在作物上喷洒草甘膦（Roundup）而杀死所有杂草而不伤害作物，听起来好得难以置信。生产商不断告诉我们要按最高剂量喷洒，以便“消灭”每一株杂草。理论上他们是对的：如果能消灭每一株杂草、一个也不漏，我们就不会遇到下一个问题——对农药产生抵抗力的杂草。我们没有意识到南方那种令人头疼的“苋菜属杂草”（以及其他杂草）会如此迅速地突变并对草甘膦产生抗性。

当然，农民曾有几年因为能轻松除草而受益，但那并未持久，现在的情况比以前更糟。如今，每个农民都知道“Palmer苋（Palmer amaranth）”这个名字。你几乎可以把草甘膦“倒”在它身上，它仍然能生长。这些杂草迅速突变并变得有抗性。

我认为新冠疫苗的情况类似。我当然不是科学家，但在我看来，既然这种疫苗主要是减轻症状而不是产生免疫，那么它很可能会加速新冠病毒的突变。这似乎符合生命的“生存竞争”原则。

这种疫苗能如此迅速上市，这也是令人担忧之处。我们实在不了解它将来会带来什么或者可能产生哪些副作用。我们不知道需要多少次加强针。目前看来，全球正被当作试验田，而就我所见，效果并不太好，许多接种过的人并不真正信任它。那些曾感染过病毒的人建立的免疫力，远远优于疫苗的保护。我们从小就知道，当我们得过某种流感时，身体会对那一株建立免疫。这是我们的造物主设计我们的方式。我亲眼所知的第一个得了新冠的人被告知他们将获得六个月的免疫期。我不禁想他们如何能这么快算出这个结论。这是新的病毒，我们对它没有可借鉴的经验。而且，我们熟悉的那些病毒通常对该株会产生终生免疫。那么这背后是什么样的科学依据？

因此，我认为更好的做法是采取预防措施并尽力增强我们的免疫系统。现在正是记住我们应当管理好神赐给我们的身体的大好时机。制定良好的饮食、锻炼和减重计划正当其时。如果你超重，就更可能受此疫病和许多其他疾病影响。如果你经常喝含糖饮料或摄入任何不健康食物，现在正是戒掉这些习惯、减少糖分摄入的好时机。如果你体重过重或体能状态不佳，没有比现在更好的时机把身体调到更健康的状态，这样你将更能抵御这种病毒和许多其他疾病。

我的信念是，从长远来看，让身体按照神所造的方式建立自身免疫会更安全更好。我明白有人因感染而殒命。我不轻视这一事实，为失去的生命感到遗憾。我也相信，作为基督徒，我们应当不断将生命交托给神，并以基督教伦理的视角审视生命整体与其保存问题。

一个病症的康复率约在99%左右，却在全世界引起如此大的骚动，这是前所未见的。我们知道如果没有社交媒体的发明，恐慌和动荡绝不会如此大。我最担心的是我们正被“条件反射式地训练”为未来更多事物做准备。谁会想到，一种流感病毒会成为推动全球性措施的工具，用来作为我们能否旅行、进入餐馆、参聚公共活动等的衡量标准。这听起来令人毛骨悚然地类似于神所说终有一天会实现的情形——他又叫一切、或小或大、或富或贫、或自主或为奴的，都在他们右手上或在他们额上受一个印记，叫他们不至于买卖，除非是那有印记、或有兽名、或有名号数目的人——启示录 13:16-17。

我差点因此被嘲笑，说我居然提到兽的印记。还有人认为这段经文应当属灵化，与末世的政府系统无关。有人认为新妇（教会）将在此事之前被提，所以我们无需担忧。我真希望其中一种看法是对的，那样我就可以默默继续生活，希望一切平安无事。

我急忙声明，我并不认为这就是“兽的印记”，而是把它视为朝那事件又近了一步。我也急忙说明，这篇文章并非为嘲弄不同信仰而写，也不是试图拼凑若干经文去支持某一教义议程，例如所有信徒会在末世事件展开前被提，从而免于圣经所称的“大灾难”。——参见马太福音 24:21 与 启示录 7:14。是时候让我们的眼睛对社会中普遍存在的“条件作用”保持警醒，特别是对这次疫苗所带来的条件作用。有各种看似合理的理由让人接种——这很有道理，不接种似乎违背科学，我甚至听过有人说接种后我们可以成为更好的见证人，诸如此类。不知不觉间，我们被“条件化”，为维持经济运行而被动顺从。

因此，我的恳求是让我们思考自己的去向。总有一天，属神的人需要跳下这世界的列车——所以主说：“你们要从他们中间出来，与他们分别，不要沾不洁净的物，我就收纳你们。”——哥林多后书 6:17。启示录 14:10-11 宣告，凡受印记的人将确定他们在地狱中的结局。下一节向圣徒发出忍耐的呼召——在此有圣徒的忍耐，他们是那些遵守神诫命和持守耶稣信心的人——启示录 14:12。

必有艰难时期——参阅马太福音 24:4-28。想想那些将要来的饥荒、瘟疫和地震。耶稣说这一切都是哀痛的开始——字面上是产难。他又说，“末期还没有到”。然而我们有胜利的应许——他们凭羔羊的血、并借着自己所作见证的话胜过他，并且不爱惜自己的性命，至于死——启示录 12:11。我再说一遍，“总有一天圣徒需要跳下经济列车。”

我认为现在正是评估我们依附何处的好时机——是连结于这世界，还是连结于我们未来的天上赏赐。让我们重新立志与那位即将来临的主与王相认同。同时，也是向一个正倾向背离造物主的社会传福音、宣讲耶稣国度的好时机。

所以，暂时而言，我满足于信靠神所造之身所具有的免疫力，并且我以新的方式立志寻求脱离罪恶之途的免疫，被从天上来的圣灵所接种。你愿与我一同立下这个决心吗？

On November 27, 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte of Ghent, Holland was martyred for her faith in the Lord, Jesus Christ. Prior to her passing, her husband had also been martyred for his faith. During the time of her imprisonment, she wrote several lengthy letters to her three youth-aged children. The following are abridged excerpts of these letters which can be found in full text on pages 646-651 in the Martyr’s Mirror.

Grace, peace, and mercy from God, the Father, and the Lord, Jesus Christ, to my dear children, David, Betgen, and Tanneken. This affectionate greeting, written by your mother in bonds, is a memorial of the truth to you. I hope to testify to this Truth by my words, my life, and my death, with the help of the Most High. May the wisdom of the Holy Ghost instruct and strengthen you, that you may be brought up in the ways of the Lord. Since it pleases the Lord to take me out of this world, I will leave you this memorial of my faith in the only true God, not of silver or gold for such jewels are perishable.

Receive admonition. First, I admonish you, my most beloved children, always allow yourselves to be instructed by those who fear the Lord. As long as you obey good admonition and instruction, God will be your Father and not leave you as orphans. For David says: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose –Psalm 25:12. Children, grieve not when you are corrected and do not speak in anger to those who correct you. A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke –Proverbs 13:1.

Guard your tongue. My dear children, guard your tongue, that it speak no evil. Do not practice deceit or backbiting with your lips. Paul teaches us to live peaceably with all men if it be possible. –see 1 Peter 3:10 and Romans 12:18. If you are crossly spoken to, learn to answer kindly, and you will be loved by all men. Humility and meekness are acceptable to both God and man.

Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight –Proverbs 12:22. I admonish you to beware of lying, since liars have no part in the kingdom of God. –see Revelation 21:8.

Be diligent in work and give alms. Always be diligent to do your work, wherever you be; for Paul says …that if any would not work, neither should he eat –2 Thessalonians 3:10. It is also written, be diligent to labor, that you …may have to give to him that needeth –Ephesians 4:28.

Do not turn your face away from the poor. Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard –Proverbs 21:13. Therefore, be diligent in prayer, and love the poor; for Christ also was poor for our sakes—For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich –2 Corinthians 8:9. Be therefore also merciful, even as your heavenly Father is merciful; for such shall be blessed, and shall obtain mercy. –see Matthew 5:7.

Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith –Proverbs 15:16. And, Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife –Proverbs 17:1. Choose to earn your bread by the labor of your hands, and to eat your bread with peace. Seek not to be a merchant, nor be anxious for great gain.

Be meek, merciful, and pure in heart. Learn to be meek and lowly in heart for such are blessed and shall inherit the earth. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Luke 6:36. And, Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth –Matthew 5:5. Finally, Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God –Matthew 5:8. Hence, my dear children, let no impure thoughts remain in your hearts. Engage yourselves with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs and evil thoughts will have no room. –see Ephesians 5:19.

Neither let filthiness proceed out of your mouth. You will have to give an account of all filthiness. –see Matthew 12:36-37. Always esteem yourselves as the least and be not wise in your own conceit. Allow yourselves to be instructed by your elders and always be silent when others speak. Humble yourselves, for …whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted –Matthew 23:12. For Christ who is the greatest made Himself the least for an example unto us. –see John 13:13-15.

Avoid a luxurious life. My children, do not desire the luxuries of fine food or wine. He that desires costly feasts will not become rich. Be content with the labor of your hands. Do not be a burden to anyone as long as you can obtain the things needful—…It is more blessed to give than to receive –Acts 20:35. Paul says: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Be sober and thankful as you have heard me read of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They were selected by the king of Babylon to be nourished with the same wine and meat which the king drank and ate at his table. But they chose to have pulse [vegetables] and water. They wanted to observe the law and commandments of their fathers with sobriety and thankfulness in the fear of God. In the end, they were fairer and fatter than those who ate of the king’s dainties, see Daniel chapter 1. Thus, faithfully they walked in the ways of the Lord. They made themselves acceptable to God in prayer and supplication, therefore, he did great things through them. He delivered them from the den of lions and out of the fiery furnace.

When Joseph was sold into Egypt, he desired no worldly dainties. When the Egyptian woman sought to seduce him, he feared God, and God preserved him. He pleased God in sobriety and prayer and God appointed him ruler over Egypt. –see Genesis chapters 37, 39, and 41. Take an example from this in your youth and you will please God. He will keep you from all seduction.

Oh, my lambs, you are still in your youth, yet you have a part in your Father’s kingdom. See that you keep it well and not as Esau who gave his inheritance or birthright for a mess of pottage, disregarding his father’s blessing. –see Genesis 25:30-34. But Jacob chose the better part, walking in the ways of the Lord with all righteousness.

Shun worldly living. Do not delight in the evils of the world such as lying, cheating, gambling, banqueting, playing, swearing, cursing, backbiting, hatred, and dancing, nor envy, drunkenness, excess, idolatry, covetousness, lasciviousness, vanity, filthy conversation. Though the world does not consider these things to be sin but rather calls them amusements, nevertheless, they are abominations in the eyes of the Lord. –see 1 Peter 4:3-4. If you take pleasure in these things, you sell your birthright (or the spiritual inheritance) from your Father, for a mess of pottage—namely, for a few temporal pleasures, which lead you to damnation.

Choose to suffer affliction with the children of God. From the time of Abel until now many have been afflicted and have suffered. They were rejected, despised, persecuted, and killed because they would not follow the wicked world and her false prophets.

My children, choose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God [that you may be rewarded with them], than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25. Unto such belong all the beautiful promises of God. It is written: …ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy –John 16:20. And, Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life –Revelation 2:10. Finally, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world –John 16:33.

Instructions to my son, David. David, my dear son, I commend you to the Lord. You are the oldest; learn wisdom, so that you may be a good example to your sisters. Beware of bad company and of playing in the street with bad boys. Diligently learn to read and write so that you may get understanding.

Love one another without contention or quarreling. Be kind to your sisters. Bear them up as the stronger and out of love help all you can. Assist them out of brotherly love.

Learn to obey your elders in that which is good. Be industrious so that people may love you. Exhort one another to good works, modesty, honorableness, and quietness. Always care for one another for the time has come that …iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold –Matthew 24:12.

Beware of deception. Remember, Jesus said …that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect –Matthew 24:24. Learn to diligently search the Scriptures so that you may not be deceived. Do not believe gossip but examine the matter.

Make no commotion when you are slandered but bear it for Christ’s sake. Love your enemies and pray for those who speak evil of you and afflict you. Suffer affliction rather than afflicting others. Suffer reproach rather than reproaching others. Be slandered rather than slandering others.

You must constantly see that you do not seek solely your own profit, but always care for those with whom you have dealings, whether they be young or old.

Instructions to my daughters Betgen and Tanneken, my beloved lambs, I admonish you in all these same things, that you obey the commandments of the Lord. Also, obey your elders and all who instruct you in virtue.

Be diligent to do your work, and you will be loved wherever you live. Don’t be quarrelsome, talkative, light-minded, proud, or surly of speech. Be kind, honorable, and quiet, as behooves young girls.

Pray the Lord for wisdom, and it shall be given you. Diligently learn to read and write, and take delight therein, and you will become wise. Take pleasure and sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Learn to please the Lord from your youth, as did the holy women and virgins of old. Esther also was a virgin who feared God; she was adorned with humility, was gracious, honorable, kind, and humble of heart; hence she pleased King Ahasuerus above all the other virgins. –see Esther 2:17. But even in her high estate she was not proud. Though she shone in royal apparel, she humbled her heart with fasting and prayer to the Lord, for her brethren, that they might be delivered out of the hands of their enemies. She did not esteem herself better than one of the least of her brethren.

When you have attained the years of understanding, see that you adorn yourselves with the works of the Spirit such as goodness, gentleness, meekness, humility, obedience, long suffering, righteousness, modesty, honorableness, purity, peaceableness, steadfastness, mercifulness, wisdom, diligence in good works, faith, hope and love. Love God above all that is in the world and do to your neighbor as you would have men do unto you. –see Galatians 5:22-23 and Titus 2:3-5. Remember that Jesus said: …Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets –Matthew 22:37-40.

Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints –Revelation 19:7-8. My daughters, this is the adornment of the saints; labor for such a wedding garment, so that you may enter into the marriage of the Lamb, where they …the righteous, [shall] shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father… –Matthew 13:43. May the Lord lead you as He led Israel out of Egypt, and bring you to the New Jerusalem, that we may see each other with joy in the day of the resurrection. I commend you to the Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; may He keep you to the end of your lives.

In conclusion, O my dear children, I have written this in tears, admonishing you out of love. My prayer and solicitude are constantly for your salvation. I hope and pray constantly that He, in His mercy, will preserve you, just as He preserved Joseph, Moses, and Daniel in the midst of wicked men. And He will do this if you give diligence to follow the truth.

This is my last farewell, my dear lambs. always remember each other in love; diligently learn to read and write and obey everyone in that which is good. I bid you adieu, my dear children Betgen, David and Tanneken. Adieu all my dear brethren and sisters, and friends everywhere.

Written by me, Soetgen van den Houte, your mother in bonds; written in haste (while trembling with cold), out of love for you all, amen.

في 27 نوفمبر 1560، تمّ استشهاد سوتِغن فان دن هاوت من غينت بهولندا بسبب إيمانها بالرب يسوع المسيح. قبل وفاتها، كان زوجها قد استُشهد أيضًا بسبب إيمانه. خلال فترة سجنها، كتبت عدة رسائل مطوّلة إلى أطفالها الثلاثة وهم في سن المراهقة. فيما يلي مقتطفات مختصرة من هذه الرسائل التي يمكن العثور على نصها الكامل في الصفحات 646-651 في مرآة الشهداء.

النِّعمة والسلام والرحمة من الله الآب والرب يسوع المسيح لإخوتي الصغار الأعزاء، داود وبيتجن وتانكن. هذه التحية المفعمة بالمودة، مكتوبة بيد أمكم مكبلة، تردُّ ذكرى للحق لكم. أرجو أن أشهد لهذا الحق بكلماتي وحياتي وموتي، بمساعدة العلي. فلتعلّمكم حكمة الروح القدس وتُقوِّيكم، لكي تُربَوا في طرق الرب. وبما أنّه يرضي الرب أن يُخرِجني من هذا العالم، أترك لكم هذه الذكرى لإيماني بالله الحق الوحيد، لا من فضة ولا من ذهب فمثل هذه الجواهر زائلة.

تلقّوا التأديب. أولاً، أُؤدِّبكم، يا أحبائي الأولاد، دَعوْا أنفسكم دومًا أن تُؤمَرُوا بمن يخافون الرب. ما دمتم تطيعون التأديب الحسن والتعليم، فالله يكون أبا لكم ولا يترككم يتامى. كما يقول داود: من الرجل الذي يخاف الرب؟ يعلمه في الطريق الذي يختاره –مزمور 25:12. يا أولادي، لا تحزنوا عندما تُؤدَّبون ولا تردّوا بغضب على مَن يؤدِّبكم. الابن الحكيم يسمع تأديب أبيه: وأما المُتهكم فلا يسمع الوبّال – أمثال 13:1.

احرسوا ألسنتكم. يا أحبابي، احرسوا ألسنتكم كي لا تنطق بالشرّ. لا تمارسوا الخداع أو الغيبة بشفتيكم. يعلمانَا بولس أن نحيَا بسلام مع جميع الناس إذا أمكن. –انظر 1 بطرس 3:10 ورومية 12:18. وإن وُجِهتم بكلمات قاسية، تَعَلَّموا أن تردّوا بلطف، فستحبّكم جميع الناس. التواضع والوداعة مقبولة لدى الله والناس.

شفاه الكذب رجس للرب: وأما الذين يعملون بالصدق فمسرّته – أمثال 12:22. أُنذركم بأن تحذروا من الكذب، لأن الكذّابين ليس لهم نصيب في ملكوت الله. –انظر رؤيا 21:8.

اجتهدوا في العمل وأعطوا صدقات. كونوا دائمًا مجتهدين في عملكم أينما كنتم؛ لأن بولس يقول: فإن لم يعمل أحد فلا يأكل أيضاً –2 تسالونيكي 3:10. ومكتوب أيضًا: اجتهدوا لتعملوا لكي …تكون لكم لتعطوا للمحتاج –أفسس 4:28.

لا تُديروا وجوهكم عن الفقراء. من يغمض أذنيه عن صيحة الفقير، أيضاً هو يصرخ ولكنه لا يُسمع – أمثال 21:13. لذا، كونوا مجتهدين في الصلاة، وأحبّوا الفقراء؛ لأن المسيح أيضًا كان فقيرًا من أجلنا—لأنكم تعلمون نعمة ربنا يسوع المسيح، أنه إذ كان غنيًا، لأجلكم صار فقيرًا، لكي تغتنيكم بفقره –2 كورنثوس 8:9. كونوا إذًا رحماء كما أن أباكم السماوي رحيم؛ لأن هؤلاء يكونون مبارَكين وينالون الرأفة. –انظر متى 5:7.

خير قليل مع خوف الرب من كنز عظيم مع همّ معه – أمثال 15:16. و: خير لقمة يابسة وسكوت معها، من بيت مليء ذبائح مع شجار – أمثال 17:1. اختاروا أن تكسبوا خبزكم بعمل أيديكم، وأن تأكلوا خبزكم بسلام. لا تسعوا لأن تكونوا تجارًا، ولا تقلقوا بشأن الربح الكبير.

كونوا وُدُعاء، رحيمين، ونقيي القلب. تعلموا أن تكونوا وُدُعاء ومنخفضي القلب لأن هؤلاء مباركون ويرثون الأرض. كونوا رحماء كما أن أباكم أيضاً رحيم. لوقا 6:36. و: طوبى للودعاء: لأنهم يرثون الأرض –متى 5:5. وأخيرًا، طوبى لمن طاهر القلب: لأنهم يُبصرون الله –متى 5:8. لذلك، يا أولادي الأعزاء، لا تدَعوا أبدًا أفكارًا نجسة تبقى في قلوبكم. شغلوا أنفسكم بالمزامير والترانيم والأناشيد الروحية فتُمحَى الأفكار الشريرة ولا تجد موطنًا. –انظر أفسس 5:19.

ولا تدعوا الأوساخ تخرج من أفواهكم. سيتعيّن عليكم أن تُجيبوا عن كل كلام فاحش. –انظر متى 12:36-37. قدّروا أنفسكم دائمًا كأدنى الناس ولا تكونوا حكماء في ظنونكم. تقبلوا تعليم الشيوخ واصمتوا حين يتكلّم الآخرون. تواضعوا، لأن …من رفع نفسه يُضعَف، ومن وضع نفسه يُرفع –متى 23:12. لأن المسيح الذي هو الأعظم جعل نفسه الأضعف لمثل لنا. –انظر يوحنا 13:13-15.

تجنّبوا حياة الرفاهية. يا أبنائي، لا تشتهوا ملذات الطعام الفاخر أو الخمر. من يشتهي الولائم الباهظة لن يَغتَنِ. ارضوا بعمل أيديكم. لا تكونوا عبئًا على أحد طالما تستطيعون الحصول على الضروري—…أكثر بركة أن تعطى منه أن تأخذ –أعمال 20:35. يقول بولس: ولكن إن كان لنا طعام وكساء فبذلك نكتفي –1 تيموثاوس 6:8.

كونوا رصينين وشاكرين كما سمعتم أني أقرأ عن دانيال وشتراك وميشأخ وعدنغو. اختاروا من قِبَل ملك بابل أن يُربَّوا بنفس النبيذ والطعام الذي كان الملك يشرب ويأكل على مائدته. لكنهم اختاروا أكل البقوليّات [الخضروات] والماء. أرادوا أن يحفظوا شريعة ووصايا آبائهم بالرُصانة والشكر وخوف الله. وفي النهاية، كانوا أبهى وأشهر من الذين أكلوا من أطعمة الملك الشهية، انظر سفر دانيال الإصحاح الأول. هكذا ساروا بأمانة في طرق الرب. أَحَبّهم الله في الصلاة والتضرع، فعمل من خلالهم أعمال عظيمة. أَنْقَذهم من جُبّ الأسود ومن أتون النار.

عندما بيع يوسف إلى مصر، لم يطلب ملذات دنيوية. عندما حاولت المرأة المصرية إغراءه، خاف الله فحفظه الله. أَرضى الله بالرُّصانة والصلاة فجعلَه والياً على مصر. –انظر تكوين الإصحاحات 37 و39 و41. خذوا مثالًا من ذلك في شبابكم فسترضون الله. سيحفظكم من كل إغراء.

آه يا حملاتي، أنتم ما زلتم في شبابكم، ومع ذلك لكم نصيب في ملكوت أبيكم. احرصوا على حفظه جيدًا ولا تكونوا كعيسو الذي باع ميراثه أو حق البكورية من أجل قدرٍ من العدس، متهاونًا بمباركة أبيه. –انظر تكوين 25:30-34. لكن يعقوب اختار النصيب الأفضل، سائرًا في طرق الرب بكل بر.

اجتنِبوا معيشة العالم. لا تفرحوا بشرور هذا العالم مثل الكذب والغش والمقامرة والولائم واللعب واليمين واللعن والغيبة والبغضاء والرقص، ولا الحسد والسُكر والتطرّف والعبادة الأوثانية وطمع النفس والشهوة والغرور وحديث النجاسة. ومع أن العالم لا يعتبر هذه الأمور خطيئة بل يسميها تسلية، إلا أنها رجاسات في أعين الرب. –انظر 1 بطرس 4:3-4. إن استمتعتم بهذه الأمور، فإنكم تبيعون حق البكورية (أو الميراث الروحي) من أبيكم مقابل قدرٍ من العدس—أي لبعض الملذات الزمنية التي تقودكم إلى الهلاك.

اختروا أن تتألّموا مع أولاد الله. منذ زمان هابيل وحتى الآن ابتلي كثيرون وتحمّلوا المعاناة. رُفضوا واحتقِروا واضطُهدوا وقُتلوا لأنهم لم يتبعوا العالم الشرير وأنبياءه الكذبة.

يا أولادي، اختاروا …بل أن تتألّموا مع شعب الله [لكي تُكافؤوا معهم] عن أن تتمتعوا بمسرّات الخطيئة لوقت –عبرانيين 11:25. لأولئك تنتمي كل وعود الله الجميلة. مكتوب: …أنتم ستبكون وتتأسَّفون، أما العالم فسيبتهج: وأنتم تحزنون، ولكن حزنك يتحوّل إلى فرح –يوحنا 16:20. و: لا تخف من الأشياء التي ستتألم بها: هوذا إبليس قد يُلقي منكم بعضًا في السجن لتمتحنوا، وسينالكم ضيق عشرة أيام: كُن أمينًا حتى الموت فأُعطيك إكليل الحياة –رؤيا 2:10. وأخيرًا، هذه الأشياء قلتها لكم لكي ينال فيَّ لكم سلام. في العالم يكون لكم ضيق، لكن تشجعوا، أنا قد غلبت العالم –يوحنا 16:33.

تعليمات لابني داود. داود، يا ابني العزيز، أوصي بك إلى الرب. أنت الأكبر؛ تعلّم الحكمة لكي تكون قدوة حسنة لأخواتك. احذر الصحبة السيئة واللعب في الطريق مع أولاد سيئين. تعلم القراءة والكتابة بجدّ لكي تَنال فهماً.

أحبّوا بعضكم بعضًا بلا تداعٍ أو شجار. كن لطيفًا مع أختيك. قوّهما كالقوي ومن محبّة أعنهم قدر الإمكان. ساعدهم بمحبة أخوية.

تعلّم أن تطيع شيوخك في ما هو حسن. كن مجتهدًا حتى يحبك الناس. عَظّوا بعضكم للّأعمال الصالحة والوقار والشرف والسكينة. اعتنوا دوماً ببعضكم لأن الزمن قد أتى حيث …تظهر الإثم وتبرد محبة كثيرين –متى 24:12.

احذروا الخداع. تذكّر، قال يسوع: …أنه لو كان ممكناً يخدعون المختارين أيضاً –متى 24:24. تعلموا أن تبحثوا الكتاب متحدّين حتى لا تُخدَعوا. لا تُصَدِّقوا النميمة بل افحصوا الأمر.

لا تُحدثوا ضجّة عندما تُغتابون بل اصبروا لذلك من أجل المسيح. أحبّوا أعداءكم وصلّوا لمن يحدث عنكم الشرّ ويضايقكم. اكفُّوا عن إيقاع الأذى واصبروا عليه بدل أن تِؤذوا الآخرين. اصبروا على العار بدل أن تعيروا الآخرين. دعوا أن تُغتابوا بدل أن تغتابوا الآخرين.

عليكم أن تُبصروا دائمًا ألا تطلبوا منفعة أنفسكم فقط، بل اعتنوا دومًا بمن تتعاملون معهم سواء كانوا صغارًا أم كبارًا.

تعليمات لبناتي بيتجن وتانكن، يا حملاتي المحبوبات، أُنذركن في كل هذه الأمور أيضاً أن تطيعن وصايا الرب. وأيضًا أطعن شيوخكن وكل من يعلّمكن فضيلة.

كونوا مجتهدات في عملكن، فستُحبْن أينما عشتنّ. لا تكونن مشاكسات، ثرثارات، فارغات الذهن، متكبّرات، أو قاسيات اللسان. كونن لطيفات، محترمات، وهادئات، كما يليق بالشابات.

صلين للرب طالبات الحكمة فتُعطى لكن. تعلمن القراءة والكتابة بجدّ واستمتعن بهما فتَصْبحنَ حكيمات. استمتعن وترنمن بالمزامير والترانيم والأناشيد الروحية. تعلمن أن تُسَرّ الرب منذ شبابكن، كما فعلت النساء القدّيسات والعذارى القدّيسات في القديم. استير أيضًا كانت عذراء تخاف الله؛ تزيّنت بالتواضع وكانت رقيقة وموقّرة ولطيفة ومتواضعة القلب؛ لذا أسرت قلب الملك أحشويروش فوق جميع العذارى الأخريات. –انظر أستير 2:17. ولكن حتى في منزلة رفيعتها لم تكن متكبّرة. ومع أنها تبرّجت باللباس الملكي، إلا أنها وضعت قلبها بالتّواضع بالصوم والصلاة إلى الرب من أجل إخوانها لكي ينجووا من أيدي أعدائهم. لم تظن نفسها أفضل من أحد أدناهم.

عندما تبلغن سن التمييز، تأكدن أن تزَيِّنَّ أنفسكن بأعمال الروح مثل الخير والرفق والوداعة والتواضع والطاعة وطول الأناة والبر والحشمة والشرف والنقاء والسلم والثبات والرحمة والحكمة والاجتهاد في الأعمال الحسنة والإيمان والرجاء والمحبة. أحبّوا الله فوق كل ما في الدنيا واعملوا لجارك كما تحبون أن يعمل الناس لكم. –انظر غلاطية 5:22-23 وتيتوس 2:3-5. تذكّروا أن يسوع قال: …فأحببت الرب إلهك من كل قلبك ومن كل نفسك ومن كل فكرك. هذه هي الوصية الأولى والعظمى. والثانية مثلها: أن تحب قريبك كنفسك. عليه تتعلق الناموس والأنبياء –متى 22:37-40.

لِنَفْرَحْ ونتهلّل ونمجّدَه، لأن عرس الحمل قد أتى، وقد أعدّت نفسه أن تكون له زوجة. وأُعطي لها أن تُلبس كتانًا نقيًا أبيضًا، لأن الكتان النقي هو بر القديسين –رؤيا 19:7-8. يا بناتي، هذا تزيّن القديسين؛ اجتهدن لصنع ثوب الزفاف هذا لكي تدخلن في عرس الحمل، حيث …الأبرار يضيئون كالشمس في ملكوت أبيهم… –متى 13:43. ليقُدِّكن الرب كما قد قاد إسرائيل خارج مصر، ويظاهر بكن إلى أورشليم الجديدة، لكي نرى بعضنا بفرح في يوم القيامة. أوصيكن إلى الرب إله إبراهيم وإله إسحاق وإله يعقوب؛ فليحفظكن حتى نهاية حياتكن.

في الختام، يا أولادي الأعزاء، كتبت هذا والدمع في عينيّ، أُؤدِّبكم بدافع المحبّة. صلاتي وقلقي ثابتا من أجل خلاصكم. أرجو وأصلي دومًا أن يحفظكم برحمته كما حفظ يوسف وموسى ودانيال في وسط شرّ الرجال. وسيفعل هذا إذا أديتم الاجتهاد لاتباع الحق.

هذا وداعي الأخير، يا حملاتي الأعزاء. تذكّروا بعضكم بعضًا دومًا بالمحبّة؛ تعلموا القراءة والكتابة بجدّ، وأطيعوا الجميع فيما هو حسن. أودّعكم يا أحبائي بيتجن وداود وتانكن. وداعًا لكل إخوتي وأخواتي وأصدقائي في كل مكان.

مكتوب بيدي، سوتجن فان دن هاوت، أمكم المكبلة؛ كُتِب على عجل (وأنا أرتعش من البرد)، بدافع المحبة لكم جميعًا، آمين.

On November 27, 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte of Ghent, Holland was martyred for her faith in the Lord, Jesus Christ. Prior to her passing, her husband had also been martyred for his faith. During the time of her imprisonment, she wrote several lengthy letters to her three youth-aged children. The following are abridged excerpts of these letters which can be found in full text on pages 646-651 in the Martyr’s Mirror.

Grace, peace, and mercy from God, the Father, and the Lord, Jesus Christ, to my dear children, David, Betgen, and Tanneken. This affectionate greeting, written by your mother in bonds, is a memorial of the truth to you. I hope to testify to this Truth by my words, my life, and my death, with the help of the Most High. May the wisdom of the Holy Ghost instruct and strengthen you, that you may be brought up in the ways of the Lord. Since it pleases the Lord to take me out of this world, I will leave you this memorial of my faith in the only true God, not of silver or gold for such jewels are perishable.

Receive admonition. First, I admonish you, my most beloved children, always allow yourselves to be instructed by those who fear the Lord. As long as you obey good admonition and instruction, God will be your Father and not leave you as orphans. For David says: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose –Psalm 25:12. Children, grieve not when you are corrected and do not speak in anger to those who correct you. A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke –Proverbs 13:1.

Guard your tongue. My dear children, guard your tongue, that it speak no evil. Do not practice deceit or backbiting with your lips. Paul teaches us to live peaceably with all men if it be possible. –see 1 Peter 3:10 and Romans 12:18. If you are crossly spoken to, learn to answer kindly, and you will be loved by all men. Humility and meekness are acceptable to both God and man.

Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight –Proverbs 12:22. I admonish you to beware of lying, since liars have no part in the kingdom of God. –see Revelation 21:8.

Be diligent in work and give alms. Always be diligent to do your work, wherever you be; for Paul says …that if any would not work, neither should he eat –2 Thessalonians 3:10. It is also written, be diligent to labor, that you …may have to give to him that needeth –Ephesians 4:28.

Do not turn your face away from the poor. Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard –Proverbs 21:13. Therefore, be diligent in prayer, and love the poor; for Christ also was poor for our sakes—For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich –2 Corinthians 8:9. Be therefore also merciful, even as your heavenly Father is merciful; for such shall be blessed, and shall obtain mercy. –see Matthew 5:7.

Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith –Proverbs 15:16. And, Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife –Proverbs 17:1. Choose to earn your bread by the labor of your hands, and to eat your bread with peace. Seek not to be a merchant, nor be anxious for great gain.

Be meek, merciful, and pure in heart. Learn to be meek and lowly in heart for such are blessed and shall inherit the earth. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Luke 6:36. And, Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth –Matthew 5:5. Finally, Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God –Matthew 5:8. Hence, my dear children, let no impure thoughts remain in your hearts. Engage yourselves with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs and evil thoughts will have no room. –see Ephesians 5:19.

Neither let filthiness proceed out of your mouth. You will have to give an account of all filthiness. –see Matthew 12:36-37. Always esteem yourselves as the least and be not wise in your own conceit. Allow yourselves to be instructed by your elders and always be silent when others speak. Humble yourselves, for …whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted –Matthew 23:12. For Christ who is the greatest made Himself the least for an example unto us. –see John 13:13-15.

Avoid a luxurious life. My children, do not desire the luxuries of fine food or wine. He that desires costly feasts will not become rich. Be content with the labor of your hands. Do not be a burden to anyone as long as you can obtain the things needful—…It is more blessed to give than to receive –Acts 20:35. Paul says: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Be sober and thankful as you have heard me read of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They were selected by the king of Babylon to be nourished with the same wine and meat which the king drank and ate at his table. But they chose to have pulse [vegetables] and water. They wanted to observe the law and commandments of their fathers with sobriety and thankfulness in the fear of God. In the end, they were fairer and fatter than those who ate of the king’s dainties, see Daniel chapter 1. Thus, faithfully they walked in the ways of the Lord. They made themselves acceptable to God in prayer and supplication, therefore, he did great things through them. He delivered them from the den of lions and out of the fiery furnace.

When Joseph was sold into Egypt, he desired no worldly dainties. When the Egyptian woman sought to seduce him, he feared God, and God preserved him. He pleased God in sobriety and prayer and God appointed him ruler over Egypt. –see Genesis chapters 37, 39, and 41. Take an example from this in your youth and you will please God. He will keep you from all seduction.

Oh, my lambs, you are still in your youth, yet you have a part in your Father’s kingdom. See that you keep it well and not as Esau who gave his inheritance or birthright for a mess of pottage, disregarding his father’s blessing. –see Genesis 25:30-34. But Jacob chose the better part, walking in the ways of the Lord with all righteousness.

Shun worldly living. Do not delight in the evils of the world such as lying, cheating, gambling, banqueting, playing, swearing, cursing, backbiting, hatred, and dancing, nor envy, drunkenness, excess, idolatry, covetousness, lasciviousness, vanity, filthy conversation. Though the world does not consider these things to be sin but rather calls them amusements, nevertheless, they are abominations in the eyes of the Lord. –see 1 Peter 4:3-4. If you take pleasure in these things, you sell your birthright (or the spiritual inheritance) from your Father, for a mess of pottage—namely, for a few temporal pleasures, which lead you to damnation.

Choose to suffer affliction with the children of God. From the time of Abel until now many have been afflicted and have suffered. They were rejected, despised, persecuted, and killed because they would not follow the wicked world and her false prophets.

My children, choose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God [that you may be rewarded with them], than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25. Unto such belong all the beautiful promises of God. It is written: …ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy –John 16:20. And, Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life –Revelation 2:10. Finally, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world –John 16:33.

Instructions to my son, David. David, my dear son, I commend you to the Lord. You are the oldest; learn wisdom, so that you may be a good example to your sisters. Beware of bad company and of playing in the street with bad boys. Diligently learn to read and write so that you may get understanding.

Love one another without contention or quarreling. Be kind to your sisters. Bear them up as the stronger and out of love help all you can. Assist them out of brotherly love.

Learn to obey your elders in that which is good. Be industrious so that people may love you. Exhort one another to good works, modesty, honorableness, and quietness. Always care for one another for the time has come that …iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold –Matthew 24:12.

Beware of deception. Remember, Jesus said …that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect –Matthew 24:24. Learn to diligently search the Scriptures so that you may not be deceived. Do not believe gossip but examine the matter.

Make no commotion when you are slandered but bear it for Christ’s sake. Love your enemies and pray for those who speak evil of you and afflict you. Suffer affliction rather than afflicting others. Suffer reproach rather than reproaching others. Be slandered rather than slandering others.

You must constantly see that you do not seek solely your own profit, but always care for those with whom you have dealings, whether they be young or old.

Instructions to my daughters Betgen and Tanneken, my beloved lambs, I admonish you in all these same things, that you obey the commandments of the Lord. Also, obey your elders and all who instruct you in virtue.

Be diligent to do your work, and you will be loved wherever you live. Don’t be quarrelsome, talkative, light-minded, proud, or surly of speech. Be kind, honorable, and quiet, as behooves young girls.

Pray the Lord for wisdom, and it shall be given you. Diligently learn to read and write, and take delight therein, and you will become wise. Take pleasure and sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Learn to please the Lord from your youth, as did the holy women and virgins of old. Esther also was a virgin who feared God; she was adorned with humility, was gracious, honorable, kind, and humble of heart; hence she pleased King Ahasuerus above all the other virgins. –see Esther 2:17. But even in her high estate she was not proud. Though she shone in royal apparel, she humbled her heart with fasting and prayer to the Lord, for her brethren, that they might be delivered out of the hands of their enemies. She did not esteem herself better than one of the least of her brethren.

When you have attained the years of understanding, see that you adorn yourselves with the works of the Spirit such as goodness, gentleness, meekness, humility, obedience, long suffering, righteousness, modesty, honorableness, purity, peaceableness, steadfastness, mercifulness, wisdom, diligence in good works, faith, hope and love. Love God above all that is in the world and do to your neighbor as you would have men do unto you. –see Galatians 5:22-23 and Titus 2:3-5. Remember that Jesus said: …Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets –Matthew 22:37-40.

Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints –Revelation 19:7-8. My daughters, this is the adornment of the saints; labor for such a wedding garment, so that you may enter into the marriage of the Lamb, where they …the righteous, [shall] shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father… –Matthew 13:43. May the Lord lead you as He led Israel out of Egypt, and bring you to the New Jerusalem, that we may see each other with joy in the day of the resurrection. I commend you to the Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; may He keep you to the end of your lives.

In conclusion, O my dear children, I have written this in tears, admonishing you out of love. My prayer and solicitude are constantly for your salvation. I hope and pray constantly that He, in His mercy, will preserve you, just as He preserved Joseph, Moses, and Daniel in the midst of wicked men. And He will do this if you give diligence to follow the truth.

This is my last farewell, my dear lambs. always remember each other in love; diligently learn to read and write and obey everyone in that which is good. I bid you adieu, my dear children Betgen, David and Tanneken. Adieu all my dear brethren and sisters, and friends everywhere.

Written by me, Soetgen van den Houte, your mother in bonds; written in haste (while trembling with cold), out of love for you all, amen.

27 नवम्बर, 1560 को, घेंट के सोतेगन वैन डेन हॉउटे, हॉलैंड को प्रभु यीशु मसीह में विश्वास के कारण शहीद कर दिया गया था। उनकी मृत्यु से पहले उनके पति को भी उनके विश्वास के कारण शहीद किया जा चुका था। कारावास के समय उन्होंने अपने तीन किशोर आयु के बच्चों को कई लंबी चिट्ठियाँ लिखी थीं। निम्नलिखित इन पत्रों के संक्षिप्त अंश हैं जो Martyr’s Mirror के पृष्ठ 646-651 पर पूर्ण पाठ में मिलते हैं।

परम पिता और प्रभु यीशु मसीह की ओर से अनुग्रह, शांति, और दया मेरे प्रिय बच्चों, डेविड, बेतगेन, और टानेकेन, पर। बंधन में तुम्हारी माता द्वारा लिखी यह स्नेहपूर्ण अभिवादन तुम्हारे लिए सत्य की एक स्मृति है। मैं सर्वोच्च की सहायता से अपने शब्दों, अपने जीवन और अपनी मृत्यु से इस सत्य का साक्ष्य देना चाहती हूँ। प्रभु की ओर से पवित्र आत्मा की बुद्धि तुम्हें निर्देश दे और बल दे, ताकि तुम प्रभु की राहों में परवरिश पाओ। चूँकि प्रभु ने मुझे इस संसार से लेने को अच्छा समझा है, मैं तुम्हें अपने केवल सच्चे परमेश्वर में विश्वास की यह स्मृति छोड़ती हूँ, न कि चांदी या सोने की, क्योंकि ऐसे आभूषण नाशशील हैं।

प्रशंसा ग्रहण करो। सर्व प्रथम, मैं तुमसे, मेरे प्रियतम बच्चों, यह उपदेश देती हूँ कि सदा उन लोगों से शिक्षा ग्रहण करना जो प्रभु से डरते हैं। जब तक तुम भली उपदेश और शिक्षाओं का पालन करोगे, परमेश्वर तुम्हारा पिता रहेगा और तुम्हें अनाथ न छोड़ेगा। क्योंकि दाऊद कहता है: पूर्ण कौन मनुष्य है जो यहोवा से डरता है? उसे वह उस मार्ग पर शिक्षा देगा जिसे वह चुनता है —भजन संहिता 25:12। बच्चे, जब तुम्हें सुधार मिले तो दू:ख मत करो और जो तुम्हें सुधारते हैं उनसे क्रोध में वाणी न करो। एक बुद्धिमान पुत्र अपने पिता की शिक्षा सुनता है; पर व्यंग्य करनेवाला प्रशंसा नहीं सुनता —नीतिवचन 13:1।

अपनी जीभ संभालो। मेरे प्रिय बच्चों, अपनी जीभ की रक्षा करो कि वह बुराई न बोले। अपने होंठों से छल या पिछलग्गू बात (बुराई बोलना) का अभ्यास न करो। पॉल हमें सिखाते हैं कि यदि संभव हो तो सभी मनुष्यों के साथ शांति से रहो। —देखो 1 पेत्रुस 3:10 और रोमियों 12:18। यदि किसी ने कठोर बात कही, तो सीखो सौम्य उत्तर देने का, और तुम सभी मनुष्यों द्वारा प्रिय रखे जाओगे। विनम्रता और नम्रता परमेश्वर और मनुष्यों दोनों को स्वीकार्य हैं।

झूठे होंठ यहोवा के लिए घृणा हैं; पर जो सत्यवाचक हैं वे उसे प्रिय हैं —नीतिवचन 12:22। मैं तुम्हें झूठ से सचेत करती हूँ, क्योंकि झूठे पुरुषों का परमेश्वर के राज्य में कोई भाग नहीं है। —देखो प्रकाशितवाक्य 21:8।

कार्य में परिश्रम करो और दान दो। जहाँ भी तुम रहो, अपने काम को हमेशा परिश्रमपूर्वक करो; क्योंकि पॉल कहते हैं …यदि कोई काम करना न चाहता हो तो न खाने दे भी —2 थिस्सलुनीकियों 3:10। ऐसा भी लिखा है, परिश्रम कर कि तुम …किसी को देने के लिए भी पा सको जो आवश्यक हो —इफिसियों 4:28।

गरीब से अपना मुख न मोड़ो। जो निर्धन के रोने पर अपने कान ठुकराता है, वह भी परेशानी में रोयेगा पर कोई सुननेवाला न होगा —नीतिवचन 21:13। अतः प्रार्थना में लगनशील रहो, और गरीबों से प्रेम रखो; क्योंकि मसीह भी हमारे कारण गरीब हुए—तुम्हें हमारा प्रभु यीशु मसीह का अनुग्रह ज्ञात है: यद्यपि वह धनवान था, पर तुम्हारे कारण वह निर्धन हुआ, कि उसकी दरिद्रता से तुम समृद्ध बनो —2 कुरिन्थियों 8:9। अतः अपने स्वर्गीय पिता के समान तुम भी दयालु बनो; क्योंकि ऐसे लोग धन्य हैं और दया पाएँगे। —देखो मत्ती 5:7।

यहोवा का डर रखने के साथ थोड़ा होना बड़े खज़ाने और उससे जुड़ी तंगी से उत्तम है —नीतिवचन 15:16। और, एक सूखा टुकड़ा और उसमें शांति ज्यादा अच्छा है, बनिस्बत बलि से भरे घर के जिसमें झगड़ा हो —नीतिवचन 17:1। अपनी रोटी को अपने हाथों के श्रम से कमाने का चुनाव करो, और अपनी रोटी शांति के साथ खाओ। व्यापारी बनने की तलब न रखो, न ही बड़े लाभ की चिंता करो।

नम्र, दयालु, और हृदय में शुद्ध बनो। नम्र और हृदय से कोमल होना सीखो क्योंकि ऐसे धन्य हैं और वे भूमिं वारिस पाएँगे। तुम इसलिए दयालु बनो, जैसे तुम्हारे पिता भी दयालु है —लूका 6:36। और, धन्य हैं वे जो नम्र हैं: क्योंकि वे पृथ्वी के वारिस होंगे —मत्ती 5:5। अंततः, धन्य हैं वे जो हृदयविहीन शुद्ध हैं: क्योंकि वे परमेश्वर को देखेंगे —मत्ती 5:8। अतः, मेरे प्रिय बच्चों, अपने हृदयों में कोई अशुद्ध विचार न रहने दो। स्तुतियाँ, भजन और आध्यात्मिक गीतों में लगे रहो और बुरे विचारों के लिए कोई स्थान न रहेगा। —देखो इफिसियों 5:19।

न ही तुम्हारे मुख से अभद्रता निकले। तुम्हें हर अभद्रता का उत्तर देना होगा। —देखो मत्ती 12:36-37। सदैव स्वयं को सबसे कम समझो और अपनी बुद्धि पर घमंड न करो। बड़ों से शिक्षा ग्रहण करने दिया करो और जब दूसरे बोलें तो सदा मौन रहो। खुद को नम्र करो, क्योंकि …जो अपना गौरव बढ़ायेगा वह नीचा होगा; और जो खुद को नीचा करेगा वह ऊँचा होगा —मत्ती 23:12। क्योंकि सबसे महान मसीह ने अपने आप को हमारी मिसाल के लिए सबसे छोटा बना लिया। —देखो यूहन्ना 13:13-15।

ऐश्वर्यपूर्ण जीवन से बचो। मेरे बच्चों, सुगन्धित भोजन या शराब की विलासिता की इच्छा मत करो। जो महंगे भोज की इच्छा करता है वह समृद्ध नहीं होगा। अपने हाथों के श्रम से संतुष्ट रहो। जब तक तुम आवश्यक वस्तुएँ स्वयं प्राप्त कर सकते हो किसी पर भार मत बनो—…देने में प्राप्त करने से अधिक धन्य है —प्रेरितों के काम 20:35। पॉल कहते हैं: और भोजना और वस्त्र उपयुक्त हों तो उसी से संतुष्ट रहें —1 तीमुथियुस 6:8।

संयमित और कृतज्ञ बनो जैसे मैंने तुम्हें दानिय्येल, शद्रक, मेशक, और अबेदनेगो के विषय में पढ़ते सुना है। उन्हें बेबीलोन के राजा ने उसी मद्य और भोजन के साथ पोषित करने के लिए चुना जो राजा अपनी मेज़ पर पीता और खाता था। पर उन्होंने दल और पानी को चुन लिया। वे अपने पिता के नियमों और आज्ञाओं का पालन संयम और कृतज्ञता में परमेश्वर के भय से करना चाहते थे। अंततः वे उन लोगों की अपेक्षा सुन्दर और ताज़ा निकले जो राजा के विलासित भोज खाते थे, देखो दानिय्येल अध्याय 1। इस प्रकार उन्होंने भक्ति से प्रभु की राहों में चलना चुना। उन्होंने प्रार्थना और विनती में स्वयं को परमेश्वर के अनुकूल बना लिया, इसलिए उसने उनके बीच बड़े कार्य किए। उसने उन्हें सिंहों के गढ़ और अग्नि के भट्ठी से निकाला।

जब यूसुफ़ को मिस्र में बेचा गया, तो उसने सांसारिक भोगों की इच्छा नहीं की। जब मिस्री स्त्री ने उसे लुभाने का प्रयत्न किया, तो उसने परमेश्वर को डरकर विरोध किया, और परमेश्वर ने उसकी रक्षा की। उसने संयम और प्रार्थना में परमेश्वर को प्रसन्न किया और परमेश्वर ने उसे मिस्र का शासक नियुक्त किया। —देखो उत्पत्ति अध्याय 37, 39, और 41। अपने युवावस्था में इस उदाहरण को अपनाओ और तुम परमेश्वर को प्रसन्न करोगे। वह तुम्हें सभी प्रलोभनों से बचाएगा।

ओ मेरे लल्ला, तुम अभी भी अपनी युवावस्था में हो, फिर भी तुम्हें अपने पिता के राज्य में हिस्सा मिला है। देखो कि तुम इसे अच्छी तरह रखो और उस एशो की तरह न बनो जिसने अपनी विरासत या जन्माधिकार को एक कटोरा दाल-खिचड़ी के लिये दे दिया, अपने पिता के आशीर्वाद की परवाह न करते हुए। —देखो उत्पत्ति 25:30-34। पर याकूब ने उत्तम भाग चुना, और सम्पूर्ण धार्मिकता के साथ प्रभु की राहों पर चला।

संसारिक जीवन से परहेज़ करो। दुनिया के बुराइयों में आनंद मत करो जैसे कि झूठ बोलना, धोखा देना, सट्टेबाज़ी, भाण्डारियों में उड़ेल-खेल, खेल, कसम खाना, शाप देना, पिछलग्गू बातें, घृणा, और नृत्य, न ही ईर्ष्या, शराबखोरी, अतिशय, मूर्तिपूजा, लालच, कामुकता, दिखावा, अशोभनीय वाणी। भले ही संसार इन बातों को पाप न मानकर मनोरंजन कहे, फिर भी ये प्रभु के सामने घृणास्पद हैं। —देखो 1 पेत्रुस 4:3-4। यदि तुम इन चीज़ों में आनंद लेते हो, तो तुम अपने पिता से अपनी जन्म-धरोहर (या आध्यात्मिक विरासत) को एक कटोरे दाल-खिचड़ी के बदले बेच देते हो—यानि कुछ अस्थायी सुखों के लिए जो तुम्हें नाश की ओर ले जाते हैं।

ईश्वर के बच्चों के साथ दुख सहना चुनो। अबेल के समय से लेकर अब तक अनेक लोग पीड़ा में रहे और कष्ट सहते आए हैं। उन्हें त्यागा गया, तिरस्कृत किया गया, उत्पीड़ित किया गया, और मारा गया क्योंकि वे दुष्ट संसार और उसकी झूठी भविष्यवाणियों का अनुसरण नहीं करते थे।

मेरे बच्चों, चुनो …बल्कि ईश्वर की प्रजा के साथ कष्ट सहना [ताकि तुम उनके साथ पुरस्कार पाओ], न कि कुछ समय के लिये पाप की विलासिता का आनंद लेना —इब्रानियों 11:25। ऐसे लोगों के लिए परमेश्वर के सभी सुंदर वादे हैं। लिखा है: …तुम रोओगे और विलाप करोगे, पर संसार आनन्द करेगा; और तुम दुखी होगे, पर तुम्हारा दुःख आनन्द में परिवर्तित हो जायेगा —यूहन्ना 16:20। और, जो कुछ तुम सहोगे उनसे न घबराओ: देखो, शैतान तुम में से कुछ को कैद करेगा कि तुम पर आज़माईश हो; और तुम दस दिन तक कष्ट प्राप्थ करोगे: मृत्यु तक निष्ठावान रहो, और मैं तुम्हें जीवन का मुकुट दूँगा —प्रकाशितवाक्य 2:10। अंततः, ये बातें मैंने तुम्हें कही हैं कि मुझ में तुम्हें शांति मिले। संसार में तुम्हें क्लेश होगा: पर उत्साह रखो; मैंने संसार पर विजय प्राप्त कर ली है —यूहन्ना 16:33।

मेरे पुत्र डेविड के लिए निर्देश। डेविड, मेरे प्रिय पुत्र, मैं तुम्हें प्रभु के भरोसे सौंपती हूँ। तुम सबसे बड़े हो; प्रज्ञा सीखो, ताकि तुम अपनी बहनों के लिए एक अच्छा उदाहरण बन सको। चरित्रहीन साथियों और सड़क पर बुरे लड़कों के साथ खेलने से सावधान रहो। पढ़ना-लिखना लगन से सीखो ताकि तुम समझ प्राप्त कर सको।

एक दूसरे से बिना तकरार और झगड़े प्रेम करो। अपनी बहनों के प्रति दयालु बनो। उन्हें अपनी शक्ति के अनुसार सहारा दो और प्रेम से जहाँ तक हो मदद करो। भाई-भाई के प्रेम से उनकी सहायता करो।

बड़ों की उस भलाई में आज्ञा करना सीखो। परिश्रमी बनो ताकि लोग तुमसे प्रेम करें। एक दूसरे को सद्भाव, शर्मीली प्रकृति, गरिमा और शान्ति के अच्छे कर्मों के लिये प्रेरित करो। एक दूसरे का ध्यान हमेशा रखो क्योंकि वह समय आ चुका है कि …अन्याय बढ़ेगा, अनेक लोगों का प्रेम शीतल हो जाएगा —मत्ती 24:12।

छल से सावधान रहो। स्मरण रखो, यीशु ने कहा …यदि संभव हो तो वे चुने हुए लोगों को भी धोखा देंगे —मत्ती 24:24। छल होने से बचने के लिये सतर्कतापूर्वक शास्त्रों की खोज करना सीखो। अफवाहों पर विश्वास मत करो पर मामले की जाँच करो।

जब तुम्हारे ऊपर बदनामियाँ आयें तो हल्ला मत मचाओ बल्कि मसीह के कारण सहो। अपने शत्रुओं से भी प्रेम रखो और जो तुम्हारे बारे में बुरा बोलते और तुम्हें सताते हैं उनके लिये प्रार्थना करो। दूसरों को कष्ट देने की बजाय कष्ट सहो। दूसरों को दोष देने के बजाय तुम अपमान सहो। दूसरों पर कीचड़ उछालने की बजाय तुम अपमान सहो।

तुम्हें निरंतर देखना चाहिए कि तुम केवल अपने ही लाभ का पीछा न करों, बल्कि सदा उन लोगों का भी ध्यान रखो जिनके साथ तुम्हारे व्यवहार हैं, चाहे वे युवा हों या वृद्ध।

मेरी पुत्रियों बेतगेन और टानेकेन के लिए निर्देश, मेरे प्रिय लल्लों, मैं तुम्हें ये सब बातें उसी प्रकार सिखाती हूँ कि तुम प्रभु की आज्ञाओं का पालन करो। साथ ही, अपने बड़ों और जो तुम्हें सदाचार में शिक्षा देते हैं, उनकी आज्ञा मानो।

अपने काम में परिश्रम करो, और जहाँ भी तुम रहो लोग तुमसे प्रेम करेंगे। कलहप्रिय, बातूनी, हल्की-मन की, घमंडी, या कटु वाणी वाली मत बनो। तुम्हारे लिये यौवनावस्था के अनुकूल है कि तुम दयालु, गरिमापूर्ण, और शांत रहो।

प्रभु से बुद्धि माँगो, और वह तुम्हें दी जायेगी। पढ़ना-लिखना लगन से सीखो, और इसमें आनन्द लो, और तुम बुद्धिमान बनोगी। स्तुतियाँ, भजन और आध्यात्मिक गीत गाकर आनन्द लो। युवावस्था से ही प्रभु को प्रसन्न करना सीखो, जैसे प्राचीन काल की पवित्र स्त्रियाँ और कुंवारीयाँ करती थीं। एस्तेर भी एक ऐसी कुंवारी थी जो परमेश्वर से डरती थी; वह विनम्रता से सजी, कृपालु, गरिमापूर्ण, दयालु और हृदय से नम्र थी; इसलिए उसने राजा अहशेरूस को सब अन्य कुंवरियों से अधिक प्रसन्न किया। —देखो एस्तेर 2:17। पर अपने उन्नत स्थान में भी वह घमंडी नहीं थी। भले ही वह शाही वस्त्रों में शोभित थी, उसने प्रार्थना और व्रत से अपने हृदय को नम्र रखा ताकि उसके भाइयों के लिये वह अपने शत्रुओं के हाथों से मुक्ति पा सके। उसने खुद को अपने भाइयों में से किसी एक से भी श्रेष्ठ नहीं माना।

जब तुम समझ की आयु प्राप्त कर लो, तब देखो कि तुम आत्मा के कर्मों से सौभ्य बनो जैसे भलाई, कोमलता, नम्रता, विनम्रता, आज्ञाकारिता, धैर्य, धार्मिकता, नम्रता, गरिमापूर्ण व्यवहार, पवित्रता, शांतिपूर्ण रहने, दृढ़ता, दयालुता, बुद्धि, भले कामों में परिश्रम, विश्वास, आशा और प्रेम। दुनिया की हर चीज से ऊपर परमेश्वर से प्रेम करो और अपने पड़ोसी के साथ वैसा व्यवहार करो जैसा तुम चाहते हो कि मनुष्य तुम्हारे साथ करे। —देखो गैलातियों 5:22-23 और तीतुस 2:3-5। स्मरण रखो कि यीशु ने कहा: …तू अपने प्रभु परमेश्वर से अपने सभी हृदय से, और अपनी सारी आत्मा से, और अपनी सारी बुद्धि से प्रेम करेगा। यही पहली और महान आज्ञा है। और दूसरी इससे समान है: तू अपने पड़ोसी से वैसा प्रेम करेगा जैसे अपने आप से। इन दोनों आज्ञाओं पर सारी व्यवस्था और भविष्यवक्ता टिकी हुई है —मत्ती 22:37-40।

आओ हम आनन्दित हों और प्रसन्न हों, और उसे मान दें: क्योंकि मेष का विवाह आया है, और उसकी पत्नी ने स्वयं को तैयार कर लिया है। और उसे सूती महीन वस्त्र पहनाने का अधिकार दिया गया: क्योंकि यह महीन वस्त्र पवित्रों की धार्मिकता है —प्रकाशितवाक्य 19:7-8। मेरी बेटियों, यह पवित्रों का आभूषण है; ऐसी वैवाहिक वस्त्र के लिये परिश्रम करो, ताकि तुम मेष के विवाह में प्रवेश कर सको, जहाँ वे …धार्मिक, अपने पिता के राज्य में सूर्य की भाँति प्रकाशमान होंगे… —मत्ती 13:43। प्रभु तुम्हें वैसे ही निर्देश दे जैसा उसने इज़राइल को मिस्र से निकाला, और तुम्हें नई यरूशलेम तक लाए, कि हम पुनरुत्थान के दिन हर्ष के साथ एक-दूसरे को देखें। मैं तुम्हें अब्राहम के परमेश्वर, इसहाक के परमेश्वर, और याकूब के परमेश्वर के भरोसे सौंपती हूँ; वह तुम्हें तुम्हारे जीवन के अंत तक सुरक्षित रखे।

अंत में, हे मेरे प्रिय बच्चों, मैंने यह आँसुओं में लिखा है, प्रेम से तुमको उपदेश देती हुई। मेरी प्रार्थना और चिन्ता सदा तुम्हारी मुक्ति के लिये है। मैं निरन्तर आशा और प्रार्थना करती हूँ कि वह अपनी करुणा में तुम्हारी रक्षा करेगा, जैसे उसने दुष्ट पुरुषों के बीच यूसुफ़, मूसा, और दानिय्येल की रक्षा की थी। और यदि तुम सत्य का अनुसरण करने में परिश्रम करोगे तो वह ऐसा करेगा।

यह मेरी अंतिम विदाई है, मेरे प्रिय लल्लों। सदा एक-दूसरे को प्रेम में स्मरण करो; पढ़ना-लिखना लगन से सीखो और जो कुछ भला हो उसमें सबकी आज्ञा मानो। मैं तुम्हें विदा कहती हूँ, मेरे प्रिय बच्चे बेतगेन, डेविड और टानेकेन। विदा मेरे प्रिय भाइयों और बहनों, और हरत्रह मित्रों को।

मेरे द्वारा लिखा गया, सोएटजन वैन डेन हॉउटे, तुम्हारी बंधन में माता; शीघ्रता में लिखी (ठंड से काँपते हुए), आप सभी के लिये प्रेम से, आमीन।

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Little did they know where this journey would lead them. They received the call, they responded to the call, and now they were on a journey that would forever change their lives. Little do we know when we choose to follow Jesus where that journey will lead us. That is why it is considered a journey of faith.

One thing is certain, walking with Jesus will lead you into a life of holiness. What exactly do we mean by holiness? Holiness is the full sum of the righteousness of Jesus manifested in our lives by the work of regeneration and the inner renewing of the Holy Ghost.

John the Baptist said of Jesus: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that cometh after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will throughly purge his floor, and gather his wheat into the garner; but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire –Matthew 3:11-12.

This speaks of the baptism of the Holy Ghost and fire, and of the thorough purging that Jesus would bring. Jesus did not come with violence and yet His righteous presence swept through Palestine like a winnowing breeze. Those who rejected Him were blown away and disappeared from the narrative. Those who loved Him were set forth as the chosen ones who became the founders of a new kingdom established on principles not known before.

The principles of this new kingdom are demonstrated in the life of Christ and explained in His teachings. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus set forth teaching that challenged the most pious Pharisee and disturbed the apathy of the sinner. Jesus’ teachings were such that they could not be lightly ignored for they stirred a deep longing in the human heart for the love and peace that they offered while at the same time exposing the innate selfishness that prevented it.

It was this promise and hope of a new humanity that drew crowds of people after Him. They followed Jesus, some hoping for a miracle, some for bread, but many were drawn to Him by a deep inner longing for deliverance from the stranglehold of sin. Those who truly sought deliverance, found it.

One such disciple was Mary Magdalene. The Scripture gives us only cursory glances of her life. She appears to have been one of several women of whom the Scriptures make mention that followed Jesus. Doctor Luke tells us that Jesus healed her of evil spirits and infirmities. Apparently, she was not only possessed of evil spirits, but also physically infirmed.

And it came to pass afterward, that he went throughout every city and village, preaching and shewing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God: and the twelve were with him, And certain women, which had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities, Mary called Magdalene, out of whom went seven devils, And Joanna the wife of Chuza Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, which ministered unto him of their substance –Luke 8:1-3.

Mary became a faithful follower of Jesus. Her presence is especially noted in the Scriptures after the death of Christ. She was first to the sepulcher early on the resurrection morning and she lingered there when the others had gone away. Her diligent pursuit of Christ was rewarded when Jesus appeared first to her.

Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away. Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself, and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master –John 20:15-16.

Mary knew Jesus the moment He spoke her name. This intimacy was born of a passion for Christ that was the fruit of her deliverance. Mary’s love for Jesus was the result of having been delivered from seven devils.

Jesus’ primary mission in coming to earth was to deliver us from the power of sin. In Luke 5, Doctor Luke records an account of a man who was paralyzed. He could not walk. His friends brought him for healing, but they could not reach Jesus because of the crowd. So, they went up onto the roof and removed enough of roof tiles to let their friend through and lowered him into the presence of Jesus. How ingenious! How desperate they were to help their friend to find healing.

And when he saw their faith, he said unto him, Man, thy sins are forgiven thee –Luke 5:20. They sought healing, but Jesus saw the deeper need of this man’s soul, so He offered forgiveness. This, of course, raised the ire of the Pharisees who …began to reason, saying, Who is this which speaketh blasphemies? Who can forgive sins, but God alone? –Luke 5:21. They were right, only God can forgive sins, but what they did not want to believe was that Jesus was God’s Son and that thus He had did have the power to forgive sins. So, Jesus went on to say: …What reason ye in your hearts? Whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Rise up and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power upon earth to forgive sins, (he said unto the sick of the palsy,) I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy couch, and go into thine house –Luke 5:22-24.

To follow Jesus is to leave your sins. We would be greatly mistaken to suggest that holiness is a product of human effort. Our journey to holiness must be a journey to Calvary. Many “holy men” and “holy women” down through the ages have sought to live a holy life in their own strength. What always happens is that we settle for a form of godliness that falls short of Christ’s righteousness. We settle for a religion that is doable.

The apostle Paul, when writing about his Jewish brethren said: For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God –Romans 10:3.

This “righteousness of God” is an inner righteousness of the heart that can only come about through the work of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Ghost. It is for this reason that our journey with Jesus must lead us to Calvary for it is there that we behold our dying Lord—bleeding, dying for our sins—for my sins—for your sins.

The blood of Jesus is the only means to the “righteousness of God”. The “righteousness of God” is imputed through forgiveness, and it is the fruit of our lives after being empowered through the Holy Spirit. Either way, the “righteousness of God” is attributed to the work of Christ on the cross. There is no other means to holiness.

In Mathew 22, Jesus told the story of a king who planned a wedding for his son. When the invited guests (the Jewish people) refused his invitation, the invitation then went out to all those who had not been invited, and the wedding was furnished with guests.

When the king came in to observe the wedding, he was pleased with what he saw until he spotted a man who was not wearing a wedding garment. (A wedding garment was a white linen garment that was provided by the master of the feast.)

I quote Adam Clark: “Among the Orientals, long white robes were worn at public festivals; and those who appeared on such occasions with any other garments were esteemed, not only highly culpable, but worthy of punishment. The person who invited the guests prepared such a garment for each, for the time being; and with which he was furnished on his application to the ruler of the feast. It was this which made the conduct of the person mentioned in the text inexcusable; he might have had a proper marriage garment, if he had applied for it”.

“Not wearing a wedding garment” was to insult the master of the feast, who provided everything, (including the wedding garment) so that all the guests would be equally suited for the occasion. No one needs to be excluded for lack of proper clothing or any other amenity. The king provided the invitation and all necessary amenities, and the guest need only to accept the invitation and receive the gracious provision of the king.

What a beautiful analogy of the Kingdom of Heaven. The King has invited us to His heavenly feast. He wants us to come and enjoy the feast with Him. He wants us to come no matter who we are or where we come from—some from the gutters of sin, some from the depth of ignorance, and some from the temples of self-righteousness. All are invited to come on equal terms—All must accept the invitation, and all must wear the wedding garment.

We are not told the exact condition of this man who refused the wedding garment, but a general understanding of human nature would indicate that he was probably a well-dressed gentleman. Those who came shabbily dressed would have welcomed the wedding garment to disguise their true condition. Most likely this man wanted to display his finery. He did not feel inclined to cover his fine clothing with a simple white cloak.

This is the condition of all who trust in their own righteousness. The best that we can bring to God falls short of the righteousness that God requires. Isaiah wrote: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away –Isaiah 64:6.

In this desperate situation we find ourselves in need of a redeemer. God has provided us with a Redeemer in His Son, Jesus. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace –Ephesians 1:7. God has invited us to His feast, and He has provided us with everything that is needed that we can be made righteous.

One attribute of a person who has been cleansed from sin through the blood of Christ, is worship. Luke tells the story of a woman who “was a sinner” who came to worship Jesus: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment, And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment. Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner –Luke 7:37-39.

We do not know her name, only that she “was a sinner”. That was her reputation—she was ‘not good’. But she apparently had had a previous encounter with Jesus. She came to Simon’s house to offer her sacrifice of thanksgiving. She brought the best that she had. An alabaster box of ointment said to have been worth a year’s wages. She anointed Jesus’ feet and washed them with her tears—tears of repentance, tears of joy, tears of relief.

Simon observed her worship. He despised her in his heart. He considered her offering a great waste. Jesus challenged him. He said to Simon: …Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head. Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet. My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment. Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little –Luke 7:44-47.

He said to the woman …Thy sins are forgiven –Luke 7:48. Forgiveness, and freedom from sin, awaken the heart to worship. When a man or woman is set free from the guilt and bondage of sin, praise flows freely. Simon was a Pharisee who was relying on his own righteousness. Yet Jesus brought him to the awareness that he was greatly lacking in love and worship.

Following Jesus will lead us to holiness of heart and life. Following Jesus brings us face to face with the cause and the cure of the sin problem. The cause of sin is our fallen carnal nature, and our fallen nature is revealed in the light of His holiness. Along with Mary Magdalene and the other disciples, as we journey with Jesus, we become aware of our need and our need cries out for His grace. The cure for our sin is Jesus—…thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins –Matthew 1:21.

In Augustus Toplady’s famous hymn, Rock of Ages we find this line–

Be of sin the double cure; save me from its guilt (through forgiveness) and power (through sanctification).

예수께서 갈릴리 바닷가를 거니실 때에 시몬이라 하는 베드로와 그의 형제 안드레가 바다에 그물을 던지는 것을 보니 그들은 고기 잡는 자라. 예수께서 저희에게 이르시되 나를 따르라 내가 너희로 사람을 낚는 어부가 되게 하리라 하시니 저희가 곧 그물을 버리고 따르니라. 거기서 더 가시매 세베대의 아들 야고보와 그의 형제 요한이 배에 아버지 세베대와 함께 있어 그물질을 깁는 것을 보시고 저희를 부르시니 저희가 곧 배와 아버지를 버리고 따르니라 -마태복음 4:18-22.

그들이 이 여정이 어디로 인도할지 거의 알지 못했습니다. 그들은 부르심을 받았고, 그 부르심에 응답했으며, 이제 그들의 삶을 영원히 바꿀 여정에 있었습니다. 우리도 예수님을 따르기로 선택할 때 그 여정이 우리를 어디로 데려갈지 거의 알지 못합니다. 그것이 바로 믿음의 여정으로 여겨지는 이유입니다.

한 가지는 분명합니다. 예수와 동행하는 것은 당신을 거룩한 삶으로 인도할 것입니다. 거룩함이 정확히 무엇을 의미하는가? 거룩함은 중생의 역사와 성령의 내적 쇄신을 통해 우리 삶에 드러난 예수의 의의 전적 합계입니다.

세례자 요한은 예수에 대해 이렇게 말했습니다: 나는 회개를 위하여 물로 너희를 세례하거니와 내 뒤에 오시는 이는 내게 능력이 많으신 이시니 나는 그의 신발을 들기도 감당치 못하겠노라 그가 너희로 성령과 불로 세례하시리라 그의 키는 그의 손에 부채와 같아 그가 곧 그의 타작마당을 깨끗하게 하여 곡식을 그의 곳간에 모으시고 쭉정이는 불로 멸하시리라 -마태복음 3:11-12.

이는 성령과 불의 세례와 예수님이 가져오실 철저한 정결을 말합니다. 예수께서는 폭력으로 오신 것이 아니지만 그의 의로운 임재는 도리어 가루질하는 바람처럼 팔레스타인 전역을 휩쓸었습니다. 그를 거부한 자들은 날려가 버려져 이야기에서 사라졌고, 그를 사랑한 자들은 선택된 자로 드러나 이전에 알려지지 않았던 원리들 위에 세워진 새 왕국의 창시자가 되었습니다.

이 새 왕국의 원리들은 그리스도의 삶에서 드러나며 그의 가르침에서 설명됩니다. 산상수훈에서 예수님은 가장 경건한 바리새인을 도전하고 죄인의 무관심을 동요시키는 가르침을 제시하셨습니다. 예수의 가르침은 가볍게 무시될 수 없는 것이었는데, 그것들은 인간의 마음에 그들이 제공하는 사랑과 평화를 향한 깊은 갈망을 불러일으키면서 동시에 그것을 방해하는 타고난 이기심을 드러냈기 때문입니다.

바로 이러한 새 인류에 대한 약속과 소망이 사람들 무리를 그에게 이끌었습니다. 어떤 이들은 기적을 바라며, 어떤 이들은 빵을 바라며 따랐지만, 많은 사람들은 죄의 옥쇄로부터의 구출을 향한 깊은 내적 갈망에 이끌려 그를 따랐습니다. 진정으로 구원을 구한 자들은 그것을 얻었습니다.

그 제자들 가운데 한 사람은 막달라 마리아였습니다. 성경은 그녀의 삶을 단편적으로만 보여줍니다. 그녀는 성경이 언급하는 여러 여성 중 한 사람으로 보이며 예수를 따랐습니다. 누가 의사(눅)는 예수께서 그녀에게서 악한 영들과 병을 고치셨다고 전합니다. 분명히 그녀는 악한 영에 사로잡혀 있었을 뿐 아니라 육체적으로도 병들어 있었습니다.

그 후에 예수께서 두루 다니사 하나님 나라의 기쁜 소식을 전하여 모든 성과 마을에 이르시니 열둘이 저와 함께하며 또 악한 영들과 병에서 고침을 받은 몇몇 여자가 있어 막달라라 하는 마리아 곧 일곱 귀신을 쫓아낸 자, 또 회자의 관리인 쿠자의 아내 요안나와 수산나와 다른 많은 여자가 있어 자기 소유로써 저희를 시중드니라 -누가복음 8:1-3.

마리아는 예수의 충실한 추종자가 되었습니다. 그녀의 존재는 특히 그리스도의 죽음 이후에 성경에서 두드러지게 기록되어 있습니다. 그녀는 부활하신 아침에 가장 먼저 무덤에 갔고 다른 이들이 떠났을 때도 그곳에 머물렀습니다. 그녀의 부지런한 그리스도 찾기는 예수께서 먼저 그녀에게 나타나셨을 때 보상받았습니다.

예수께서 그녀에게 이르시되 여자여 어찌하여 울느냐 누구를 찾느냐 하시니 그녀가 돌봐 생각하여 농부인 줄로 여겨 가로되 주여 만일 그를 옮기셨거든 어디 두셨는지 내게 말하옵소서 내가 가져가리이다 예수께서 그에게 이름을 부르시되 마리아라 하시니 그녀가 돌아서서 가로되 라보니라 곧 번역하면 선생이시라 -요한복음 20:15-16.

예수께서 그녀의 이름을 부르신 그 순간 마리아는 예수를 알아보았습니다. 이 친밀감은 그녀의 구원 열매로 태어난 그리스도에 대한 열정에서 비롯된 것이었습니다. 마리아의 예수에 대한 사랑은 일곱 귀신에게서 구원받은 결과였습니다.

예수께서 이 땅에 오신 주된 사명은 우리를 죄의 권세에서 건져내는 것이었습니다. 눅 5장에서 누가 의사는 한 마비된 사람의 이야기를 기록합니다. 그는 걸을 수 없었습니다. 그의 친구들이 그를 고침 받게 하려고 데려왔으나 무리 때문에 예수께 이를 수 없었습니다. 그래서 그들은 지붕 위로 올라가 기와를 조금 떼어내고 친구를 예수의 앞에 내리니 얼마나 기발한가! 친구를 고치려는 그들의 간절함이 얼마나 절박했는가를 보여줍니다.

예수께서 그들의 믿음을 보시고 중풍병자에게 이르시되 인자여 네 죄들이 사함을 받았느니라 하시니라 -누가복음 5:20. 그들은 고침을 구했지만 예수께서는 그 사람 영혼의 더 깊은 필요를 보시고 용서를 제안하셨습니다. 이것은 바리새인들의 분노를 불러일으켰는데 그들은 …이는 누가 하나님 외에 죄를 사하느냐 하고 마음에 정죄하며 말하더라 -누가복음 5:21. 그들이 옳은 점은 오직 하나님만이 죄를 사할 수 있다는 것이었습니다. 그러나 그들이 믿지 않으려 했던 것은 예수께서 하나님의 아들이시며 그러므로 죄를 사할 권세가 있다는 사실이었습니다. 그래서 예수께서는 계속하여 말씀하셨습니다: 너희가 마음에 무슨 생각을 하느냐 말하노니 이르기를 네 죄들이 사함을 받았느니라 하는 것이 쉬운가 혹은 네가 일어나 걸으라 하는 것이 쉬운가 그러나 인자가 땅 위에서 죄를 사하는 권세가 있는 줄을 너희로 알게 하려 함이니라 하시고 중풍병자에게 이르시되 네가 일어나 네가 누운 상을 들고 네 집으로 가라 하시니라 -누가복음 5:22-24.

예수를 따르는 것은 당신의 죄를 떠나는 것입니다. 거룩함이 인간의 노력의 산물이라고 주장한다면 우리는 크게 오해하는 것입니다. 거룩함을 향한 우리의 여정은 반드시 골고다로 향해야 합니다. 많은 ‘거룩한 남자들’과 ‘거룩한 여자들’이 세월을 통해 자신의 힘으로 거룩한 삶을 살려고 했습니다. 그러나 항상 일어나는 일은 우리가 그리스도의 의에 미치지 못하는 외형적 경건에 안주한다는 것입니다. 우리는 실행 가능한 종교를 선택하게 됩니다.

사도 바울은 그의 유대인 형제들에 대해 쓸 때 말했습니다: 저희가 하나님의 의를 알지 못하고 자기의 의를 세우려고 힘쓰다가 하나님의 의에 복종하지 아니하였느니라 -로마서 10:3.

이 ‘하나님의 의’는 중생과 성령의 쇄신을 통해서만 이루어질 수 있는 마음의 내적 의입니다. 이러한 이유로 우리와 함께하는 예수와의 여정은 우리를 반드시 골고다로 인도해야 합니다. 그곳에서 우리는 우리의 죽어가는 주—피 흘리시며 우리 죄를 위해 죽으시는—를 바라보기 때문입니다—나의 죄를 위하여—너의 죄를 위하여.

예수의 피만이 ‘하나님의 의’에 이르는 유일한 수단입니다. ‘하나님의 의’는 용서를 통해 전가되며, 성령의 능력으로 말미암아 우리 삶의 열매가 됩니다. 어떤 경우든 ‘하나님의 의’는 십자가에서 이루어진 그리스도의 사역에 기인합니다. 거룩함에 이르는 다른 수단은 없습니다.

마태복음 22장에서 예수께서는 어떤 왕이 자기 아들을 위하여 혼인 잔치를 베풀기로 한 이야기를 하셨습니다. 초대받은 손님들(유대인들)이 초청을 거절할 때 초청은 초대받지 못한 모든 이에게로 나갔고 잔치는 손님들로 채워졌습니다.

왕이 잔치를 살피러 들어왔을 때 그가 보는 것은 마음에 드는 것이었으나 혼인 예복을 입지 않은 사람을 보자 기쁨이 사라졌습니다. (혼인 예복은 잔치 주인이 제공한 흰 마포 예복이었습니다.)

아담 클라크를 인용합니다: “동방인들 사이에서는 공중한 잔치에 긴 흰 예복을 입었고 그런 자리에서 다른 옷을 입고 나타나는 자는 크게 비난받을 뿐 아니라 처벌받을 만하다고 여겨졌다. 초청자는 그때에 잠시 입을 예복을 각각 준비하였고 손님이 잔치 관원에게 요청하면 그 예복으로 몸을 갖추게 하였다. 본문에 언급된 자의 행위가 용서받지 못할 것이었던 것은 그가 그 예복을 요청했더라면 적절한 혼인 예복을 입을 수 있었기 때문이다.”

“혼인 예복을 입지 않은 것”은 모든 것을 제공한 잔치 주인을 모욕하는 것이었습니다(혼인 예복을 포함하여) 그래야 모든 손님이 행사에 공평히 어울릴 수 있었습니다. 적절한 옷이나 다른 편의가 없어서 누구도 제외될 필요가 없습니다. 왕은 초청과 필요한 모든 것을 제공했으며 손님은 단지 초청을 받아 왕의 은혜로운 제공을 수용하면 됩니다.

천국의 아름다운 비유가 아닙니까. 왕은 우리를 그의 하늘 잔치에 초청하셨습니다. 그는 우리가 와서 그와 함께 잔치를 즐기기를 원합니다. 그는 우리가 누구이든 어디서 왔든 오기를 원합니다—어떤 이는 죄의 도랑에서, 어떤 이는 무지의 깊은 곳에서, 어떤 이는 자의식의 성전에서 왔든 상관없이. 모두가 동등한 조건으로 초대받았습니다—모두 초청을 받아야 하고 모두 혼인 예복을 입어야 합니다.

혼인 예복을 거부한 이 사람의 정확한 상태는 알려지지 않았지만 인간 본성에 대한 일반적 이해로 보면 그는 아마도 잘 차려입은 신사였을 것입니다. 초라하게 온 자들은 자신의 참모습을 가리기 위해 혼인 예복을 반겼을 것입니다. 아마도 이 사람은 자신의 화려한 옷차림을 과시하고 싶어했을 것입니다. 그는 단순한 흰 망토로 자신의 훌륭한 옷을 가리려고 하지 않았습니다.

이것이 자신의 의를 신뢰하는 모든 사람의 상태입니다. 우리가 하나님께 가져갈 수 있는 최선은 하나님이 요구하시는 의에 미치지 못합니다. 이사야는 썼습니다: 우리는 다 부정하고 우리의 의는 다 더러운 해불이니이다 우리가 다 잎과 같이 쇠하였고 우리의 죄악 같이 바람에 끌려가나이다 -이사야 64:6.

이 절망적인 상태에서 우리는 구속자가 필요함을 깨닫습니다. 하나님은 그의 아들 예수 안에서 우리에게 구속자를 제공하셨습니다. 그 안에서 우리가 그의 피로 말미암아 구속 곧 죄 사함을 얻었으니 이는 그 은혜의 풍성함을 따라 된 것이니라 -에베소서 1:7. 하나님은 우리를 그의 잔치에 초청하셨고 우리가 의롭게 될 수 있도록 필요한 모든 것을 제공하셨습니다.

그리스도의 피로 죄에서 깨끗하게 된 사람의 한 가지 특징은 예배입니다. 누가는 “죄인”인 한 여자가 예수를 경배하러 온 이야기를 전합니다: 보라 어떤 성중에 죄인이 있는 한 여자가 있어 예수가 바리새인의 집에서 상을 먹는 것을 알고 향합 곧 값 비싼 향료 단지를 가지고 와서 그 뒤에서 그의 발 곁에 서서 울며 눈물로 그의 발을 씻고 자기 머리털로 닦고 그의 발에 입을 맞추고 향을 바르더라 그를 초대한 바리새인이 보고 속으로 말하되 이 사람이 선지자이면 누구이며 어떤 여자 인 줄을 알리라 그가 만지는 자라 이는 죄인이라 하더라 -누가복음 7:37-39.

우리는 그녀의 이름을 알지 못합니다. 다만 그녀가 “죄인”이었다는 것만 압니다. 그것이 그녀의 평판이었습니다—그녀는 ‘좋지 않다’고 여겨졌습니다. 그러나 분명히 그녀는 이전에 예수를 만난 적이 있었습니다. 그녀는 감사의 제물을 바치려 시몬의 집에 왔습니다. 그녀는 가진 것 중 최고를 가져왔습니다. 한 해치고의 품삯에 해당한다고 하는 값비싼 향료 단지를 가져왔습니다. 그녀는 예수의 발에 향을 부으며 눈물—회개의 눈물, 기쁨의 눈물, 안도감의 눈물—로 그의 발을 씻었습니다.

시몬은 그녀의 예배를 관찰했습니다. 그는 마음속으로 그녀를 경멸했습니다. 그는 그녀의 헌물을 큰 낭비로 여겼습니다. 예수께서 그에게 도전하셨습니다. 예수께서 시몬에게 말씀하시기를 이 여자를 보느냐 내가 네 집에 들어왔을 때 내 발에 물을 주지 아니하였으나 이 사람은 눈물로 내 발을 씻고 자기 머리털로 닦았느니라 네가 내게 입맞춤을 주지 아니하였으나 이 사람은 내가 들어온 때부터 내 발에 입맞추기를 그치지 아니하였느니라 네가 내 머리에 기름을 바르지 아니하였으나 이 사람은 향을 내 발에 발랐느니라 이러므로 내가 네게 말하노니 많은 죄를 용서받은 까닭에 저가 많은 사랑을 하였느니라 적게 용서받는 자는 적게 사랑하느니라 -누가복음 7:44-47.

예수께서 그 여자에게 이르시되 네 죄사함을 받았느니라 -누가복음 7:48. 용서와 죄로부터의 자유는 마음을 예배로 일깨웁니다. 남자나 여자가 죄의 죄책과 결박에서 해방될 때 찬양은 자유롭게 흘러나옵니다. 시몬은 자기 의에 의지하는 바리새인이었습니다. 그러나 예수께서는 그가 사랑과 예배에 크게 부족함을 깨닫게 하셨습니다.

예수를 따르는 것은 우리를 마음과 삶의 거룩함으로 이끕니다. 예수를 따르는 것은 우리를 죄 문제의 원인과 치유 앞에 마주 서게 합니다. 죄의 원인은 우리의 타락한 육체적 본성이며, 우리의 타락한 본성은 그의 거룩의 빛 안에서 드러납니다. 막달라 마리아와 다른 제자들과 함께 예수와 동행하는 가운데 우리는 우리의 필요를 인식하게 되며 우리의 필요는 그의 은혜를 간구합니다. 우리의 죄에 대한 치유는 예수입니다—그의 이름을 네가 예수라 하라 이는 그가 자기 백성을 그들의 죄에서 구원할 자이심이라 -마태복음 1:21.

어거스터스 톱래디의 유명한 찬송가 반석이신 주에서 우리는 이런 구절을 찾습니다—

죄에 대한 이중의 치료가 되소서; 그 죄의 죄책으로부터(용서를 통해)와 능력으로부터(성화를 통하여) 나를 구원하소서.
