En Jesus, wandelend langs die see van Galilea, sien Hy twee broers, Simon, genoem Petrus, en Andreas sy broer, wat ’n net in die see gooi het; want hulle was vissers. En Hy sê tot hulle: Volg My, en Ek sal julle maak tot vissers van mense. En hulle laat dadelik hulle nette agter en volg Hom. En van daar afgaande, sien Hy ander twee broers, Jakobus, die seun van Sebedeüs, en Johannes sy broer, in ’n boot saam met Sebedeüs hulle vader, wat hulle nette herstel; en Hy roep hulle. En hulle laat dadelik die boot en hulle vader agter en volg Hom – Matteus 4:18-22.

Hulle het skaars geweet waarheen hierdie reis hulle sou lei. Hulle het die oproep ontvang, hulle het op die oproep geantwoord, en nou was hulle op ’n reis wat vir altyd hul lewens sou verander. Min weet ons wanneer ons kies om Jesus te volg waarheen daardie reis ons sal lei. Daarom word dit as ’n reis van geloof beskou.

Een ding is seker: om met Jesus te wandel sal jou in ’n lewe van heiligheid bring. Wat bedoel ons presies met heiligheid? Heiligheid is die volle som van Jesus se geregtigheid wat in ons lewens gemanifesteer word deur die werk van wedergeboorte en die innerlike vernuwing van die Heilige Gees.

Johannes die Doper het van Jesus gesê: Ek doop julle wel met water tot bekering: maar Hy wat ná my kom, is sterker as ek, wiens skoene ek nie waardig is om te dra nie: Hy sal julle doop met die Heilige Gees en met vuur: Hy het sy dorswa in sy hand, en Hy sal sy dorsvloer skoonmaak, en sy koring in die skuur ingaar; maar Hy sal die kaf met onsblusbare vuur verbrand – Matteus 3:11-12.

Hierdie praat van die doop met die Heilige Gees en vuur, en van die deeglike suiwering wat Jesus sou bring. Jesus het nie met geweld gekom nie, en tog het Sy regverdige teenwoordigheid deur Palestina soos ’n dorswa-breeze gewaai. Dikwels is diegene wat Hom verwerp het weggedryf en het uit die verhaal verdwyn. Dikwels is diegene wat Hom liefgehad het uitgestel as die uitverkorenes wat die grundleggers geword het van ’n nuwe koninkryk gevestig op beginsels wat voorheen nie bekend was nie.

Die beginsels van hierdie nuwe koninkryk word in die lewe van Christus gedemonstreer en in Sy onderrig verduidelik. In die Bergpredikasie het Jesus onderrig gegee wat die vroomste Fariseër uitgedaag het en die apatie van die sondaars ontstel het. Jesus se onderrig was sulke dat dit nie liglik geïgnoreer kon word nie, want dit het ’n diep verlange in die menslike hart aangespreek na die liefde en vrede wat dit aangebied het, terwyl dit terselfdertyd die aangebore selfsug blootgelê het wat dit verhinder het.

Dit was die belofte en hoop op ’n nuwe mensdom wat skares mense na Hom toe gelok het. Hulle het Jesus gevolg, sommige in die hoop op ’n wonder, sommige vir brood, maar baie is deur ’n diep innerlike verlange na bevryding van die verstikkende mag van sonde na Hom toe getrek. Diegene wat werklik na bevryding gesoek het, het dit gevind.

Eén so ’n dissipel was Maria Magdalena. Die Skrif gee ons slegs oppervlakkige kykies in haar lewe. Sy blyk een te wees van verskeie vroue van wie die Skrifte melding maak wat Jesus gevolg het. Doktor Lukas vertel ons dat Jesus haar van bose geeste en ongesteldhede genees het. Skynbaar was sy nie net beset deur bose geeste nie, maar ook liggaamlik ongesteld.

En dit het daarna gebeur, dat Hy deur elke stad en dorp gegaan het, verkondigend en die blye boodskap van die koninkryk van God wysend: en die twaalf was by Hom, En sekere vroue, wat van bose geeste en ongesteldhede genees was, Maria genaamd Magdalena, waaruit vyf duiwels uitgegaan het, En Joana, die vrou van Chuza, Herodes se intendant, en Susanna, en baie ander, wat vir Hom uit hulle eiendom gedien het – Lukas 8:1-3.

Maria het ’n getroue volgeling van Jesus geword. Haar teenwoordigheid word veral in die Skrifte opgemerk ná die dood van Christus. Sy was die eerste by die graf vroeg op die opstandingsoggend en sy het daar gebly toe die ander weggegaan het. Haar ywerige agtervolging van Christus is beloon toe Jesus eers aan haar verskyn het.

Jesus sê tot haar: Vrou, waarom huil jy? Wie soek jy? Sy, in die veronderstelling dat Hy die tuinier was, sê tot Hom: Here, as U Hom hier weggeneem het, sê my waar U Hom gelê het, en Ek sal Hom weghaal. Jesus sê tot haar: Maria. Sy draai om en sê tot Hom: Rabboni; wat beteken Meester – Johannes 20:15-16.

Maria het Jesus reguit herken toe Hy haar naam uitgespreek het. Hierdie intimiteit is gebore uit ’n passie vir Christus wat die vrug van haar bevryding was. Maria se liefde vir Jesus was die gevolg daarvan dat sy van vyf duiwels bevry is.

Jesus se primêre sending in die koms na die aarde was om ons te bevry van die mag van sonde. In Lukas 5 vertel Doktor Lukas die verhaal van ’n man wat verlam was. Hy kon nie loop nie. Sy vriende het hom gebring vir genesing, maar hulle kon nie by Jesus uitkom weens die skare nie. Toe het hulle op die dak gegaan en genoeg dakteëls weggeneem om hulle vriend deur te laat en hom in die teenwoordigheid van Jesus af te laat. Hoe vindingryk! Hoe wanhopig was hulle om hul vriend te help om genesing te vind.

En toe Hy hulle geloof sien, sê Hy tot hom: Mens, jou sondes is jou vergewe – Lukas 5:20. Hulle het genesing gesoek, maar Jesus het die dieper behoefte van hierdie man se siel gesien, daarom het Hy vergifnis aangebied. Dit het natuurlik die Fariseërs se woede opgewek wat …begin het te redeneer en te sê: Wie is hierdie wat godslasteringe praat? Wie kan sondes vergewe anders as God alleen? – Lukas 5:21. Hulle het reg gehad: slegs God kan sondes vergewe, maar wat hulle nie wou glo nie, was dat Jesus die Seun van God was en dat Hy dus die mag gehad het om sondes te vergewe. Daarom sê Jesus verder: …Wat redeneer julle in julle harte? Wat is makliker om te sê: Jou sondes is jou vergewe; of om te sê: Staan op en loop? Maar dat julle mag weet dat die Seun van die mens mag het op die aarde om sondes te vergewe, (hy sê toe tot die siek van die verlamming,) Ek sê tot jou, Staan op, neem jou bed op, en gaan na jou huis – Lukas 5:22-24.

Om Jesus te volg beteken om jou sonde te verlaat. Ons sou grootliks verkeerd wees om te sê dat heiligheid ’n produk van menslike poging is. Ons reis na heiligheid moet ’n reis na Kalvarie wees. Baie “heilige mans” en “heilige vroue” deur die eeue het gepoog om ’n heilige lewe in hulle eie krag te leef. Wat altyd gebeur, is dat ons ons tevrede stel met ’n vorm van vroomheid wat kortval van Christus se geregtigheid. Ons tevrede ons met ’n godsdiens wat moontlik is.

Die apostel Paulus, toe hy oor sy Joodse broeders skryf, het gesê: Want hulle, wat die geregtigheid van God nie ken nie en probeer om hulle eie regverdigheid te vestig, het hulle nie onderwerp aan die geregtigheid van God nie – Romeine 10:3.

Hierdie “geregtigheid van God” is ’n innerlike regverdigheid van die hart wat slegs kan voortkom deur die werk van wedergeboorte en die vernuwing van die Heilige Gees. Dit is om hierdie rede dat ons reis met Jesus ons na Kalvarie moet lei, want dit is daar dat ons ons sterwende Here aanskou—bloedend, sterwend vir ons sondes—for my sondes—for jou sondes.

Die bloed van Jesus is die enigste middel tot die “geregtigheid van God”. Die “geregtigheid van God” word toegeteken deur vergifnis, en dit is die vrug van ons lewens nadat ons deur die Heilige Gees bemagtig is. Hoe dit ook al sy, die “geregtigheid van God” word aan die werk van Christus aan die kruis toegeskryf. Daar is geen ander middel tot heiligheid nie.

In Matteus 22 het Jesus die verhaal vertel van ’n koning wat ’n huwelik vir sy seun beplan het. Toe die genooide gaste (die Joodse mense) sy uitnodiging weier, is die uitnodiging toe uitgestuur aan al die wat nie genooi was nie, en die huwelik is met gaste gevul.

Toe die koning inkom om die huwelik te beskou, was hy tevrede met wat hy sien totdat hy ’n man sien wat nie ’n huwelikskleed dra nie. (’n Huwelikskleed was ’n wit serwelingsaatklere wat deur die huisheer van die fees voorsien is.)

Ek haal Adam Clark aan: “Onder die Oos-mense is lang wit rodens by publieke feesvierings gedra; en diegene wat by sulke geleenthede met ander kleed gedra het, is nie net hoogs skuldig geag nie, maar waardig om gestraf te word. Die persoon wat die gaste uitgenooi het, het so ’n kleed vir elk voorberei, vir die tyd; en waarmee hy hulle voorsien het op hulle aansoek by die heerser van die fees. Dit was dit wat die optrede van die persoon in die teks onvergeeflik gemaak het; hy kon ’n behoorlike huwelikskleed gehad het, as hy daarvoor aansoek gedoen het.”

“Nie om ’n huwelikskleed te dra nie” was om die huisheer van die fees te beledig, wat alles voorsien het (insluitend die huwelikskleed) sodat al die gaste gelyk geskik sou wees vir die geleentheid. Niemand hoef uitgesluit te word weens gebrek aan behoorlike klere of enige ander gerief nie. Die koning het die uitnodiging en alle nodige geriewe verskaf, en die gas hoef net die uitnodiging te aanvaar en die genadige voorsiening van die koning te ontvang.

Wat ’n pragtige analogie van die Koninkryk van die Hemel. Die Koning het ons na Sy hemelse fees genooi. Hy wil hê ons moet kom en die fees saam met Hom geniet. Hy wil hê ons moet kom maak nie saak wie ons is of waarvandaan ons kom nie—sommiges uit die riole van sonde, sommige uit die dieptes van onkunde, en sommige uit die tempels van selfregverdigheid. Almal is op gelyke voet uitgenooi—Almal moet die uitnodiging aanvaar, en almal moet die huwelikskleed dra.

Ons word nie die presiese toestand van hierdie man wat die huwelikskleed geweier het vertel nie, maar ’n algemene begrip van die menslike natuur sal aandui dat hy waarskynlik ’n mooi geskikte gentleman was. Diegene wat vaal geklee gekom het sou die huwelikskleed verwelkom het om hulle ware toestand te verberg. Die waarskynlikheid is dat hierdie man sy sierlikheid wou vertoon. Hy het nie geneig gevoel om sy fyn klere te bedek met ’n eenvoudige wit mantel nie.

Dit is die toestand van almal wat op hulle eie regverdigheid vertrou. Die beste wat ons aan God kan bring, val kort van die geregtigheid wat God vereis. Jesaja het geskryf: Maar ons is almal soos ’n onrein ding, en al ons geregtighede is soos ’n besmette lap; en ons verdwyn almal soos ’n blaar; en ons ongerymdhede het ons weggevoer soos die wind – Jesaja 64:6.

In hierdie wanhopige toestand vind ons onsself in behoeftes van ’n Verlosser. God het vir ons ’n Verlosser voorsien in Sy Seun, Jesus. In Hom het ons die verlossing deur Sy bloed, die vergifnis van sondes, volgens die rykdom van Sy genade – Efesiërs 1:7. God het ons na Sy fees genooi, en Hy het vir ons alles voorsien wat nodig is sodat ons regverdig gemaak kan word.

Een kenmerk van ’n persoon wat van sonde gesuiwer is deur die bloed van Christus, is aanbidding. Lukas vertel die verhaal van ’n vrou wat “’n sondares” was en na Jesus toe gekom het om Hom te aanbid: En, kyk, ’n vrou in die stad, wat ’n sondares was, as sy gehoor het dat Jesus by ’n Fariseër aan tafel gesit het, het ’n alabasterbottel van salf gebring, En by sy voete agter Hom gaan staan en huilend begin sy sy voete met trane te was, en met die hare van haar hoof af te droog, en sy het sy voete gekus en met die salf aangewrig. En die Fariseër wat Hom genader het, het dit in homself gesê en gesê: Hierdie Man, as Hy ’n profeet was, sou Hy geweet het wie en wat vir ’n soort vrou dit is wat Hom aanraak: want sy is ’n sondares – Lukas 7:37-39.

Ons ken nie haar naam nie, net dat sy “’n sondares” was. Dit was haar reputasie—sy was ‘nie goed nie’. Maar sy het kennelik ’n vorige ontmoeting met Jesus gehad. Sy het na Simon se huis gekom om haar dankoffers te bring. Sy het die beste gebring wat sy gehad het. ’n Alabasterbottel salf wat gesê word ter waarde van ’n jaar se lone. Sy het Jesus se voete aangewrig en dit met haar trane gewas—trane van bekering, trane van vreugde, trane van verligting.

Simon het haar aanbidding waargeneem. Hy het haar in sy hart verag. Hy het haar offer as ’n groot vermorsing aangesien. Jesus het hom uitgedaag. Hy sê vir Simon: …Sien jy hierdie vrou? Ek het in jou huis ingegaan, jy het My geen water vir My voete gegee nie: maar sy het My voete met trane gewas en met die hare van haar hoof afgevee. Jy het My geen soen gegee nie: maar hierdie vrou sedert die tyd dat Ek ingekom het, het nie opgehou om My voete te soen nie. My hoof met olie het jy nie aangewrig nie: maar hierdie vrou het My voete met salf aangewrig. Daarom sê Ek tot jou, Haar sondes wat baie is, is vergewe; want sy het baie liefgehad: maar aan wie min vergewe is, die hou ook min lief – Lukas 7:44-47.

Hy sê tot die vrou: …Jou sondes is vergewe – Lukas 7:48. Vergifnis en vryheid van sonde wek die hart tot aanbidding. Wanneer ’n man of vrou van die skuld en band van sonde vrygestel word, vloei lof spontaan. Simon was ’n Fariseër wat op sy eie regverdigheid vertrou het. Tog het Jesus hom tot die bewustheid gebring dat hy grootliks gebrek aan liefde en aanbidding gehad het.

Om Jesus te volg sal ons lei tot die heiligheid van hart en lewe. Om Jesus te volg bring ons gesig na gesig met die oorsaak en die genesing van die sondeprobleem. Die oorsaak van sonde is ons gevalle vleeslike natuur, en ons gevalle natuur word aan die lig van Sy heiligheid openbaar. Saam met Maria Magdalena en die ander dissipels, soos ons met Jesus reis, word ons bewus van ons behoefte en ons behoefte roep uit vir Sy genade. Die genesing van ons sonde is Jesus—…jy sal sy naam noem JESUS: want Hy sal sy volk red van hulle sondes – Matteus 1:21.

In Augustus Toplady se bekende lied, Rock of Ages, vind ons hierdie reël–

Wees die dubbele geneesmiddel van sonde; red my van sy skuld (deur vergifnis) en mag (deur heiligmaking).

“Dr. Waldron,” the lady sitting across from me said. “I have been struggling a lot lately.”

“Tell me what’s going on,” I said.

“I don’t know how to explain it,” she hesitated… “I just feel tired most of the time. I can’t concentrate anymore, and I just don’t enjoy most of the things that I used to enjoy. I’m getting through my days, but that’s about it. Do you think I have a thyroid problem or am low in some mineral or vitamin?”

“That could be,” I told her. “We can certainly check those things, but I think something else is going on here.”

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

I am a family doctor and probably thirty percent of the people who come to my office to see me have symptoms of depression. This doesn’t mean that they are on medication for it or feel that they need special help, but it does say that these symptoms are widespread in our world.

Even in Christian circles, surveys indicate that about 15 percent of Christians self-report having been diagnosed with depression at some point in their life. This is 25 percent lower than in society as a whole, but it is still higher than we would like to believe.

In the very beginning, God created the world and Adam and Eve. And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31. Before the Fall, everything was perfect.

I don’t think we know entirely what this meant. Obviously, there were no physical diseases or maladies to afflict either the humans or the flora and fauna of Eden. More than that, Adam and Eve didn’t suffer from anxiety or depression. Their hormones didn’t get out of balance, they didn’t get stressed out (even if there could have been stress in a perfect garden), and they wouldn’t have gotten upset or angry at any point.

Everything changed with Adam and Eve sinning. We see this in the tension between them after they ate the fruit with Adam blaming Eve, and Eve blaming the snake. And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat –Genesis 3:12-13.

Feeding a family suddenly became hard work. Viruses and bacteria became pathogenic and at some point, in the first families, people would have begun to struggle with emotional and mental health challenges.

Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:16-19.

I would like to explore what depression is as defined by the medical world, some of the sources of it, and then discuss how we can deal with it, both in our own lives and in the lives of our friends and family.

Diagnosing Depression

As mentioned earlier, many people have some symptoms of depression. They may feel more fatigued, cry easily, or have other symptoms that aren’t usual for them. Most of them do not actually have true clinical depression.

Most people do not have all of these symptoms, but when they are continually present without dissipating for two weeks or more, especially if they are strong enough to hinder normal day-to-day responsibilities or the ability to get proper rest, then it is time to do something.

It is important to remember that there is a large or broad continuum regarding depression. Some people have mild discouragement, some have deep feelings of sadness, and some have enough depression that they are at risk to cause harm to themselves or others.

Causes of Depression

There are different examples of people in the Bible who seem to have exhibited symptoms consistent with depression. Two of them stand out to me.

First is Naomi. We know that she went with her husband and her two sons to Moab because of a famine that was affecting southern Israel. She spent ten years in this foreign land and during that time, her husband and both of her sons died.

The book of Ruth tells us that when she returned to Bethlehem, she said to the people, …Call me not Naomi [pleasant], call me Mara [bitter]: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the LORD hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me? –Ruth 1:20-21.

There is no way to interview Naomi and find out all the things that she was feeling, but this seems to be more than simple grief. She had lost all the things that were of value to her, and to her it seemed that even God had turned against her.

As we read the story of Ruth, we see that things did improve for her throughout the book—mostly through the ministry of her daughter-in-law, Ruth, but also, through God gradually restoring things of value back into her life, and through others encouraging her in the Lord’s goodness. And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel. And he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him. And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it –Ruth 4:14-16.

Another one that comes to mind is the Prophet Jeremiah. Jeremiah was called when he was a young man, and he had a very long career speaking God’s Word to a group of kings and other people who simply weren’t interested in what he had to say.

Jeremiah’s life was constantly under threat. At one time, he was thrown into a dungeon full of mud and was only rescued at the last minute. Jerusalem was besieged three different times before the Babylonians razed it. Through his decades of ministry, Jeremiah told the people what God was asking of them, and the people constantly ignored it.

Perhaps it is no wonder that Jeremiah is known today as the weeping prophet. He said, Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed. Cursed be the man who brought tidings to my father, saying, A man child is born unto thee; making him very glad. And let that man be as the cities which the LORD overthrew, and repented not: and let him hear the cry in the morning, and the shouting at noontide … Wherefore came I forth out of the womb to see labour and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame? –Jeremiah 20:14-18.

It is important to note that in both of these examples from the Bible, sin is not revealed to be the issue (or the reason) that pushed these people into depression. For Naomi it was probably a mixture of isolation from her homeland and loss of people she loved dearly. For Jeremiah, it was the constant stress of trying to serve God in a nation that didn’t care about God.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Depression is always multi-factorial. That is to say, there are usually a mixture of internal and external factors that break a person down.

There are genetic and hormonal components that come into play here. There is no doubt that some individuals and some families are more prone to depression than others. It is thought by many doctors and researchers that changes in genes which transport the chemical, Serotonin, through the brain can make some people more susceptible to depression than others.

These differences in genetic makeup can help us understand why some people require very little stress to bring them down, while others seem very resilient. Since we can’t change our genetic makeup, there is no sense gloating if we have a more upbeat personality than someone else. And, if we recognize that we have a greater tendency towards depression, we don’t need to feel discouraged by this fact. If God created us in such a way that we tend towards being moody instead of being naturally upbeat, we need to use wisdom in doing what we can to manage as many external factors as we can so as to minimize the risk of debilitating (extreme) depression.

External stressors are often the thing that triggers these sorts of feelings (discouragement). It can be the death of a close friend or family member, or it can be a financial misfortune. It is important to remember that even good events can produce large amounts of stress. Mothers with newborns are often functioning on very little sleep, even while they have large physical changes taking place in their bodies.

Some people may have poor coping skills. Unfortunately, many turn to street drugs or alcohol to try to smother the feelings that they can’t control otherwise.

As a final thing, sin and guilt can trigger depression or make it worse. We can see this present in David and Saul’s lives. (See Psalm chapter 32) This is not to say that all depression is the result of sin—far from it—but sin needs to be dealt with, and repented of, in order to move forward.

Perhaps as a side note, I will mention that in my experience, deeply depressed people often struggle with horrible guilt. They don’t even know what sin they might have committed; they are only certain that God is angry with them, and they must have done something wrong. Fixing the depression will help with the assurance of salvation issues that these people tend to deal with.

This leaves us with the question of how to help someone who is dealing with this sort of thinking.

Listen

Listening is a powerful tool for helping other people. Listen actively and without jumping in to interrupt negative thinking.

You may be able to see that all is not terrible and that there is much positive in the world. The fact that they can’t see these things has more to do with their mindset than with how terrible things really are. A person struggling with depression may know that there are people worse off in the world, but it doesn’t really help them much to point that out to them.

Encourage

Encouragement can simply be saying good things that you see in the life of the person who is struggling. This is something that all of us need more of.

More than this, we need to encourage people to do things that are healthy for themselves. They need to get out of their home, they should try to exercise, and they should make an attempt to eat healthy. We can help them do better in all of these areas. (See Galatians 6:2)

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

These people need someone to pray with them. They need someone to pray for them. Jesus asks us to pray in secret, but it is also really encouraging for someone who is struggling to hear themselves being prayed for. This helps them to know that there are many people who are lifting them up with prayer support.

Be Willing to be the Initiator

People with depression have very low energy levels. Beyond that, they don’t see themselves as having any value. At least such that someone else would want to spend time with them. They aren’t going to call or text, and they certainly won’t set up a lunch meeting or prayer time.

Even though they crave all of these things, it is just really difficult for them to take the first step to reach out to others. It therefore falls to the rest of us to be willing to do those things.

Don’t Jump to Conclusions

We know the story of Job’s friends. They rode up to see Job after disaster fell on him and sat quietly in shock for several days upon seeing the devastation that had happened to him. When they finally began to speak, it was to judge him for the terrible sin they assumed he had committed.

It isn’t wrong to ask about sin, but there are plenty of times where depression isn’t sin-related. Focusing in on sin prematurely, or if it is assumed, will simply drive wedges that will make it less likely that you can help a person find healing.

What if you are the person struggling with depression? How should you deal with it and what things can help?

Deal With Issues Early

Everyone has moments when they are stressed out and really discouraged. We use terms like “burn-out” and “compassion fatigue” in the medical field when people are heading in the wrong direction. These struggles manifest themselves when we are being irritable with the people around us, when we’re feeling tired most of the time, or when we’re feeling discouraged most of the time. When we see that these symptoms are popping up, it is time to do something to keep things from getting worse.

Maybe a first step is simply knowing our limitations. There are times where we will simply need to say no to work projects or even to church activities because it doesn’t leave us sufficient time to rest. Certain times of the year could be worse—many people struggle more during the winter months because of less sunlight.

Cutting back in whatever areas we can is important when we see that we are on the wrong trajectory.

Don’t Do Comparisons

Everyone is different. Identifying people who seem to “have it altogether” when you are struggling doesn’t help you and it probably will make you feel worse.

Struggling with discouragement does not mean that you aren’t a Christian or that God is done with you. It means that you are human living in a fallen world. You don’t want to continue to live with a depressed spirit, but neither should you believe that you are the only one who has dealt with this. (See 2 Corinthians 10:12)

Exercise

Cardiovascular exercise is really important to boost the chemicals in the brain that are associated with depression. It doesn’t really matter what type of exercise you do. What does matter, is that it increases your heart rate 25 to 30 percent above your baseline heart rate.

Exercise is something that is hard to do, even when you aren’t dealing with depression. It is particularly hard when you are fatigued and feeling down.

Spend Time with Encouragers

People need community. When we are dealing with depressive feelings, we really need other people around to lift us up, to pray with us, and to give us encouragement. None of us is better from spending extended times alone. (See Proverbs 27:17)

Deal with Sin

Sin can make prayer feel ineffective. That isn’t to say that simply confessing sin will suddenly make someone’s depression lift, but it is an important part of reaching healing. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed… –James 5:16.

Be Willing to Take Medication

Not everyone needs medication. The hope is that if you do the right (helpful) things (some of which are listed above), you can keep things from getting bad enough that you would need medical help. But there are plenty of situations where someone simply needs to start on some medication in order to aid them in a number of ways: to sleep, to rest a weary mind that will not stop, to dull the emotional pain, etc.

People with severe enough depression may be a risk to themselves. They may even be completely unable to respond to counseling or any of the other non-medical treatments for these feelings. These people really need to start on medication with the goal to transition off of those medications down the road when they are thinking clearly enough to continue on the right path.

Unfortunately, the benefits of these medications seem to be short-lived. Long-term use of antidepressant medications really does not seem to improve quality of life for many patients. A recent study looked at patients who took antidepressant medications and compared them to those who did not and found similar levels of health-related quality of life in the two groups. In other words, when comparing two groups of depressed patients, with the one group taking medication and the other group not, after a period of time (approximately 6 months) there were no longer any observable differences in their depression levels. So, while these medications may help to stabilize a person who has severe depression, after a period of time the actual medical “help” of the medication starts to diminish. Hopefully, by this time, the person will be stable enough that a safe taper can be taken towards weaning off the medication.

With this in mind, it is very important to do things other than medication to attempt to improve the situation.

Continue, Even When You Feel Better

Many times, when someone has a medical issue, they will consciously change their diet and lifestyle to improve their situation. The problem is that when the symptoms get better, the tendency is to fall back into old eating and behavioral patterns.

If you have dealt with depression in the past, it is important that you continue a path of healthy choices. Exercise regularly, eat healthy meals, manage your stress level (as much as you can), don’t over-schedule, and make a conscious effort to meet regularly with godly friends for times of prayer and support.

Periodically take an inventory of how you are doing. If you are struggling, figure out what you are going to change to make things better.

Depression is very common in our society and in our churches. We can have victory over it alone, but with God’s help and with the support of Christian brothers and sisters, we can move forward.

You may not be gloriously happy all of the time, but by God’s grace, you will have the joy of the Lord in your heart, even on the most stressful days.

“Dr. Waldron,” kata wanita yang duduk di hadapan saya. “Akhir-akhir ini saya banyak berjuang.”

“Ceritakan apa yang sedang terjadi,” saya berkata.

“Saya tidak tahu bagaimana menjelaskannya,” dia ragu… “Saya hanya merasa lelah sepanjang waktu. Saya tak lagi bisa berkonsentrasi, dan saya tak lagi menikmati sebagian besar hal yang dulu saya nikmati. Saya menjalani hari-hari saya, tetapi itu saja. Menurut Anda apakah saya punya masalah tiroid atau kekurangan mineral atau vitamin?”

“Bisa saja,” jawab saya. “Kita tentu bisa memeriksa hal-hal itu, tetapi saya pikir ada sesuatu yang lain terjadi di sini.”

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Saya seorang dokter keluarga dan mungkin tiga puluh persen orang yang datang ke kantor saya untuk menemui saya memiliki gejala depresi. Ini tidak berarti bahwa mereka sedang mengonsumsi obat untuk itu atau merasa perlu bantuan khusus, tetapi ini menunjukkan bahwa gejala-gejala ini tersebar luas di dunia kita.

Bahkan di lingkaran Kristen, survei menunjukkan bahwa sekitar 15 persen orang Kristen melaporkan diri pernah didiagnosis dengan depresi pada suatu titik dalam hidup mereka. Ini 25 persen lebih rendah dibandingkan masyarakat secara keseluruhan, tetapi tetap lebih tinggi daripada yang ingin kita akui.

Pada mulanya, Allah menciptakan dunia dan Adam serta Hawa. Dan Allah melihat segala sesuatu yang telah dibuat-Nya, dan lihatlah, itu sangat baik… –Kejadian 1:31. Sebelum Kejatuhan, segala sesuatu sempurna.

Saya tidak berpikir kita sepenuhnya tahu apa arti hal ini. Jelas, tidak ada penyakit fisik atau kelaziman yang menyerang manusia maupun flora dan fauna taman Eden. Lebih dari itu, Adam dan Hawa tidak menderita kecemasan atau depresi. Hormon mereka tidak terganggu, mereka tidak stres (meskipun mungkin ada tekanan dalam taman yang sempurna), dan mereka tidak akan marah atau tersinggung pada titik manapun.

Semuanya berubah ketika Adam dan Hawa berbuat dosa. Kita melihat ini dalam ketegangan antara mereka setelah mereka memakan buah itu, dengan Adam menyalahkan Hawa, dan Hawa menyalahkan ular. Dan manusia berkata, Perempuan yang Engkau taruhkan bersama-sama dengan aku, dialah yang memberikan dari pohon itu kepadaku, maka aku makan. Lalu berkatalah TUHAN Allah kepada perempuan itu, Apakah yang telah engkau perbuat itu? Dan perempuan itu menjawab, Ular itu menipu aku, maka aku makan –Kejadian 3:12-13.

Mencari nafkah untuk keluarga tiba-tiba menjadi pekerjaan yang sulit. Virus dan bakteri menjadi patogen dan pada suatu saat, dalam keluarga-keluarga pertama, orang akan mulai bergumul dengan tantangan kesehatan emosional dan mental.

Kepada perempuan itu ia berfirman: Aku akan sungguh-sungguh memperbanyak kesengsaraanmu dan anak-anak yang akan kaulahirkan; dengan kesakitan engkau akan bersalin anak-anak; dan kepadamu akanlah cenderung nafsu suamimu, tetapi ia akan berkuasa atasmu. Kepada Adam ia berfirman: Karena engkau mendengarkan suara istrimu, dan makan dari pohon yang telah Kuperintahkan kepadamu, mengatakan: Jangan makan dari padanya; maka terkutuklah tanah karena sebabmu; dengan susah payah engkau akan mencari rezekimu dari tanah seumur hidupmu; semak duri dan rumput berduri akan dihasilkannya bagimu, dan engkau akan makan tumbuhan di padang; dengan peluh mukamu engkau akan makan roti, sampai engkau kembali menjadi tanah, karena dari situlah engkau diambil: sebab engkau debu dan engkau akan kembali menjadi debu –Kejadian 3:16-19.

Saya ingin mengeksplorasi apa itu depresi sebagaimana didefinisikan oleh dunia medis, beberapa sumbernya, dan kemudian membahas bagaimana kita dapat menghadapinya, baik dalam kehidupan kita sendiri maupun dalam kehidupan teman dan keluarga kita.

Mendiagnosis Depresi

Seperti disebutkan sebelumnya, banyak orang memiliki beberapa gejala depresi. Mereka mungkin merasa lebih lelah, mudah menangis, atau memiliki gejala lain yang tidak biasa bagi mereka. Sebagian besar dari mereka sebenarnya tidak menderita depresi klinis sejati.

Kebanyakan orang tidak memiliki semua gejala ini, tetapi ketika gejala-gejala tersebut terus hadir tanpa mereda selama dua minggu atau lebih, terutama jika cukup kuat hingga menghambat tanggung jawab sehari-hari atau kemampuan untuk mendapatkan istirahat yang layak, maka saatnya melakukan sesuatu.

Penting untuk diingat bahwa terdapat spektrum yang luas mengenai depresi. Beberapa orang mengalami kekecewaan ringan, beberapa mengalami perasaan sedih yang mendalam, dan beberapa mengalami depresi yang cukup parah sehingga berisiko membahayakan diri sendiri atau orang lain.

Penyebab Depresi

Ada berbagai contoh orang dalam Alkitab yang tampaknya menunjukkan gejala yang konsisten dengan depresi. Dua di antaranya menonjol bagi saya.

Pertama adalah Naomi. Kita tahu bahwa ia pergi bersama suaminya dan kedua putranya ke Moab karena kelaparan yang melanda selatan Israel. Ia menghabiskan sepuluh tahun di negeri asing itu dan selama waktu itu, suaminya dan kedua putranya meninggal.

Kitab Rut memberi tahu kita bahwa ketika ia kembali ke Betlehem, ia berkata kepada orang-orang, …Janganlah kamu memanggil aku Naomi [manis], tetapi panggillah aku Mara [pahit]: sebab Yang Mahakuasa telah memperlakukan aku dengan sangat pahit. Aku dahulu pergi penuh, tetapi TUHAN telah membawa aku pulang dengan kosong: mengapa kamu memanggil aku Naomi, padahal TUHAN telah bersaksi melawan aku, dan Yang Mahakuasa telah mencela aku? –Rut 1:20-21.

Tidak mungkin mewawancarai Naomi dan mengetahui semua yang ia rasakan, tetapi ini tampak lebih dari sekadar duka sederhana. Ia telah kehilangan semua hal yang bernilai baginya, dan baginya tampak seolah-olah bahkan Allah pun telah berpaling darinya.

Saat kita membaca kisah Rut, kita melihat bahwa keadaan membaik baginya sepanjang kitab itu—sebagian besar melalui pelayanan menantunya, Rut, tetapi juga melalui pemulihan bertahap oleh Allah atas hal-hal bernilai dalam hidupnya, dan melalui dorongan orang lain tentang kebaikan Tuhan. Dan perempuan-perempuan berkata kepada Naomi: Terpujilah TUHAN, yang tidak membiarkan engkau hari ini tanpa orang yang berkeluarga, supaya namanya disebut dalam Israel. Dialah penolong hidupmu dan pemelihara hari tua kaubarang: sebab menantumu, yang mengasihi engkau dan yang lebih baik bagimu dari pada tujuh orang anak laki-laki, telah melahirkannya. Lalu Naomi mengambil anak itu dan meletakkannya di pangkuannya dan menjadi pengasuh baginya –Rut 4:14-16.

Satu lagi yang terlintas dalam pikiran saya adalah Nabi Yeremia. Yeremia dipanggil ketika ia masih muda, dan ia memiliki karier yang sangat panjang menyampaikan firman Allah kepada sekelompok raja dan orang lain yang tampaknya tidak tertarik dengan apa yang ia katakan.

Hidup Yeremia selalu dalam ancaman. Pada suatu waktu, ia dilemparkan ke dalam penjara yang penuh lumpur dan hanya diselamatkan pada menit terakhir. Yerusalem diserang tiga kali berbeda sebelum orang Babel meratakannya. Sepanjang puluhan tahun pelayanannya, Yeremia memberitahu bangsa itu apa yang Allah kehendaki dari mereka, dan bangsa itu terus-menerus mengabaikannya.

Mungkin tidaklah mengherankan bahwa Yeremia dikenal hari ini sebagai nabi yang menangis. Ia berkata, Terkutuklah hari ketika aku dilahirkan: biarlah hari ketika ibuku melahirkanku tidak diberkati. Terkutuklah orang yang memberi kabar kepada ayahku, mengatakan: Seorang anak lelaki telah lahir kepadamu; ia telah membuatnya sangat bersukacita. Biarlah orang itu menjadi seperti kota-kota yang TUHAN telah musnahkan, dan tidak bertobat: biarlah ia mendengar ratapan pada pagi hari dan sorak-sorai pada tengah hari … Untuk apa aku keluar dari kandungan untuk melihat kerja dan dukacita, supaya hari-hariku habis dengan kehinaan? –Yeremia 20:14-18.

Penting dicatat bahwa dalam kedua contoh dari Alkitab ini, dosa tidak diungkapkan sebagai masalah (atau alasan) yang mendorong orang-orang ini ke dalam depresi. Bagi Naomi kemungkinan besar merupakan campuran antara keterasingan dari tanah airnya dan kehilangan orang-orang yang sangat dicintainya. Bagi Yeremia, itu adalah tekanan konstan dalam berusaha melayani Allah di sebuah bangsa yang tidak peduli kepada Allah.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Depresi selalu bersifat multifaktorial. Artinya, biasanya ada campuran faktor internal dan eksternal yang meruntuhkan seseorang.

Ada komponen genetik dan hormonal yang berperan di sini. Tidak diragukan bahwa beberapa individu dan beberapa keluarga lebih rentan terhadap depresi daripada yang lain. Banyak dokter dan peneliti berpendapat bahwa perubahan gen yang mentranspor zat kimia, Serotonin, melalui otak dapat membuat beberapa orang lebih rentan terhadap depresi dibandingkan yang lain.

Perbedaan dalam susunan genetik ini dapat membantu kita memahami mengapa beberapa orang memerlukan sedikit tekanan untuk menjatuhkan mereka, sementara yang lain tampak sangat tangguh. Karena kita tidak dapat mengubah susunan genetik kita, tidak ada gunanya bersombong jika kita memiliki kepribadian yang lebih ceria daripada orang lain. Dan, jika kita menyadari bahwa kita memiliki kecenderungan lebih besar terhadap depresi, kita tidak perlu berkecil hati oleh fakta ini. Jika Allah menciptakan kita sedemikian rupa sehingga kita cenderung moody daripada ceria secara alami, kita perlu menggunakan hikmat dalam melakukan apa yang kita bisa untuk mengelola sebanyak mungkin faktor eksternal agar meminimalkan risiko depresi yang melemahkan (ekstrem).

Pemicu eksternal sering kali adalah hal yang memicu perasaan semacam ini (kecewa). Bisa berupa kematian teman atau anggota keluarga yang dekat, atau bisa pula sebuah kemalangan finansial. Penting untuk diingat bahwa bahkan peristiwa baik dapat menimbulkan stres dalam jumlah besar. Ibu-ibu dengan bayi baru sering kali berfungsi dengan sangat sedikit tidur, sekalipun mereka mengalami banyak perubahan fisik dalam tubuh mereka.

Beberapa orang mungkin memiliki keterampilan koping yang buruk. Sayangnya, banyak yang beralih ke obat jalanan atau alkohol untuk mencoba menenggelamkan perasaan yang tidak bisa mereka kontrol dengan cara lain.

Sebagai hal terakhir, dosa dan rasa bersalah dapat memicu depresi atau memperburuknya. Kita dapat melihat ini hadir dalam kehidupan Daud dan Saul. (Lihat Mazmur pasal 32) Ini bukan berarti semua depresi merupakan akibat dosa—jauh dari itu—tetapi dosa perlu ditangani, dan bertobat, agar dapat melangkah maju.

Mungkin sebagai catatan sampingan, saya akan menyebutkan bahwa menurut pengalaman saya, orang yang sangat tertekan sering bergumul dengan rasa bersalah yang mengerikan. Mereka bahkan tidak tahu dosa apa yang mungkin telah mereka lakukan; mereka hanya yakin bahwa Allah murka kepada mereka, dan mereka pasti telah berbuat salah. Memperbaiki depresi akan membantu dalam masalah kepastian keselamatan yang cenderung dihadapi orang-orang ini.

Ini menyisakan pertanyaan bagaimana membantu seseorang yang bergumul dengan pola pikir semacam ini.

Mendengarkan

Mendengarkan adalah alat yang ampuh untuk membantu orang lain. Dengarkan secara aktif dan tanpa langsung memotong pikiran negatif mereka.

Anda mungkin bisa melihat bahwa segala sesuatu tidak seburuk itu dan bahwa ada banyak hal positif di dunia. Fakta bahwa mereka tidak dapat melihat hal-hal ini lebih berkaitan dengan pola pikir mereka daripada betapa buruknya keadaan sebenarnya. Seseorang yang bergumul dengan depresi mungkin tahu ada orang yang lebih sengsara di dunia, tetapi itu tidak banyak membantu jika Anda menunjukkannya kepada mereka.

Mendorong

Dorongan bisa sekadar mengatakan hal-hal baik yang Anda lihat dalam hidup orang yang bergumul. Ini adalah sesuatu yang kita semua butuhkan lebih banyak.

Lebih dari itu, kita perlu mendorong orang melakukan hal-hal yang sehat bagi diri mereka sendiri. Mereka perlu keluar dari rumah, mereka harus mencoba berolahraga, dan mereka harus berusaha makan sehat. Kita dapat membantu mereka menjadi lebih baik dalam semua bidang ini. (Lihat Galatia 6:2)

Berdoa

…Doa orang benar, bila dengan yakin didoakan, sangat besar kuasanya –Yakobus 5:16.

Orang-orang ini membutuhkan seseorang yang berdoa bersama mereka. Mereka membutuhkan seseorang yang mendoakan mereka. Yesus meminta kita berdoa secara diam-diam, tetapi juga sangat menguatkan bagi orang yang bergumul untuk mendengar doa yang dipanjatkan bagi dirinya. Ini membantu mereka mengetahui bahwa ada banyak orang yang mengangkat mereka dengan dukungan doa.

Berani Mengambil Inisiatif

Orang dengan depresi memiliki tingkat energi yang sangat rendah. Selain itu, mereka tidak melihat diri mereka memiliki nilai. Setidaknya tidak sampai orang lain mau menghabiskan waktu bersama mereka. Mereka tidak akan menelepon atau mengirim pesan, dan tentu tidak akan mengatur pertemuan makan siang atau waktu doa.

Walaupun mereka merindukan semua hal ini, sangat sulit bagi mereka untuk mengambil langkah pertama menjangkau orang lain. Oleh karena itu menjadi tanggung jawab kita yang lain untuk bersedia melakukan hal-hal tersebut.

Jangan Cepat Menyimpulkan

Kita tahu kisah teman-teman Ayub. Mereka datang untuk melihat Ayub setelah bencana menimpanya dan duduk diam terpana beberapa hari ketika melihat kehancuran yang menimpa dia. Ketika akhirnya mereka mulai berbicara, itu adalah untuk menghakimi dia atas dosa besar yang mereka anggap telah dilakukannya.

Tidak salah menanyakan tentang dosa, tetapi ada banyak kali di mana depresi tidak terkait dosa. Fokus pada dosa terlalu dini, atau jika itu diasumsikan, hanya akan menciptakan jurang yang membuat Anda kurang mungkin dapat membantu seseorang menemukan penyembuhan.

Bagaimana jika Anda sendiri orang yang bergumul dengan depresi? Bagaimana Anda harus mengatasinya dan hal-hal apa yang dapat membantu?

Menangani Masalah Sejak Dini

Setiap orang memiliki momen ketika mereka stres dan sangat kecewa. Kami menggunakan istilah seperti “kelelahan” dan “kelelahan kasih” di bidang medis ketika orang bergerak ke arah yang salah. Pergumulan ini muncul ketika kita menjadi mudah tersinggung dengan orang di sekitar kita, ketika kita merasa lelah sepanjang waktu, atau ketika kita merasa kecewa sepanjang waktu. Ketika kita melihat gejala-gejala ini muncul, saatnya melakukan sesuatu agar tidak menjadi lebih buruk.

Mungkin langkah pertama hanyalah mengetahui keterbatasan kita. Ada saat-saat di mana kita harus berkata tidak pada proyek kerja atau bahkan kegiatan gereja karena hal itu tidak memberi kita waktu istirahat yang cukup. Waktu tertentu dalam setahun bisa lebih buruk—banyak orang bergumul lebih banyak selama bulan-bulan musim dingin karena sinar matahari yang lebih sedikit.

Mengurangi beban di area mana pun yang kita bisa penting ketika kita melihat bahwa kita berada pada lintasan yang salah.

Jangan Membandingkan

Setiap orang berbeda. Mengidentifikasi orang yang tampak “sempurna” saat Anda sedang bergumul tidak membantu Anda dan kemungkinan besar akan membuat Anda merasa lebih buruk.

Bergumul dengan kekecewaan bukan berarti Anda bukan seorang Kristen atau bahwa Allah telah berhenti mengasihi Anda. Itu berarti Anda manusia yang hidup di dunia yang telah jatuh. Anda tidak ingin terus hidup dengan semangat yang tertekan, tetapi Anda juga jangan percaya bahwa hanya Anda satu-satunya yang menghadapi ini. (Lihat 2 Korintus 10:12)

Berolahraga

Latihan kardiovaskular sangat penting untuk meningkatkan zat kimia di otak yang terkait dengan depresi. Tidak terlalu penting jenis olahraga apa yang Anda lakukan. Yang penting adalah peningkatan denyut jantung Anda sebesar 25 hingga 30 persen di atas denyut jantung dasar Anda.

Olahraga adalah sesuatu yang sulit dilakukan, bahkan ketika Anda tidak bergumul dengan depresi. Ini sangat sulit ketika Anda merasa lelah dan sedih.

Habiskan Waktu dengan Orang-Orang yang Memberi Semangat

Manusia membutuhkan komunitas. Ketika kita bergumul dengan perasaan depresi, kita sangat membutuhkan orang lain di sekitar untuk mengangkat kita, berdoa bersama kita, dan memberi dorongan. Tidak ada dari kita yang diuntungkan dengan menghabiskan waktu berlama-lama sendirian. (Lihat Amsal 27:17)

Menangani Dosa

Dosa dapat membuat doa terasa tidak efektif. Itu bukan berarti sekadar mengaku dosa akan tiba-tiba mengangkat depresi seseorang, tetapi itu adalah bagian penting dari mencapai penyembuhan. Aku tidak tahan lagi, aku harus mengaku dosa-dosaku kepadamu; aku akan menyatakan pelanggaranku terhadap-Mu, maka engkau mengampuni kesalahan orang berdosa –Yakobus 5:16.

Bersedia Mengonsumsi Obat

Tidak semua orang membutuhkan obat. Harapannya adalah jika Anda melakukan hal-hal yang benar (yang membantu) (beberapa tercantum di atas), Anda dapat mencegah keadaan menjadi cukup buruk sehingga Anda memerlukan bantuan medis. Tetapi ada banyak situasi di mana seseorang memang perlu mulai mengonsumsi obat untuk membantu mereka dalam sejumlah cara: tidur, menenangkan pikiran yang lelah yang tak berhenti, meredakan rasa sakit emosional, dll.

Orang dengan depresi yang cukup parah mungkin berisiko membahayakan diri sendiri. Mereka mungkin bahkan benar-benar tidak mampu merespons konseling atau perawatan non-medis lainnya untuk perasaan ini. Orang-orang ini benar-benar perlu memulai pengobatan dengan tujuan beralih dari obat-obatan tersebut nanti ketika mereka cukup jernih untuk melanjutkan ke jalan yang benar.

Sayangnya, manfaat obat-obatan ini tampaknya bersifat sementara. Penggunaan jangka panjang obat antidepresan memang tampaknya tidak meningkatkan kualitas hidup bagi banyak pasien. Sebuah studi baru-baru ini meneliti pasien yang menggunakan obat antidepresan dan membandingkannya dengan mereka yang tidak, dan menemukan tingkat kualitas hidup terkait kesehatan yang serupa di kedua kelompok. Dengan kata lain, ketika membandingkan dua kelompok pasien depresi—satu kelompok mengonsumsi obat dan kelompok lain tidak—setelah jangka waktu tertentu (sekitar 6 bulan) tidak lagi ada perbedaan yang dapat diamati dalam tingkat depresi mereka. Jadi, meskipun obat-obatan ini dapat membantu menstabilkan seseorang yang mengalami depresi berat, setelah beberapa waktu manfaat medis aktual dari obat tersebut mulai berkurang. Mudah-mudahan, pada saat ini, orang tersebut cukup stabil sehingga dapat dilakukan penurunan dosis yang aman untuk menghentikan penggunaan obat.

Dengan hal ini dalam pikiran, sangat penting melakukan hal-hal selain obat untuk berusaha memperbaiki situasi.

Lanjutkan, Bahkan Saat Anda Merasa Lebih Baik

Seringkali, ketika seseorang memiliki masalah medis, mereka akan secara sadar mengubah pola makan dan gaya hidup untuk memperbaiki keadaan mereka. Masalahnya adalah ketika gejala membaik, kecenderungan adalah kembali ke pola makan dan perilaku lama.

Jika Anda pernah berurusan dengan depresi di masa lalu, penting untuk melanjutkan jalur pilihan sehat. Berolahragalah secara teratur, makan makanan sehat, kelola tingkat stres Anda (sejauh yang Anda bisa), jangan menjadwalkan terlalu penuh, dan lakukan upaya sadar untuk bertemu secara teratur dengan teman-teman saleh untuk saat-saat doa dan dukungan.

Secara berkala lakukan pemeriksaan terhadap bagaimana keadaan Anda. Jika Anda bergumul, cari tahu apa yang akan Anda ubah untuk membuat keadaan membaik.

Depresi sangat umum dalam masyarakat dan gereja kita. Kita dapat memperoleh kemenangan atasnya sendiri, tetapi dengan pertolongan Allah dan dukungan saudara-saudari Kristen, kita dapat maju.

Anda mungkin tidak akan bahagia sepanjang waktu secara gemilang, tetapi oleh kasih karunia Allah, Anda akan memiliki sukacita Tuhan dalam hati, bahkan pada hari-hari yang paling penuh tekanan.

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb –Exodus 3:1.

The back side of the desert has long been understood as God’s school wherewith He has instructed many of His servants, of whom Moses stands chief. At the prime age of 40, he found himself …learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel –Acts 7:22-23.

I have no doubt that God can, and does, use men of great ability, capacity, and training, but spiritual leadership requires an ingredient that is not derived from doing, attaining, and accomplishing. The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh. This pride and restlessness is not dealt with in a seminary nor is it normally exterminated during vigilant duty. For many of God’s servants, it is extracted from the soul on the soil of deserted sands. This arid and abandoned acreage that appears void of life and fruitfulness is where many servants learn to put their face in the dust and yield to what may seem to be inactivity, unfruitfulness, and rejection.

Moses’ life could be divided into three sections. He spent his first forty years learning the wisdom of Egypt, the next forty as a shepherd in Midian, and a final forty as the shepherd of Israel. We can imagine that the first third of his pilgrimage was filled with tremendous activity, advancement, and accomplishment. It had undoubtedly been rehearsed to him that at his birth he …was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months –Acts 7:20.

The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter would serve to confirm that he was destined to be an instrument of God’s divine orchestration. As a centerpiece of national attention, it is certainly understandable how this man who …was mighty in words and in deeds –Acts 7:22, was brimming with self-confidence in his ability to accomplish God’s bidding.

In today’s economy, Moses would be esteemed as the ideal candidate for church leadership. He was in every way qualified. He stood above his countrymen in education, and he possessed above-normal natural, financial, and spiritual endowments. He had emerged from the “University” of Egypt as a man mighty in word and deed and he had an obvious call from God upon his life. He was a conservative man who chose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25.

Still, amidst all his fine credentials he was yet deficient for the work that God had called him to. And so, God conveniently conducted him into the land of Midian to enroll him in another school to feed upon the bitter herbs of disappointment and rejection, obscurity and loneliness, and unfulfilled dreams and longings. While it was his earlier ambition to voluntarily align himself with the people of God, this chapter of his life was enacted by compulsion.

We learn from the account in Exodus that the latter third of his life was loaded with intricate involvement and major ministry. While the exit from Egypt is an exciting read and provides great insight, most of us cannot honestly relate to the mighty Moses and his dynamic coalition with God. Rather, it is the uneventful 40-year mid-section of his life that many of us find ourselves in. Though there are but a few dozen verses that represent these four decades of his life, we assume that it was a thorough schooling that inscribed immense patience, soul searching, and perhaps a bit of frustration.

For us, it represents a period when the parched sands of time about us seem to be producing nothing more fruitful than a revelation of our dry, crusty heart—shriveled and wasted by the consequences of our failures and past sins. It is at these times that we can have a lapse in faith, not that we blame God for our circumstances, but that we may begin to see our lives as futile, and that each day is the same as the previous one. Perhaps we begin to walk around in a visionless stupor—through a fog of spiritual depression—as we grope for encouragement and a reminder that God has not forgotten us. At times, it even seems that our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over. During extended times of trials and testing, we can feel abandoned. We can even imagine that God has turned against us. We look up to Heaven and ask, “Why Lord?” We will never experience rejection and being forsaken to the extent that the Lord Jesus did, but when we experience them in our petty little realm, it seems to sap all our spiritual strength and vigor. We think… If the Lord should require forty years of this from us there would be no time left in our lives to capitalize on what we have learned. But God’s timing is perfect. Thus, it behooves us to not concern ourselves so much with the longevity of our schooling, but to be thoroughly acquainted with the message from Midian. While some receive the bitter strokes of Midian and retreat to stand cynically on the sidelines, we must shake off the dust of the desert and arise with an understanding of…

God’s Purpose

God has a purpose for every detail of our lives. He may plant us in a difficult position, to forge in us a new vocation. It was alone in Midian where Moses learned of his own pride, self-confidence, lack of faith, and the utter folly that his own hands had participated in. Here in his Midian, he was alone and yet not alone; numerous other saints have joined him there. The sons of Jacob and the wife of Potiphar sent another vibrant servant there—Joseph. The wild rage of a jealous king sent a gifted young harpist there. Even an old and foolish king who refused to be taught found himself in a wilderness eating grass like an ox until he recanted of his pride.

Throughout the pages of history, countless saints have realized that ‘the darker the valley, the more I learned to pray’. While they arrive at the threshold of the new day loaded down with bountiful exuberance, they are soon stripped naked in a metamorphic change and finally emerge with nothing but the rod of God in their hands. Gone are the days when they were swift to speak, swift to act, and slow to hear. In Midian, the student learns to shift his focus from, “I will do great things for God” to “What wilt thou have me to do?”

And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do –Acts 9:6. The new arrivals in Midian have many answers, but most of them involve a one-act-play with self as the main character. The graduates walk out silent and sober, for they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…

God’s Purging

The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts –Proverbs 17:3. As Moses passed through the gates of Midian, the first scene that God set before his eyes was an injustice at a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters… –Exodus 2:16, who were being driven away by a band of uncouth shepherds. But Moses had been well trained in every dimension of Egyptian plutocracy, which would have included all aspects of military expertise and worldly leadership skills. Thus, when he stepped in to assist the helpless shepherdesses, he would have been quite capable to do so. These daughters of the priest of Midian appreciated the help which they recounted to their father that …An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock –Exodus 2:19. Upon hearing this tale, their father, Reuel, was so impressed that he gave Moses a reception, a job, and a wife… all in one verse. –see Exodus 2:21.

…Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them –Mark 10:42. While Moses’ quest for justice may have been noble, his orientation was merely Gentile. This may work for establishing pecking order in a hen house, but it is destined for failure in leading forth the people of God. But … whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all –Mark 10:43-44.

This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well. Many good and talented men can successfully operate a business using Gentile authority, but it rarely works in their home, and it is even more futile in a church. Thus, God moved His chosen vessel from royalty to proletariat (the working class), almost overnight. He is then given a job which was loathed by the people who had trained him—…for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians –Genesis 46:34. This fining pot is not just to teach us a much-needed lesson, but to guide us into…

God’s Provision

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way –Psalm 25:9. God will never abandon us on the back side of the desert; instead, He tailors our life circumstances to bring us into His fullness. If we resist the temptation to espouse an attitude of anger, then God will be able to teach us His ways. But to Moses, the situation presented itself such that God’s divine direction was the last thing he would suspect was happening.

Happening…? It seemed that nothing was happening. The weeks melted into months, the months into years, and the years into decades, all the while the gifted Moses remained an underachieving shepherd. One of the hardest things that we struggle with is “waiting.” Almost every Christian will face a long time of tribulation and we are told to: …think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you –1 Peter 4:12. But we should not judge God’s means by our feeble sense, for in the meantime, the wonderful working of waiting prepares us for…

God’s Promotion

38, 39, … 40 years. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt –Exodus 3:10.

Perhaps God is enamored with the number 40, but more than likely, it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation. His self-esteem has been fully extinguished, and he humbly asks: …Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? –Exodus 3:11.

Moses was not less qualified than he was forty years prior to this time, but his presumption had evaporated in the heat of the desert sun. The experience gleaned in the rugged pastures with the stubborn sheep has brought him to the understanding that this will be nearly an impossible feat. But there is no ordained calling issued independently from…

God’s Promise

…Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain –Exodus 3:12.

Not that Moses had attained perfection, for we find Moses provoking God to anger in the very next chapter—And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses… –Exodus 4:14. Then soon again he is the direct object in the path of God’s sword—And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24. Even so, while his vessel is still made of clay, it has met with a firing that has prepared him for the Lord’s service, and for us God will not revoke His promises in the wind of our whims. Thus, the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14, has laid upon human shoulders the immense and eternal task of leading His people. But this charge is not to be executed without…

God’s Power

What was the real refinement from Moses’ time spent in the desert? We notice his rash willingness to wield the sword before his arrival, but upon his exit, he only bore a rod in his hand. With the sword he had overcome an Egyptian offender, but with the rod he overcame the entire forces of Egypt. The rod of God brought forth the water in the wilderness. It was the rod of God, that, when lifted high by feeble hands secured the victory over Amalek. What is the rod of God? Before his days in Midian, he hardly knew it existed. Forty years later there hardly exists a scene without it.

The rod is the power of God unto salvation. It is the wisdom of God, the truth of God, the testimony of God, but more than all of these it is the chastening of God. Without it, man does not receive nor perceive the love of God for without it man is not connected to God. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.

This same Moses, who at one time was willing to exercise lordship (Gentile authority) over God’s people now finds himself entreating God and staying His wrath from destroying them. The people who accused Moses of leading them out to kill them and even at one point were ready to stone him are now at the center of his heart and affection, even though they are at the cause of his failure to enter the promised land. This is the love of Christ. But where is this learned except under the rod of God, on the back side of the desert, in the Egyptian dungeons, in the caves of Adullam, in the straits of Arabia, and in the silent solitude of the back burner where God has ordained that many of His people go until they learn to …learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls –Matthew 11:29. Surely that is where Moses secured the character known to the biblical scholar as the meekest man to walk the face of the earth. Surely there is no more opposite place on earth to learn it but in the school of suffering.

And so here we shall abide as well, so that we …may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10.

والآن كان موسى راعياً لغامِل شوعه حبوبين، الكاهن المدياني، فقاد الغنم إلى وراء البرية وجاء إلى جبل الله، إلى حوريب –خروج 3:1.

لقد فُهم منذ زمن بعيد أن وراء البرية هي مدرسة الله التي علّم بها كثيرين من عبيده، والذين يقف موسى في مقدمتهم. في سن الأربعين الأولى وجد نفسه …مُتَعلِّماً في كل حكمة المصريين، وكان قوي الكلام والأفعال. ولما كان قد أتم أربعين سنة، تجول في قلبه أن يزور إخوته بني إسرائيل –أعمال الرسل 7:22-23.

لا أشك في أن الله يستطيع ويستخدم رجالاً ذوي قدرات عظيمة وسعة تدريب، لكن القيادة الروحية تتطلب عنصراً لا ينتج عن الفعل أو التحصيل أو الإنجاز. شقاء المبادر غالباً ما يكون قلة الثقة بالله وكثرة الثقة بالجسد. هذا الكبرياء والاضطراب لا يعالَجان في كلية لاهوتية ولا يُبادان عادة أثناء الواجب اليقظ. لكثير من عباد الله يُستخرَجان من النفس على تربة رمال مقفرة. هذه الأرض الجرداء والمتروكة التي تبدو خاوية من الحياة والثمار هي حيث يتعلّم كثير من الخدام وضع وجوههم في الغبار والخضوع لما قد يبدو خمولاً، وعدم ثمر، ورفضاً.

يمكن تقسيم حياة موسى إلى ثلاثة أقسام. قضى أول أربعين سنة وهو يتعلّم حكمة مصر، والأربعين التالية راعياً في مديان، والأربعين الأخيرة راعياً لإسرائيل. يمكننا تخيل أن الثلث الأول من رحلته كان مليئاً بالنشاط الهائل والتقدّم والإنجاز. لا شك أنه عُرض عليه منذ ولادته أنه …كان حسنُ الهيئة جداً، رباه في بيت والده ثلاثة أشهر –أعمال الرسل 7:20.

إنّ الإنقاذ العجيب على النهر بواسطة ابنة فرعون كان ليؤكد أنه مُقدّر أن يكون أداة في تدبير الله الإلهي. وكموضوع جذب وطني، فليس مستغرباً كيف أن هذا الرجل الذي …كان قوياً في الكلام والأفعال –أعمال الرسل 7:22، كان مفعماً بالثقة بالنفس في قدرته على إنجاز مشيئة الله.

في اقتصاد اليوم، كان سيُقدَّر موسى كمرشح مثالي لقيادة الكنيسة. كان مؤهلاً بكل وجه. كان متقدماً على قومه في التعليم، وامتلك مواهب طبيعية ومالية وروحية فوق المعدل. خرج من “جامعة” مصر رجلاً قوياً في الكلمة والفعل وكان عليه دعوة واضحة من الله. كان رجلاً محافظاً اختار …بل أن يتحمل آلاماً مع شعب الله، لا أن ينعم بملذات الخطيئة زماناً –عبرانيين 11:25.

ومع ذلك، وسط كل مؤهلاته الرائعة كان لا يزال ناقصاً للعمل الذي دعا إليه الله. فإذًا، قاده الله بسهولة إلى أرض مديان ليُسجّله في مدرسة أخرى يتغذى فيها على أعشاب مراّرة من خيبة الأمل والرفض، والغموض والوحدة، والأحلام والحنين غير المُحقّق. بينما كانت طموحاته السابقة أن ينضم طوعاً إلى شعب الله، تم تمثيل هذا الفصل من حياته بالقسر.

نتعلم من السرد في خروج أن الثلث الأخير من حياته كان محمّلاً بتورّط معقَّد وخدمة عظيمة. وفي حين أن الخروج من مصر قراءة مثيرة وتوفر فهماً عظيماً، إلا أن معظمنا لا يستطيع بصدق أن يتعرّف على موسى العظيم وتحالفه الديناميكي مع الله. بالأحرى، هو القسم الأوسط الذي دام أربعين سنة من حياته الذي يجد كثيرون منا أنفسهم فيه. ورغم أن هناك بضعة عشرات من الآيات التي تمثل هذه العقود الأربع من حياته، فإننا نفترض أنها كانت تربية دقيقة نقشَت فيها صبر عظيم وتدبّر للذات وربما قليل من الإحباط.

بالنسبة لنا، تمثل فترة يبدو فيها أن رمال الزمن اليابسة حولنا لا تنتج أكثر من كشف لقلبنا الجاف والمتقشّر—منكمش ومهدر بعواقب إخفاقاتنا وخطايانا السابقة. وفي هذه الأوقات قد نصاب بزلة في الإيمان، ليس أننا نُلقي اللوم على الله في ظروفنا، بل أننا قد نبدأ برؤية حياتنا عبثاً، وأن كل يوم هو نفس اليوم الذي قبله. ربما نبدأ بالتجوال في سبات بلا رؤية—عبر ضباب اكتئاب روحي—ونتحسس عن تشجيع وتذكير بأن الله لم ينسَنا. أحياناً يبدو أن صلواتنا تضرب السقف وتعود تقفز هجواً منا مكذبة ومتهكمة أن منفعتنا في ملكوت الله قد انتهت. خلال فترات ممتدة من التجارب والاختبار قد نشعر بالهجران. قد نتخيل حتى أن الله قد مال علينا. نرفع أعيننا إلى السماء ونسأل، «لماذا يا رب؟» لن نختبر الرفض والهجران إلى المدى الذي اختبره الرب يسوع، لكن عندما نختبرهما في نطاقنا الصغير يبدو أنهما تستنزفان كل قوتنا ونشاطنا الروحي. نفكر… لو طلب الرب منا أربعين سنة من هذا فلن يبقَ في حياتنا وقت لنستثمر ما تعلمناه. لكن توقيت الله كامل. لذا، يليق بنا ألا نقلق كثيراً بشأن طول مدة تربيتنا، بل أن نكون على دراية تامة برسالة مديان. بينما يستقبل بعض الناس ضربات مديان المرة ويرجعون واقفين ساخرين على الهامش، يجب أن ننتف الغبار عن الصحراء ونقوم بفهم…

غاية الله

للَّه غاية في كل تفصيل من تفاصيل حياتنا. قد يزرعنا في موقف صعب ليصوغ فينا مهنة جديدة. ففي مديان وحده تعلّم موسى كبرياءه وثقته بنفسه وقلة إيمانه والغباء التام الذي شاركت به يداه. هنا في مديانه كان وحيداً ومع ذلك ليس بمفرده؛ لقد انضمّ إليه هناك عدد من القديسين أيضاً. أبناء يعقوب وزوجة فوطيفار أرسلوا عبدًا نابضًا آخر هناك—يوسف. غضب ملك غيور أرسل عازف قيثارة موهوباً هناك. حتى ملك عجوز جاهل رفض أن يُعلَّم فوجد نفسه في برية يأكل عشباً كالبقرة حتى تراجع عن كبريائه.

عبر صفحات التاريخ، أدرك عدد لا يحصى من القديسين أن «كلما اتسعت الظلمة في الوادي تعلمت أنا الصلاة أكثر». بينما يصلون إلى عتبة اليوم الجديد محمَّلين بحيوية وافرَة، يُعرَّون قريباً في تحول شكلي ويظهرون في النهاية لا يحملون شيئاً سوى عصا الله في أيديهم. ولّت أيام كونهم سريعي اللسان، سريعي الفعل، وبطيئي السمع. في مديان يتعلم الطالب تحويل تركيزه من «سأفعل أموراً عظيمة لله» إلى «ماذا تريد أن أفعل؟»

فارتعب وقال: يا رب ماذا تريد أن أفعل؟ فقال له الرب: قم وادخل إلى المدينة فتقال لك ماذا ينبغي لك أن تفعل –أعمال الرسل 9:6. الوافدون الجدد إلى مديان لديهم الكثير من الأجوبة، لكن أغلبها ينطوي على مسرحية من فعل واحد يكون الذات فيها الشخصية الرئيسية. الخريجون يخرجون صامتين ورصينين، لأنهم اجتازوا عملية شاقة لفصل الجسد عن الروح التي أُنجِزت بواسطة…

تطهير الله

إنبوت الفضة للتطهير والنار للذهب، وأما الرب فيجرب القلوب –أمثال 17:3. عندما مرَّ موسى عبر بوابات مديان، كان المشهد الأول الذي وضعه الله أمام عينيه ظلماً عند بئر. وكان للكاهن المدياني سبع بنات… –خروج 2:16 كنّ يُطردن من جماعة رعاة فظين. لكن موسى قد تدرّب تدريباً جيداً في كل بُعد من بُنى الثروة المصرية، والتي كانت ستشمل كل جوانب الخبرة العسكرية ومهارات القيادة العالمية. لذا، عندما تدخل لمساعدة الراعيات العاجزات، لكان قادراً تمام القدرة على ذلك. وقد قدرّت بنات كاهن مديان المساعدة وأخبرن أبيهن أن …مِصريّاً خلّصنا من يد الرعاة، وسقا الغنم بسقٍ كافٍ –خروج 2:19. عند سماع هذه الحكاية تأثر أَبُوهُنَّ رعوئيل حتى قدّم لموسى ضيافة ووظيفة وزوجة… كل ذلك في آية واحدة. –انظر خروج 2:21.

وتعلمون أن الذين يُعتَقد أنهم يتسلطون على الأمم يستعبدونهم، وعظماؤهم يظهِرون عليهم سلطاناً –مرقس 10:42. بينما قد تكون سعي موسى للعدل نبيلاً، كانت جهته مجرد جهة أممية. قد يصلح هذا لتثبيت ترتيب في بيت الدجاج، لكنه محكوم عليه بالفشل في قيادة شعب الله. وأما مَنْ أراد أن يكون بينكم عظيماً فليكن لكم خادماً. ومَنْ أراد أن يكون بينكم أولاً فليكن لكم عبداً للجميع –مرقس 10:43-44.

هذا المبدأ كان غريباً على مصر وعلى موسى أيضاً. كثير من الرجال الطيبين والموهوبين يمكنهم إدارة عمل تجاري بنجاح باستخدام سلطة أممية، لكنه نادراً ما ينجح في بيتهم، وأكثر فشلاً في كنيسة. لذلك، نَقَل الله إناءه المختار من الملكية إلى البروليتاريا (الطبقة العاملة)، تقريباً بين ليلة وضحاها. ثم أُعطي عملاً كان مكروهاً لدى الناس الذين درّبوه—…لأن كل راعٍ رجس عند المصريين –تكوين 46:34. هذا بوت التطهير ليس فقط ليعلّمنا درساً ضرورياً، لكن ليهدينا إلى…

عناية الله

إرشاد للودعاء في القضاء، ويوجه الودعاء طريقه –مزمور 25:9. لن يتخلى عنا الله أبداً في وراء البرية؛ بل يكيّف ظروف حياتنا ليأتي بنا إلى ملئه. إن قاومنا إغراء تبنّي موقف من الغضب، فسيتمكن الله من تعليمنا طرقه. لكن بالنسبة لموسى، قدّمته الظروف بحيث كانت التوجيه الإلهي آخر ما كان يتوقع حدوثه.

حدوث…؟ بدا أنه لا يحدث شيء. الأسابيع انصهرت إلى شهور، والشهور إلى سنوات، والسنين إلى عقود، وكل ذلك بينما ظل موسى الموهوب راعياً متدني الأداء. من أصعب الأشياء التي نكافح معها هو «الانتظار». يكاد كل مسيحي يواجه زمناً طويلاً من الضيقات ويُؤمر أن: …لا تتعجبوا عن نار التجربة التي تجري عليكم كأن شيئاً غريباً يحدث لكم –رسالة بطرس الأولى 4:12. لكن لا ينبغي أن نحكم على وسائل الله بحواسنا الضعيفة، فبينما نحن ننتظر، فإن العمل العجيب للانتظار يُعدّنا من أجل…

ترفيع الله

38، 39، … 40 سنة. فالآن فَأَنا مُرسِلُكَ إلى فرعون لتُخرِجَ شعبي بني إسرائيل من مصر –خروج 3:10.

ربما الله مولع بالرقم أربعين، لكن على الأرجح كان ذلك الزمن الذي استغرقه ليصل موسى إلى مقام الاستسلام. لقد أطفأت ثقته بنفسه تماماً، وسأل بتواضع: …من أنا حتى أذهب إلى فرعون وأخرج بني إسرائيل من مصر؟ –خروج 3:11.

لم يكن موسى أقل مؤهلاً مما كان عليه قبل أربعين سنة، لكن افتراضه تبخر في حرارة شمس الصحراء. التجربة التي اكتسبها في المراعي الوعرة مع الخراف العنيدة أوصلته إلى فهم أن هذا سيكون عملاً يكاد يكون مستحيلاً. لكن لا توجد دعوة مَنَحَوية صادرة مستقلة عن…

وعد الله

…أنا لأكُون معك بالتأكيد، وهذه علامة لك أني أرسلتك: متى أَخرجتَ الشعب من مصر فتعبدون الله على هذا الجبل –خروج 3:12.

ليس أن موسى بلغ الكمال، فنجد موسى يثير غضب الله في الفصل التالي مباشرة—واشتد غضب الرب على موسى… –خروج 4:14. ثم سرعان ما كان أيضاً هدفاً في طريق سيف الله—فحدث في الطريق في المنزل إن الرب قابله لِيَقتلَه –خروج 4:24. ومع ذلك، بينما كان إناؤه لا يزال من طين، فقد تم تعريضه لنار أعدته لخدمة الرب، ولن يلغى الله وعوده بفعل هواهاتنا. وهكذا، العظيم «أنا هو الذي أنا» –انظر خروج 3:14 وضع على أكتاف بشرية المهمة العظيمة الأبدية لقيادة شعبه. لكن هذه التكاليف لا تُنفَّذ دون…

قوة الله

ما كان التطهير الحقيقي من زمن موسى في الصحراء؟ نلاحظ استعداده المتهور لحمل السيف قبل مجيئه، لكن عند خروجه لم يحمل إلا عصا في يده. بالسيف تغلب على مضايق مصري، لكن بالعصا تغلب على جيوش مصر كلها. عصا الله أخرجت الماء في البرية. كانت عصا الله، عندما رفعت عالياً بيدين واهنتين، هي التي أمّنت النصر على عمّالِقَةَ عمّاليق. ما هي عصا الله؟ قبل أيامه في مديان، كان بالكاد يعلم بوجودها. بعد أربعين سنة لا يكاد يوجد مشهد بدونها.

العصا هي قوة الله نحو الخلاص. هي حكمة الله، وحق الله، وشهادة الله، لكن أكثر من كل هذا هي تأديب الله. بدونها لا ينال الإنسان ولا يدرك محبة الله إذ بدونها لا يرتبط الإنسان بالله. فمن يحبه الرب يؤدبه ويجلده كل ابن يقبله. فإن كان تحت التئدة فتحاسبهم كما لآبناء، لأنه أي ابن من الآب لا يؤدبه؟ وأمّا إن كنتم بلا تأديب الذي شارك فيه الجميع فأنتم أبناؤنا غير شرعيين ولسستم أبناء –عبرانيين 12:6-8.

نفس موسى هذا، الذي كان في وقت من الأوقات مستعداً لممارسة الربوبية (السلطة الأممية) على شعب الله، يجد نفسه الآن يستجدي الله ويكبح غضبه عن تدميرهم. الشعب الذي اتهم موسى بأنه أخرجهم ليُقتلوا وكان في وقتٍ ما مستعداً لرمي الحجارة عليه هو الآن محور قلبه ومودته، رغم أنهم كانوا سبب فشله في الدخول إلى أرض الميعاد. هذه هي محبة المسيح. لكن أين يُتعلَّم هذا إن لم يكن تحت عصا الله، في خلفية البرية، في سجون مصر، في مغارات عدّولام، في ضيِّق العرب، وفي وحدة هادئة على الموقد الخلفي حيث قضى الله أن يذهب كثير من شعبه حتى يتعلّموا أن …تعلموا مني لأني وديع ومتواضع القلب فتجدوا راحة لنفوسكم –متى 11:29. بلا شك هناك حصل موسى على الخلق المعروف لدى عالم الكتاب المقدس بأنه أضعف رجل سلك على وجه الأرض. حقاً لا يوجد مكان أقسى على الأرض لتعلّم ذلك إلا في مدرسة المعاناة.

وبذلك سنقيم نحن أيضاً هناك، لكي …نعرفه وقوة قيامته وشركة آلامه متحولين على شبه موته –فيلبي 3:10.

The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them –Psalm 34:7.

“Tell us a story, Grandma,” begged two eager children as they crowded around her rocking chair.

“My, my, you children like to hear stories, don’t you?” replied Grandma, with a twinkle in her eye. “All right, I’ll tell you about a time when I was about eight years old, and my sister Lori was nine.

We lived on an old farm, back a short lane along a dirt road. One morning, Mother called us in from our play and said she was out of sugar. She asked us to walk to Mrs. Brightbill to see if she had any sugar to spare. You see, we didn’t have telephones when I was a little girl, so she couldn’t call the neighbor and ask her. Neighbors often shared back and forth because we didn’t go shopping at the store very often either. So, mother gave us a container, and we started out on our long walk as Mother called after us and reminded us not to loiter along the way.”

“How far was it to the Brightbills?” asked Sharon.

“Oh, it was about half a mile to our closest neighbor, the Rhine’s place, and then about another quarter of a mile to the Brightbills,” replied Grandma.

“Oh, that’s far. Mother won’t let us walk on the road at all,” added Micah.

“I’m sure you are right,” agreed Grandma. “And I hope you never walk on the road without your parents’ permission. But things were much different when I was a little girl. We also walked every day to school, which was quite a bit further than the Brightbill farm. So, the little errand we were doing on this morning for Mother seemed like fun. There was only one problem though. The Rhine family had an old man living in their summer house. His name was Pierce, and he had a very fierce dog; at least he acted very fierce! He was kept behind a high wire fence connected to an old shed.

Every day when we walked to school, that dog frightened us terribly with his fierce barking and growling. But Mother always reminded us to pray and remember the Bible verse which says: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3. Still, we hurried by as fast as our legs could take us.

Lori and I started out happily on our errand for Mother. We skipped along, watching the dust swirl beneath our feet on that warm summer morning. Everything seemed unusually quiet and still as we passed through the gully, over the rippling creek, and up the steep hill right before Neighbor Rhine’s place. There before us was the old shed, and on the other side was the high fence which kept in Pierce’s mean dog. My heart began to thump rapidly. ‘Maybe that bad dog hadn’t seen us yet,’ I thought gratefully as I whispered once more to myself, ‘I will trust and not be afraid.’

Suddenly, the air was shattered by the ferocious barking of that mean dog as he sprang around the corner of the old shed! Lori and I froze in our tracks! As that angry dog raced toward us, Lori screamed. The next moment, I realized she had fallen down and was sitting in the middle of the dirt road, with her hands behind her on the hard packed gravel, feet and legs in the air, kicking and kicking, spinning around and around as that angry dog circled her, jumping in at her and nipping at her feet and legs! I was so scared. I just stood frozen to the spot. I don’t remember if I screamed, or if I prayed. But suddenly there was a shout! It was Pierce, with a whip in his hand. He came running around the shed and out on the road. He whipped and whipped that dog and finally got him away from Lori and back inside the fence where he belonged, as Lori and I stood there, trembling, and crying with relief.”

“Wow!” exclaimed Sharon. “That was really scary, wasn’t it?”

“Did Pierce need to get rid of his dog?” asked Micah.

“Yes, Sharon, it was very scary,” answered Grandma. “And no, Micah, Pierce did not get rid of his dog. We children needed to keep trusting the good Lord to keep us safe every day.”

“I don’t remember what happened after Pierce got the dog away that day, or if we ever got Mother’s sugar, but I will never forget what happened that day.

It was a miracle that Lori and I were not injured. There is a verse in Psalms which says: Save me from the lion’s mouth… –Psalm 22:21. How thankful we were to be delivered from the dog’s mouth! I like to think that the Lord’s angel had his sword drawn in front of that dog’s mouth every time he leaped at my dear sister.”
