On November 27, 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte of Ghent, Holland was martyred for her faith in the Lord, Jesus Christ. Prior to her passing, her husband had also been martyred for his faith. During the time of her imprisonment, she wrote several lengthy letters to her three youth-aged children. The following are abridged excerpts of these letters which can be found in full text on pages 646-651 in the Martyr’s Mirror.

Grace, peace, and mercy from God, the Father, and the Lord, Jesus Christ, to my dear children, David, Betgen, and Tanneken. This affectionate greeting, written by your mother in bonds, is a memorial of the truth to you. I hope to testify to this Truth by my words, my life, and my death, with the help of the Most High. May the wisdom of the Holy Ghost instruct and strengthen you, that you may be brought up in the ways of the Lord. Since it pleases the Lord to take me out of this world, I will leave you this memorial of my faith in the only true God, not of silver or gold for such jewels are perishable.

Receive admonition. First, I admonish you, my most beloved children, always allow yourselves to be instructed by those who fear the Lord. As long as you obey good admonition and instruction, God will be your Father and not leave you as orphans. For David says: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose –Psalm 25:12. Children, grieve not when you are corrected and do not speak in anger to those who correct you. A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke –Proverbs 13:1.

Guard your tongue. My dear children, guard your tongue, that it speak no evil. Do not practice deceit or backbiting with your lips. Paul teaches us to live peaceably with all men if it be possible. –see 1 Peter 3:10 and Romans 12:18. If you are crossly spoken to, learn to answer kindly, and you will be loved by all men. Humility and meekness are acceptable to both God and man.

Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight –Proverbs 12:22. I admonish you to beware of lying, since liars have no part in the kingdom of God. –see Revelation 21:8.

Be diligent in work and give alms. Always be diligent to do your work, wherever you be; for Paul says …that if any would not work, neither should he eat –2 Thessalonians 3:10. It is also written, be diligent to labor, that you …may have to give to him that needeth –Ephesians 4:28.

Do not turn your face away from the poor. Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard –Proverbs 21:13. Therefore, be diligent in prayer, and love the poor; for Christ also was poor for our sakes—For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich –2 Corinthians 8:9. Be therefore also merciful, even as your heavenly Father is merciful; for such shall be blessed, and shall obtain mercy. –see Matthew 5:7.

Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith –Proverbs 15:16. And, Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife –Proverbs 17:1. Choose to earn your bread by the labor of your hands, and to eat your bread with peace. Seek not to be a merchant, nor be anxious for great gain.

Be meek, merciful, and pure in heart. Learn to be meek and lowly in heart for such are blessed and shall inherit the earth. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Luke 6:36. And, Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth –Matthew 5:5. Finally, Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God –Matthew 5:8. Hence, my dear children, let no impure thoughts remain in your hearts. Engage yourselves with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs and evil thoughts will have no room. –see Ephesians 5:19.

Neither let filthiness proceed out of your mouth. You will have to give an account of all filthiness. –see Matthew 12:36-37. Always esteem yourselves as the least and be not wise in your own conceit. Allow yourselves to be instructed by your elders and always be silent when others speak. Humble yourselves, for …whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted –Matthew 23:12. For Christ who is the greatest made Himself the least for an example unto us. –see John 13:13-15.

Avoid a luxurious life. My children, do not desire the luxuries of fine food or wine. He that desires costly feasts will not become rich. Be content with the labor of your hands. Do not be a burden to anyone as long as you can obtain the things needful—…It is more blessed to give than to receive –Acts 20:35. Paul says: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Be sober and thankful as you have heard me read of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They were selected by the king of Babylon to be nourished with the same wine and meat which the king drank and ate at his table. But they chose to have pulse [vegetables] and water. They wanted to observe the law and commandments of their fathers with sobriety and thankfulness in the fear of God. In the end, they were fairer and fatter than those who ate of the king’s dainties, see Daniel chapter 1. Thus, faithfully they walked in the ways of the Lord. They made themselves acceptable to God in prayer and supplication, therefore, he did great things through them. He delivered them from the den of lions and out of the fiery furnace.

When Joseph was sold into Egypt, he desired no worldly dainties. When the Egyptian woman sought to seduce him, he feared God, and God preserved him. He pleased God in sobriety and prayer and God appointed him ruler over Egypt. –see Genesis chapters 37, 39, and 41. Take an example from this in your youth and you will please God. He will keep you from all seduction.

Oh, my lambs, you are still in your youth, yet you have a part in your Father’s kingdom. See that you keep it well and not as Esau who gave his inheritance or birthright for a mess of pottage, disregarding his father’s blessing. –see Genesis 25:30-34. But Jacob chose the better part, walking in the ways of the Lord with all righteousness.

Shun worldly living. Do not delight in the evils of the world such as lying, cheating, gambling, banqueting, playing, swearing, cursing, backbiting, hatred, and dancing, nor envy, drunkenness, excess, idolatry, covetousness, lasciviousness, vanity, filthy conversation. Though the world does not consider these things to be sin but rather calls them amusements, nevertheless, they are abominations in the eyes of the Lord. –see 1 Peter 4:3-4. If you take pleasure in these things, you sell your birthright (or the spiritual inheritance) from your Father, for a mess of pottage—namely, for a few temporal pleasures, which lead you to damnation.

Choose to suffer affliction with the children of God. From the time of Abel until now many have been afflicted and have suffered. They were rejected, despised, persecuted, and killed because they would not follow the wicked world and her false prophets.

My children, choose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God [that you may be rewarded with them], than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25. Unto such belong all the beautiful promises of God. It is written: …ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy –John 16:20. And, Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life –Revelation 2:10. Finally, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world –John 16:33.

Instructions to my son, David. David, my dear son, I commend you to the Lord. You are the oldest; learn wisdom, so that you may be a good example to your sisters. Beware of bad company and of playing in the street with bad boys. Diligently learn to read and write so that you may get understanding.

Love one another without contention or quarreling. Be kind to your sisters. Bear them up as the stronger and out of love help all you can. Assist them out of brotherly love.

Learn to obey your elders in that which is good. Be industrious so that people may love you. Exhort one another to good works, modesty, honorableness, and quietness. Always care for one another for the time has come that …iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold –Matthew 24:12.

Beware of deception. Remember, Jesus said …that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect –Matthew 24:24. Learn to diligently search the Scriptures so that you may not be deceived. Do not believe gossip but examine the matter.

Make no commotion when you are slandered but bear it for Christ’s sake. Love your enemies and pray for those who speak evil of you and afflict you. Suffer affliction rather than afflicting others. Suffer reproach rather than reproaching others. Be slandered rather than slandering others.

You must constantly see that you do not seek solely your own profit, but always care for those with whom you have dealings, whether they be young or old.

Instructions to my daughters Betgen and Tanneken, my beloved lambs, I admonish you in all these same things, that you obey the commandments of the Lord. Also, obey your elders and all who instruct you in virtue.

Be diligent to do your work, and you will be loved wherever you live. Don’t be quarrelsome, talkative, light-minded, proud, or surly of speech. Be kind, honorable, and quiet, as behooves young girls.

Pray the Lord for wisdom, and it shall be given you. Diligently learn to read and write, and take delight therein, and you will become wise. Take pleasure and sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Learn to please the Lord from your youth, as did the holy women and virgins of old. Esther also was a virgin who feared God; she was adorned with humility, was gracious, honorable, kind, and humble of heart; hence she pleased King Ahasuerus above all the other virgins. –see Esther 2:17. But even in her high estate she was not proud. Though she shone in royal apparel, she humbled her heart with fasting and prayer to the Lord, for her brethren, that they might be delivered out of the hands of their enemies. She did not esteem herself better than one of the least of her brethren.

When you have attained the years of understanding, see that you adorn yourselves with the works of the Spirit such as goodness, gentleness, meekness, humility, obedience, long suffering, righteousness, modesty, honorableness, purity, peaceableness, steadfastness, mercifulness, wisdom, diligence in good works, faith, hope and love. Love God above all that is in the world and do to your neighbor as you would have men do unto you. –see Galatians 5:22-23 and Titus 2:3-5. Remember that Jesus said: …Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets –Matthew 22:37-40.

Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints –Revelation 19:7-8. My daughters, this is the adornment of the saints; labor for such a wedding garment, so that you may enter into the marriage of the Lamb, where they …the righteous, [shall] shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father… –Matthew 13:43. May the Lord lead you as He led Israel out of Egypt, and bring you to the New Jerusalem, that we may see each other with joy in the day of the resurrection. I commend you to the Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; may He keep you to the end of your lives.

In conclusion, O my dear children, I have written this in tears, admonishing you out of love. My prayer and solicitude are constantly for your salvation. I hope and pray constantly that He, in His mercy, will preserve you, just as He preserved Joseph, Moses, and Daniel in the midst of wicked men. And He will do this if you give diligence to follow the truth.

This is my last farewell, my dear lambs. always remember each other in love; diligently learn to read and write and obey everyone in that which is good. I bid you adieu, my dear children Betgen, David and Tanneken. Adieu all my dear brethren and sisters, and friends everywhere.

Written by me, Soetgen van den Houte, your mother in bonds; written in haste (while trembling with cold), out of love for you all, amen.

Il 27 novembre 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte di Gand, Olanda, fu martirizzata per la sua fede nel Signore, Gesù Cristo. Prima della sua morte, anche suo marito era stato martirizzato per la sua fede. Durante il periodo della sua prigionia, ella scrisse diverse lunghe lettere ai suoi tre figli in età giovanile. Seguono estratti abbreviati di queste lettere che si possono trovare per intero alle pagine 646-651 nel Martyr’s Mirror.

Grazia, pace e misericordia da Dio Padre e dal Signore, Gesù Cristo, ai miei cari figli, David, Betgen e Tanneken. Questo affettuoso saluto, scritto dalla vostra madre in catene, è un memoriale della verità per voi. Spero di testimoniare questa Verità con le mie parole, la mia vita e la mia morte, con l’aiuto dell’Altissimo. Possano la sapienza dello Spirito Santo istruirvi e fortificarvi, affinché siate educati nelle vie del Signore. Poiché è volontà del Signore togliermi da questo mondo, vi lascio questo memoriale della mia fede nell’unico vero Dio, non d’argento o d’oro poiché tali gioielli sono corruttibili.

Ricevete ammonimento. Innanzitutto, vi esorto, miei diletti figli, di lasciarvi sempre istruire da coloro che temono il Signore. Finché obbedirete a buoni ammonimenti e insegnamenti, Dio sarà vostro Padre e non vi lascerà orfani. Poiché Davide dice: Qual è l’uomo che teme il SIGNORE? Egli lo ammonirà nella via che deve scegliere –Salmo 25:12. Figli, non vi rattristate quando venite corretti e non parlate con ira a coloro che vi correggono. Un figlio saggio ascolta l’istruzione del padre: ma lo schernitore non ascolta la riprensione –Proverbi 13:1.

Custodite la vostra lingua. Miei cari figli, custodite la lingua, perché non parli male. Non praticate inganno né diffamazione con le vostre labbra. Paolo ci insegna a vivere pacificamente con tutti, se è possibile. –vedi 1 Pietro 3:10 e Romani 12:18. Se vi si parla con durezza, imparate a rispondere con gentilezza, e sarete amati da tutti. Umiltà e mansuetudine sono gradite a Dio e agli uomini.

Le labbra bugiarde sono abominio per il SIGNORE: ma quelli che agiscono con verità gli sono graditi –Proverbi 12:22. Vi esorto a guardare dalla menzogna, poiché i bugiardi non avranno parte nel regno di Dio. –vedi Apocalisse 21:8.

Siate diligenti nel lavoro e date elemosina. Siate sempre diligenti nel fare il vostro lavoro, ovunque siate; poiché Paolo dice …se qualcuno non vuol lavorare, neppure mangi –2 Tessalonicesi 3:10. È anche scritto: siate solleciti nel lavorare, affinché …abbiate da dare a chi è nel bisogno –Efesini 4:28.

Non volgere il volto dal povero. Chi chiude le orecchie al grido del povero, anch’egli griderà e non sarà esaudito –Proverbi 21:13. Perciò, siate diligenti nella preghiera e amate i poveri; poiché Cristo stesso fu povero per amor nostro—Voi conoscete la grazia del nostro Signore Gesù Cristo, che benché ricco, per amor vostro si fece povero, perché voi, mediante la sua povertà, diventaste ricchi –2 Corinzi 8:9. Siate dunque anche misericordiosi, così come il vostro Padre celeste è misericordioso; poiché tali saranno beati e otterranno misericordia. –vedi Matteo 5:7.

Meglio poco con il timore del SIGNORE che grandi tesori e con essi afflizione –Proverbi 15:16. E, Meglio un boccone secco e la tranquillità con esso, che una casa piena di sacrifici con contesa –Proverbi 17:1. Scegliete di guadagnarvi il pane con il lavoro delle vostre mani e di mangiare il pane nella pace. Non cercate di diventare mercanti né siate ansiosi di grandi guadagni.

Siate mansueti, misericordiosi e puri di cuore. Imparate ad essere mansueti e umili di cuore perché costoro sono beati e erediteranno la terra. Siate dunque misericordiosi, come è misericordioso anche il vostro Padre –Luca 6:36. E, Beati i miti, perché erediteranno la terra –Matteo 5:5. Infine, Beati i puri di cuore, perché vedranno Dio –Matteo 5:8. Pertanto, miei cari figli, non lasciate che rimangano nei vostri cuori pensieri impuri. Impegnatevi in salmi, inni e cantici spirituali e i pensieri maligni non avranno luogo. –vedi Efesini 5:19.

Non lasciate uscire dal vostro bocca volgarità. Dovrete rendere conto di ogni volgarità. –vedi Matteo 12:36-37. Consideratevi sempre i più umili e non siate saggi secondo la vostra propria opinione. Lasciatevi istruire dagli anziani e state sempre zitti quando gli altri parlano. Umiliatevi, perché …chi si esalta sarà umiliato; e chi si umilia sarà esaltato –Matteo 23:12. Poiché Cristo, che è il più grande, si fece il più piccolo come esempio per noi. –vedi Giovanni 13:13-15.

Evitate una vita lussuosa. Figli miei, non desiderate i piaceri della tavola o del vino pregiato. Chi desidera conviti costosi non diventerà ricco. Siate contenti del lavoro delle vostre mani. Non siate gravosi a nessuno finché potete ottenere le cose necessarie—…È più beato dare che ricevere –Atti 20:35. Paolo dice: E avendo cibo e vesti, con queste cose siamo soddisfatti –1 Timoteo 6:8.

Siate sobri e riconoscenti come avete udito che io leggevo di Daniele, Sadrach, Mesac e Abednego. Essi furono scelti dal re di Babilonia per essere nutriti con lo stesso vino e cibi che il re beveva e mangiava alla sua tavola. Ma essi scelsero di mangiare legumi [verdure] e bere acqua. Volevano osservare la legge e i comandamenti dei loro padri con sobrietà e riconoscenza nel timore di Dio. Alla fine, erano più sani e più robusti di coloro che mangiavano le delicatezze del re; vedi Daniele capitolo 1. Così, fedelmente camminarono nelle vie del Signore. Si resero accetti a Dio in preghiera e supplica, perciò Dio compì grandi cose per mezzo loro. Li liberò dalla fossa dei leoni e dalla fornace ardente.

Quando Giuseppe fu venduto in Egitto, non desiderò prelibatezze mondane. Quando la donna egiziana cercò di sedurlo, egli temette Dio, e Dio lo preservò. Piacque a Dio nella sobrietà e nella preghiera e Dio lo pose governatore dell’Egitto. –vedi Genesi capitoli 37, 39 e 41. Prendete esempio da questo nella vostra giovinezza e piacerete a Dio. Egli vi terrà da ogni seduzione.

Oh, miei agnelli, siete ancora giovani, tuttavia avete una parte nel regno del Padre. Vegliate di conservarla bene e non come Esaù che vendette la sua eredità o il suo diritto di primogenitura per una minestra, disprezzando la benedizione del padre. –vedi Genesi 25:30-34. Ma Giacobbe scelse la parte migliore, camminando nelle vie del Signore con tutta giustizia.

Sfuggite la vita mondana. Non vi compiacete dei mali del mondo come menzogna, inganno, gioco d’azzardo, banchetti, giuochi, giuramenti, imprecazioni, diffamazione, odio e danza, né invidia, ubriachezza, eccedenza, idolatria, cupidigia, lussuria, vanità, discorsi volgari. Sebbene il mondo non consideri queste cose come peccato ma le chiami divertimenti, nondimeno sono abominazioni agli occhi del Signore. –vedi 1 Pietro 4:3-4. Se vi piaceete in queste cose, vendete il vostro diritto di primogenitura (o l’eredità spirituale) dal Padre, per una ciotola di minestra—ossia per pochi piaceri temporanei, che vi conducono alla dannazione.

Scegliete di soffrire afflizione con i figli di Dio. Dal tempo di Abele fino ad ora molti sono stati afflitti e hanno sofferto. Sono stati rigettati, disprezzati, perseguitati e uccisi perché non volevano seguire il mondo malvagio e i suoi falsi profeti.

Miei figli, scegliete …piuttosto di soffrire afflizione con il popolo di Dio [affinché siate ricompensati con loro], che di godere i piaceri del peccato per un tempo –Ebrei 11:25. A costoro appartengono tutte le belle promesse di Dio. È scritto: …voi piangerete e vi lamenterete, ma il mondo gioirà: voi sarete addolorati, ma il vostro dolore si muterà in gioia –Giovanni 16:20. E, Non temere alcuna delle cose che devi soffrire: ecco, il diavolo metterà in prigione alcuni di voi, affinché siate provati; e avrete tribolazione per dieci giorni: sii fedele fino alla morte, e io ti darò la corona della vita –Apocalisse 2:10. Infine, Queste cose vi ho dette, affinché abbiate pace in me. Nel mondo avrete tribolazione; ma fatevi coraggio, io ho vinto il mondo –Giovanni 16:33.

Istruzioni a mio figlio, David. David, mio caro figlio, ti raccomando al Signore. Sei il più anziano; apprendi saggezza, affinché tu sia un buon esempio per le tue sorelle. Guardati dalle cattive compagnie e dal giocare in strada con ragazzi cattivi. Impara diligentemente a leggere e scrivere affinché tu possa ottenere discernimento.

Amavi l’un l’altro senza contesa né litigi. Sii benevolo con le tue sorelle. Sostienile come il più forte e per amore aiutale quanto puoi. Assistile con amore fraterno.

Impara a obbedire agli anziani nelle cose buone. Sii operoso affinché la gente ti voglia bene. Esortatevi a vicenda a opere buone, modestia, onorevolezza e quiete. Preoccupatevi sempre l’uno dell’altro perché è giunto il tempo in cui …l’iniquità abbonderà, e l’amore di molti si raffredderà –Matteo 24:12.

Guardatevi dall’inganno. Ricordate, Gesù disse …che, se fosse possibile, ingannerebbero perfino gli eletti –Matteo 24:24. Imparate a cercare diligentemente le Scritture affinché non siate ingannati. Non credete alle dicerie ma esaminate la questione.

Non fate clamore quando siete calunniati ma sopportatelo per amor di Cristo. Amate i vostri nemici e pregate per quelli che parlano male di voi e vi affliggono. Soffrite afflizione piuttosto che affliggere gli altri. Sopportate la riprovazione piuttosto che riprovare altri. Siate calunniati piuttosto che calunniare gli altri.

Dovete sempre fare in modo di non cercare solo il vostro profitto, ma badare sempre a coloro con cui avete a che fare, siano essi giovani o vecchi.

Istruzioni alle mie figlie Betgen e Tanneken, mie amate agnelline, vi esorto in tutte queste medesime cose, affinché obbediate ai comandamenti del Signore. Obbedite inoltre agli anziani e a tutti coloro che vi istruiscono nella virtù.

Siate diligenti nel fare il vostro lavoro, e sarete amate ovunque viviate. Non siate litigiose, chiacchierone, frivole, orgogliose o scontrose nel parlare. Siate gentili, onorevoli e quiete, come si addice a giovani ragazze.

Pregate il Signore per la sapienza, e vi sarà data. Imparate diligentemente a leggere e scrivere, e trovatevi piacere in ciò, e diventerete sagge. Godetevi e cantate salmi, inni e cantici spirituali. Imparate a piacere al Signore fin dalla giovinezza, come fecero le sante donne e le vergini d’un tempo. Anche Ester fu una vergine che temeva Dio; era adornata di umiltà, era graziosa, onorevole, buona e umile di cuore; perciò piacque al re Assuero più di tutte le altre vergini. –vedi Ester 2:17. Ma anche nella sua alta condizione non fu orgogliosa. Benché brillasse in vesti regali, umiliò il suo cuore con digiuno e preghiera al Signore, per i suoi fratelli, affinché fossero liberati dalle mani dei loro nemici. Non si considerò migliore di uno dei più piccoli fra i suoi fratelli.

Quando avrete raggiunto l’età della ragione, vegliate a adornarvi con le opere dello Spirito come bontà, dolcezza, mansuetudine, umiltà, obbedienza, pazienza, giustizia, modestia, onorevolezza, purezza, pacificità, fermezza, misericordia, saggezza, sollecitudine nelle opere buone, fede, speranza e carità. Amate Dio al di sopra di tutto ciò che è nel mondo e fate al vostro prossimo come vorreste che gli uomini facessero a voi. –vedi Galati 5:22-23 e Tito 2:3-5. Ricordate che Gesù disse: …Amerai il Signore Dio tuo con tutto il tuo cuore, e con tutta la tua anima, e con tutta la tua mente. Questo è il primo e grande comandamento. E il secondo è simile a questo: Amerai il tuo prossimo come te stesso. Da questi due comandamenti dipendono tutta la legge e i profeti –Matteo 22:37-40.

Rallegriamoci e gioiamo, e rendiamo onore a lui: poiché è venuto il matrimonio dell’Agnello, e la sua sposa si è preparata. E le fu concesso di vestirsi di lino fino, puro e candido: poiché il lino fino sono le opere giuste dei santi –Apocalisse 19:7-8. Figlie mie, questo è l’ornamento dei santi; lavorate per avere un tale indumento nuziale, affinché possiate entrare alle nozze dell’Agnello, dove essi …i giusti, risplenderanno come il sole nel regno del loro Padre… –Matteo 13:43. Possa il Signore guidarvi come condusse Israele fuori dall’Egitto e portarvi alla Nuova Gerusalemme, affinché ci si possa vedere con gioia nel giorno della risurrezione. Vi raccomando al Signore, al Dio di Abramo, al Dio di Isacco e al Dio di Giacobbe; possa Egli custodirvi fino alla fine delle vostre vite.

In conclusione, O miei cari figli, ho scritto questo in lacrime, ammonendovi per amore. La mia preghiera e la mia sollecitudine sono costantemente per la vostra salvezza. Spero e prego incessantemente che Egli, nella Sua misericordia, vi conservi, proprio come conservò Giuseppe, Mosè e Daniele in mezzo a uomini malvagi. E così farà se vi sforzerete diligentemente di seguire la verità.

Questo è il mio ultimo addio, miei cari agnelli. ricordatevi sempre l’uno dell’altro con amore; imparate diligentemente a leggere e scrivere e obbedite a tutti nelle cose buone. Vi do addio, miei cari figli Betgen, David e Tanneken. Addio a tutti i miei cari fratelli e sorelle, e amici ovunque.

Scritto da me, Soetgen van den Houte, vostra madre in catene; scritto in fretta (mentre tremavo dal freddo), per amore di tutti voi, amen.

On November 27, 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte of Ghent, Holland was martyred for her faith in the Lord, Jesus Christ. Prior to her passing, her husband had also been martyred for his faith. During the time of her imprisonment, she wrote several lengthy letters to her three youth-aged children. The following are abridged excerpts of these letters which can be found in full text on pages 646-651 in the Martyr’s Mirror.

Grace, peace, and mercy from God, the Father, and the Lord, Jesus Christ, to my dear children, David, Betgen, and Tanneken. This affectionate greeting, written by your mother in bonds, is a memorial of the truth to you. I hope to testify to this Truth by my words, my life, and my death, with the help of the Most High. May the wisdom of the Holy Ghost instruct and strengthen you, that you may be brought up in the ways of the Lord. Since it pleases the Lord to take me out of this world, I will leave you this memorial of my faith in the only true God, not of silver or gold for such jewels are perishable.

Receive admonition. First, I admonish you, my most beloved children, always allow yourselves to be instructed by those who fear the Lord. As long as you obey good admonition and instruction, God will be your Father and not leave you as orphans. For David says: What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose –Psalm 25:12. Children, grieve not when you are corrected and do not speak in anger to those who correct you. A wise son heareth his father’s instruction: but a scorner heareth not rebuke –Proverbs 13:1.

Guard your tongue. My dear children, guard your tongue, that it speak no evil. Do not practice deceit or backbiting with your lips. Paul teaches us to live peaceably with all men if it be possible. –see 1 Peter 3:10 and Romans 12:18. If you are crossly spoken to, learn to answer kindly, and you will be loved by all men. Humility and meekness are acceptable to both God and man.

Lying lips are abomination to the LORD: but they that deal truly are his delight –Proverbs 12:22. I admonish you to beware of lying, since liars have no part in the kingdom of God. –see Revelation 21:8.

Be diligent in work and give alms. Always be diligent to do your work, wherever you be; for Paul says …that if any would not work, neither should he eat –2 Thessalonians 3:10. It is also written, be diligent to labor, that you …may have to give to him that needeth –Ephesians 4:28.

Do not turn your face away from the poor. Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard –Proverbs 21:13. Therefore, be diligent in prayer, and love the poor; for Christ also was poor for our sakes—For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich –2 Corinthians 8:9. Be therefore also merciful, even as your heavenly Father is merciful; for such shall be blessed, and shall obtain mercy. –see Matthew 5:7.

Better is little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure and trouble therewith –Proverbs 15:16. And, Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife –Proverbs 17:1. Choose to earn your bread by the labor of your hands, and to eat your bread with peace. Seek not to be a merchant, nor be anxious for great gain.

Be meek, merciful, and pure in heart. Learn to be meek and lowly in heart for such are blessed and shall inherit the earth. Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful. Luke 6:36. And, Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth –Matthew 5:5. Finally, Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God –Matthew 5:8. Hence, my dear children, let no impure thoughts remain in your hearts. Engage yourselves with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs and evil thoughts will have no room. –see Ephesians 5:19.

Neither let filthiness proceed out of your mouth. You will have to give an account of all filthiness. –see Matthew 12:36-37. Always esteem yourselves as the least and be not wise in your own conceit. Allow yourselves to be instructed by your elders and always be silent when others speak. Humble yourselves, for …whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted –Matthew 23:12. For Christ who is the greatest made Himself the least for an example unto us. –see John 13:13-15.

Avoid a luxurious life. My children, do not desire the luxuries of fine food or wine. He that desires costly feasts will not become rich. Be content with the labor of your hands. Do not be a burden to anyone as long as you can obtain the things needful—…It is more blessed to give than to receive –Acts 20:35. Paul says: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content –1 Timothy 6:8.

Be sober and thankful as you have heard me read of Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They were selected by the king of Babylon to be nourished with the same wine and meat which the king drank and ate at his table. But they chose to have pulse [vegetables] and water. They wanted to observe the law and commandments of their fathers with sobriety and thankfulness in the fear of God. In the end, they were fairer and fatter than those who ate of the king’s dainties, see Daniel chapter 1. Thus, faithfully they walked in the ways of the Lord. They made themselves acceptable to God in prayer and supplication, therefore, he did great things through them. He delivered them from the den of lions and out of the fiery furnace.

When Joseph was sold into Egypt, he desired no worldly dainties. When the Egyptian woman sought to seduce him, he feared God, and God preserved him. He pleased God in sobriety and prayer and God appointed him ruler over Egypt. –see Genesis chapters 37, 39, and 41. Take an example from this in your youth and you will please God. He will keep you from all seduction.

Oh, my lambs, you are still in your youth, yet you have a part in your Father’s kingdom. See that you keep it well and not as Esau who gave his inheritance or birthright for a mess of pottage, disregarding his father’s blessing. –see Genesis 25:30-34. But Jacob chose the better part, walking in the ways of the Lord with all righteousness.

Shun worldly living. Do not delight in the evils of the world such as lying, cheating, gambling, banqueting, playing, swearing, cursing, backbiting, hatred, and dancing, nor envy, drunkenness, excess, idolatry, covetousness, lasciviousness, vanity, filthy conversation. Though the world does not consider these things to be sin but rather calls them amusements, nevertheless, they are abominations in the eyes of the Lord. –see 1 Peter 4:3-4. If you take pleasure in these things, you sell your birthright (or the spiritual inheritance) from your Father, for a mess of pottage—namely, for a few temporal pleasures, which lead you to damnation.

Choose to suffer affliction with the children of God. From the time of Abel until now many have been afflicted and have suffered. They were rejected, despised, persecuted, and killed because they would not follow the wicked world and her false prophets.

My children, choose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God [that you may be rewarded with them], than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25. Unto such belong all the beautiful promises of God. It is written: …ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy –John 16:20. And, Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life –Revelation 2:10. Finally, These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world –John 16:33.

Instructions to my son, David. David, my dear son, I commend you to the Lord. You are the oldest; learn wisdom, so that you may be a good example to your sisters. Beware of bad company and of playing in the street with bad boys. Diligently learn to read and write so that you may get understanding.

Love one another without contention or quarreling. Be kind to your sisters. Bear them up as the stronger and out of love help all you can. Assist them out of brotherly love.

Learn to obey your elders in that which is good. Be industrious so that people may love you. Exhort one another to good works, modesty, honorableness, and quietness. Always care for one another for the time has come that …iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold –Matthew 24:12.

Beware of deception. Remember, Jesus said …that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect –Matthew 24:24. Learn to diligently search the Scriptures so that you may not be deceived. Do not believe gossip but examine the matter.

Make no commotion when you are slandered but bear it for Christ’s sake. Love your enemies and pray for those who speak evil of you and afflict you. Suffer affliction rather than afflicting others. Suffer reproach rather than reproaching others. Be slandered rather than slandering others.

You must constantly see that you do not seek solely your own profit, but always care for those with whom you have dealings, whether they be young or old.

Instructions to my daughters Betgen and Tanneken, my beloved lambs, I admonish you in all these same things, that you obey the commandments of the Lord. Also, obey your elders and all who instruct you in virtue.

Be diligent to do your work, and you will be loved wherever you live. Don’t be quarrelsome, talkative, light-minded, proud, or surly of speech. Be kind, honorable, and quiet, as behooves young girls.

Pray the Lord for wisdom, and it shall be given you. Diligently learn to read and write, and take delight therein, and you will become wise. Take pleasure and sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Learn to please the Lord from your youth, as did the holy women and virgins of old. Esther also was a virgin who feared God; she was adorned with humility, was gracious, honorable, kind, and humble of heart; hence she pleased King Ahasuerus above all the other virgins. –see Esther 2:17. But even in her high estate she was not proud. Though she shone in royal apparel, she humbled her heart with fasting and prayer to the Lord, for her brethren, that they might be delivered out of the hands of their enemies. She did not esteem herself better than one of the least of her brethren.

When you have attained the years of understanding, see that you adorn yourselves with the works of the Spirit such as goodness, gentleness, meekness, humility, obedience, long suffering, righteousness, modesty, honorableness, purity, peaceableness, steadfastness, mercifulness, wisdom, diligence in good works, faith, hope and love. Love God above all that is in the world and do to your neighbor as you would have men do unto you. –see Galatians 5:22-23 and Titus 2:3-5. Remember that Jesus said: …Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets –Matthew 22:37-40.

Let us be glad and rejoice, and give honour to him: for the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife hath made herself ready. And to her was granted that she should be arrayed in fine linen, clean and white: for the fine linen is the righteousness of saints –Revelation 19:7-8. My daughters, this is the adornment of the saints; labor for such a wedding garment, so that you may enter into the marriage of the Lamb, where they …the righteous, [shall] shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father… –Matthew 13:43. May the Lord lead you as He led Israel out of Egypt, and bring you to the New Jerusalem, that we may see each other with joy in the day of the resurrection. I commend you to the Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob; may He keep you to the end of your lives.

In conclusion, O my dear children, I have written this in tears, admonishing you out of love. My prayer and solicitude are constantly for your salvation. I hope and pray constantly that He, in His mercy, will preserve you, just as He preserved Joseph, Moses, and Daniel in the midst of wicked men. And He will do this if you give diligence to follow the truth.

This is my last farewell, my dear lambs. always remember each other in love; diligently learn to read and write and obey everyone in that which is good. I bid you adieu, my dear children Betgen, David and Tanneken. Adieu all my dear brethren and sisters, and friends everywhere.

Written by me, Soetgen van den Houte, your mother in bonds; written in haste (while trembling with cold), out of love for you all, amen.

Le 27 novembre 1560, Sotegen Van Den Houte de Gand, Hollande, fut martyrisée pour sa foi en le Seigneur Jésus-Christ. Avant son décès, son mari avait également été martyrisé pour sa foi. Pendant son emprisonnement, elle écrivit plusieurs longues lettres à ses trois enfants encore jeunes. Ce qui suit sont des extraits abrégés de ces lettres que l’on peut trouver en texte intégral aux pages 646-651 du Miroir des Martyrs.

Grâce, paix et miséricorde de la part de Dieu le Père et du Seigneur Jésus-Christ à mes chers enfants, David, Betgen et Tanneken. Cette salutation affectueuse, écrite par votre mère en chaînes, est un témoignage de la vérité pour vous. J’espère rendre témoignage à cette Vérité par mes paroles, ma vie et ma mort, avec l’aide du Très-Haut. Que la sagesse du Saint-Esprit vous instruise et vous fortifie, afin que vous soyez élevés dans les voies du Seigneur. Puisqu’il plaît au Seigneur de me retirer de ce monde, je vous laisse ce mémorial de ma foi en le seul vrai Dieu, non pas en argent ni en or car ces bijoux sont périssables.

Recevez l’avertissement. D’abord, je vous avertis, mes enfants bien-aimés, laissez-vous toujours instruire par ceux qui craignent le Seigneur. Tant que vous obéirez aux bonnes admonitions et instructions, Dieu sera votre Père et ne vous laissera pas orphelins. Car David dit : Quel homme est celui qui craint l’ÉTERNEL? Il l’instruira dans la voie qu’il doit choisir –Psaume 25:12. Enfants, ne vous affligez pas quand vous êtes corrigés et ne parlez pas avec colère à ceux qui vous corrigent. Un fils sage écoute l’instruction de son père ; mais le moqueur n’écoute point la réprimande –Proverbes 13:1.

Gardez votre langue. Mes chers enfants, gardez votre langue pour qu’elle ne dise point de mal. Ne pratiquez pas la tromperie ni la médisance avec vos lèvres. Paul nous enseigne de vivre paisiblement avec tous les hommes si cela est possible. –voir 1 Pierre 3:10 et Romains 12:18. Si l’on vous parle durement, apprenez à répondre aimablement, et vous serez aimés de tous les hommes. L’humilité et la douceur sont agréables à Dieu comme aux hommes.

Les lèvres menteuses sont en abomination à l’ÉTERNEL; mais ceux qui agissent avec vérité lui sont agréables –Proverbes 12:22. Je vous exhorte à vous garder du mensonge, car les menteurs n’ont point de part au royaume de Dieu. –voir Apocalypse 21:8.

Soyez diligents au travail et faites l’aumône. Soyez toujours diligents à faire votre ouvrage, partout où vous serez; car Paul dit …si quelqu’un ne veut pas travailler, qu’il ne mange point non plus –2 Thessaloniciens 3:10. Il est aussi écrit, soyez diligents à travailler, afin que vous …ayez de quoi donner à celui qui est dans le besoin –Éphésiens 4:28.

Ne détournez pas votre visage du pauvre. Celui qui ferme l’oreille au cri du pauvre criera lui-même et n’aura point de réponse –Proverbes 21:13. C’est pourquoi, soyez diligents en prière, et aimez les pauvres; car Christ aussi fut pauvre pour notre salut — Vous connaissez la grâce de notre Seigneur Jésus-Christ: bien qu’il fût riche, à cause de vous il s’est fait pauvre, afin que vous par sa pauvreté soyez enrichis –2 Corinthiens 8:9. Montrez donc aussi de la miséricorde, comme votre Père céleste est miséricordieux; car ceux-là seront bénis et obtiendront miséricorde. –voir Matthieu 5:7.

Mieux vaut peu avec la crainte de l’ÉTERNEL, qu’un grand trésor accompagné d’inquiétude –Proverbes 15:16. Et, Mieux vaut une bouchée sèche et le repos avec elle, qu’une maison pleine de sacrifices avec des querelles –Proverbes 17:1. Choisissez de gagner votre pain par le travail de vos mains, et de manger votre pain dans la paix. Ne cherchez pas à être marchand, et ne vous inquiétez pas d’un grand profit.

Soyez doux, miséricordieux et purs de cœur. Apprenez à être doux et humbles de cœur car ceux-là sont bénis et hériteront la terre. Soyez donc miséricordieux, comme votre Père est miséricordieux. Luc 6:36. Et, Heureux les doux, car ils hériteront la terre –Matthieu 5:5. Enfin, Heureux les cœurs purs, car ils verront Dieu –Matthieu 5:8. Ainsi, mes chers enfants, qu’aucune pensée impure ne demeure dans vos cœurs. Engagez-vous dans les psaumes, les hymnes et les cantiques spirituels et les pensées mauvaises n’auront point de place. –voir Éphésiens 5:19.

Ne laissez pas non plus la bassesse sortir de votre bouche. Vous devrez rendre compte de toute bassesse. –voir Matthieu 12:36-37. Estimez-vous toujours comme les plus faibles et ne soyez pas sages à vos propres yeux. Laissez-vous instruire par vos aînés et gardez le silence quand les autres parlent. Humiliez-vous, car …quiconque s’élèvera sera abaissé; et celui qui s’abaissera sera élevé –Matthieu 23:12. Car Christ, qui est le plus grand, s’est fait le moindre pour nous donner un exemple. –voir Jean 13:13-15.

Évitez une vie luxueuse. Mes enfants, ne désirez pas les luxes des mets fins ni du vin. Celui qui désire des festins coûteux ne s’enrichira pas. Contentez-vous du travail de vos mains. Ne soyez pas un fardeau pour quiconque tant que vous pouvez obtenir les choses nécessaires—…Il y a plus de bonheur à donner qu’à recevoir –Actes 20:35. Paul dit : Ayant nourriture et vêtement, nous en serons contents –1 Timothée 6:8.

Soyez sobres et reconnaissants comme je vous ai fait lire au sujet de Daniel, de Sadrac, Méshac et Abed-Nego. Ils furent choisis par le roi de Babylone pour être nourris du même vin et des mêmes mets que le roi buvait et mangeait à sa table. Mais ils choisirent d’avoir des légumes [légumes] et de l’eau. Ils voulurent observer la loi et les commandements de leurs pères avec sobriété et reconnaissance dans la crainte de Dieu. À la fin, ils étaient plus beaux et plus gras que ceux qui avaient mangé des plats délicats du roi, voir Daniel chapitre 1. Ainsi, fidèlement ils marchèrent dans les voies du Seigneur. Ils se rendirent agréables à Dieu par la prière et la supplication, aussi fit-il de grandes choses par eux. Il les délivra de la fosse aux lions et du four ardent.

Quand Joseph fut vendu en Égypte, il ne désira point de délices du monde. Quand la femme égyptienne chercha à le séduire, il craignit Dieu, et Dieu le préserva. Il plut à Dieu par sa sobriété et sa prière et Dieu le fit gouverneur de l’Égypte. –voir Genèse chapitres 37, 39 et 41. Prenez-en exemple dès votre jeunesse et vous plairez à Dieu. Il vous gardera de toute séduction.

Ô, mes agneaux, vous êtes encore dans votre jeunesse, et cependant vous avez part au royaume de votre Père. Veillez à bien le garder et non comme Ésaü qui vendit son héritage ou son droit d’aînesse pour un plat de lentilles, méprisant la bénédiction de son père. –voir Genèse 25:30-34. Mais Jacob choisit la meilleure part, marchant dans les voies du Seigneur avec toute justice.

Écartez la vie mondaine. Ne vous réjouissez pas des mœurs du monde comme le mensonge, la fraude, les jeux d’argent, les banquets, les divertissements, les jurons, les malédictions, la médisance, la haine et la danse, ni l’envie, l’ivresse, l’excès, l’idolâtrie, la cupidité, la luxure, la vanité, la conversation impure. Bien que le monde ne considère pas ces choses comme des péchés et les appelle plutôt des amusements, néanmoins elles sont des abominations aux yeux du Seigneur. –voir 1 Pierre 4:3-4. Si vous prenez plaisir en ces choses, vous vendez votre droit d’aînesse (ou l’héritage spirituel) de votre Père pour un plat de lentilles—c’est-à-dire pour quelques plaisirs temporels qui vous conduisent à la damnation.

Choisissez de souffrir l’affliction avec les enfants de Dieu. Depuis le temps d’Abel jusqu’à présent beaucoup ont été affligés et ont souffert. Ils furent rejetés, méprisés, persécutés et tués parce qu’ils ne voulaient pas suivre le monde méchant et ses faux prophètes.

Mes enfants, choisissez …plutôt de souffrir l’affliction avec le peuple de Dieu [afin que vous soyez récompensés avec eux], que de jouir des plaisirs du péché pour un temps –Hébreux 11:25. À ceux-ci appartiennent toutes les belles promesses de Dieu. Il est écrit : …vous pleurerez et serez dans l’affliction, mais le monde se réjouira: vous serez dans la tristesse, mais votre tristesse sera changée en joie –Jean 16:20. Et, N’aie point peur de ce que tu vas souffrir: voici, le diable jettera quelques-uns de vous en prison, afin que vous soyez éprouvés; et vous aurez une tribulation de dix jours: sois fidèle jusqu’à la mort, et je te donnerai la couronne de vie –Apocalypse 2:10. Enfin, Je vous ai dit ces choses, afin que vous ayez la paix en moi. Dans le monde vous aurez des tribulations: mais prenez courage; j’ai vaincu le monde –Jean 16:33.

Instructions à mon fils David. David, mon cher fils, je te recommande au Seigneur. Tu es l’aîné; apprends la sagesse, afin que tu sois un bon exemple pour tes sœurs. Méfie-toi des mauvaises fréquentations et de jouer dans la rue avec des garçons malvenus. Apprends assidûment à lire et à écrire afin d’acquérir de l’intelligence.

Aimez-vous les uns les autres sans dispute ni querelle. Sois bon envers tes sœurs. Soutiens-les comme le plus fort et par amour aide-les autant que tu pourras. Aide-les par amour fraternel.

Apprends à obéir à tes aînés en ce qui est bon. Sois industrieux afin que les gens t’aiment. Exhortez-vous les uns les autres aux bonnes œuvres, à la modestie, à l’honorabilité et au calme. Prenez toujours soin les uns des autres car le temps est venu où …l’iniquité abondera, et l’amour de plusieurs se refroidira –Matthieu 24:12.

Méfie-toi de la tromperie. Souviens-toi, Jésus a dit …et si cela était possible, ils séduiraient même les élus –Matthieu 24:24. Apprends à scruter diligemment les Écritures afin de ne pas être trompé. Ne crois pas les commérages mais examine la chose.

Ne fais point d’agitation quand on te calomnie mais souffre-le pour l’amour du Christ. Aime tes ennemis et prie pour ceux qui disent du mal de toi et qui t’affligent. Souffre l’affliction plutôt que d’affliger les autres. Supporte le mépris plutôt que de mépriser autrui. Sois calomnié plutôt que de calomnier les autres.

Veille constamment à ne pas ne chercher que ton propre profit, mais prends toujours soin de ceux avec qui tu as des rapports, qu’ils soient jeunes ou vieux.

Instructions à mes filles Betgen et Tanneken, mes agneaux bien-aimés, je vous exhorte en toutes ces mêmes choses, afin que vous obéissiez aux commandements du Seigneur. Obéissez aussi à vos aînés et à tous ceux qui vous instruisent dans la vertu.

Soyez diligentes à faire votre ouvrage, et vous serez aimées partout où vous vivrez. Ne soyez pas querelleuses, bavardes, frivoles, orgueilleuses ou hargneuses dans la parole. Soyez bienveillantes, honorables et réservées, comme convient aux jeunes filles.

Priez le Seigneur pour la sagesse, et elle vous sera donnée. Apprenez assidûment à lire et à écrire, et prenez-y plaisir, et vous deviendrez sages. Prenez plaisir à chanter des psaumes, des hymnes et des cantiques spirituels. Apprenez à plaire au Seigneur dès votre jeunesse, comme les saintes femmes et les vierges d’autrefois. Esther aussi était une vierge qui craignait Dieu; elle était parée d’humilité, gracieuse, honorable, aimable et humble de cœur; ainsi elle plut à l’empereur Assuérus plus que toutes les autres vierges. –voir Esther 2:17. Mais même dans son haut rang elle n’était pas orgueilleuse. Bien qu’elle brillât en vêtements royaux, elle humilia son cœur par le jeûne et la prière au Seigneur, pour ses frères, afin qu’ils soient délivrés des mains de leurs ennemis. Elle ne se considérait pas meilleure que le moindre de ses frères.

Quand vous aurez atteint l’âge de la compréhension, veillez à vous orner des œuvres de l’Esprit telles que la bonté, la douceur, l’humilité, l’obéissance, la patience, la justice, la modestie, l’honneur, la pureté, la paix, la fermeté, la miséricorde, la sagesse, la diligence dans les bonnes œuvres, la foi, l’espérance et l’amour. Aimez Dieu au-dessus de tout ce qui est au monde et faites à votre prochain ce que vous voudriez que les hommes vous fassent. –voir Galates 5:22-23 et Tite 2:3-5. Rappelez-vous que Jésus a dit : Tu aimeras le Seigneur ton Dieu de tout ton cœur, de toute ton âme, et de toute ta pensée. C’est le premier et le plus grand commandement. Et le second lui est semblable: Tu aimeras ton prochain comme toi-même. De ces deux commandements dépendent toute la loi et les prophètes –Matthieu 22:37-40.

Réjouissons-nous et soyons dans l’allégresse, et donnons-lui gloire: car les noces de l’Agneau sont venues, et son épouse s’est préparée. Et il lui fut donné qu’elle se fût parée d’un fin lin, éclatant et pur: car le fin lin, ce sont les justes –Apocalypse 19:7-8. Mes filles, c’est là l’ornement des saints; travaillez pour un tel vêtement nuptial, afin que vous puissiez entrer aux noces de l’Agneau, où …les justes resplendiront comme le soleil dans le royaume de leur Père… –Matthieu 13:43. Puisse le Seigneur vous conduire comme il conduisit Israël hors d’Égypte, et vous amener à la Nouvelle Jérusalem, afin que nous puissions nous voir avec joie au jour de la résurrection. Je vous recommande au Seigneur, le Dieu d’Abraham, le Dieu d’Isaac et le Dieu de Jacob; qu’il vous garde jusqu’à la fin de vos vies.

En conclusion, Ô mes chers enfants, j’ai écrit ceci en larmes, vous avertissant par amour. Ma prière et ma sollicitude sont constamment pour votre salut. J’espère et prie sans cesse qu’il, dans sa miséricorde, vous préservera, comme il préserva Joseph, Moïse et Daniel au milieu des hommes méchants. Et il le fera si vous vous donnez de la peine à suivre la vérité.

Ceci est mon dernier adieu, mes chers agneaux. souvenez-vous toujours les uns des autres dans l’amour; apprenez assidûment à lire et à écrire et obéissez à chacun en ce qui est bien. Je vous dis adieu, mes chers enfants Betgen, David et Tanneken. Adieu à tous mes chers frères et sœurs, et amis partout.

Écrit par moi, Soetgen van den Houte, votre mère en chaînes; écrit à la hâte (tremblant de froid), par amour pour vous tous, amen.

Being a ruler over a group of people is marked with stress, hard decisions, and sleepless nights—certainly not a position for the mentally weak or immature. The position is difficult, be it sheriff, mayor, governor, or president. The average person does not fully mature until the age of 25, according to neuroscientific studies.1 And yet, in AD 54, a ruler was appointed who was only seventeen years old. This was no petty judge or political secretary. He was crowned ruler over one of the largest empires of the world at that time. The boy’s name was Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus—commonly called Nero. He was the fifth emperor of Rome.

Nero was not brought into power by any election or choice of his citizens. His mother, Agrippina, had married Caesar Claudius (her uncle), emperor of Rome. Claudius adopted Nero as his son. Nero would go on to marry Claudius’ daughter Octavia, his own cousin and stepsister.

On October 13, A.D. 54, Agrippina poisoned her powerful husband, and her son Nero became emperor. It was rumored that Nero and his mother had an incestuous relationship, but the new ruler was well received by his subjects and seemed eager to please them, ordering grand public buildings to be built, as well as lowering taxes and the price of food. However, it was not to last.

Nero soon killed his brother-in-law, who was fourteen, which angered his wife. At this point, the emperor was in a relationship with a freedwoman (a formerly enslaved person), so he had his wife exiled. When this sparked public outrage, he had Octavia beheaded on false charges of being unfaithful.

He then became infatuated with a woman named Poppaea Sabina, who was scheming to marry him. Sabina roused Nero to such fear and jealousy that he decided to kill his mother for fear of losing the throne. The plan was simple—while Agrippina was on a cruise ship, it would be discreetly sunk, and Nero’s mother would drown. However, this was not to be. Agrippina was a strong swimmer and escaped with her life. Undeterred, Nero dispatched his executioners to stab her to death in broad daylight. Unfortunately, things had just gotten started for the most powerful man in the empire and these bizarre and inhuman acts were only a sampling of what was to come.

Nero was given to fits of rage and became violent towards his wife in one such outburst. He kicked Sabina repeatedly until both she and her unborn child died. Nero is said to have regretted this, and he soon started a hunt for anyone who looked like Sabina, his dead wife. He finally found a slave that is said to have resembled her strongly, and they were married. The catch? The slave was a man. Nero took to dressing him in the clothing of a woman and referring to him as a lady. At this point, Nero’s slippery slope was only getting more slippery. He believed himself to be an artist—a genius, even—and gave massive public performances. If you were in attendance, you could not leave. Why? The doors were locked. Nero also dreamed of singing to his enemies and bringing them to tears for their perceived wrongdoings.

But the emperor was not content with only putting on musical performances. In A.D. 67, he entered into the Olympic Games, which was against the rules (no emperor was allowed to compete in the Games). Nevertheless, Nero entered. He introduced new competitions, such as trumpeting and acting. He entered into several and won each one. His actions caused much outrage since the Olympics were considered a sacred event and Nero had changed them.

However, Nero had an even bigger goal in mind. The chariot races were the biggest spectacle the Olympics had to offer. In them, chariot riders were allowed a team of four horses. Teams would race around a massive arena for a total of seven laps. Sometimes wheels fell off, or chariots crashed into each other. It was not uncommon for drivers to be thrown from their ride and to be trampled to death or to be dragged by their own team of horses. However, the winner would be celebrated and highly paid.

Knowing all the difficulty, danger, and stress involved, you can only imagine how the charioteers felt to see Emperor Nero roll up to the racetrack in an expensive chariot and a team consisting of not four, but ten horses. As it turns out, Nero was inexperienced and out of shape. Almost immediately, he lost control of his team and was thrown from the chariot, being seriously injured in the process. Despite never finishing the race, Nero won first place.

This incident does a good job of demonstrating Nero’s attitude toward his authority at this point in his reign. In fact, in A.D. 66, he won more than 1,800 first-place prizes for his supposed exhibits of artistry. Here was a man that could not be told “no”.

On the night of July 18, A.D. 64, a fire started in Rome’s Circus Maximus. The fire grew and spread, becoming out of control. The fire would rage for the next six days, leaving almost no part of the city untouched. It was devastating for the citizens of Rome and would go on to be the incident Nero would be most widely known for. Many ancient writers blamed Nero for starting the fire, although he was not in the city when it began. Whether or not he started the fire, Nero needed someone to blame. He chose a group of people who were despised and feared by the Romans and tortured them relentlessly. That group was known as the Christians. Tacitus, a secular Roman writer, described it as such, “Nero fastened the guilt and inflicted the most exquisite tortures on a class hated for their abominations, called Christians by the populace. Mockery of every sort was added to their deaths. Covered with the skins of beasts, they were torn by dogs and perished, or were nailed to crosses, or were doomed to the flames and burnt, to serve as nightly illumination when daylight had expired.”

Meanwhile, Nero grew even more wicked. He ruthlessly slaughtered Christian men, women, and children, and plunged ever deeper into immorality. Finally, On June 9, AD 68, Nero, the last emperor of Rome killed himself after having been declared a public enemy by the Roman Senate. He was only 31 years old.

So, here is a man corrupt in every way. His lifestyle was deeply offensive to Christianity, and his persecution was one of the most horrible in history. How would we respond to such a ruler? How did Christians respond to him?

Paul lived under Nero’s reign. He saw all the horrible things detailed above. Yet, he gave the church the following admonition: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake –Romans 13: 1-5.

These words seem impossible when we consider the situation. Yet the Word of God tells us that our governmental authorities are put in place by God Himself. What a testimony! How much more, then, are we called to respect our authorities—to not slander them; to obey them in all possible aspects; to stay away from their elections and campaigns; and yet, to yield ourselves to God and His authority as our final say?! Or, as Paul put it, Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God… –Romans 13:1.

The believers of the early church saw Nero—the murderous, bloodthirsty, corrupt emperor—as a man ordained of God. They sought to honor and respect him in his authority, while ultimately yielding to the higher authority of God. Herein, we see a potential paradox, that the earthly authorities are “ministers of God” to be honored and obeyed, yet IF the time would come wherein the believer is required by the civil authorities to disobey God, we then have a higher responsibility—…We ought to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29.

This all puts a great responsibility on our shoulders today as Christians living in an increasingly corrupt and evil society. Can we find that biblical balance between honoring our governmental leaders while still obeying God in all things? Or do we fail just like the unregenerate around us in picking apart the faults of our earthly authorities when we feel our “easy living” being trodden upon?

See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is –Ephesians 5:15-17. And Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful –1 Corinthians 4:2.

Let each one of us as committed, born-again, Bible-believing Christians walk circumspectly, redeeming the time. For we all want to be found faithful in that soon-coming day when we all will stand before the judgment seat to receive our just reward.

Om ’n heerser oor ’n groep mense te wees, gaan gepaard met spanning, moeilike besluite en slapelose nagte—sekerlik nie ’n posisie vir die geestelik swak of onvolwasse nie. Die amp is moeilik, of dit nou ’n skofthoof, burgemeester, goewerneur of president is. Volgens neurowetenskaplike studies word die gemiddelde persoon nie ten volle volwassen tot omtrent 25 jaar nie.1 En tog is daar in n.C. 54 ’n heerser aangestel wat slegs sewentien jaar oud was. Dit was geen gering regter of politiek sekretaris nie. Hy is gekroon as heerser oor een van die grootste ryke van daardie tyd. Die seun se naam was Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus—algemeen Nero genoem. Hy was die vyfde keiser van Rome.

Nero is nie deur ’n verkiesing of die keuse van sy burgers aan bewind gebring nie. Sy moeder, Agrippina, het met Caesar Claudius (haar oom) getrou, die keiser van Rome. Claudius het Nero as sy seun aangeneem. Nero sou later Claudius se dogter Octavia, sy eie niggie en stiefsuster, trou.

Op 13 Oktober n.C. 54 het Agrippina haar magtige man vergiftig en haar seun Nero is keiser geword. Daar is gerugte dat Nero en sy moeder ’n incestuele verhouding gehad het, maar die nuwe heerser is goed deur sy onderdane ontvang en het gelyk of hy hulle wou behaag: hy beveel grootskaalse openbare geboue, verlaagde belasting en verlaagde voedselpryse. Dit het egter nie lank geduur nie.

Nero het kort daarna sy swaer, wat veertien was, vermoor, wat sy vrou woedend gemaak het. Teen hierdie tyd het die keiser ’n verhouding gehad met ’n bevryde vrou (’n voorheen slaaf), en hy het sy vrou verban. Toe dit openbare verontwaardiging ontketen het, het hy Octavia op valse aanklagte van ontrouheid laat onthoof.

Hy het toe verlief geraak op ’n vrou met die naam Poppaea Sabina, wat sameswering gemaak het om hom te trou. Sabina het Nero tot so ’n vrees en jaloesie aangevuur dat hy besluit het om sy moeder te vermoor uit vrees om die troon te verloor. Die plan was eenvoudig—terwyl Agrippina op ’n rondvaartboot was, sou dit heimlik laat sink en Nero se moeder sou verdrink. Dit het egter nie gebeur nie. Agrippina was ’n sterk swemmer en het haar lewe gespaar. Onverstoord het Nero sy uitvoerders gestuur om haar in die openbaar af te steek. Ongelukkig was dit net die begin vir die magtigste man in die ryk, en hierdie bisarre en onmenslike dade was slegs ’n voorsmakie van wat sou kom.

Nero het buie van woede gehad en is in een sulke uitbarsting geweldadig teenoor sy vrou. Hy het Sabina herhaaldelik geskop totdat sy en haar ongeboorte kind dood was. Nero sou berou oor dit gevoel het, en hy het gou ’n jag op enigiemand begin wat soos Sabina gelyk het, sy dooie vrou. Uiteindelik het hy ’n slaaf gevind wat na bewering sterk na haar gelyk het, en hulle is getroud. Die vangst? Die slaaf was ’n man. Nero het hom in vroueklere laat aantrek en na hom as ’n dame verwys. Teen hierdie tyd het Nero se glybaan net glibberiger geraak. Hy het homself as ’n kunstenaar—ja, ’n genie—gesien en het massiewe openbare optredes gegee. As jy teenwoordig was, kon jy nie vertrek nie. Waarom nie? Die deure is gesluit. Nero het ook daarvan gedroom om vir sy vyande te sing en hulle tot trane te beweeg oor wat hy as hul oortredings beskou het.

Maar die keiser het nie daarin gesien om net musiekuitvoerings te gee nie. In n.C. 67 het hy aan die Olimpiese Spele deelgeneem, wat teen die reëls was (geen keiser was toegelaat om aan die Spele deel te neem nie). Nietemin het Nero ingeskryf. Hy het nuwe kompetisies ingestel, soos trompette en toneelspel. Hy het aan verskeie deelgeneem en elkeen gewen. Sy optrede het veel verontwaardiging veroorsaak aangesien die Olimpiese Spele as ’n heilige gebeurtenis beskou is en Nero dit verander het.

Nero het egter ’n nog groter doel voor oë gehad. Die strydwa-renne was die grootste vertoning wat die Olimpiese Spele aangebied het. Daarin was strydwagbestuurders toegelaat om ’n span van vier perde te hê. Spanlede sou sewe rondes om ’n massiewe arena jaag. Soms het wiele afgeval of strydwaens in mekaar vasgery. Dit was nie ongewoon dat bestuurders uit hul waens gegooi is en vertrap of deur hul eie perde meegesleep is nie. Die wenner sou egter gevier en hoog betaal word.

Met al die moeilikheid, gevaar en spanning for eyes, kan jy net jou voorstel hoe die strydwagbestuurders gevoel het toe Keiser Nero in ’n duur strydwa met ’n span nie van vier nie, maar tien perde op die renbaan aangery kom. Soos dit blyk, was Nero onervare en uit vorm. Byna onmiddellik het hy die beheer oor sy span verloor en van die strydwa gegooi, en ernstig beseer. Ondanks dat hy die wedren nie voltooi het nie, het Nero eerste plek gewen.

Hierdie voorval illustreer goed Nero se houding teenoor sy gesag teen hierdie tyd in sy bewind. In werklikheid het hy in n.C. 66 meer as 1 800 eerste plek pryse gewen vir sy veronderstelde uitstallings van kuns. Hier was ’n man aan wie nie “nee” gesê kon word nie.

In die nag van 18 Julie n.C. 64 het ’n vuur in Rome se Circus Maximus begin. Die vuur het gegroei en versprei en buite beheer geraak. Die brand het die volgende ses dae woedend gebrand en min dele van die stad ongeskonde gelaat. Dit was verwoestend vir die burgers van Rome en sou die voorval wees waarvoor Nero die mees wydbekende reputasie sou dra. Baie antieke skrywers het Nero daarvan beskuldig dat hy die vuur aangesteek het, alhoewel hy nie in die stad was toe dit begin het nie. Of hy die vuur begin het of nie, Nero het iemand nodig gehad om die skuld te dra. Hy het ’n groep mense gekies wat deur die Romeine veragte en gevrees is en hulle genadeloos gefolter. Daardie groep is deur die volk Christene genoem. Tacitus, ’n sekulêre Romeinse skrywer, het dit so beskryf: “Nero fastened the guilt and inflicted the most exquisite tortures on a class hated for their abominations, called Christians by the populace. Mockery of every sort was added to their deaths. Covered with the skins of beasts, they were torn by dogs and perished, or were nailed to crosses, or were doomed to the flames and burnt, to serve as nightly illumination when daylight had expired.”

Intussen het Nero nog slegter geword. Hy het Christelike mans, vroue en kinders meedogenloos afgeslag en het steeds dieper in immoraliteit weggesak. Uiteindelik het Nero op 9 Junie n.C. 68, die laaste keiser van Rome, selfmoord gepleeg nadat hy deur die Romeinse Senaat as ’n openbare vyand verklaar is. Hy was slegs 31 jaar oud.

So, hier is ’n man wat in elke opsig korrup is. Sy leefstyl was diep aanstootlik vir die Christendom, en sy vervolging was een van die gruwelikste in die geskiedenis. Hoe sou ons op so ’n heerser reageer? Hoe het Christene werklik op hom gereageer?

Pawul het onder Nero se bewind geleef. Hy het al die verskriklike dinge hierbo gesien. Tog het hy die kerk die volgende aansporing gegee: Laat elke siel aan die magte wat bo haar is onderwerp wees. Want daar is geen mag behalwe van God nie: die magte wat daar is, is deur God bestel. Wie daarom die magte verset, verset die bestel van God; en dié wat daarteen in opstand kom, sal ’n veroordeling ontvang. Want die regering is nie ’n skrik vir die goeie daad nie, maar vir die kwaad. Wil jy dan nie die mag vrees nie? Doen wat goed is en jy sal lof van haar ontvang: want sy is ’n dienstelike van God tot jou ten goede. Maar as jy kwaad doen, wees bevrees; want sy dra die swaard nie tevergeefs: sy is ’n dienares van God, ’n wreker om die toorn uit te voer oor hom wat kwaad doen. Daarom moet julle onderwerp wees, nie alleen weens die toorn nie, maar ook weens die gewete. –Romeine 13:1-5.

Hierdie woorde lyk onmoontlik gesien die omstandighede. Tog leer die Woord van God ons dat ons regeringsowerhede deur God Self in plek gehou word. Wat ’n getuie! Hoeveel meer word ons dan geroep om ons owerhede te respekteer—om hulle nie te laster nie; om hulle in alle moontlike opsigte te gehoorsaam; om weg te bly van hul verkiesings en veldtogte; en tog om ons aan God en Sy gesag as ons finale gesag te onderwerp?! Of, soos Pawul dit stel, Laat elke siel aan die magte wat bo haar is onderwerp wees. Want daar is geen mag behalwe van God nie… –Romeine 13:1.

Die gelowiges van die vroeë kerk het Nero—die moorddadige, bloeddriftige, korrupte keiser—as ’n man gesien wat deur God beveel is. Hulle het gestreef om hom in sy gesag te eer en te respekteer, terwyl hulle uiterlik aan die hoër gesag van God onderwerp gebly het. Hierin sien ons ’n moontlike paradoks: aardse owerhede is “dienaars van God” wat geëer en gehoorsaam moet word, maar AS die tyd sou kom waarin die gelowige deur die burgerlike owerhede vereis word om God te ongehoorsaam, dra ons dan ’n hoër verantwoordelikheid—…Ons behoort God te gehoorsaam eerder as mense –Handelinge 5:29.

Dit plaas ’n groot verantwoordelikheid op ons skouers vandag as Christene wat in ’n toenemend korrupte en bose samelewing leef. Kan ons daardie Bybelse balans vind tussen die eer van ons regeringsleiers terwyl ons steeds God in alles gehoorsaam? Of misluk ons soos die ongeregenerate rondom ons deur die foute van ons aardse owerhede uit te pluk wanneer ons voel dat ons “gemaklike lewe” getrap word?

Sien dan dat julle verstandig wandel, nie as stommes nie, maar as wyse, die tyd uitkogend, omdat die dae boos is. Wees dan nie onverstandig nie, maar verstaan wat die wil van die Here is –Efesiërs 5:15-17. En Laat ’n mens so oor ons dink as oor Christus se dienaars en as oor die huishoudmeesters van God se raaisels. Nou is dit van huishoudmeesters vereis, dat ’n mens trou gevind word –1 Korintiërs 4:1-2.

Laat elkeen van ons as toegewyde, wedergebore, Bybel-gelowige Christene verstandig wandel en die tyd uitkoop. Want ons almal wil getrou bevind word in daardie naderende dag wanneer ons voor die oordeelstoel sal staan om ons billike beloning te ontvang.
