Salutations d’amour au nom de Jésus ! Nous avons un grand Dieu qui mérite toute notre louange, tout notre amour et toute notre vie !

Nous vivons à une époque où il y a beaucoup de distractions. Le prince de ce monde cherche véritablement à détruire la vie des gens, quel qu’en soit le prix. Nous avons des parcs d’attractions, des salles d’arcade, des théâtres, Internet, Facebook, des centres commerciaux de la mode et tout ce que vous pouvez imaginer — tout cela existe. Mais Dieu veut que nos cœurs soient remués pour ne pas être enlacés par ces distractions, mais plutôt pour travailler pour Lui et pour Son royaume. Si nous sommes enlacés par les affaires de cette vie, il ne nous restera plus de temps pour notre Seigneur. Nous ne pouvons servir deux maîtres. Il semble qu’il existe des choses qui essaient de voler le temps de nos chères sœurs (jeunes et âgées). Soyons conscientes de ces choses afin d’en être libérées et d’être alors libres de servir le Seigneur de tout notre cœur.

La première chose dont nous devons être conscientes s’appelle l’ornement, et l’autre est la folie ou la légèreté. Il m’est si étonnant de voir comment Dieu agit. Il nous dit dans Sa Parole ce dont il ne faut pas nous parer, mais Il nous dit aussi ce dont il faut nous parer. Il nous dit quels fruits devraient sortir de nos vies, et quels fruits ne devraient pas en sortir. Pour chaque mauvaise voie qui existe, Dieu nous montre aussi la voie droite. Je sais que beaucoup d’entre nous n’iraient pas dans des centres commerciaux de la mode pour acheter leurs vêtements, mais je crains que beaucoup d’entre nous cherchent encore des vêtements qui accentuent le corps plutôt que de glorifier notre Seigneur. Jésus a dit : Heureux les cœurs purs, car ils verront Dieu – Matthew 5:8.

Que l’ornement des femmes ne soit pas les cheveux tressés, ni l’or, ni les vêtements qu’elles portent ; mais qu’elles se parent de l’homme intérieur du cœur, de ce qui ne périt point, d’un esprit doux et paisible, qui est d’un grand prix devant Dieu. Car c’est ainsi que naguère aussi les saintes qui espéraient en Dieu s’ornaient, en étant soumises à leurs maris ; comme Sara obéissait à Abraham, l’appelant seigneur : de qui vous êtes les filles, si vous faites le bien, et si vous n’avez pas peur d’aucune frayeur – 1 Peter 3:3-6.

Adorner : parer ou embellir ; mettre en valeur ; embellir par quelque chose d’externe ou d’accessoire ; montrer la beauté ou l’excellence.

Souvenez-vous, Dieu veut que nous nous parions de choses qui Lui rendront gloire. Selon le type de vêtements que je choisis de porter, l’attention des autres est d’abord attirée par mes vêtements, au lieu de mon visage. Quand cela arrive, je reçois toute la gloire parce que l’attention porte sur mon habillement. Mais si quelqu’un me voit et peut voir la clarté de mon visage et peut dire que j’ai été avec Jésus, alors il rendra à Dieu toute la gloire qu’Il mérite, et nous montrerons la beauté ou l’excellence de l’esprit de Dieu dans nos vies.

Examinons maintenant quelques autres mots que l’on trouve dans notre texte scripturaire et considérons leur sens :

Plaiting (tressage) : replier, doubler, tresser.

Apparel (habillement) : vêtements ; habillements externes ou décorations.

Ornament (ornement) : ce qui embellit ; ou quelque chose qui, ajouté à une autre chose, la rend la plus belle aux yeux.

Comme il est beau pour notre Seigneur quand nous naissons de nouveau, que nous avons un esprit brisé, et que nous devenons doux et paisibles. Les gens peuvent-ils voir les fruits de l’Esprit de Dieu dans nos vies — comme des ornements ? Vraiment c’est un ornement d’un grand prix. Souvenez-vous que nous pouvons ajouter des ornements externes à nos vies qui attristent notre Père. Ne le faisons pas honteux de nous appeler Ses fils et Ses filles.

Meek (doux) : tempérament doux ; tendre ; gentil ; qui ne se provoque ni ne s’irrite facilement ; soumis, enclin à la patience face aux offenses.

Sommes-nous irritées si quelqu’un a quelque chose à nous dire qui nous aidera dans notre marche avec le Seigneur ? Souvenez-vous que notre Seigneur veut le fruit de la douceur parant nos vies converties.

Quiet (paisible) : immobile ; étant dans un état de repos ; ne bougeant pas ; paisible ; non turbulent ; ne donnant pas d’offense ; n’excitant pas la controverse, le désordre ou le trouble ; doux ; humble ; content.

À chaque nouvelle mode qui apparaît parmi nous, sommes-nous prompts à changer pour aucune autre raison que d’ajouter quelque chose à nos corps qui ne fait que nous rendre gloire ? Sommes-nous contentes de la norme biblique de Dieu pour nos vies ? Sommes-nous fermes et ancrées dans ce que nous croyons ? Savons-nous pourquoi nous croyons ce que nous croyons ?

Subjection (soumission) : l’acte de soumettre ; l’acte de vaincre et de mettre sous la domination d’un autre.

Sommes-nous sous la domination de notre Seigneur dans chaque aspect de nos vies ?

Afraid (effrayées) : saisies par la peur ou l’appréhension.

Amazement (stupéfaction) : étonnement ; confusion ou perplexité causée par une impression soudaine de peur, de surprise ou d’émerveillement.

Nous sommes filles de Sara tant que nous faisons le bien, et que nous ne sommes pas saisies par la peur ni par quelque confusion ou perplexité. Dieu n’est pas l’auteur de la confusion — La loi de l’Éternel est parfaite, elle restaure l’âme… – Psalm 19:7. Rappelez-vous : La crainte de l’Éternel est le commencement de la sagesse [et non de la confusion]… – Proverbs 9:10.

Entangleth (enlacer) : tordre ou entrelacer de telle manière qu’on ne peut pas facilement séparer ; perplexer ou distraire, comme par des soucis.

Permettons-nous que nos vies soient entrelacées avec les modes et la folie de ce monde ?

Aucun soldat engagé dans la guerre ne s’encombre des affaires de la vie ; il le fait afin de plaire à celui qui l’a enrôlé. Fuis aussi les propos vains et profanes : car ils avanceront vers une plus grande impiété. Éloigne-toi aussi des passions de la jeunesse ; et recherche la justice, la foi, la charité, la paix, avec ceux qui invoquent le Seigneur d’un cœur pur – 2 Timothy 2:4-22.

Shun (éviter) : éviter ; se tenir à l’écart ; ne pas tomber sur ou entrer en contact avec ; ne pas mélanger ni fréquenter.

Évitons-nous les pratiques de ce monde ? Plus précisément, évitons-nous la conversation légère et vaine ?

Profane : irrévérencieux envers ce qui est sacré ; pollué ; impur.

Vain (vain) : vide ; sans valeur ; n’ayant ni substance, ni valeur, ni importance.

Ce dont nous nous emplissons ressortira. Si nous nous emplissons de la sainte Parole de Dieu, alors cela coulera de nos vies. Cependant, si nous nous emplissons de choses vaines, cela ressortira aussi.

Babblings (babillages) : paroles folles.

Notre conversation est-elle centrée sur la Bible, ou est-elle centrée sur les nouvelles choses que nous avons achetées comme un nouveau vêtement ou un véhicule, ou peut‑être sur toutes les personnes que nous avons rencontrées sur Facebook ?

Flee (fuir) : courir rapidement, comme pour échapper au danger ; se hâter pour échapper au danger ou au mal attendu.

Si nous sommes avec un groupe de personnes dont la conversation est folle, restons‑nous par peur de perdre des amies ou marchons‑nous (ou courons‑nous) loin du mal attendu ou dangereux ? Plus nous entrelaçons nos vies aux voies du monde, plus il est difficile de nous en démêler.

Lusts (passions) : désir ardent ; empressement à posséder ou à jouir ; appétit charnel ; désir illicite de plaisir charnel.

Dieu nous donnera les véritables désirs de notre cœur. Nous pouvons dire que nous désirons des choses pures, mais si notre cœur aspire à des choses illicites, nous céderons à ces choses. Nos vies ne consistent pas seulement en ce que nous disons, mais plus important encore en ce que nous vivons. Prenez courage : les désirs intérieurs de notre cœur peuvent être changés à jamais par l’opération spirituelle ou la « nouvelle naissance ».

Righteousness (justice) : l’obéissance active et passive du Christ, par laquelle la loi de Dieu est accomplie.

Si nous devons suivre la justice, cela signifie que nous devons suivre l’obéissance active et passive que le Christ nous montre par son exemple.

Faith (foi) : l’objet de la croyance ; une doctrine ou un système de doctrines cru(e)s.

Quelle est la réalité de notre foi ? Croyons‑nous vraiment en Dieu et en ce qu’Il nous dit par Sa Parole écrite ? C’est parce qu’Abraham crut à Dieu qu’il put « offrir » son fils unique Isaac, par qui la postérité d’Abraham serait comptée. – voir Hebrews 11:17 et Genesis 22:13. Si Dieu nous dit dans Sa Parole d’éviter l’impiété parce qu’elle mène à plus d’impiété, alors nous devons croire Dieu et fuir ces choses, et nous ne devons pas nous permettre de penser qu’un peu de plaisir n’aura pas d’importance.

Charity (charité) : amour ; bienveillance ; bonne volonté ; cette disposition du cœur qui incline l’homme à penser favorablement à son prochain et à lui faire du bien ; elle comprend l’amour suprême pour Dieu notre Créateur et une bonne volonté universelle envers les hommes.

Avons‑nous l’amour de Dieu habitant en nous et coulant de nos vies comme une source d’eau vive ?

Peace (paix) : repos céleste ; harmonie ; liberté de perturbation ou d’agitation.

Nous devons suivre l’exemple de notre cher Sauveur Jésus-Christ dont toute la vie fut en parfaite harmonie avec Dieu le Père. Christ n’était pas troublé ni perturbé par les voies de ce monde, mais Il était en repos faisant la volonté de Son Père. Et nous ?

Pure (pur) : clair ; exempt de souillure morale ; sans tache ; saint ; incorruptible.

Nous devons avoir ces fruits parant nos vies et les pratiquer aussi avec ceux qui pratiquent les mêmes choses dans leurs propres vies. Un peu de levain lève toute la pâte.

De même aussi, que les femmes se parent d’habillements modestes, avec pudeur et modestie ; non pas de cheveux tressés, ni d’or, ni de perles, ni d’un vêtement coûteux ; mais (ce qui convient aux femmes qui professent la piété) avec de bonnes œuvres – 1 Timothy 2:9-10.

Shamefacedness (pudeur) : timidité ; excès de modestie.

Nous devons être ornées de pudeur et non d’étourderie ou de sensualité.

Sobriety (sérieux) : sobriété habituelle ; sérieux ; gravité sans tristesse ni mélancolie.

Même si nous sommes sobres, nous n’avons pas besoin d’être tristes mais nous pouvons avoir la joie du Seigneur parant nos vies. Il devrait y avoir une lumière dans nos yeux parce que Jésus est la lumière de nos vies. Vraiment, si l’Esprit de Dieu habite en nous, nous avons tant de choses pour lesquelles être reconnaissantes. Cela devrait être évident dans chaque aspect de nos vies.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Car la grâce de Dieu qui apporte le salut a été manifestée à tous les hommes, nous instruisant pour repousser l’impiété et les convoitises mondaines, et pour vivre dans ce monde présent sobrement, justement et pieusement – Titus 2:11-12.

Je me réjouirai avec une grande joie en l’Éternel, Mon âme sera joyeuse en mon Dieu ; car il m’a revêtu des vêtements du salut, il m’a couvert du manteau de la justice, comme un époux se pare d’ornements, et comme une fiancée se pare de ses bijoux – Isaiah 61:10.

Les ornements de modestie, de pudeur, de sérieux, de foi, de charité, de paix, de justice, de douceur et de tranquillité sont vraiment des bijoux d’un grand prix. Ces bijoux sont si précieux qu’il vaut la peine d’abandonner nos vies entières au Dieu des cieux, notre Créateur et notre Rédempteur, afin que nous puissions les avoir ornant nos vies. Mais de même, si nous sommes livrées au dieu de ce monde nous aurons les ornements de l’orgueil, de l’envie, de la haine, de la jalousie, et ainsi de suite. Lesquels sont les plus beaux ?

Et je Jean vis la ville sainte, la nouvelle Jérusalem, descendre d’auprès de Dieu du ciel, prête comme une épouse qui s’est parée pour son mari. Et j’entendis une grande voix venant du ciel qui disait : Voici la tente de Dieu avec les hommes, et il habitera avec eux, et ils seront son peuple, et Dieu lui‑même sera avec eux, et sera leur Dieu. – Revelation 21:2-3.

Nous préparons‑nous à rencontrer Jésus ? Dieu habite‑t‑Il en nous ? Est‑Il notre Dieu et sommes‑nous son peuple ?

Souvenez‑vous que le temps passe rapidement. Nous pouvons être ici aujourd’hui et partis demain. Voulons‑nous être avec Jésus pour toute l’éternité, ou voulons‑nous être avec le diable et ses anges ? Les choix que nous faisons pour nos vies aujourd’hui auront un impact sur l’endroit où nous passerons l’éternité.

Ne vous y trompez pas ; on ne se moque pas de Dieu : ce qu’un homme aura semé, il le moissonnera aussi – Galatians 6:7. Ne soyez pas induites en erreur. Ce verset s’adresse aussi au croyant, pas seulement à l’impénitent. Chacune de nous peut se demander ce qu’elle sème. Concernant l’ornement, semons‑nous la pensée que la beauté extérieure est très importante ou semons‑nous la pensée que la beauté intérieure est la chose la plus précieuse à posséder et à obtenir ? Pour clarifier, je ne parle pas d’être sale et négligée. Dieu est un Dieu d’ordre et de propreté, mais Il n’est pas un Dieu de rubans, de nœuds, de froufrous, de dentelles et de vêtements coûteux et séduisants. Souvenez‑vous que la plupart des personnes qui créent de nouvelles modes vestimentaires se concentrent sur la conception de vêtements de manière à ce qu’ils soient attrayants et agréables à l’œil. C’est ce qui pousse les gens à les acheter.

Encore, quand les gens nous regardent glorifient‑ils notre corps charnel ou louent‑ils Dieu pour l’œuvre qu’Il accomplit dans nos vies ? Aussi, concernant la folie et la légèreté, si nous sommes ancrées dans la parole de Dieu, nous n’aurons pas de temps pour des babillages vains et l’oisiveté à la recherche du plaisir. Soyons occupées à faire l’œuvre de notre Seigneur, comme aider notre voisin qui pourrait avoir besoin d’un coup de main, ou partager notre témoignage avec les personnes que nous rencontrons.

Et ne craignez point ceux qui tuent le corps, et qui après n’ont rien davantage à faire ; craignez plutôt celui qui peut faire périr l’âme et le corps dans la géhenne – Matthew 10:28. Alors que nous vivons en ces derniers temps, le message qui nous entoure est que tant que tu crois en un Dieu, tout ira bien. C’est un message faux. Jésus nous dit qu’il n’y a qu’un seul chemin. Jésus lui dit : Je suis le chemin, la vérité, et la vie ; nul ne vient au Père que par moi. Si vous m’aviez connu, vous auriez connu aussi mon Père ; et dès maintenant vous le connaissez, et vous l’avez vu – John 14:6-7. Louez le Seigneur que Dieu nous ait donné un exemple à suivre.

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb –Exodus 3:1.

The back side of the desert has long been understood as God’s school wherewith He has instructed many of His servants, of whom Moses stands chief. At the prime age of 40, he found himself …learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel –Acts 7:22-23.

I have no doubt that God can, and does, use men of great ability, capacity, and training, but spiritual leadership requires an ingredient that is not derived from doing, attaining, and accomplishing. The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh. This pride and restlessness is not dealt with in a seminary nor is it normally exterminated during vigilant duty. For many of God’s servants, it is extracted from the soul on the soil of deserted sands. This arid and abandoned acreage that appears void of life and fruitfulness is where many servants learn to put their face in the dust and yield to what may seem to be inactivity, unfruitfulness, and rejection.

Moses’ life could be divided into three sections. He spent his first forty years learning the wisdom of Egypt, the next forty as a shepherd in Midian, and a final forty as the shepherd of Israel. We can imagine that the first third of his pilgrimage was filled with tremendous activity, advancement, and accomplishment. It had undoubtedly been rehearsed to him that at his birth he …was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months –Acts 7:20.

The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter would serve to confirm that he was destined to be an instrument of God’s divine orchestration. As a centerpiece of national attention, it is certainly understandable how this man who …was mighty in words and in deeds –Acts 7:22, was brimming with self-confidence in his ability to accomplish God’s bidding.

In today’s economy, Moses would be esteemed as the ideal candidate for church leadership. He was in every way qualified. He stood above his countrymen in education, and he possessed above-normal natural, financial, and spiritual endowments. He had emerged from the “University” of Egypt as a man mighty in word and deed and he had an obvious call from God upon his life. He was a conservative man who chose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25.

Still, amidst all his fine credentials he was yet deficient for the work that God had called him to. And so, God conveniently conducted him into the land of Midian to enroll him in another school to feed upon the bitter herbs of disappointment and rejection, obscurity and loneliness, and unfulfilled dreams and longings. While it was his earlier ambition to voluntarily align himself with the people of God, this chapter of his life was enacted by compulsion.

We learn from the account in Exodus that the latter third of his life was loaded with intricate involvement and major ministry. While the exit from Egypt is an exciting read and provides great insight, most of us cannot honestly relate to the mighty Moses and his dynamic coalition with God. Rather, it is the uneventful 40-year mid-section of his life that many of us find ourselves in. Though there are but a few dozen verses that represent these four decades of his life, we assume that it was a thorough schooling that inscribed immense patience, soul searching, and perhaps a bit of frustration.

For us, it represents a period when the parched sands of time about us seem to be producing nothing more fruitful than a revelation of our dry, crusty heart—shriveled and wasted by the consequences of our failures and past sins. It is at these times that we can have a lapse in faith, not that we blame God for our circumstances, but that we may begin to see our lives as futile, and that each day is the same as the previous one. Perhaps we begin to walk around in a visionless stupor—through a fog of spiritual depression—as we grope for encouragement and a reminder that God has not forgotten us. At times, it even seems that our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over. During extended times of trials and testing, we can feel abandoned. We can even imagine that God has turned against us. We look up to Heaven and ask, “Why Lord?” We will never experience rejection and being forsaken to the extent that the Lord Jesus did, but when we experience them in our petty little realm, it seems to sap all our spiritual strength and vigor. We think… If the Lord should require forty years of this from us there would be no time left in our lives to capitalize on what we have learned. But God’s timing is perfect. Thus, it behooves us to not concern ourselves so much with the longevity of our schooling, but to be thoroughly acquainted with the message from Midian. While some receive the bitter strokes of Midian and retreat to stand cynically on the sidelines, we must shake off the dust of the desert and arise with an understanding of…

God’s Purpose

God has a purpose for every detail of our lives. He may plant us in a difficult position, to forge in us a new vocation. It was alone in Midian where Moses learned of his own pride, self-confidence, lack of faith, and the utter folly that his own hands had participated in. Here in his Midian, he was alone and yet not alone; numerous other saints have joined him there. The sons of Jacob and the wife of Potiphar sent another vibrant servant there—Joseph. The wild rage of a jealous king sent a gifted young harpist there. Even an old and foolish king who refused to be taught found himself in a wilderness eating grass like an ox until he recanted of his pride.

Throughout the pages of history, countless saints have realized that ‘the darker the valley, the more I learned to pray’. While they arrive at the threshold of the new day loaded down with bountiful exuberance, they are soon stripped naked in a metamorphic change and finally emerge with nothing but the rod of God in their hands. Gone are the days when they were swift to speak, swift to act, and slow to hear. In Midian, the student learns to shift his focus from, “I will do great things for God” to “What wilt thou have me to do?”

And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do –Acts 9:6. The new arrivals in Midian have many answers, but most of them involve a one-act-play with self as the main character. The graduates walk out silent and sober, for they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…

God’s Purging

The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts –Proverbs 17:3. As Moses passed through the gates of Midian, the first scene that God set before his eyes was an injustice at a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters… –Exodus 2:16, who were being driven away by a band of uncouth shepherds. But Moses had been well trained in every dimension of Egyptian plutocracy, which would have included all aspects of military expertise and worldly leadership skills. Thus, when he stepped in to assist the helpless shepherdesses, he would have been quite capable to do so. These daughters of the priest of Midian appreciated the help which they recounted to their father that …An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock –Exodus 2:19. Upon hearing this tale, their father, Reuel, was so impressed that he gave Moses a reception, a job, and a wife… all in one verse. –see Exodus 2:21.

…Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them –Mark 10:42. While Moses’ quest for justice may have been noble, his orientation was merely Gentile. This may work for establishing pecking order in a hen house, but it is destined for failure in leading forth the people of God. But … whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all –Mark 10:43-44.

This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well. Many good and talented men can successfully operate a business using Gentile authority, but it rarely works in their home, and it is even more futile in a church. Thus, God moved His chosen vessel from royalty to proletariat (the working class), almost overnight. He is then given a job which was loathed by the people who had trained him—…for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians –Genesis 46:34. This fining pot is not just to teach us a much-needed lesson, but to guide us into…

God’s Provision

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way –Psalm 25:9. God will never abandon us on the back side of the desert; instead, He tailors our life circumstances to bring us into His fullness. If we resist the temptation to espouse an attitude of anger, then God will be able to teach us His ways. But to Moses, the situation presented itself such that God’s divine direction was the last thing he would suspect was happening.

Happening…? It seemed that nothing was happening. The weeks melted into months, the months into years, and the years into decades, all the while the gifted Moses remained an underachieving shepherd. One of the hardest things that we struggle with is “waiting.” Almost every Christian will face a long time of tribulation and we are told to: …think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you –1 Peter 4:12. But we should not judge God’s means by our feeble sense, for in the meantime, the wonderful working of waiting prepares us for…

God’s Promotion

38, 39, … 40 years. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt –Exodus 3:10.

Perhaps God is enamored with the number 40, but more than likely, it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation. His self-esteem has been fully extinguished, and he humbly asks: …Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? –Exodus 3:11.

Moses was not less qualified than he was forty years prior to this time, but his presumption had evaporated in the heat of the desert sun. The experience gleaned in the rugged pastures with the stubborn sheep has brought him to the understanding that this will be nearly an impossible feat. But there is no ordained calling issued independently from…

God’s Promise

…Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain –Exodus 3:12.

Not that Moses had attained perfection, for we find Moses provoking God to anger in the very next chapter—And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses… –Exodus 4:14. Then soon again he is the direct object in the path of God’s sword—And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24. Even so, while his vessel is still made of clay, it has met with a firing that has prepared him for the Lord’s service, and for us God will not revoke His promises in the wind of our whims. Thus, the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14, has laid upon human shoulders the immense and eternal task of leading His people. But this charge is not to be executed without…

God’s Power

What was the real refinement from Moses’ time spent in the desert? We notice his rash willingness to wield the sword before his arrival, but upon his exit, he only bore a rod in his hand. With the sword he had overcome an Egyptian offender, but with the rod he overcame the entire forces of Egypt. The rod of God brought forth the water in the wilderness. It was the rod of God, that, when lifted high by feeble hands secured the victory over Amalek. What is the rod of God? Before his days in Midian, he hardly knew it existed. Forty years later there hardly exists a scene without it.

The rod is the power of God unto salvation. It is the wisdom of God, the truth of God, the testimony of God, but more than all of these it is the chastening of God. Without it, man does not receive nor perceive the love of God for without it man is not connected to God. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.

This same Moses, who at one time was willing to exercise lordship (Gentile authority) over God’s people now finds himself entreating God and staying His wrath from destroying them. The people who accused Moses of leading them out to kill them and even at one point were ready to stone him are now at the center of his heart and affection, even though they are at the cause of his failure to enter the promised land. This is the love of Christ. But where is this learned except under the rod of God, on the back side of the desert, in the Egyptian dungeons, in the caves of Adullam, in the straits of Arabia, and in the silent solitude of the back burner where God has ordained that many of His people go until they learn to …learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls –Matthew 11:29. Surely that is where Moses secured the character known to the biblical scholar as the meekest man to walk the face of the earth. Surely there is no more opposite place on earth to learn it but in the school of suffering.

And so here we shall abide as well, so that we …may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10.

Sekarang Musa menggembalakan kawanan domba Yitro, mertuanya, imam Madian; dan ia membawa kawanan itu ke belakang padang gurun, lalu datanglah ia ke gunung Allah, yaitu Horeb –Keluaran 3:1.

Belakang padang gurun sejak lama dipahami sebagai sekolah Allah tempat Ia mendidik banyak hamba-Nya, yang tertinggi di antaranya adalah Musa. Pada usia prima 40 tahun, ia mendapati dirinya …telah belajar segala kebijaksanaan orang Mesir, dan telah kuat akan perkataan dan perbuatan. Dan ketika ia genap berumur empat puluh tahun, timbullah dalam hatinya untuk mengunjungi saudara-saudaranya, orang-orang Israel –Kisah Para Rasul 7:22-23.

Saya tak ragu bahwa Allah dapat, dan memang memakai, orang-orang yang berbakat besar, berkapasitas, dan terlatih, tetapi kepemimpinan rohani memerlukan unsur yang tidak berasal dari melakukan, mencapai, dan meraih prestasi. Musibah kaum fanatik seringkali adalah terlalu sedikit percaya kepada Allah dan terlalu banyak percaya kepada daging. Kesombongan dan kegelisahan ini tidak ditangani di seminari maupun biasanya tidak dimusnahkan selama tugas yang teliti. Bagi banyak hamba Allah, hal itu dicabut dari jiwa di tanah berpasir tandus. Lahan kering dan ditinggalkan ini yang tampak kosong hidup dan kesuburan adalah tempat banyak hamba belajar menempelkan wajah mereka ke debu dan menyerah pada apa yang tampak sebagai ketidakaktifan, ketidakberbuah, dan penolakan.

Hidup Musa dapat dibagi menjadi tiga bagian. Ia menghabiskan empat puluh tahun pertama mempelajari kebijaksanaan Mesir, empat puluh tahun berikutnya sebagai gembala di Madian, dan empat puluh tahun terakhir sebagai gembala Israel. Kita dapat membayangkan bahwa sepertiga pertama dari peziarahannya dipenuhi aktivitas luar biasa, kemajuan, dan pencapaian. Tanpa diragukan lagi kepadanya telah diceritakan bahwa saat kelahirannya ia …sangat cantik rupa, dan diasuh di rumah ayahnya tiga bulan lamanya –Kisah Para Rasul 7:20.

Penyelamatan di sungai secara mujizat oleh putri Firaun akan mengonfirmasi bahwa ia ditakdirkan menjadi alat orchestrasi ilahi Allah. Sebagai pusat perhatian nasional, sangat dapat dimengerti bagaimana orang ini yang …kuat akan perkataan dan perbuatan –Kisah Para Rasul 7:22, penuh percaya diri akan kemampuannya melaksanakan kehendak Allah.

Dalam ekonomi masa kini, Musa akan dinilai sebagai kandidat ideal untuk kepemimpinan gereja. Ia dalam segala hal memenuhi syarat. Ia menonjol di atas bangsanya dalam pendidikan, dan ia memiliki karunia alamiah, finansial, dan rohani di atas rata‑rata. Ia muncul dari “Universitas” Mesir sebagai orang yang kuat dalam perkataan dan perbuatan dan ia memiliki panggilan yang nyata dari Allah atas hidupnya. Ia adalah orang konservatif yang memilih …lebih baik menderita sengsara bersama umat Allah daripada menikmati kenikmatan dosa untuk sementara waktu –Ibrani 11:25.

Namun, di tengah semua kredensialnya yang baik ia masih kekurangan untuk pekerjaan yang dipanggilnya. Maka, Allah dengan bijaksana membawanya ke tanah Madian untuk mendaftarkannya di sekolah lain agar ia memakan pahitnya kekecewaan dan penolakan, keterasingan dan kesepian, dan mimpi serta kerinduan yang tidak terpenuhi. Sementara sebelumnya ambisinya adalah dengan sukarela menyelaraskan dirinya dengan umat Allah, babak hidupnya ini dimainkan oleh paksaan.

Kita belajar dari catatan di Keluaran bahwa sepertiga terakhir hidupnya dipenuhi keterlibatan rumit dan pelayanan besar. Walau keluarnya dari Mesir adalah bacaan yang menggembirakan dan memberi wawasan besar, kebanyakan dari kita tidak dapat jujur berhubungan dengan Musa yang perkasa dan koalisi dinamisnya dengan Allah. Sebaliknya, adalah bagian tengah 40 tahun hidupnya yang tak berperistiwa itulah tempat banyak dari kita mendapati diri. Meski hanya ada beberapa puluh ayat yang mewakili empat dekade hidupnya ini, kita berasumsi bahwa itu adalah sekolah menyeluruh yang menanamkan kesabaran besar, pencarian jiwa, dan mungkin sedikit frustrasi.

Bagi kita, itu mewakili masa ketika pasir kering waktu di sekitar kita tampak tidak menghasilkan apa pun yang lebih berbuah selain menyingkap hati kita yang kering dan mengeras—menyusut dan terbuang oleh akibat kegagalan dan dosa-dosa masa lalu kita. Pada masa-masa inilah iman kita bisa goyah, bukan karena kita menyalahkan Allah atas keadaan kita, tetapi karena kita mungkin mulai melihat hidup kita sebagai sia‑sia, dan bahwa setiap hari sama seperti hari sebelumnya. Mungkin kita mulai berjalan tanpa visi—melalui kabut depresi rohani—sementara kita meraba untuk mendapatkan dorongan dan pengingat bahwa Allah belum melupakan kita. Kadang-kadang, tampak pula seolah-olah doa‑doa kita mengenai langit dan memantul kembali, menertawakan dan menipu kita dengan ejekan kelam bahwa kegunaan kita dalam Kerajaan Allah telah berakhir. Selama masa-masa panjang pencobaan dan ujian, kita dapat merasa ditinggalkan. Kita bahkan bisa membayangkan bahwa Allah telah berbalik melawan kita. Kita menengadah ke Surga dan bertanya, “Mengapa, Tuhan?” Kita tidak akan pernah mengalami penolakan dan ditinggalkan sampai sejauh yang Dialami oleh Tuhan Yesus, tetapi ketika kita mengalaminya dalam ranah remeh kita, hal itu tampak menguras seluruh kekuatan dan semangat rohani kita. Kita berpikir… Jika Tuhan menuntut empat puluh tahun ini dari kita, tidak akan ada waktu lagi dalam hidup kita untuk memanfaatkan apa yang telah kita pelajari. Tetapi waktu Allah sempurna. Oleh karena itu, semestinya kita tidak terlalu mempermasalahkan lamanya masa sekolah kita, melainkan menjadi benar‑benar mengenal pesan dari Madian. Sementara beberapa menerima pukulan pahit dari Madian dan mundur untuk berdiri sinis di pinggir lapangan, kita harus mengibas debu gurun dan bangkit dengan pengertian akan…

Tujuan Allah

Allah mempunyai tujuan untuk setiap detail hidup kita. Ia mungkin menanamkan kita dalam posisi yang sulit, untuk menempa dalam diri kita suatu panggilan baru. Di Madian sendirilah Musa belajar tentang kesombongan, percaya diri, kurang iman, dan kebodohan yang telah diperbuat oleh tangannya sendiri. Di sinilah di Madian, ia sendirian namun tidak sendiri; banyak orang kudus lain telah menyertainya di sana. Anak‑anak Yakub dan istri Potifar mengirim seorang hamba yang bersemangat ke sana—Yusuf. Amarah liar seorang raja yang cemburu mengirim seorang pemain kecapi muda yang berbakat ke sana. Bahkan seorang raja tua dan bodoh yang menolak diajar mendapati dirinya di padang gurun memakan rumput seperti lembu sampai ia mengaku kembali kesombongannya.

Sepanjang halaman sejarah, tak terhitung orang kudus menyadari bahwa ‘semakin gelap lembah, semakin aku belajar berdoa’. Ketika mereka tiba di ambang hari baru dengan penuh sorak gembira, mereka segera dilucuti dalam perubahan metamorfosis dan akhirnya muncul dengan tidak lain kecuali tongkat Allah di tangan mereka. Hilang sudah hari‑hari ketika mereka cepat berbicara, cepat bertindak, dan lambat mendengar. Di Madian, murid belajar mengalihkan fokusnya dari, “Aku akan melakukan hal‑hal besar bagi Allah” menjadi “Apa yang Kau kehendaki aku lakukan?”

Dan ia gemetar serta terkejut lalu berkata: Tuan, apa yang kehendaki-Mu supaya aku perbuat? Jawab Tuhan kepadanya: Bangunlah, pergi ke kota, maka akan diberitahukan kepadamu apa yang harus kauperbuat –Kisah Para Rasul 9:6. Pendatang baru di Madian memiliki banyak jawaban, tetapi kebanyakan melibatkan sandiwara satu babak dengan diri sendiri sebagai pemeran utama. Lulusan keluar dengan diam dan tenang, sebab mereka telah melalui proses berat memisahkan daging dari roh yang dikerjakan oleh…

Penyucian Allah

Ketel itu untuk perak, dan tungku itu untuk emas; tetapi TUHAN menguji hati –Amsal 17:3. Ketika Musa melewati gerbang Madian, adegan pertama yang Allah letakkan di hadapannya adalah suatu ketidakadilan di sebuah sumur. Sekarang imam Madian mempunyai tujuh anak perempuan… –Keluaran 2:16, yang diusir oleh rombongan penggembala kasar. Tetapi Musa sudah terlatih dalam segala dimensi plutokrasi Mesir, yang termasuk segala aspek keahlian militer dan keterampilan kepemimpinan duniawi. Jadi, ketika ia turun tangan menolong gembala‑gembala perempuan yang tak berdaya itu, ia tentu mampu melakukannya. Anak‑anak perempuan imam Madian menghargai bantuan itu sehingga mereka menceritakannya kepada ayah mereka bahwa …Seorang Mesir telah melepaskan kami dari tangan para gembala, bahkan ia menarik air secukupnya bagi kami dan memberi minum kawanan domba –Keluaran 2:19. Setelah mendengar cerita ini, ayah mereka, Reuel, begitu terkesan sehingga ia memberi Musa sebuah jamuan, sebuah pekerjaan, dan seorang istri… semua dalam satu ayat. –lihat Keluaran 2:21.

…Kamu tahu bahwa mereka yang dianggap memerintah atas bangsa‑bangsa sewenang‑wenang memerintah mereka; dan orang‑orang besar mereka berkuasa atas mereka –Markus 10:42. Walau perjuangan Musa untuk keadilan mungkin mulia, orientasinya hanya bersifat kebangsaan asing (Gentile). Ini mungkin berhasil untuk menetapkan urutan dalam kandang ayam, tetapi ditakdirkan gagal dalam memimpin umat Allah. Akan tetapi barangsiapa hendak menjadi besar di antara kamu, hendaklah ia menjadi pelayanmu: Dan barangsiapa di antara kamu hendak menjadi yang terdahulu, hendaklah ia menjadi hamba bagi semua –Markus 10:43-44.

Doktrin ini asing bagi Mesir dan bagi Musa juga. Banyak orang yang baik dan berbakat dapat berhasil mengoperasikan sebuah usaha dengan otoritas kebangsaan asing, tetapi itu jarang berhasil di rumah mereka, dan bahkan lebih sia‑sia di dalam gereja. Maka, Allah memindahkan bejana pilihan‑Nya dari kerajaan ke kaum proletariat (kelas pekerja), hampir dalam semalam. Ia kemudian diberi pekerjaan yang dibenci oleh orang‑orang yang telah melatihnya—…sebab tiap‑tiap gembala itu menghinakan orang Mesir –Kejadian 46:34. Ketel penyucian ini bukan sekadar untuk mengajarkan pelajaran yang sangat dibutuhkan, tetapi untuk membimbing kita ke dalam…

Penyelenggaraan Allah

Orang‑yang lemah hati akan Ia tunjukkan jalan dalam penghakiman: dan orang‑yang lemah hati akan Ia ajarkan jalan‑Nya –Mazmur 25:9. Allah tidak akan pernah meninggalkan kita di belakang padang gurun; sebaliknya, Ia menyesuaikan keadaan hidup kita untuk membawa kita ke dalam kepenuhan-Nya. Jika kita menahan godaan untuk mengadopsi sikap marah, maka Allah akan dapat mengajarkan kita jalan‑Nya. Tetapi bagi Musa, situasi memperlihatkan dirinya sedemikian rupa sehingga petunjuk ilahi Allah adalah hal terakhir yang akan ia curigai sedang terjadi.

Terjadi…? Tampaknya tidak ada yang terjadi. Minggu‑minggu mencair menjadi bulan, bulan menjadi tahun, dan tahun menjadi dekade, sementara Musa yang berbakat itu tetap menjadi gembala yang berkinerja rendah. Salah satu hal tersulit yang kita perjuangkan adalah “menunggu.” Hampir setiap orang Kristen akan menghadapi masa panjang kesengsaraan dan kita diberi tahu: …janganlah kamu heran akan nyala pepercobaan yang datang ke padamu, seakan‑akan sesuatu yang ganjil menimpa kamu –1 Petrus 4:12. Tetapi kita tidak boleh menilai cara‑cara Allah menurut rasa kita yang lemah, sebab sementara itu, pekerjaan menakjubkan dari menunggu mempersiapkan kita untuk…

Kenaikan Allah

38, 39, … 40 tahun. Karena itu, sekarang pergilah, sebab Aku akan mengutus engkau kepada Firaun, supaya engkau membawa umat-Ku, anak‑anak Israel, keluar dari Mesir –Keluaran 3:10.

Mungkin Allah menyukai angka 40, tetapi lebih mungkin, itulah waktu yang diperlukan bagi Musa untuk sampai pada kursi pengunduran diri. Harga dirinya telah sepenuhnya dipadamkan, dan ia dengan rendah hati bertanya: …Siapakah gerangan aku ini, sehingga aku pergi kepada Firaun dan membawa orang‑orang Israel keluar dari Mesir? –Keluaran 3:11.

Musa tidak kurang memenuhi syarat dibandingkan empat puluh tahun sebelumnya, tetapi prasangkanya telah menguap dalam teriknya matahari gurun. Pengalaman yang diperoleh di padang rumput yang keras bersama domba‑domba yang keras kepala telah membawanya pada pengertian bahwa ini akan menjadi usaha yang nyaris mustahil. Tetapi tidak ada panggilan yang ditetapkan yang dikeluarkan secara independen dari…

Janji Allah

…Sesungguhnya Aku akan menyertai engkau; dan ini akan menjadi tanda bagimu, bahwa Aku telah mengutus engkau: Apabila engkau telah membawa umat itu keluar dari Mesir, maka kamu akan beribadah kepada Allah di gunung ini –Keluaran 3:12.

Bukan bahwa Musa telah mencapai kesempurnaan, sebab kita dapati Musa memprovokasi murka Allah dalam pasal berikutnya—Dan murka TUHAN menyala terhadap Musa… –Keluaran 4:14. Lalu tak lama kemudian ia menjadi obyek langsung di jalan pedang Allah—Dan sesampainya mereka di rumah penginapan di jalan, TUHAN bertemu dengannya dan berusaha membunuh dia –Keluaran 4:24. Demikianlah, meskipun bejananya masih dari tanah liat, ia telah bertemu dengan pembakaran yang mempersiapkannya untuk pelayanan Tuhan, dan bagi kita Allah tidak akan mencabut janji‑Nya karena hembusan keinginan kita. Jadi, AKULAH AKU –lihat Keluaran 3:14, telah meletakkan di atas bahu manusia tugas yang amat besar dan kekal untuk memimpin umat‑Nya. Namun amanat ini tidak boleh dilaksanakan tanpa…

Kuasasa Allah

Apa penyucian sejati dari masa Musa di padang gurun? Kita memperhatikan kesediaannya yang gegabah untuk mengangkat pedang sebelum kedatangannya, tetapi ketika ia keluar, ia hanya memegang sebuah tongkat di tangannya. Dengan pedang ia telah mengalahkan seorang orang Mesir, tetapi dengan tongkat ia mengalahkan seluruh kekuatan Mesir. Tongkat Allah memunculkan air di padang gurun. Itulah tongkat Allah yang, ketika diangkat tinggi oleh tangan yang lemah mengamankan kemenangan atas Amalek. Apa itu tongkat Allah? Sebelum hari‑harinya di Madian, ia hampir tidak mengetahuinya. Empat puluh tahun kemudian hampir tidak ada adegan tanpa itu.

Tongkat itu adalah kuasa Allah membawa keselamatan. Itu adalah hikmat Allah, kebenaran Allah, kesaksian Allah, tetapi lebih dari semua itu adalah pengajaran Allah dengan tegas. Tanpanya, manusia tidak menerima maupun menyadari kasih Allah sebab tanpanya manusia tidak terhubung kepada Allah. Allah mengasihi semua orang yang Ia hukum; Ia memukul dan menegur setiap anak yang Ia terima. Jika kamu menanggung pengajaran, maka Allah memperlakukan kamu sebagai anak‑anak; sebab anak manakah yang tidak dipukul oleh bapanya? Tetapi jika kamu tiada mendapat didikan, yang semuanya memperoleh bagian dalam itu, maka kamu adalah anak haram dan bukan anak –Ibrani 12:6-8.

Musa yang sama ini, yang pada suatu ketika bersedia menggunakan kekuasaan (otoritas kebangsaan asing) atas umat Allah kini mendapati dirinya memohon kepada Allah dan menahan murka-Nya agar tidak menghancurkan mereka. Orang‑orang yang menuduh Musa membawa mereka keluar untuk membunuh mereka dan bahkan pada satu titik siap melempari dia dengan batu kini berada di pusat hati dan kasih sayangnya, meskipun mereka menjadi penyebab kegagalannya memasuki tanah perjanjian. Inilah kasih Kristus. Tetapi di manakah kasih ini dipelajari kecuali di bawah tongkat Allah, di belakang padang gurun, di penjara‑penjara Mesir, di gua‑gua Adulam, di kesusahan Arab, dan dalam kesunyian tempat cadangan di mana Allah telah menetapkan banyak umat‑Nya pergi sampai mereka belajar untuk …belajar dari pada-Ku; karena Aku lemah lembut dan rendah hati dalam hati: dan kamu akan mendapat ketenteraman bagi jiwamu –Matius 11:29. Pasti di sanalah Musa memperoleh watak yang dikenal oleh sarjana alkitabiah sebagai orang yang paling lemah lembut yang pernah berjalan di muka bumi. Pasti tidak ada tempat yang lebih bertentangan di bumi untuk mempelajarinya selain di sekolah penderitaan.

Dan di sinilah kita juga harus tinggal, supaya kita …dapat mengenal Dia dan kuasa kebangkitan-Nya dan persekutuan pada penderitaan‑Nya, sehingga kita menjadi serupa dengan kematian‑Nya –Filipi 3:10.

“Dr. Waldron,” the lady sitting across from me said. “I have been struggling a lot lately.”

“Tell me what’s going on,” I said.

“I don’t know how to explain it,” she hesitated… “I just feel tired most of the time. I can’t concentrate anymore, and I just don’t enjoy most of the things that I used to enjoy. I’m getting through my days, but that’s about it. Do you think I have a thyroid problem or am low in some mineral or vitamin?”

“That could be,” I told her. “We can certainly check those things, but I think something else is going on here.”

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

I am a family doctor and probably thirty percent of the people who come to my office to see me have symptoms of depression. This doesn’t mean that they are on medication for it or feel that they need special help, but it does say that these symptoms are widespread in our world.

Even in Christian circles, surveys indicate that about 15 percent of Christians self-report having been diagnosed with depression at some point in their life. This is 25 percent lower than in society as a whole, but it is still higher than we would like to believe.

In the very beginning, God created the world and Adam and Eve. And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31. Before the Fall, everything was perfect.

I don’t think we know entirely what this meant. Obviously, there were no physical diseases or maladies to afflict either the humans or the flora and fauna of Eden. More than that, Adam and Eve didn’t suffer from anxiety or depression. Their hormones didn’t get out of balance, they didn’t get stressed out (even if there could have been stress in a perfect garden), and they wouldn’t have gotten upset or angry at any point.

Everything changed with Adam and Eve sinning. We see this in the tension between them after they ate the fruit with Adam blaming Eve, and Eve blaming the snake. And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat. And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat –Genesis 3:12-13.

Feeding a family suddenly became hard work. Viruses and bacteria became pathogenic and at some point, in the first families, people would have begun to struggle with emotional and mental health challenges.

Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee. And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life; Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field; In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:16-19.

I would like to explore what depression is as defined by the medical world, some of the sources of it, and then discuss how we can deal with it, both in our own lives and in the lives of our friends and family.

Diagnosing Depression

As mentioned earlier, many people have some symptoms of depression. They may feel more fatigued, cry easily, or have other symptoms that aren’t usual for them. Most of them do not actually have true clinical depression.

Most people do not have all of these symptoms, but when they are continually present without dissipating for two weeks or more, especially if they are strong enough to hinder normal day-to-day responsibilities or the ability to get proper rest, then it is time to do something.

It is important to remember that there is a large or broad continuum regarding depression. Some people have mild discouragement, some have deep feelings of sadness, and some have enough depression that they are at risk to cause harm to themselves or others.

Causes of Depression

There are different examples of people in the Bible who seem to have exhibited symptoms consistent with depression. Two of them stand out to me.

First is Naomi. We know that she went with her husband and her two sons to Moab because of a famine that was affecting southern Israel. She spent ten years in this foreign land and during that time, her husband and both of her sons died.

The book of Ruth tells us that when she returned to Bethlehem, she said to the people, …Call me not Naomi [pleasant], call me Mara [bitter]: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me. I went out full, and the LORD hath brought me home again empty: why then call ye me Naomi, seeing the LORD hath testified against me, and the Almighty hath afflicted me? –Ruth 1:20-21.

There is no way to interview Naomi and find out all the things that she was feeling, but this seems to be more than simple grief. She had lost all the things that were of value to her, and to her it seemed that even God had turned against her.

As we read the story of Ruth, we see that things did improve for her throughout the book—mostly through the ministry of her daughter-in-law, Ruth, but also, through God gradually restoring things of value back into her life, and through others encouraging her in the Lord’s goodness. And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel. And he shall be unto thee a restorer of thy life, and a nourisher of thine old age: for thy daughter in law, which loveth thee, which is better to thee than seven sons, hath born him. And Naomi took the child, and laid it in her bosom, and became nurse unto it –Ruth 4:14-16.

Another one that comes to mind is the Prophet Jeremiah. Jeremiah was called when he was a young man, and he had a very long career speaking God’s Word to a group of kings and other people who simply weren’t interested in what he had to say.

Jeremiah’s life was constantly under threat. At one time, he was thrown into a dungeon full of mud and was only rescued at the last minute. Jerusalem was besieged three different times before the Babylonians razed it. Through his decades of ministry, Jeremiah told the people what God was asking of them, and the people constantly ignored it.

Perhaps it is no wonder that Jeremiah is known today as the weeping prophet. He said, Cursed be the day wherein I was born: let not the day wherein my mother bare me be blessed. Cursed be the man who brought tidings to my father, saying, A man child is born unto thee; making him very glad. And let that man be as the cities which the LORD overthrew, and repented not: and let him hear the cry in the morning, and the shouting at noontide … Wherefore came I forth out of the womb to see labour and sorrow, that my days should be consumed with shame? –Jeremiah 20:14-18.

It is important to note that in both of these examples from the Bible, sin is not revealed to be the issue (or the reason) that pushed these people into depression. For Naomi it was probably a mixture of isolation from her homeland and loss of people she loved dearly. For Jeremiah, it was the constant stress of trying to serve God in a nation that didn’t care about God.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Depression is always multi-factorial. That is to say, there are usually a mixture of internal and external factors that break a person down.

There are genetic and hormonal components that come into play here. There is no doubt that some individuals and some families are more prone to depression than others. It is thought by many doctors and researchers that changes in genes which transport the chemical, Serotonin, through the brain can make some people more susceptible to depression than others.

These differences in genetic makeup can help us understand why some people require very little stress to bring them down, while others seem very resilient. Since we can’t change our genetic makeup, there is no sense gloating if we have a more upbeat personality than someone else. And, if we recognize that we have a greater tendency towards depression, we don’t need to feel discouraged by this fact. If God created us in such a way that we tend towards being moody instead of being naturally upbeat, we need to use wisdom in doing what we can to manage as many external factors as we can so as to minimize the risk of debilitating (extreme) depression.

External stressors are often the thing that triggers these sorts of feelings (discouragement). It can be the death of a close friend or family member, or it can be a financial misfortune. It is important to remember that even good events can produce large amounts of stress. Mothers with newborns are often functioning on very little sleep, even while they have large physical changes taking place in their bodies.

Some people may have poor coping skills. Unfortunately, many turn to street drugs or alcohol to try to smother the feelings that they can’t control otherwise.

As a final thing, sin and guilt can trigger depression or make it worse. We can see this present in David and Saul’s lives. (See Psalm chapter 32) This is not to say that all depression is the result of sin—far from it—but sin needs to be dealt with, and repented of, in order to move forward.

Perhaps as a side note, I will mention that in my experience, deeply depressed people often struggle with horrible guilt. They don’t even know what sin they might have committed; they are only certain that God is angry with them, and they must have done something wrong. Fixing the depression will help with the assurance of salvation issues that these people tend to deal with.

This leaves us with the question of how to help someone who is dealing with this sort of thinking.

Listen

Listening is a powerful tool for helping other people. Listen actively and without jumping in to interrupt negative thinking.

You may be able to see that all is not terrible and that there is much positive in the world. The fact that they can’t see these things has more to do with their mindset than with how terrible things really are. A person struggling with depression may know that there are people worse off in the world, but it doesn’t really help them much to point that out to them.

Encourage

Encouragement can simply be saying good things that you see in the life of the person who is struggling. This is something that all of us need more of.

More than this, we need to encourage people to do things that are healthy for themselves. They need to get out of their home, they should try to exercise, and they should make an attempt to eat healthy. We can help them do better in all of these areas. (See Galatians 6:2)

Pray

…The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:16.

These people need someone to pray with them. They need someone to pray for them. Jesus asks us to pray in secret, but it is also really encouraging for someone who is struggling to hear themselves being prayed for. This helps them to know that there are many people who are lifting them up with prayer support.

Be Willing to be the Initiator

People with depression have very low energy levels. Beyond that, they don’t see themselves as having any value. At least such that someone else would want to spend time with them. They aren’t going to call or text, and they certainly won’t set up a lunch meeting or prayer time.

Even though they crave all of these things, it is just really difficult for them to take the first step to reach out to others. It therefore falls to the rest of us to be willing to do those things.

Don’t Jump to Conclusions

We know the story of Job’s friends. They rode up to see Job after disaster fell on him and sat quietly in shock for several days upon seeing the devastation that had happened to him. When they finally began to speak, it was to judge him for the terrible sin they assumed he had committed.

It isn’t wrong to ask about sin, but there are plenty of times where depression isn’t sin-related. Focusing in on sin prematurely, or if it is assumed, will simply drive wedges that will make it less likely that you can help a person find healing.

What if you are the person struggling with depression? How should you deal with it and what things can help?

Deal With Issues Early

Everyone has moments when they are stressed out and really discouraged. We use terms like “burn-out” and “compassion fatigue” in the medical field when people are heading in the wrong direction. These struggles manifest themselves when we are being irritable with the people around us, when we’re feeling tired most of the time, or when we’re feeling discouraged most of the time. When we see that these symptoms are popping up, it is time to do something to keep things from getting worse.

Maybe a first step is simply knowing our limitations. There are times where we will simply need to say no to work projects or even to church activities because it doesn’t leave us sufficient time to rest. Certain times of the year could be worse—many people struggle more during the winter months because of less sunlight.

Cutting back in whatever areas we can is important when we see that we are on the wrong trajectory.

Don’t Do Comparisons

Everyone is different. Identifying people who seem to “have it altogether” when you are struggling doesn’t help you and it probably will make you feel worse.

Struggling with discouragement does not mean that you aren’t a Christian or that God is done with you. It means that you are human living in a fallen world. You don’t want to continue to live with a depressed spirit, but neither should you believe that you are the only one who has dealt with this. (See 2 Corinthians 10:12)

Exercise

Cardiovascular exercise is really important to boost the chemicals in the brain that are associated with depression. It doesn’t really matter what type of exercise you do. What does matter, is that it increases your heart rate 25 to 30 percent above your baseline heart rate.

Exercise is something that is hard to do, even when you aren’t dealing with depression. It is particularly hard when you are fatigued and feeling down.

Spend Time with Encouragers

People need community. When we are dealing with depressive feelings, we really need other people around to lift us up, to pray with us, and to give us encouragement. None of us is better from spending extended times alone. (See Proverbs 27:17)

Deal with Sin

Sin can make prayer feel ineffective. That isn’t to say that simply confessing sin will suddenly make someone’s depression lift, but it is an important part of reaching healing. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed… –James 5:16.

Be Willing to Take Medication

Not everyone needs medication. The hope is that if you do the right (helpful) things (some of which are listed above), you can keep things from getting bad enough that you would need medical help. But there are plenty of situations where someone simply needs to start on some medication in order to aid them in a number of ways: to sleep, to rest a weary mind that will not stop, to dull the emotional pain, etc.

People with severe enough depression may be a risk to themselves. They may even be completely unable to respond to counseling or any of the other non-medical treatments for these feelings. These people really need to start on medication with the goal to transition off of those medications down the road when they are thinking clearly enough to continue on the right path.

Unfortunately, the benefits of these medications seem to be short-lived. Long-term use of antidepressant medications really does not seem to improve quality of life for many patients. A recent study looked at patients who took antidepressant medications and compared them to those who did not and found similar levels of health-related quality of life in the two groups. In other words, when comparing two groups of depressed patients, with the one group taking medication and the other group not, after a period of time (approximately 6 months) there were no longer any observable differences in their depression levels. So, while these medications may help to stabilize a person who has severe depression, after a period of time the actual medical “help” of the medication starts to diminish. Hopefully, by this time, the person will be stable enough that a safe taper can be taken towards weaning off the medication.

With this in mind, it is very important to do things other than medication to attempt to improve the situation.

Continue, Even When You Feel Better

Many times, when someone has a medical issue, they will consciously change their diet and lifestyle to improve their situation. The problem is that when the symptoms get better, the tendency is to fall back into old eating and behavioral patterns.

If you have dealt with depression in the past, it is important that you continue a path of healthy choices. Exercise regularly, eat healthy meals, manage your stress level (as much as you can), don’t over-schedule, and make a conscious effort to meet regularly with godly friends for times of prayer and support.

Periodically take an inventory of how you are doing. If you are struggling, figure out what you are going to change to make things better.

Depression is very common in our society and in our churches. We can have victory over it alone, but with God’s help and with the support of Christian brothers and sisters, we can move forward.

You may not be gloriously happy all of the time, but by God’s grace, you will have the joy of the Lord in your heart, even on the most stressful days.

“월드런 박사님,” 내 맞은편에 앉아 있던 여자가 말했다. “최근에 많이 힘들어요.”

“무슨 일이 있는지 말해 보세요.” 내가 말했다.

“설명하기가 잘 모르겠어요.” 그녀가 머뭇거렸다… “대부분의 시간에 피곤함을 느껴요. 더 이상 집중이 안 되고, 예전에는 즐겼던 많은 일들을 더 이상 즐기지 못해요. 그저 하루하루 버티고 있는 정도예요. 갑상선 이상이나 미네랄이나 비타민이 부족한 걸까요?”

“그럴 수 있습니다.” 내가 그녀에게 말했다. “그런 것들은 분명히 검사해 볼 수 있지만, 저는 다른 문제가 있다고 생각합니다.”

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

나는 가정의학과 의사이고, 진료실을 찾아오는 사람들 중 아마도 30퍼센트가 우울 증상을 호소한다. 이것이 그들이 약물을 복용하고 있거나 특별한 도움이 필요하다고 느낀다는 뜻은 아니지만, 이런 증상들이 우리 사회에 널리 퍼져 있음을 말해 준다.

심지어 기독교권에서도 설문조사에 따르면 평생 동안 우울증 진단을 받은 적이 있다고 자가 보고하는 그리스도인의 비율은 약 15퍼센트이다. 이는 전체 사회보다 25퍼센트 낮은 수치이지만, 우리가 믿고 싶어 하는 것보다 여전히 높은 수치다.

아주 처음에 하나님은 세상과 아담과 하와를 창조하셨다. 하나님이 지으신 모든 것을 보시니 보시기에 심히 좋았더라… –창세기 1:31. 타락 이전에는 모든 것이 완전했다.

이것이 정확히 무슨 의미인지 우리는 완전히 알지 못한다고 생각한다. 분명 에덴의 인간이나 식물과 동물에게 육체적 질병이나 병적 상태가 없었을 것이다. 그보다 더하여 아담과 하와는 불안이나 우울증으로 고통받지 않았다. 그들의 호르몬이 불균형해지지 않았고, 스트레스를 받지 않았으며(완전한 동산에도 스트레스가 있을 수는 있었겠지만), 어떤 시점에서도 화를 내거나 속상해하지 않았을 것이다.

아담과 하와의 죄로 모든 것이 달라졌다. 우리는 그들이 열매를 먹은 후 서로 긴장하는 모습을 본다. 아담은 하와를 탓하고, 하와는 뱀을 탓한다. 아담이 말하되 네가 나와 함께 있게 한 그 여자가 나에게 그 나무를 주므로 내가 먹었나이다. 여호와 하나님이 여자에게 이르시되 네가 무엇을 하였느냐 여자가 말하되 뱀이 나를 미혹하므로 내가 먹었나이다 –창세기 3:12-13.

가정을 먹여 살리는 일이 갑자기 힘든 일이 되었다. 바이러스와 박테리아가 병원성이 되었고, 최초의 가정들 가운데 어느 시점부터 사람들은 정서적·정신적 건강 문제로 고생하기 시작했을 것이다.

여자에게 이르시되 내가 네 고생을 심히 더하리니 네가 수고하며 자식을 낳을 것이며 네가 남편을 사모할 것이요 그는 네를 다스릴 것이며 아담에게는 이르시되 네가 네 아내의 말을 들었고 내가 네게 명하여 이르기를 네는 그것을 먹지 말라 한 그 나무의 실과를 네가 먹었으므로 땅이 네게 판결을 받아 네가 수고하여 평생토록 그 소산을 먹을 것이라 가시덤불과 엉겅퀴를 네게 낼 것이요 또 채소를 먹을 것이며 얼굴에 땀을 흘려야 네가 빵을 먹고 네가 흙으로 돌아갈 때까지 네가 흙이니 흙으로 돌아가리라 –창세기 3:16-19.

이제 나는 의학계에서 정의하는 우울증이 무엇인지, 그 원인 가운데 일부가 무엇인지 살펴보고, 우리 자신의 삶과 친구와 가족의 삶에서 어떻게 대처할 수 있는지 논의하고자 한다.

우울증 진단하기

앞서 말했듯 많은 사람들이 일부 우울 증상을 가지고 있다. 더 피곤함을 느끼거나 쉽게 울음을 터뜨리거나 평소와 다른 다른 증상을 보일 수 있다. 이들 중 대부분은 실제로는 진정한 임상적 우울증을 가지고 있지는 않다.

대부분의 사람들은 모든 증상을 갖고 있지는 않지만, 이러한 증상들이 2주 이상 지속되어 사라지지 않고, 특히 정상적인 일상 책임을 수행하거나 제대로 쉬는 능력을 방해할 정도로 강력하다면, 무언가를 해야 할 때이다.

우울증에는 넓은 연속체가 있다는 것을 기억하는 것이 중요하다. 어떤 사람들은 가벼운 낙담을 겪고, 어떤 사람들은 깊은 슬픔의 감정을 느끼며, 어떤 사람들은 자신이나 타인에게 해를 끼칠 위험이 있을 정도로 심한 우울을 겪는다.

우울증의 원인

성경에는 우울증과 일치하는 증상을 보인 것으로 보이는 여러 사람이 있다. 그중 두 사람이 내게 특히 떠오른다.

첫째는 나오미이다. 우리는 기근 때문에 그녀가 남편과 두 아들과 함께 모압으로 갔다는 것을 안다. 그녀는 그 이방 땅에서 십 년을 보냈고 그 기간에 남편과 두 아들이 죽었다.

룻기에는 그녀가 베들레헴으로 돌아왔을 때 사람들에게 이렇게 말한 것이 기록되어 있다. 너희는 나를 나오미라 부르지 말고 마라라 하라 주 곧 전능하신 이가 나를 심히 괴롭게 하셨음이니라 내가 배부름에 나갔으나 여호와께서 나를 빈손으로 이끌어 돌아오게 하셨도다 어찌하여 나를 나오미라 부르느냐 여호와께서 나를 대적하시고 전능하신 이가 나를 해하셨도다 –룻기 1:20-21.

나오미의 모든 감정을 인터뷰해서 알아낼 수는 없지만, 이것은 단순한 슬픔 이상의 것으로 보인다. 그녀는 자신에게 가치 있던 모든 것을 잃었고, 심지어 하나님께서도 그녀를 대적하신 것처럼 느꼈다.

룻기의 이야기를 읽다 보면 그녀의 상황이 책 전반에 걸쳐 호전되었음을 보게 된다—대체로 며느리 룻의 섬김을 통해서였지만, 또한 하나님께서 점차적으로 그녀의 삶에 가치 있는 것들을 회복시키시고 다른 사람들이 주님 안에서 그녀를 격려함으로써였다. 여자들이 나오미에게 이르되 오늘날 네게 친족이 없게 하지 아니하신 여호와를 찬송하리로다 그의 이름이 이스라엘 중에 유명하게 될 것이라 그는 네 생명을 회복하게 하며 네 늙은 때를 기르게 하리니 네게 사랑하는 네 며느리로서 네게 좋은 이는 일곱 아들보다 나으니라. 나오미가 아이를 취하여 그 무릎에 안고 그 기생이 되매 –룻기 4:14-16.

또 하나 떠오르는 인물은 예언자 예레미야이다. 예레미야는 젊었을 때 소명을 받았고, 관심이 전혀 없는 여러 왕들과 사람들에게 오랫동안 하나님의 말씀을 전하는 긴 사역을 했다.

예레미야의 삶은 끊임없이 위협받았다. 한때 그는 진흙으로 가득한 감옥에 던져졌다가 간신히 구출되기도 했다. 여호와의 심판으로 바벨론이 예루살렘을 파괴하기 전에 예루살렘은 세 번 포위되었다. 여러 해의 사역 동안 예레미야는 백성에게 하나님이 요구하시는 것을 전했으나 백성들은 계속 무시하였다.

아마도 오늘날 예레미야가 우는 선지자로 알려진 것은 놀랄 일이 아니다. 그는 이렇게 말했다. 내가 낳은 날을 저주하리로다 어머니가 나를 낳은 그 날에 복이 있으리요 말지어다 내 아버지에게 기쁜 소식을 전하여 내게 아이가 낳았다 한 그 사람은 저주를 받을지어다 그 사람은 여호와가 치러 버리고 돌이키지 아니한 성읍과 같을지며 아침의 부르짖음과 낮의 울부짖음을 듣게 하소서 … 내가 어찌하여 태에서 나와 수고와 근심을 보며 나의 날들이 수치로 소멸되게 하였느냐 –예레미야 20:14-18.

성경의 이 두 사례에서 중요한 점은, 이들을 우울로 몰아넣은 원인으로 죄가 드러나고 있지는 않다는 것이다. 나오미에게는 고국에서의 고립과 사랑하던 사람들의 상실이 복합적으로 작용했을 가능성이 크다. 예레미야에게는 하나님을 섬기려 했으나 그 나라가 하나님을 신경 쓰지 않는 가운데 지속된 스트레스가 원인이었다.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

우울증은 항상 다요인적이다. 즉, 보통은 내부적 요소와 외부적 요소가 혼합되어 사람을 무너뜨린다.

여기에는 유전적 및 호르몬적 요소가 작용한다. 어떤 개인과 가계는 다른 사람들보다 우울증에 더 취약하다는 것은 의심의 여지가 없다. 많은 의사와 연구자들은 세로토닌이라는 화학물질을 뇌로 운반하는 유전자의 변화가 어떤 사람들을 다른 사람들보다 우울에 더 취약하게 만들 수 있다고 생각한다.

이러한 유전적 차이는 왜 어떤 사람들은 아주 적은 스트레스로 무너지기 쉬운 반면, 어떤 사람들은 매우 회복력이 있는지 이해하는 데 도움을 준다. 유전적 구성을 바꿀 수 없으므로, 우리가 다른 사람보다 더 쾌활한 성격을 가졌다고 해서 자만할 이유는 없다. 그리고 우리가 우울 경향이 더 강하다는 것을 인식한다면, 이 사실 때문에 낙담할 필요도 없다. 하나님이 우리를 기질상 우울한 쪽으로 만드셨다면, 우리는 극심한 우울의 위험을 최소화하기 위해 가능한 외부 요인들을 지혜롭게 관리해야 한다.

외부적 스트레스 요인이 이러한 감정(낙담)을 유발하는 경우가 흔하다. 가까운 친구나 가족의 죽음 같은 사건일 수도 있고, 재정적 불운일 수도 있다. 심지어 좋은 사건들도 큰 스트레스를 유발할 수 있다는 점을 기억하는 것이 중요하다. 갓난아기를 둔 어머니들은 신체적으로 큰 변화가 일어나는 동안에도 종종 매우 적은 수면으로 생활한다.

대처 능력이 부족한 사람들도 있다. 불행하게도 많은 이들이 통제할 수 없는 감정을 진정시키기 위해 마약이나 알코올에 의지한다.

마지막으로, 죄와 죄책감이 우울증을 유발하거나 악화시킬 수 있다. 우리는 다윗과 사울의 삶에서 이를 볼 수 있다. (시편 32장 참조) 이것이 모든 우울증이 죄의 결과라는 뜻은 결코 아니다—그와는 거리가 멀다—그러나 죄는 해결되고 회개되어야 앞으로 나아갈 수 있다.

부수적으로 말하자면, 내 경험에서 심하게 우울한 사람들은 종종 끔찍한 죄책감으로 고통받는다. 그들은 자신이 어떤 죄를 범했는지조차 알지 못하지만 분명히 하나님이 그들에게 노하셨고 자신이 무언가 잘못했음에 틀림없다고 확신한다. 우울증을 호전시키면 이들이 겪는 구원 확신 문제에도 도움이 된다.

이제 이러한 사고방식으로 고통받는 사람을 어떻게 도울 것인가 하는 질문이 남는다.

경청하라

경청은 다른 사람을 돕는 강력한 도구이다. 적극적으로 경청하고 부정적 사고를 끊으려 급히 끼어들지 말라.

당신은 모든 것이 끔찍하지 않으며 세상에는 긍정적인 면이 많다는 것을 볼 수 있을지 모른다. 그들이 이러한 것들을 보지 못하는 것은 실제 상황이 끔찍해서가 아니라 그들의 사고방식 때문이다. 우울을 겪는 사람은 세상에 더 불쌍한 사람이 있다는 것을 알더라도, 그것을 지적하는 것이 그들에게 큰 도움이 되지 않는다.

격려하라

격려는 단순히 고통받는 사람의 삶에서 당신이 보는 좋은 점들을 말해 주는 것일 수 있다. 이것은 우리 모두에게 더 필요한 일이다.

그보다 더 나아가 우리는 사람들이 자신에게 건강한 일을 하도록 격려해야 한다. 집에서 벗어나게 도와주고, 운동을 시도하게 하며, 건강한 식사를 하도록 노력하게 해야 한다. 우리는 이 모든 영역에서 그들이 더 잘할 수 있도록 도울 수 있다. (갈라디아서 6:2 참조)

기도하라

의인의 간구는 역사하는 힘이 많으니라 –야고보서 5:16.

이런 사람들은 누군가와 함께 기도받을 필요가 있다. 그들을 위해 기도해 줄 사람이 필요하다. 예수님은 우리가 은밀히 기도하라고 요구하시지만, 고통받는 사람이 자신을 위해 기도하는 소리를 듣는 것은 정말로 큰 격려가 된다. 이것은 많은 사람들이 기도로 그들을 위한 중보를 하고 있음을 알게 하는 데 도움이 된다.

시작하는 사람(주도자)이 되기를 기꺼이 하라

우울증을 가진 사람들은 에너지 수준이 매우 낮다. 그뿐만 아니라 스스로를 아무런 가치가 없는 사람으로 보며, 다른 누군가가 시간을 함께 보내고 싶어 할 만큼의 가치가 있다고 보지 못한다. 그들은 전화하거나 문자를 하지 않을 것이고, 점심 약속이나 기도 모임을 정하지도 않을 것이다.

그들은 이 모든 것을 갈망하지만 타인에게 먼저 손을 내미는 첫걸음을 내딛기 어려워한다. 그러므로 나머지 우리가 기꺼이 그 일들을 해 주어야 한다.

성급하게 결론 내리지 말라

우리는 욥의 친구들의 이야기를 알고 있다. 재난이 그에게 닥쳤을 때 그들은 급히 올라와 며칠 동안 충격으로 조용히 앉아 있었고, 마침내 말하기 시작했을 때 그들이 가정한 끔찍한 죄 때문에 그를 판단했다.

죄에 대해 묻는 것이 잘못된 것은 아니지만, 우울증이 항상 죄와 관련된 것은 아니다. 죄에 대해 성급하게, 혹은 당연하게 가정하면, 치유를 돕기보다는 오히려 간극을 만들 수 있다.

만약 당신이 우울증으로 고생하는 사람이라면? 어떻게 대처해야 하고 어떤 것이 도움이 될까?

문제를 일찍 다루라

모든 사람에게 스트레스를 받고 정말 낙담하는 순간은 있다. 우리는 사람들이 잘못된 방향으로 가고 있을 때 의학 분야에서 ‘번아웃’과 ‘연민 피로(compassion fatigue)’ 같은 용어를 사용한다. 이러한 고난은 우리가 주변 사람들에게 짜증을 내거나 대부분의 시간 피곤함을 느끼거나 대부분의 시간 낙담을 느낄 때 나타난다. 이러한 증상이 나타나면 상황이 악화되는 것을 막기 위해 무언가를 해야 할 때이다.

첫걸음은 단지 자신의 한계를 아는 것일 수 있다. 때로 우리는 쉬기에 충분한 시간을 남기지 못하므로 업무 프로젝트나 교회 활동에 ‘아니오’라고 말해야 할 때가 있다. 연중 특정 시기가 더 나쁠 수 있다—많은 이들이 일조량이 적은 겨울철에 더 많이 고생한다.

우리가 잘못된 궤도에 있음을 알게 되면 가능한 영역에서 줄이는 것이 중요하다.

비교하지 말라

모든 사람은 다르다. 당신이 고통받을 때 ‘모든 것을 갖춘 것처럼 보이는’ 사람들을 찾는 것은 당신에게 도움이 되지 않으며 오히려 기분을 더 나쁘게 만들 것이다.

낙담을 겪는다고 해서 당신이 그리스도인이 아니거나 하나님께서 당신과 일을 끝내셨다는 뜻은 아니다. 그것은 당신이 타락한 세상에 살고 있는 인간이라는 것을 의미한다. 우울한 영으로 계속 살고 싶지는 않겠지만, 또한 이것을 겪은 사람이 당신뿐이라고 믿어서는 안 된다. (고린도후서 10:12 참조)

운동하라

심혈관 운동은 우울증과 관련된 뇌의 화학물질을 증가시키는 데 매우 중요하다. 어떤 종류의 운동을 하는지는 크게 중요하지 않다. 중요한 것은 기초 심박수보다 25~30퍼센트 정도 심박수가 증가하는 것이다.

운동은 우울증이 없을 때에도 하기 힘들다. 피곤하고 기분이 가라앉아 있을 때는 특히 더 어렵다.

격려자가 있는 곳에 머물라

사람들은 공동체가 필요하다. 우리가 우울한 감정을 다룰 때 우리는 다른 사람들이 곁에 있어 우리를 일으켜 세우고 함께 기도하며 격려해 주는 것을 정말로 필요로 한다. 누구도 장기간 홀로 지내는 것으로 나아지지 않는다. (잠언 27:17 참조)

죄를 다루라

죄는 기도가 효과가 없는 것처럼 느끼게 만들 수 있다. 그렇다고 해서 단순히 죄를 고백한다고 해서 누군가의 우울증이 갑자기 사라지는 것은 아니지만, 치유에 이르는 중요한 부분이다. 너희 죄를 서로 고백하라 그리하면 너희가 병 나음을 얻으리라… –야고보서 5:16.

약물 복용을 기꺼이 받아들여라

모든 사람이 약물이 필요한 것은 아니다. 여기서의 희망은 올바른(도움이 되는) 일들을(위에 열거한 것들 일부를 포함) 하면 상황이 악화되어 의학적 도움이 필요할 만큼 나빠지는 것을 막을 수 있다는 것이다. 그러나 수면을 돕고, 멈추지 않는 지친 마음을 쉬게 하며, 정서적 고통을 둔화시키는 등 여러 면에서 도움을 주기 위해 단지 약물 복용을 시작해야 하는 상황이 많이 있다.

심한 우울증을 가진 사람들은 스스로에게 위험을 초래할 수 있다. 상담이나 다른 비의학적 치료에 전혀 반응하지 못하는 경우도 있다. 이런 사람들은 약물 치료를 시작하여 나중에 생각이 충분히 명료해졌을 때 점진적으로 약물을 줄여 끊는 것을 목표로 해야 한다.

불행히도 이러한 약물의 이점은 단기간에만 지속되는 것으로 보인다. 항우울제의 장기 사용은 많은 환자들의 삶의 질을 실제로 향상시키지 못하는 것 같다. 최근의 한 연구는 항우울제를 복용한 환자들과 복용하지 않은 환자들을 비교했을 때 두 그룹의 건강 관련 삶의 질 수준이 유사함을 발견했다. 다시 말해, 우울증 환자 두 그룹을 비교했을 때 한 그룹은 약물을 복용하고 다른 그룹은 복용하지 않았는데, 일정 기간(약 6개월) 후에는 더 이상 우울 수준에 관찰 가능한 차이가 없었다. 따라서 이러한 약물들은 심한 우울증을 안정시키는 데 도움이 될 수 있지만, 일정 시간이 지나면 약물의 실제적인 의학적 ‘도움’은 감소하기 시작한다. 희망컨대 그때쯤이면 환자가 충분히 안정되어 안전하게 약물을 감량할 수 있을 것이다.

이 점을 염두에 두고, 상황을 개선하기 위해 약물 이외의 방법을 시도하는 것이 매우 중요하다.

좋아졌을 때도 계속하라

많은 경우 누군가가 의학적 문제를 겪으면 상황을 개선하기 위해 의식적으로 식단과 생활 방식을 바꾼다. 문제는 증상이 좋아지면 예전의 식사와 행동 패턴으로 되돌아가는 경향이 있다는 것이다.

과거에 우울증을 다룬 적이 있다면, 계속해서 건강한 선택의 길을 유지하는 것이 중요하다. 규칙적으로 운동하고, 건강한 식사를 하고, 가능한 한 스트레스 수준을 관리하며, 과도한 일정을 잡지 말고, 기도와 지지를 위해 경건한 친구들과 정기적으로 만나도록 의식적으로 노력하라.

주기적으로 자신의 상태를 점검하라. 힘들다면 상황을 개선하기 위해 무엇을 바꿀지 계획하라.

우울증은 우리 사회와 교회에서 매우 흔하다. 우리는 혼자서도 우울을 이길 수 있지만, 하나님의 도움과 그리스도인 형제자매들의 지지로 함께 나아갈 수 있다.

항상 찬란하게 행복하지는 않을지라도 하나님의 은혜로 가장 스트레스가 많은 날에도 주님의 기쁨을 마음에 품고 있을 것이다.
