تحيات محبة باسم يسوع! لنا إله عظيم يستحق كل تسبيحنا وكل محبتنا وكل حياتنا!

نعيش في زمنٍ فيه الكثير من الملهيات. أمير هذا العالم حقًا مسعىٌ لتدمير حياة الناس مهما كان الثمن. لدينا مدن ملاهي، وألعاب فيديو، ودور سينما، والإنترنت، وفيسبوك، ومراكز تسوق الأزياء، وكل ما تتصوّره—كل ذلك خارج هناك. لكن الله يريد قلوبنا أن تُحرَّك لئلا نتورط في هذه الملهيات، بل لنعمل لأجله ولأجل ملكوته. إذا تقاطعت حياتنا وهموم هذه الدنيا سنفقد كل الوقت المخصص لربنا. لا نستطيع أن نخدم سيدين. يبدو أن هناك أشياء تحاول سرقة وقت أخواتنا العزيزات (صغيرات وكبيرات على حد سواء). فلنكن واعيات لهذه الأمور حتى نتحرر منها ثم نتحرر لخدمة الرب بكامل قلوبنا.

الشيء الواحد الذي ينبغي أن ننتبه له يُسمى التأنق والآخر الحماقة أو الانفلات. كم يدهشني كيف يعمل الله. في كلمته يُخبرنا بما لا ينبغي أن نتزين به، لكنه أيضًا يخبرنا بما ينبغي أن نتزين به. يخبرنا ما الثمر الذي يجب أن ينبع من حياتنا، وما الثمر الذي لا ينبغي أن ينبع منها. لكل طريق شرير يوجد عند الله أيضًا الطريق الصحيح. أعلم أن كثيرين منا لن يذهبن إلى مراكز الأزياء لشراء ملابسنا، لكن أخشى أن كثيرات منا لا زلن يبحثن عن ملابس تشدّ الانتباه إلى الجسم بدلًا من تمجيد ربنا. قال يسوع: طوبى لأنقياء القلب لأنهم يبصرون الله – متى 5:8.

أما تأنقهن فلا يكون في ضفر الشعر أو في التزيُّن بالذهب أو في ارتداء الثياب، بل الرجل الداخلي القلبي، غير الفانٍ، زينة الروح المهذبة الوديعة التي هي أمام الله ذات تقدير عظيم. لأن هكذا كانت تتزيَّن قديمًا النساء القديمات اللاتي كن يتركن في الله خاضعات لأزواجهن؛ كما سارة كانت تطيع إبراهيم داعية إياه سيدًا؛ وأماثلكن بنات، متى عملتن خيرًا ولم تخفن شيئًا من الدهشة – بطرس الأولى 3:3-6.

تزَيَّن: أن تزخرف أو تجعل أجمل؛ تبرز؛ تزيّن بشيء خارجي أو عرضي؛ أن تعرض الجمال أو الفضيلة.

تذكري، يريدنا الله أن نتزين بأشياء تجلب المجد له. اعتمادًا على نوع الملابس التي أختار ارتدائها، ينجذب انتباه الآخرين إلى لباسِي أولًا بدلًا من ملامح وجهي. عندما يحدث ذلك فأنا آخذ كل المجد لأن التركيز على ثيابي. لكن إذا رآني أحدهم ورأى الصفاء الظاهر على وجهي واستطاع أن يقول إنني كنت مع يسوع، فسَيُعطي الله كل المجد الذي يستحقه، وسنعرض جمال أو فضيلة روح الله في حياتنا.

الآن دعونا نلقي نظرة على بعض الكلمات الموجودة في نصنا الكتابي وننظر في معانيها:

الضفر: الطيّ، أو المضاعفة، أو الضفّ.

الثياب: الملابس؛ اللباس الخارجي أو الزينة.

الزينة: ما يزخرف؛ أو شيء يضاف لشيء آخر فيجعله أجمل للعين.

كم هو جميل لربنا حين نولد من جديد، ونمتلك روحًا منكسرة، ونصبح وديعات هادئات. هل يستطيع الناس أن يروا ثمار روح الله في حياتنا—كزينة؟ حقًا تلك زينة ذات ثمن عظيم. تذكري أننا قد نضيف زينات خارجية على حياتنا تجرح أبانا. لا نجعله يخجل من أن يدعونا أولادًا وبناتًا له.

وديع: خفيف المزاج؛ رخيم؛ لطيف؛ غير سهل الاستثارة أو التهيّج؛ متسامح، يميل إلى التحمل عند الإساءات.

هل نتضايق إن قالت لنا إحداهن شيئًا قد يساعدنا في مشينا مع الرب؟ تذكري أن ربنا يريد ثمر الوداعة يزيّن حياتنا المتبدلة.

هادئ: ساكن؛ في حالة راحة؛ غير متحرك؛ مسالم؛ غير مضطرب؛ لا يسبب إساءة؛ لا يثير خلافًا أو فوضى أو متاعب؛ لطيف؛ وديع؛ راضٍ.

مع كل أسلوب جديد يأتي بيننا هل نغيّر سريعًا لمجرد إضافة شيء إلى أجسادنا يجلُب المجد لأنفسنا فقط؟ هل نحن راضيات بمعيار الله الكتابي لحياتنا؟ هل نحن ثابتات ومتأصلات فيما نؤمن به؟ هل نعرف لماذا نؤمن بما نؤمن به؟

خضوع: فعل إخضاع؛ فعل قهر وإلحاق تحت سلطان آخر.

هل نحن تحت سلطان ربنا في كل جانب من جوانب حياتنا؟

خائف: متأثر بالخوف أو القلق.

دهشة: اندهاش؛ ارتباك أو حيرة من انطباع مفاجئ للخوف أو الدهشة أو التعجّب.

نحن بنات سارة طالما فعلنا الخير ولم نتأثر بالخوف أو بأي ارتباك أو حيرة. الله ليس مؤلفًا للحيرة—نَاموسُ الرَّبِّ كَامِلٌ، يُحَوِّلُ النَّفْسَ… – مزمور 19:7. تذكري: بداية الحكمة مخافة الرب [وليس الحيرة] … – أمثال 9:10.

يتورّط: أن يَلفّ أو يَتشابك بطريقة لا تُفك بسهولة؛ أن يُحيّر أو يُشتّت كهموم.

هل نسمح لحياتنا أن تتشابك مع أزياء وحماقات هذا العالم؟

ولا يشتبك أحد في شؤون الدنيا ليمتع من انتخبه جنديًا. ولا تَتَّبِعِ الْهَذَيَانَ الْباطِلَ، لأَنَّهُ يَزْدَادُ إِلَى المَرْتَكَةِ. واهْرُبِ الشَّهَوَاتِ الشَّبَابِيَّةِ، وَاتَّبِعِ الْبِرَّ وَالإِيمَانَ وَالْمَحَبَّةَ وَالسَّلامَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ الرَّبَّ مِنْ قَلْبٍ نَقِيٍّ – 2 تيموثاوس 2:4-22.

اجتناب: أن تتجنب؛ أن تبقى بعيدًا؛ أن لا تقع أو تقترب؛ أن لا تختلط أو ترتبط.

هل نَتجنَّب ممارسات هذا العالم؟ وبشكل أخص، هل نَتجنَّب الكلام الفضفاض الفارغ؟

مجدِّف: مُهين لكل ما هو مقدس؛ مُنجَس؛ غير نقي.

باطل: فارغ؛ لا قيمة له؛ بلا مادة أو أهمية.

ما نملأ به أنفسنا سيخرج منا. إذا كنا نملأ أنفسنا بكلمة الله المقدسة، فسيتدفق ذلك من حياتنا. ومع ذلك، إذا كنا نملأ أنفسنا بأشياء باطلة فسوف يظهر ذلك أيضًا.

هذيان: كلام سخيف.

هل حديثنا يتركز على الكتاب المقدس، أم على الأشياء الجديدة التي اشتريناها مثل ثوب جديد أو مركبة، أو ربما على كل الأشخاص الذين التقيناهم على فيسبوك؟

اهرب: أن تركضي بسرعة، كما من خطر؛ أن تسرعي عن الخطر أو الشر المتوقع.

إذا كنا مع مجموعة كلامهن سخيف، هل نبقى خوفًا من فقدان الصديقات أم نمشي (أو نجري) بعيدًا عن الشر المتوقع أو الخطر؟ كلما تشابكت حياتنا مع طرق العالم صار من الأصعب أن نفك أنفسنا.

شهوات: رغبة ملحة؛ حرص على التملك أو التلذذ؛ شهوة جسدية؛ رغبة غير مشروعة للمتعة الجسدية.

سيعطينا الله الرغبات الحقيقية لقلبنا. قد نقول إننا نرغب أشياء طاهرة، لكن إن كان قلبنا يتوق إلى أشياء غير مشروعة فسنسلّم لتلك الأشياء. حياتنا لا تتكون فقط مما نقول، بل الأهم مما نعيشه. أيضًا، تشجعوا، فالرغبات الداخلية لقلبنا يمكن أن تتغير إلى الأبد عن طريق العمل الروحي أو «الولادة الجديدة».

برّ: طاعة المسيح الفاعلة والسلبية، التي بها يُوفى ناموس الله.

إذا كنا نتبع البر فذلك يعني أنه ينبغي أن نتبع الطاعة الفاعلة والسلبية التي يظهرها المسيح بمثاله.

إيمان: موضوع الإيمان؛ عقيدة أو نظام عقائد يٌؤمن به.

ما حقيقة إيماننا؟ هل نؤمن حقًا بالله وما يقوله لنا عبر كلمته المكتوبة؟ لأن إبراهيم آمن بالله فتمكّن أن «يقدّم» ابنه الوحيد إسحاق الذي سيُحسب منه نسل إبراهيم. —انظر عبرانيين 11:17 وتكوين 22:13. إن أخبرنا الله في كلمته أن نتجنّب الردّة لأنها تقود إلى ردّة أعظم، فنحتاج أن نؤمن بالله ونهرب من تلك الأشياء، ولا يجب أن نسمح لأنفسنا أن نظن أن قليلًا من التسلية لا يهم.

محبة: محبة؛ إحسان؛ رغبة الخير؛ تلك ميزة القلب التي تميل بالإنسان لينظر بعين الرحمة إلى أخيه الإنسان ويعمل له خيرًا؛ تشمل المحبة العليا لله خالقنا وحسن النية الكلية تجاه البشر.

هل تسكن محبة الله فينا وتتدفق من حياتنا كنبع ماء جاري؟

سلام: راحة سماوية؛ وئام؛ خلو من الاضطراب أو القلق.

علينا أن نتبع مثل مخلصنا الحبيب يسوع المسيح الذي كانت حياته كلها في انسجام تام مع الله الآب. لم يُزعج المسيح أو يُشتَّت بأحوال هذا العالم، بل كان مرتاحًا نافذًا صوب إرادة أبيه. هل نحن كذلك؟

طاهر: صفاء؛ خالٍ من الدنس الأخلاقي؛ بلا عيب؛ مقدس؛ غير فاسد.

علينا أن نتحلّى أو نزيّن هذه الثمرات في حياتنا وأن نمارسها أيضًا مع الذين يمارسون نفس الأمور في حياتهم. قليل من الخميرة يخمّر الخبز كله.

كما ينبغي للنساء أيضًا أن يتزينَّ بملابس محتشمة، بخجل وتقوى؛ لا بشعر مضفور، ولا ذهب، ولا لآلئ، ولا لباس غالٍ؛ بل بأعمال صالحة، التي تليق بالنساء اللواتي يعلن عن التقوى – 1 تيموثاوس 2:9-10.

خجل: حياء؛ إفراط في الحشمة.

ينبغي أن نكون متزينات بالخجل لا بالرهبة أو الحسّية.

قَوامة: يقظة معتادة؛ جدية؛ هيبة من دون حزن أو اكتئاب.

حتى إن كنا متجردات من التهوّل فلا يلزم أن نكون حزينات بل يمكن أن نتحلى بفرح الرب الذي يزيّن حياتنا. يجب أن يكون هناك نور في أعيننا لأن يسوع هو نور حياتنا. حقًا إن كان روح الله يسكن فينا فلدينا ما نشكر من أجله. ينبغي أن يكون ذلك ظاهرًا في كل جانب من جوانب حياتنا.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

لأنه قد ظهرت نعمة الله المخلّصة للناس كافة، معلّمة إيانا أن منكرين التدين والشهوات الدنيوية يجب أن نسلك متعقلين، مستقيمين وتقويين في هذا الدهر – تيطس 2:11-12.

أَفْرَحُ فَرَحًا عظيمًا فِي الرَّبِّ، تَفْرَحُ نَفْسِي بِإِلَهِي، لأَنَّهُ لَبِسَنِي ثِيَابَ الْخَلَاصِ، وَلَبِسَنِي جَبَّةَ الْبِرِّ، كَمَا يُتَنَطَّقُ الْعَرِيسُ بِزِينَتِهِ، وَالْعَرُوسُ تُزَيِّنُ نَفْسَهَا – إشعياء 61:10.

زينة الحشمة، الخجل، القوامة، الإيمان، المحبة، السلام، البر، الوداعة، والهدوء حقًا جواهر ذات ثمن عظيم. هذه الجواهر ثمينة جدًا حتى تستحق تسليم حياتنا كلها لإله السماوات، خالقنا ومخلصنا، لكي تزيّن حياتنا. ولكن بالمثل، إن كنّا مستسلمات لإله هذا العالم فسنحمل زينات الكبرياء والحسد والكراهية والغيرة، وما إلى ذلك. أيّها أجمل؟

ورأيت أيضًا مدينة مقدّسةٍ، أُورشليم الجديدة، نازلةً من عند الله من السماء، مستعدةً كعروس مهيأة لزوجها. وسمعت صوتًا عظيمًا من السماء قائلًا: هوذا مسكن الله مع الناس، وسيقيم معهم، وسيكونون شعبه، وسيكون الله نفسه معهم إلههم – رؤيا 21:2-3.

هل نستعد لملاقاة يسوع؟ هل يسكن الله فينا؟ هل هو إلهنا وهل نحن شعبه؟

تذكري أن الزمن يمر بسرعة. قد نكون هنا اليوم ونغادر غدًا. هل نريد أن نكون مع يسوع كل الدهر، أم نريد أن نكون مع إبليس وملائكته؟ الاختيارات التي نتخذها في حياتنا اليوم ستؤثر أين نقضي الأبدية.

لا تُخَطَّأُوا، اللهٌ لَيْسَ مُسْتَهْزَأً: مَا يَزْرَعُهُ الْإِنْسَانُ فَهَذَا يَحْصُدُهُ – غلاطية 6:7. لا تغتري. هذه الآية أيضًا للمؤمن، ليست فقط لغير المتحولين. كل واحد منا يمكنه أن يسأل نفسه ماذا يزرع. بخصوص التأنق، هل نزرع فكر أن الجمال الخارجي مهم جدًا أم نزرع فكر أن الجمال الداخلي هو أكثر ما ثمين ويجب الحصول عليه؟ للتوضيح، لا أتحدث عن أن نكون قذرات وغير مهتمات بالنظافة. الله إله نظام ونظافة، لكنه ليس إله شرائط أو أقواس أو دانتيل أو ملابس باهظة وجذابة. تذكري أن معظم من يخلقون صيحات أزياء جديدة يركزون على تصميم ملابس تكون جذابة للعين. هذا ما يجعل الناس يشترونها.

مرة أخرى، عندما ينظر الناس إلينا هل يمجدون جسدنا الدنيوي أم يمدحون الله على العمل الذي يقوم به في حياتنا؟ أيضًا، في ما يخص الحماقة والانفلات، إن كنا متأصلات في كلمة الله فلن يكون لدينا وقت للهراء والكسل الباحث عن المتعة. فلتكن مشغولات بعمل ربنا، مثل مساعدة جار محتاج إلى يد إضافية، أو مشاركة شهادتنا مع الناس الذين نلتقيهم.

وَلاَ تَخَافُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَقْتُلُونَ الْجَسَدَ بَلْ لاَ يَقْدِرُونَ أَنْ يَقْتُلُوا النَّفْسَ، بل اخشَ الَّذِي يَقدِرُ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ النَّفْسَ وَالْجَسَدَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ – متى 10:28. ونحن نعيش في هذه الأزمنة الأخيرة، الرسالة المحيطة بنا هي أنه طالما تؤمن بوجود إله فستكون بخير. هذه رسالة كاذبة. يقول لنا يسوع إن هناك طريقًا واحدًا فقط. قال له يسوع: «أنا هو الطريق والحق والحياة، لا يأتي أحد إلى الآب إلا بي. لو كنتم قد عرفتموني لعرفتم أبي أيضًا، ومن الآن تعرفونه وقد رأيتموه» – يوحنا 14:6-7. الحمد لله أن الله أعطانا مثالًا نتبعه.

Greetings of love in Jesus’ name! We have a great God who is worthy of all our praise, all our love, and our whole life!

We live in a time where there are many distractions. The prince of this world is truly out to destroy people’s lives at whatever cost. We have amusement parks, video arcades, theaters, internet, Facebook, fashion malls, and whatever else you can think of—it’s out there. But God would have our hearts stirred to not be entangled with these distractions, but rather to work for Him and His Kingdom. If we are entangled with the affairs of this life, we will have no time left for our Lord. We cannot serve two masters. There seem to be some things trying to steal the time of our dear sisters (young and old alike). Let us be aware of these things so that we can be free from them and then be free to serve the Lord with our whole hearts.

The one thing we should be aware of is called adornment and the other is foolishness or looseness. To me it is so amazing how God works. He tells us in His Word what not to adorn ourselves with, but He also tells us what to adorn ourselves with. He tells us what fruit should be coming from our lives, and what fruit should not be coming from our lives. For every evil way that there is, God also shows us the right way. I know many of us would not go to fashion malls to buy our clothes, but I fear that many of us are still looking for clothes that accent the body rather than glorify our Lord. Jesus said: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God –Matthew 5:8.

Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement –1 Peter 3:3-6.

Adorn: to deck or beautify; set off; to embellish by anything external or adventitious; to display the beauty or excellence of.

Remember, God wants us to adorn ourselves with things that will bring glory to Him. Depending on the type of clothing that I choose to wear, the focus of others is drawn to my clothing first, instead of my countenance. When this happens then I am getting all the glory because the focus is on my apparel. But if somebody sees me and they can see the clear countenance on my face and they can tell that I’ve been with Jesus, then they will give God all the glory that He deserves, and we will be displaying the beauty or excellence of God’s spirit in our lives.

Now let’s take a look at some more of the words found in our Scripture text and consider their meaning:

Plaiting: folding, doubling, braiding.

Apparel: clothing; external habiliments or decorations.

Ornament: That which embellishes; or something which, added to another thing, renders it most beautiful to the eye.

How beautiful it is to our Lord when we become born again, have a broken spirit, and become meek and quiet. Can people see the fruits of God’s spirit in our lives—as ornaments? Truly that is an ornament of great price. Remember we can add external ornaments to our lives that bring sadness to our Father. Let us not make Him ashamed to call us His sons and daughters.

Meek: mild of temper; soft; gentle; not easily provoked or irritated; yielding, given to forbearance under injuries.

Are we irritated if somebody has something to share with us that will help us in our walk with the Lord? Remember our Lord wants the fruit of meekness adorning our converted lives.

Quiet: still; being in a state of rest; not moving; peaceable; not turbulent; not giving offence; not exciting controversy, disorder, or trouble; mild; meek; contented.

With every new style that comes in among us are we quick to change for no reason other than adding something to our bodies that only brings glory to us? Are we content with the biblical standard of God for our lives? Are we firm and grounded in what we believe? Do we know why we believe in what we believe?

Subjection: the act of subduing; the act of vanquishing and bringing under the dominion of another.

Are we under the dominion of our Lord in every aspect of our lives?

Afraid: impressed with fear or apprehension.

Amazement: astonishment; confusion or perplexity from a sudden impression of fear, surprise, or wonder.

We are daughters of Sarah as long as we do well, and are not impressed with fear or any confusion or perplexity. God is not the author of confusion—The law of the LORD is perfect, converting the soul… –Psalm 19:7. Remember: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom [not confusion]… –Proverbs 9:10.

Entangleth: to twist or interweave in such a manner as not to be easily separated; to perplex or distract, as with cares.

Are we allowing our lives to be interwoven with the fashions and foolishness of this world?

No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier. But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness. Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart –2 Timothy 2:4-22.

Shun: to avoid; to keep clear of; not to fall on or come in contact with; not to mix or associate with.

Are we shunning the practices of this world? More specifically, are we shunning loose and empty talk?

Profane: irreverent to anything sacred; polluted; not pure.

Vain: empty; worthless; having no substance, value, or importance.

What we fill ourselves with will come out. If we are filling ourselves with God’s holy Word, then that will be flowing out of our lives. However, if we are filling ourselves with vain things then that shall come out as well.

Babblings: foolish talk.

Is our talk centered on the Bible, or is it centered on the new things that we have bought such as a new garment or a vehicle, or maybe it’s on all the people we have met on Facebook?

Flee: to run with rapidity, as from danger; to hasten from danger; or expected evil.

If we are with a group of people whose talk is foolish, do we stay for fear of losing friends or do we walk (or run) away from the expected or dangerous evil? The more we interweave our lives with the ways of the world, the harder it is to untangle ourselves.

Lusts: longing desire; eagerness to possess or enjoy; carnal appetite; unlawful desire of carnal pleasure.

God will give us the true desires of our heart. We may say that we desire pure things, but if our heart is yearning for unlawful things, we shall yield to those things. Our lives consist not only in what we say, but more importantly what we live. Also, take courage, the inward desires of our heart can be forever changed through the spiritual operation or “new birth”.

Righteousness: the active and passive obedience of Christ, by which the law of God is fulfilled.

If we are to follow righteousness, then that means we should follow the active and passive obedience that Christ shows us by his example.

Faith: the object of belief; a doctrine or system of doctrines believed.

What is the reality of our faith? Do we really believe God and what He tells us through His written Word? It was because Abraham believed God that he was able to “offer up” his only son Isaac through whom Abraham’s descendants would be counted. –see Hebrews 11:17 and Genesis 22:13. If God tells us in His Word to shun ungodliness because it will lead to more ungodliness, then we need to believe God and flee those things, and we must not allow ourselves to think that just a little bit of fun will not matter.

Charity: love; benevolence; goodwill; that disposition of the heart which inclines men to think favorably of their fellow men, and to do them good; it includes supreme love to God our Maker and universal good will to men.

Do we have the Love of God dwelling within and flowing out of our lives like a spring of running water?

Peace: heavenly rest; harmony; freedom from disturbance or agitation.

We are to follow the example of our dear Savior Jesus Christ whose whole life was in perfect harmony with God the Father. Christ was not disturbed or disrupted by the ways of this world, but He was at rest doing His Father’s will. Are we?

Pure: clear; free from moral defilement; without spot; holy; incorrupt.

We are to follow or have these fruits adorned in our lives and also practicing these with those who are practicing the same things in their own lives. A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump.

In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; But (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works –1 Timothy 2:9-10.

Shamefacedness: bashfulness; excess of modesty.

We should be adorned with shamefacedness and not giddiness or sensuality.

Sobriety: habitual soberness; seriousness; gravity without sadness or melancholy.

Even if we are sober we don’t need to be sad but we can have the joy of the Lord adorning our lives. There should be a light in our eyes because Jesus is the light of our lives. Truly if God’s spirit is dwelling within us we have so much to be thankful for. It should be evident in every aspect of our lives.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world –Titus 2:11-12.

I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels –Isaiah 61:10.

The ornaments of modesty, shamefacedness, sobriety, faith, charity, peace, righteousness, meekness, and quietness are truly jewels of great price. These jewels are so valuable that it is worth surrendering our whole lives to the God of Heaven, our Maker, and our Redeemer, so that we may have them adorning our lives. But likewise, if we are surrendered to the god of this world we will have the ornaments of pride, envy, hate, jealousy, and so forth. Which ones are the more beautiful?

And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. –Revelation 21:2-3.

Are we preparing to meet Jesus? Is God dwelling in us? Is He our God and are we His people?

Remember time is swiftly passing by. We can be here today and gone tomorrow. Do we want to be with Jesus throughout all eternity, or do we want to be with the devil and his angels? The choices we make for our lives today will affect where we spend eternity.

Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap –Galatians 6:7. Don’t be misled. That verse is also for the believer, not just for the unconverted. Each one of us can ask ourselves what we are sowing. Concerning adornment, are we sowing the thought that outward beauty is very important or are we sowing the thought that inward beauty is the most precious thing to have and obtain? For clarification, I am not talking about being dirty and unkempt. God is a God of order and cleanliness, but He is not a God of ribbons, bows, frills, lace, and expensive, attractive clothing. Remember that most people who create new clothing fashions focus on designing garments so that they will be appealing and attractive to the eye. That is what makes people buy them.

Again, when people look at us do they glorify our fleshly body or are they praising God for the work that He is doing in our lives? Also, concerning foolishness and looseness, if we are grounded in the word of God, we will not have time for vain babblings and pleasure-seeking idleness. Let us be busy doing the work of our Lord, such as helping our neighbor who could use an extra hand, or sharing our testimony with people that we meet.

And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell –Matthew 10:28. As we live in these last times, the message that is all around us is that as long as you believe in a God, you will be okay. That is a false message. Jesus tells us there is only one way. Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also: and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him –John 14:6-7. Praise the Lord that God has given us an example to follow.

Hälsningar av kärlek i Jesu namn! Vi har en stor Gud som är värd all vår lovsång, all vår kärlek och hela vårt liv!

Vi lever i en tid där det finns många distraktioner. denna världens furste är verkligen ute efter att förstöra människors liv till vilket pris som helst. Vi har nöjesparker, spelhallar, teatrar, internet, Facebook, modemallar och allt annat man kan tänka sig—det finns därute. Men Gud vill att våra hjärtan ska röras så att vi inte trasslar in oss i dessa distraktioner, utan i stället arbetar för Honom och Hans rike. Om vi är upptagna med livets angelägenheter kommer vi inte att ha någon tid kvar för vår Herre. Vi kan inte tjäna två herrar. Det verkar finnas vissa ting som försöker stjäla tiden från våra kära systrar (både unga och gamla). Låt oss vara medvetna om dessa ting så att vi kan bli fria från dem och därefter fria att tjäna Herren med hela våra hjärtan.

Det ena vi bör vara medvetna om kallas prydnad och det andra är dårskap eller lättsinne. För mig är det så förunderligt hur Gud verkar. Han talar i sitt Ord om vad vi inte ska prydas med, men Han säger oss också vad vi ska prydas med. Han visar vilken frukt som borde komma från våra liv, och vilken frukt som inte borde komma från våra liv. För varje ond väg visar Gud oss också den rätta vägen. Jag vet att många av oss inte skulle gå till modemallar för att köpa våra kläder, men jag fruktar att många av oss ändå letar efter kläder som framhäver kroppen snarare än förhärligar vår Herre. Jesus sade: Saliga är de rena i hjärtat, för de ska få se Gud – Matteus 5:8.

Er prydnad får icke vara utvändig, med flätat hår och med guldsmycken eller klädedräkt; utan den inre människan i hjärtat, den otrötta, en mild och stilla andes smycke, som är mycket värdefullt i Guds ögon. Så klädde sig också de heliga kvinnorna i forna tider, som hoppades på Gud, när de underkastade sig sina män; liksom Sara lydde Abraham och kallade honom herre. Ni är hennes döttrar, så länge ni gör det som är gott och icke fruktar för något skräck – 1 Petrus 3:3–6.

Pryda: att prunka eller göra vacker; framhäva; att försköna med något yttre eller tillfälligt; att uppvisa skönheten eller utmärkelsen av.

Kom ihåg, Gud vill att vi prys med ting som ska förhärliga Honom. Beroende på vilken typ av kläder jag väljer, dras andras uppmärksamhet först till min klädsel istället för till mitt uppsyn. När detta sker får jag all ära eftersom fokus är på min klädsel. Men om någon ser mig och kan se det klara uttrycket i mitt ansikte och kan avgöra att jag har varit hos Jesus, då kommer de att ge Gud all den ära Han förtjänar, och vi kommer att visa Guds Andes skönhet eller utmärkelse i våra liv.

Låt oss nu se på några fler ord i vår skriftskrift och överväga deras innebörd:

Fläta: vika, dubbla, fläta.

Klädsel: kläder; yttre dräkter eller prydnader.

Smycke: det som förskönar; eller något som, tillagt ett annat föremål, gör det mest vackert för ögat.

Hur vackert är det inte för vår Herre när vi blir födda på nytt, har en krossad ande och blir milda och stilla. Kan människor se Guds Andes frukter i våra liv—som smycken? Sannerligen är det ett smycke av stor prisklass. Kom ihåg att vi kan lägga till yttre prydnader i våra liv som bringar sorg åt vår Fader. Låt oss inte göra Honom skamsen att kalla oss sina söner och döttrar.

Mild: ljum i temperament; mjuk; ömsint; icke lättretad eller irriterad; eftergiven, benägen att utstå oförrätter.

Blir vi irriterade om någon har något att dela med oss som hjälper oss i vår vandring med Herren? Kom ihåg att vår Herre vill att frukten av mildhet ska pryda våra omvända liv.

Still: stilla; vara i ett tillstånd av vila; inte i rörelse; fridsam; icke upprörd; icke stötande; icke väcka kontrovers, oordning eller bekymmer; mild; foglig; tillfreds.

Med varje ny stil som kommer bland oss är vi snabba att ändra oss utan annan anledning än att lägga något till våra kroppar som endast förhärligar oss? Är vi tillfreds med Guds bibliska norm för våra liv? Står vi fast och förankrade i vad vi tror? Vet vi varför vi tror vad vi tror?

Underkastelse: handlingen att besegra; handlingen att bringa under en annans herravälde.

Lever vi under vår Herres herravälde i alla aspekter av våra liv?

Rädd: påverkad av fruktan eller oro.

Förskräckelse: förbluffelse; förvirring eller olust genom ett plötsligt intryck av fruktan, överraskning eller förundran.

Vi är Sa ras döttrar så länge vi gör gott och icke är påverkade av fruktan eller någon förvirring. Gud är icke förvirringens upphov—HERRENS lag är uppenbar, förvandlar själen… – Psaltaren 19:7. Kom ihåg: HERRANS fruktan är vishetens begynnelse [inte förvirring] … – Ordspråksboken 9:10.

Invecklar: att tvinnas eller sammanflätas så att det inte lätt kan skiljas; att förbrylla eller distrahera, såsom med bekymmer.

Låter vi våra liv bli sammanflätade med tidens mode och världens dårskap?

Ingen som strider invecklar sig i världsliga angelägenheter, för att han må behaga den som har utvalt honom till att vara soldat. Undvik okysk och fåfäng babbel; det leder bara till mer ogudaktighet. Fly även ungdomens lustar; men följ rättfärdighet, tro, kärlek, frid, med dem som åkallar Herren av rent hjärta – 2 Timoteus 2:4–22.

Undvik: att akta sig för; att hålla sig borta från; att icke gripa an eller komma i kontakt med; att icke blanda sig eller umgås med.

Undviker vi världens sedvänjor? Mer specifikt, undviker vi lös och tomt prat?

Vanhelga: hädisk mot något heligt; förorenad; icke ren.

Fåfäng: tom; värdelös; utan substans, värde eller betydelse.

Det vi fyller oss med kommer att komma ut. Om vi fyller oss med Guds heliga Ord, så kommer det att flöda ur våra liv. Men om vi fyller oss med fåfänga ting så kommer även det att komma ut.

Prat: dåraktigt tal.

Är vårt samtal centrerat på Bibeln, eller är det centrerat på det nya vi köpt, såsom ett nytt plagg eller ett fordon, eller kanske på alla människor vi träffat på Facebook?

Fly: att springa snabbt, såsom från fara; att skynda bort från fara; eller väntat ont.

Om vi är med en grupp människor vars samtal är dåraktigt, stannar vi av rädsla för att förlora vänner eller går vi (eller springer) bort från det förväntade eller farliga onda? Ju mer vi sammanflätar våra liv med världens sätt, desto svårare blir det att reda ut oss.

Lust: längtan; iver att äga eller njuta; köttslig aptit; otillåten begäran efter köttslig njutning.

Gud ska ge oss de sanna begären i vårt hjärta. Vi kan säga att vi åtrår rena ting, men om vårt hjärta längtar efter otillåtna ting, kommer vi att ge vika för dem. Våra liv består inte bara i vad vi säger, utan ännu viktigare vad vi lever. Tag också mod; de innersta begären i vårt hjärta kan för alltid förändras genom den andliga verkan eller "pånyttfödelsen".

Rättfärdighet: Kristi aktiva och passiva lydnad, genom vilken Guds lag uppfylles.

Om vi ska följa rättfärdighet innebär det att vi bör följa den aktiva och passiva lydnad som Kristus visar oss i sitt exempel.

Tro: föremålet för tro; en lära eller system av läror som tros.

Vad är verkligheten i vår tro? Tror vi verkligen Gud och vad Han säger oss genom sitt skrivna Ord? Det var därför Abraham trodde Gud att han kunde "offra" sin ende son Isak genom vilken Abrahams avkomlingar skulle räknas. – se Hebréerna 11:17 och Första Moseboken 22:13. Om Gud säger åt oss i sitt Ord att undvika ogudaktighet eftersom det leder till mer ogudaktighet, då måste vi tro Gud och fly dessa ting, och vi får icke tillåta oss att tänka att bara lite nöje inte spelar någon roll.

Kärlek: kärlek; välvilja; god vilja; den sinnesstämning i hjärtat som får människor att tänka väl om sina medmänniskor och göra dem gott; det inbegriper högsta kärlek till Gud vår Skapare och allmän välvilja mot människor.

Har vi Guds kärlek boende inom oss och flödande ut ur våra liv som en vår av rinnande vatten?

Frid: himmelsk vila; harmoni; frihet från störning eller oro.

Vi ska följa vårt kära Frälsarens Jesu Kristi exempel, vars hela liv var i fullständig harmoni med Gud Fadern. Kristus blev icke störd eller uppbruten av världens sätt, utan Han var i vila och gjorde Faderns vilja. Är vi det?

Ren: klar; fri från moralisk orenhet; utan fläck; helig; oförvitlig.

Vi ska ha dessa frukter prydda i våra liv och också utöva dem tillsammans med dem som praktiserar samma ting i sina egna liv. En liten surdeg syrar hela degen.

På samma sätt bör även kvinnorna klä sig i vederbörlig skamfullhet och blygsamhet, icke med flätat hår eller guld eller pärlor eller dyrbara kläder; utan sådant som passar dem som bekänner gudsfruktan: goda gärningar – 1 Timoteus 2:9–10.

Blygsel: blyghet; överdriven anspråkslöshet.

Vi bör vara prydda med blygsel och inte med virrighet eller sinnlighet.

Lugn: vanemässig nykterhet; allvar; allvarsamhet utan sorg eller melankoli.

Även om vi är lugna behöver vi inte vara sorgsna utan vi kan ha Herrens glädje prydande våra liv. Det bör finnas ett ljus i våra ögon eftersom Jesus är livets ljus. Verkligen, om Guds Ande bor inom oss har vi så mycket att vara tacksamma för. Det bör vara uppenbart i varje aspekt av våra liv.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Guds nåd, som frälser alla människor, har uppenbarats och lär oss att vi, då vi förnekar ogudaktighet och världsliga lustar, skall leva nyktligt, rättfärdigt och gudfruktigt i denna världen – Titus 2:11–12.

Jag ska fröjdas storligen i HERREN, min själ ska vara glad i min Gud; ty han har klätt mig i frälsningens klädnad, han har omsorgsfullt täckt mig med rättfärdighetens mantel, såsom en brudgum pryder sig med prydnader, och såsom en brud smyckar sig med sina juveler – Jesaja 61:10.

Prydnaderna av blygsamhet, blygsel, nykterhet, tro, kärlek, frid, rättfärdighet, mildhet och stillhet är verkligen juveler av stort värde. Dessa juveler är så värdefulla att det är värt att överlämna hela våra liv åt Himlens Gud, vår Skapare och vår Frälsare, så att vi må ha dem prydande våra liv. Men likaledes, om vi är överlämnade åt denna världens gud kommer vi att ha prydnader av stolthet, avund, hat, svartsjuka och så vidare. Vilka är vackrare?

Och jag såg den heliga staden, det nya Jerusalem, komma ner från Gud utav himmelen, beredd såsom en brud smyckad för sin man. Och jag hörde en hög röst från himmelen säga: Se, Guds boning är hos människorna, och han skall bo hos dem, och de skola vara hans folk, och Gud själv skall vara hos dem och vara deras Gud. – Uppenbarelseboken 21:2–3.

Förbereder vi oss att möta Jesus? Bor Gud i oss? Är Han vår Gud och är vi hans folk?

Kom ihåg att tiden går hastigt förbi. Vi kan vara här i dag och borta i morgon. Vill vi vara med Jesus i all evighet, eller vill vi vara med djävulen och hans änglar? De val vi gör för våra liv i dag kommer att påverka var vi tillbringar evigheten.

Låt er icke bedra: Gud blir icke hånad. Det som människan sår, det skall hon också skörda – Galaterna 6:7. Låt er inte vilseledas. Den versen är även för den troende, inte bara för de oomvända. Var och en av oss kan fråga sig vad vi sår. Beträffande prydnad, sår vi tanken att yttre skönhet är mycket viktig eller sår vi tanken att inre skönhet är det mest dyrbara att ha och uppnå? För tydlighetens skull, jag talar inte om att vara smutsig och ovårdad. Gud är en Gud av ordning och renlighet, men Han är icke en Gud av band, rosetter, volanger, spets eller dyra, tilltalande kläder. Kom ihåg att de flesta som skapar nya modetrender fokuserar på att designa plagg så att de ska vara tilltalande och attraktiva för ögat. Det är det som får människor att köpa dem.

Igen, när människor ser på oss, förhärligar de vår kroppsliga gestalt eller prisar de Gud för det arbete som Han utför i våra liv? Också, beträffande dårskap och lättsinne, om vi är grundade i Guds ord, kommer vi inte att ha tid för fåfängt babbel och nöjessökande slöhet. Låt oss vara upptagna med att utföra vår Herres verk, såsom att hjälpa vår granne som kan behöva en extra hand, eller att dela vårt vittnesbörd med människor vi möter.

Frukta icke dem som dödar kroppen, men icke kunna döda själen; frukta snarare honom som kan förgöra både själ och kropp i Gehenna – Matteus 10:28. När vi lever i dessa sista tider är budskapet som omger oss att så länge du tror på en Gud kommer du att klara dig. Det är ett falskt budskap. Jesus säger att det bara finns en väg. Jesus säger till honom: Jag är vägen, sanningen och livet; ingen kommer till Fadern utom genom mig. Om ni hade känt mig, skulle ni också ha känt min Fader; och från nu känner ni honom och har sett honom – Joh 14:6–7. Prisad vare Herren att Gud har givit oss ett exempel att följa.

Being a ruler over a group of people is marked with stress, hard decisions, and sleepless nights—certainly not a position for the mentally weak or immature. The position is difficult, be it sheriff, mayor, governor, or president. The average person does not fully mature until the age of 25, according to neuroscientific studies.1 And yet, in AD 54, a ruler was appointed who was only seventeen years old. This was no petty judge or political secretary. He was crowned ruler over one of the largest empires of the world at that time. The boy’s name was Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus—commonly called Nero. He was the fifth emperor of Rome.

Nero was not brought into power by any election or choice of his citizens. His mother, Agrippina, had married Caesar Claudius (her uncle), emperor of Rome. Claudius adopted Nero as his son. Nero would go on to marry Claudius’ daughter Octavia, his own cousin and stepsister.

On October 13, A.D. 54, Agrippina poisoned her powerful husband, and her son Nero became emperor. It was rumored that Nero and his mother had an incestuous relationship, but the new ruler was well received by his subjects and seemed eager to please them, ordering grand public buildings to be built, as well as lowering taxes and the price of food. However, it was not to last.

Nero soon killed his brother-in-law, who was fourteen, which angered his wife. At this point, the emperor was in a relationship with a freedwoman (a formerly enslaved person), so he had his wife exiled. When this sparked public outrage, he had Octavia beheaded on false charges of being unfaithful.

He then became infatuated with a woman named Poppaea Sabina, who was scheming to marry him. Sabina roused Nero to such fear and jealousy that he decided to kill his mother for fear of losing the throne. The plan was simple—while Agrippina was on a cruise ship, it would be discreetly sunk, and Nero’s mother would drown. However, this was not to be. Agrippina was a strong swimmer and escaped with her life. Undeterred, Nero dispatched his executioners to stab her to death in broad daylight. Unfortunately, things had just gotten started for the most powerful man in the empire and these bizarre and inhuman acts were only a sampling of what was to come.

Nero was given to fits of rage and became violent towards his wife in one such outburst. He kicked Sabina repeatedly until both she and her unborn child died. Nero is said to have regretted this, and he soon started a hunt for anyone who looked like Sabina, his dead wife. He finally found a slave that is said to have resembled her strongly, and they were married. The catch? The slave was a man. Nero took to dressing him in the clothing of a woman and referring to him as a lady. At this point, Nero’s slippery slope was only getting more slippery. He believed himself to be an artist—a genius, even—and gave massive public performances. If you were in attendance, you could not leave. Why? The doors were locked. Nero also dreamed of singing to his enemies and bringing them to tears for their perceived wrongdoings.

But the emperor was not content with only putting on musical performances. In A.D. 67, he entered into the Olympic Games, which was against the rules (no emperor was allowed to compete in the Games). Nevertheless, Nero entered. He introduced new competitions, such as trumpeting and acting. He entered into several and won each one. His actions caused much outrage since the Olympics were considered a sacred event and Nero had changed them.

However, Nero had an even bigger goal in mind. The chariot races were the biggest spectacle the Olympics had to offer. In them, chariot riders were allowed a team of four horses. Teams would race around a massive arena for a total of seven laps. Sometimes wheels fell off, or chariots crashed into each other. It was not uncommon for drivers to be thrown from their ride and to be trampled to death or to be dragged by their own team of horses. However, the winner would be celebrated and highly paid.

Knowing all the difficulty, danger, and stress involved, you can only imagine how the charioteers felt to see Emperor Nero roll up to the racetrack in an expensive chariot and a team consisting of not four, but ten horses. As it turns out, Nero was inexperienced and out of shape. Almost immediately, he lost control of his team and was thrown from the chariot, being seriously injured in the process. Despite never finishing the race, Nero won first place.

This incident does a good job of demonstrating Nero’s attitude toward his authority at this point in his reign. In fact, in A.D. 66, he won more than 1,800 first-place prizes for his supposed exhibits of artistry. Here was a man that could not be told “no”.

On the night of July 18, A.D. 64, a fire started in Rome’s Circus Maximus. The fire grew and spread, becoming out of control. The fire would rage for the next six days, leaving almost no part of the city untouched. It was devastating for the citizens of Rome and would go on to be the incident Nero would be most widely known for. Many ancient writers blamed Nero for starting the fire, although he was not in the city when it began. Whether or not he started the fire, Nero needed someone to blame. He chose a group of people who were despised and feared by the Romans and tortured them relentlessly. That group was known as the Christians. Tacitus, a secular Roman writer, described it as such, “Nero fastened the guilt and inflicted the most exquisite tortures on a class hated for their abominations, called Christians by the populace. Mockery of every sort was added to their deaths. Covered with the skins of beasts, they were torn by dogs and perished, or were nailed to crosses, or were doomed to the flames and burnt, to serve as nightly illumination when daylight had expired.”

Meanwhile, Nero grew even more wicked. He ruthlessly slaughtered Christian men, women, and children, and plunged ever deeper into immorality. Finally, On June 9, AD 68, Nero, the last emperor of Rome killed himself after having been declared a public enemy by the Roman Senate. He was only 31 years old.

So, here is a man corrupt in every way. His lifestyle was deeply offensive to Christianity, and his persecution was one of the most horrible in history. How would we respond to such a ruler? How did Christians respond to him?

Paul lived under Nero’s reign. He saw all the horrible things detailed above. Yet, he gave the church the following admonition: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake –Romans 13: 1-5.

These words seem impossible when we consider the situation. Yet the Word of God tells us that our governmental authorities are put in place by God Himself. What a testimony! How much more, then, are we called to respect our authorities—to not slander them; to obey them in all possible aspects; to stay away from their elections and campaigns; and yet, to yield ourselves to God and His authority as our final say?! Or, as Paul put it, Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God… –Romans 13:1.

The believers of the early church saw Nero—the murderous, bloodthirsty, corrupt emperor—as a man ordained of God. They sought to honor and respect him in his authority, while ultimately yielding to the higher authority of God. Herein, we see a potential paradox, that the earthly authorities are “ministers of God” to be honored and obeyed, yet IF the time would come wherein the believer is required by the civil authorities to disobey God, we then have a higher responsibility—…We ought to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29.

This all puts a great responsibility on our shoulders today as Christians living in an increasingly corrupt and evil society. Can we find that biblical balance between honoring our governmental leaders while still obeying God in all things? Or do we fail just like the unregenerate around us in picking apart the faults of our earthly authorities when we feel our “easy living” being trodden upon?

See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is –Ephesians 5:15-17. And Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful –1 Corinthians 4:2.

Let each one of us as committed, born-again, Bible-believing Christians walk circumspectly, redeeming the time. For we all want to be found faithful in that soon-coming day when we all will stand before the judgment seat to receive our just reward.

Essere sovrano su un gruppo di persone è caratterizzato da stress, decisioni difficili e notti insonni—certamente non una posizione per i mentalmente deboli o immaturi. La carica è difficile, sia che si tratti di sceriffo, sindaco, governatore o presidente. Secondo studi neuroscientifici, la persona media non raggiunge la piena maturità fino all'età di 25 anni.1 Eppure, nell'anno 54 d.C. fu nominato un sovrano che aveva solo diciassette anni. Non era un giudice di poco conto o un segretario politico. Fu incoronato sovrano su uno dei più grandi imperi del mondo di allora. Il ragazzo si chiamava Nero Claudio Cesare Augusto Germanico—comunemente chiamato Nerone. Fu il quinto imperatore di Roma.

Nerone non fu portato al potere tramite alcuna elezione o scelta dei suoi cittadini. Sua madre, Agrippina, aveva sposato Cesare Claudio (suo zio), imperatore di Roma. Claudio adottò Nerone come suo figlio. Nerone andò poi in sposa a Ottavia, la figlia di Claudio, sua cugina e sorellastra.

Il 13 ottobre dell'anno 54 d.C., Agrippina avvelenò il suo potente marito, e suo figlio Nerone divenne imperatore. Si vociferava che Nerone e sua madre avessero avuto una relazione incestuosa, ma il nuovo sovrano fu ben accolto dai suoi sudditi e sembrava desideroso di compiacerli, ordinando la costruzione di grandi edifici pubblici, oltre ad abbassare le tasse e il prezzo del cibo. Tuttavia, non sarebbe durato.

Presto Nerone uccise suo cognato, che aveva quattordici anni, il che fece infuriare sua moglie. A quel punto, l'imperatore aveva una relazione con una liberta (una persona precedentemente schiava), così mandò in esilio sua moglie. Quando ciò suscitò indignazione pubblica, fece decapitare Ottavia con false accuse di infedeltà.

Si infatuò poi di una donna di nome Poppea Sabina, che tramava per sposarlo. Sabina suscitò in Nerone tale paura e gelosia che egli decise di uccidere sua madre per timore di perdere il trono. Il piano era semplice—mentre Agrippina si trovava su una nave da crociera, questa sarebbe stata discretamente affondata, e la madre di Nerone sarebbe annegata. Tuttavia, non andò così. Agrippina era un'abile nuotatrice e si salvò. Indifferente, Nerone mandò i suoi esecutori a pugnalarla a morte in pieno giorno. Sfortunatamente, per l'uomo più potente dell'impero le cose erano appena cominciate e questi atti bizzarri e disumani furono solo un assaggio di ciò che sarebbe seguito.

Nerone era soggetto a scoppi d'ira e divenne violento verso sua moglie in uno di questi accessi. Calciò ripetutamente Poppea finché sia lei che il suo bambino non nato morirono. Si dice che Nerone se ne pentì, e presto diede inizio a una caccia a chiunque somigliasse a Poppea, la sua moglie morta. Alla fine trovò uno schiavo che si diceva la somigliasse molto, e si sposarono. Il problema? Lo schiavo era un uomo. Nerone cominciò a vestirlo con abiti femminili e a riferirsi a lui come signora. A questo punto, la china di Nerone diventava sempre più scivolosa. Si credeva un artista—un genio, addirittura—andò in scena in grandi esibizioni pubbliche. Se eri presente, non potevi andartene. Perché? Le porte erano chiuse a chiave. Nerone sognava anche di cantare ai suoi nemici e di farli piangere per i loro presunti torti.

Ma l'imperatore non si accontentava di esibirsi musicalmente. Nell'anno 67 d.C. partecipò ai Giochi Olimpici, cosa vietata (nessun imperatore poteva competere ai Giochi). Nonostante ciò, Nerone partecipò. Introdusse nuove competizioni, come il suonare la tromba e la recitazione. Vi prese parte e vinse in ciascuna. Le sue azioni causarono grande sdegno poiché le Olimpiadi erano considerate un evento sacro e Nerone le aveva mutate.

Tuttavia, Nerone aveva in mente un obiettivo ancora più grande. Le corse dei carri erano lo spettacolo più grande delle Olimpiadi. In esse, ai cocchieri era permessa una squadra di quattro cavalli. Le squadre correvano intorno a un'enorme arena per un totale di sette giri. Talvolta capitava che si staccassero le ruote o che i carri si schiantassero l'uno contro l'altro. Non era raro che i guidatori venissero scaraventati dal loro mezzo e calpestati a morte o trascinati dalla propria squadra di cavalli. Tuttavia, il vincitore veniva celebrato e ben ricompensato.

Conoscendo tutte le difficoltà, i pericoli e lo stress implicati, potete solo immaginare come si sentirono i cocchieri nel vedere l'imperatore Nerone arrivare alla pista con un carro costoso e una squadra composta non da quattro, ma da dieci cavalli. Si scoprì che Nerone era inesperto e fuori forma. Quasi immediatamente, perse il controllo della sua squadra e fu sbalzato dal carro, rimanendo gravemente ferito nel processo. Nonostante non avesse mai terminato la gara, Nerone ottenne il primo posto.

Questo episodio illustra bene l'atteggiamento di Nerone verso la sua autorità in quel periodo del suo regno. Infatti, nell'anno 66 d.C. vinse più di 1.800 premi per il primo posto per le sue presunte dimostrazioni di genialità artistica. Era un uomo a cui non si poteva dire “no”.

La notte del 18 luglio dell'anno 64 d.C. scoppiò un incendio nel Circo Massimo di Roma. L'incendio crebbe e si diffuse, diventando incontrollabile. L'incendio infuriò per i successivi sei giorni, lasciando quasi nessuna parte della città intatta. Fu devastante per i cittadini di Roma e divenne l'episodio per cui Nerone fu maggiormente conosciuto. Molti scrittori antichi lo accusarono di aver appiccato l'incendio, anche se non si trovava in città quando iniziò. Che lo avesse appiccato o no, Nerone aveva bisogno di qualcuno da incolpare. Scelse un gruppo di persone disprezzate e temute dai Romani e le torturò senza pietà. Quel gruppo era conosciuto come cristiani. Tacito, uno scrittore romano laico, lo descrisse così: “Nerone impose la colpa e inflisse le più squisite torture a una categoria odiata per le loro abominazioni, chiamata cristiani dalla popolazione. A ogni sorta di scherno fu aggiunta alle loro morti: ricoperti delle pelli delle bestie, furono sbranati dai cani e perirono, o furono inchiodati alle croci, o furono destinati alle fiamme e arsi, per servire come illuminazione notturna quando il giorno era passato.”

Nel frattempo, Nerone divenne ancor più malvagio. Macellò spietatamente uomini, donne e bambini cristiani e sprofondò sempre più nell'immoralità. Infine, il 9 giugno dell'anno 68 d.C., Nerone, l'ultimo imperatore di Roma, si uccise dopo essere stato dichiarato nemico pubblico dal Senato romano. Aveva solo 31 anni.

Quindi, ecco un uomo corrotto in ogni aspetto. Il suo stile di vita era profondamente offensivo per il cristianesimo, e la sua persecuzione fu una delle più orribili della storia. Come dovremmo rispondere a un simile sovrano? Come risposero i cristiani a lui?

Pablo visse sotto il regno di Nerone. Vide tutte le orribili cose sopra descritte. Eppure, diede alla chiesa il seguente ammonimento: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God. Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation. For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same: For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake –Romans 13: 1-5.

Queste parole sembrano impossibili se consideriamo la situazione. Eppure la Parola di Dio ci dice che le autorità governative sono poste in carica da Dio stesso. Che testimonianza! Quanto più allora siamo chiamati a rispettare le nostre autorità—to not slander them; to obey them in all possible aspects; to stay away from their elections and campaigns; and yet, to yield ourselves to God and His authority as our final say?! Oppure, come Paolo lo mise, Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God… –Romans 13:1.

I credenti della chiesa primitiva videro Nerone—l'imperatore assassino, assetato di sangue, corrotto—come un uomo ordinato da Dio. Cercarono di onorarlo e rispettarlo nella sua autorità, pur sottomettendosi in ultima istanza all'autorità superiore di Dio. Qui vediamo un paradosso potenziale: le autorità terrene sono “ministri di Dio” da onorare e obbedire, eppure SE venisse il tempo in cui il credente fosse costretto dalle autorità civili a disobbedire a Dio, abbiamo allora una responsabilità superiore—…We ought to obey God rather than men –Acts 5:29.

Tutto ciò pone oggi su di noi una grande responsabilità come cristiani che vivono in una società sempre più corrotta e malvagia. Possiamo trovare quell'equilibrio biblico tra onorare i nostri leader governativi e al contempo obbedire a Dio in ogni cosa? O falliamo proprio come gli irreligiosi intorno a noi nel mettere a nudo i difetti delle nostre autorità terrene quando sentiamo che il nostro “vivere comodo” viene calpestato?

See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is –Ephesians 5:15-17. And Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful –1 Corinthians 4:2.

Ognuno di noi, in quanto cristiani rinati, credenti della Bibbia e impegnati, cammini con prudenza, redimendo il tempo. Tutti vogliamo infatti essere trovati fedeli in quel giorno ormai prossimo in cui staremo davanti al tribunale per ricevere la nostra giusta ricompensa.

Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb –Exodus 3:1.

The back side of the desert has long been understood as God’s school wherewith He has instructed many of His servants, of whom Moses stands chief. At the prime age of 40, he found himself …learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds. And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Israel –Acts 7:22-23.

I have no doubt that God can, and does, use men of great ability, capacity, and training, but spiritual leadership requires an ingredient that is not derived from doing, attaining, and accomplishing. The bane of the zealot is often too little confidence in God and too much confidence in the flesh. This pride and restlessness is not dealt with in a seminary nor is it normally exterminated during vigilant duty. For many of God’s servants, it is extracted from the soul on the soil of deserted sands. This arid and abandoned acreage that appears void of life and fruitfulness is where many servants learn to put their face in the dust and yield to what may seem to be inactivity, unfruitfulness, and rejection.

Moses’ life could be divided into three sections. He spent his first forty years learning the wisdom of Egypt, the next forty as a shepherd in Midian, and a final forty as the shepherd of Israel. We can imagine that the first third of his pilgrimage was filled with tremendous activity, advancement, and accomplishment. It had undoubtedly been rehearsed to him that at his birth he …was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months –Acts 7:20.

The miraculous river rescue by Pharoah’s daughter would serve to confirm that he was destined to be an instrument of God’s divine orchestration. As a centerpiece of national attention, it is certainly understandable how this man who …was mighty in words and in deeds –Acts 7:22, was brimming with self-confidence in his ability to accomplish God’s bidding.

In today’s economy, Moses would be esteemed as the ideal candidate for church leadership. He was in every way qualified. He stood above his countrymen in education, and he possessed above-normal natural, financial, and spiritual endowments. He had emerged from the “University” of Egypt as a man mighty in word and deed and he had an obvious call from God upon his life. He was a conservative man who chose …rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season –Hebrews 11:25.

Still, amidst all his fine credentials he was yet deficient for the work that God had called him to. And so, God conveniently conducted him into the land of Midian to enroll him in another school to feed upon the bitter herbs of disappointment and rejection, obscurity and loneliness, and unfulfilled dreams and longings. While it was his earlier ambition to voluntarily align himself with the people of God, this chapter of his life was enacted by compulsion.

We learn from the account in Exodus that the latter third of his life was loaded with intricate involvement and major ministry. While the exit from Egypt is an exciting read and provides great insight, most of us cannot honestly relate to the mighty Moses and his dynamic coalition with God. Rather, it is the uneventful 40-year mid-section of his life that many of us find ourselves in. Though there are but a few dozen verses that represent these four decades of his life, we assume that it was a thorough schooling that inscribed immense patience, soul searching, and perhaps a bit of frustration.

For us, it represents a period when the parched sands of time about us seem to be producing nothing more fruitful than a revelation of our dry, crusty heart—shriveled and wasted by the consequences of our failures and past sins. It is at these times that we can have a lapse in faith, not that we blame God for our circumstances, but that we may begin to see our lives as futile, and that each day is the same as the previous one. Perhaps we begin to walk around in a visionless stupor—through a fog of spiritual depression—as we grope for encouragement and a reminder that God has not forgotten us. At times, it even seems that our prayers hit the ceiling and bounce back, laughing and lying to us in grim mockery that our usefulness in the Kingdom of God is over. During extended times of trials and testing, we can feel abandoned. We can even imagine that God has turned against us. We look up to Heaven and ask, “Why Lord?” We will never experience rejection and being forsaken to the extent that the Lord Jesus did, but when we experience them in our petty little realm, it seems to sap all our spiritual strength and vigor. We think… If the Lord should require forty years of this from us there would be no time left in our lives to capitalize on what we have learned. But God’s timing is perfect. Thus, it behooves us to not concern ourselves so much with the longevity of our schooling, but to be thoroughly acquainted with the message from Midian. While some receive the bitter strokes of Midian and retreat to stand cynically on the sidelines, we must shake off the dust of the desert and arise with an understanding of…

God’s Purpose

God has a purpose for every detail of our lives. He may plant us in a difficult position, to forge in us a new vocation. It was alone in Midian where Moses learned of his own pride, self-confidence, lack of faith, and the utter folly that his own hands had participated in. Here in his Midian, he was alone and yet not alone; numerous other saints have joined him there. The sons of Jacob and the wife of Potiphar sent another vibrant servant there—Joseph. The wild rage of a jealous king sent a gifted young harpist there. Even an old and foolish king who refused to be taught found himself in a wilderness eating grass like an ox until he recanted of his pride.

Throughout the pages of history, countless saints have realized that ‘the darker the valley, the more I learned to pray’. While they arrive at the threshold of the new day loaded down with bountiful exuberance, they are soon stripped naked in a metamorphic change and finally emerge with nothing but the rod of God in their hands. Gone are the days when they were swift to speak, swift to act, and slow to hear. In Midian, the student learns to shift his focus from, “I will do great things for God” to “What wilt thou have me to do?”

And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do –Acts 9:6. The new arrivals in Midian have many answers, but most of them involve a one-act-play with self as the main character. The graduates walk out silent and sober, for they’ve come through the arduous process of separating the flesh from the spirit which was accomplished by…

God’s Purging

The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but the LORD trieth the hearts –Proverbs 17:3. As Moses passed through the gates of Midian, the first scene that God set before his eyes was an injustice at a well. Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters… –Exodus 2:16, who were being driven away by a band of uncouth shepherds. But Moses had been well trained in every dimension of Egyptian plutocracy, which would have included all aspects of military expertise and worldly leadership skills. Thus, when he stepped in to assist the helpless shepherdesses, he would have been quite capable to do so. These daughters of the priest of Midian appreciated the help which they recounted to their father that …An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock –Exodus 2:19. Upon hearing this tale, their father, Reuel, was so impressed that he gave Moses a reception, a job, and a wife… all in one verse. –see Exodus 2:21.

…Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them –Mark 10:42. While Moses’ quest for justice may have been noble, his orientation was merely Gentile. This may work for establishing pecking order in a hen house, but it is destined for failure in leading forth the people of God. But … whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all –Mark 10:43-44.

This doctrine was foreign to Egypt and to Moses as well. Many good and talented men can successfully operate a business using Gentile authority, but it rarely works in their home, and it is even more futile in a church. Thus, God moved His chosen vessel from royalty to proletariat (the working class), almost overnight. He is then given a job which was loathed by the people who had trained him—…for every shepherd is an abomination unto the Egyptians –Genesis 46:34. This fining pot is not just to teach us a much-needed lesson, but to guide us into…

God’s Provision

The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way –Psalm 25:9. God will never abandon us on the back side of the desert; instead, He tailors our life circumstances to bring us into His fullness. If we resist the temptation to espouse an attitude of anger, then God will be able to teach us His ways. But to Moses, the situation presented itself such that God’s divine direction was the last thing he would suspect was happening.

Happening…? It seemed that nothing was happening. The weeks melted into months, the months into years, and the years into decades, all the while the gifted Moses remained an underachieving shepherd. One of the hardest things that we struggle with is “waiting.” Almost every Christian will face a long time of tribulation and we are told to: …think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you –1 Peter 4:12. But we should not judge God’s means by our feeble sense, for in the meantime, the wonderful working of waiting prepares us for…

God’s Promotion

38, 39, … 40 years. Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt –Exodus 3:10.

Perhaps God is enamored with the number 40, but more than likely, it was the time that it took for Moses to land at the seat of resignation. His self-esteem has been fully extinguished, and he humbly asks: …Who am I, that I should go unto Pharaoh, and that I should bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt? –Exodus 3:11.

Moses was not less qualified than he was forty years prior to this time, but his presumption had evaporated in the heat of the desert sun. The experience gleaned in the rugged pastures with the stubborn sheep has brought him to the understanding that this will be nearly an impossible feat. But there is no ordained calling issued independently from…

God’s Promise

…Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain –Exodus 3:12.

Not that Moses had attained perfection, for we find Moses provoking God to anger in the very next chapter—And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Moses… –Exodus 4:14. Then soon again he is the direct object in the path of God’s sword—And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the LORD met him, and sought to kill him –Exodus 4:24. Even so, while his vessel is still made of clay, it has met with a firing that has prepared him for the Lord’s service, and for us God will not revoke His promises in the wind of our whims. Thus, the great I AM THAT I AM –see Exodus 3:14, has laid upon human shoulders the immense and eternal task of leading His people. But this charge is not to be executed without…

God’s Power

What was the real refinement from Moses’ time spent in the desert? We notice his rash willingness to wield the sword before his arrival, but upon his exit, he only bore a rod in his hand. With the sword he had overcome an Egyptian offender, but with the rod he overcame the entire forces of Egypt. The rod of God brought forth the water in the wilderness. It was the rod of God, that, when lifted high by feeble hands secured the victory over Amalek. What is the rod of God? Before his days in Midian, he hardly knew it existed. Forty years later there hardly exists a scene without it.

The rod is the power of God unto salvation. It is the wisdom of God, the truth of God, the testimony of God, but more than all of these it is the chastening of God. Without it, man does not receive nor perceive the love of God for without it man is not connected to God. For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not? But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons –Hebrews 12:6-8.

This same Moses, who at one time was willing to exercise lordship (Gentile authority) over God’s people now finds himself entreating God and staying His wrath from destroying them. The people who accused Moses of leading them out to kill them and even at one point were ready to stone him are now at the center of his heart and affection, even though they are at the cause of his failure to enter the promised land. This is the love of Christ. But where is this learned except under the rod of God, on the back side of the desert, in the Egyptian dungeons, in the caves of Adullam, in the straits of Arabia, and in the silent solitude of the back burner where God has ordained that many of His people go until they learn to …learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls –Matthew 11:29. Surely that is where Moses secured the character known to the biblical scholar as the meekest man to walk the face of the earth. Surely there is no more opposite place on earth to learn it but in the school of suffering.

And so here we shall abide as well, so that we …may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death –Philippians 3:10.

现在摩西牧养他岳父米甸祭司叶忒罗的羊群；他把羊群赶到旷野的后边，来到神的山，就是何烈山。——出埃及记 3:1。

旷野的后边长期被理解为神的学堂，祂在那裡教训过祂的许多仆人，其中以摩西为首。四十岁壮年时，他发现自己…在埃及一切的学问上都受了教训，且有权势，言语和作为都显大能。既满了四十岁，就起意往他的弟兄那里去看他们的情形。——使徒行传 7:22-23。

我毫不怀疑神能够并且确实使用有大才能、能力和训练的人，但属灵的领导需要一种不是来自做事、成就与达成的成分。热心者的祸患常常是对神信心太少，对血肉信心太多。这种骄傲与不安在神学院里得不到处理，通常在谨慎服事中也不能根除。对许多神的仆人来说，这些成分是在荒凉的沙地上从心灵里被抽出来的。那片干旱被遗弃、看似无生命和无丰产的地，是许多仆人学会把脸贴在尘土里，顺服看起来像不作为、无果和被弃绝的地方。

摩西的生命可以分成三段。他用头四十年学习埃及的智慧，接下来的四十年在米甸做牧羊人，最后四十年作以色列的牧者。我们可以想象，他朝圣之路的前一段充满了极大的活动、晋升和成就。毫无疑问，人们早已向他重申他出世时…甚是俊美，且在他父家三个月被养活。——使徒行传 7:20。

法老女儿在河边的奇迹救援证实了他注定要成为神旨意工具的事实。作为一位受全国关注的中心人物，可以理解这位…言语和作为都显大能的⸺使徒行传 7:22男子，如何充满自信，相信自己能完成神的差遣。

在今日的环境中，摩西会被看作教会领导的理想候选人。他在各方面都合格：在教育上远胜同胞，并具备超常的自然、财务和属灵恩赐。他从埃及的“大学”出来，成为言语与作为上显大能的人，而且生命上有明显的神的呼召。他是个保守的人，宁可…与神的百姓一同受苦，不肯暫時享受罪的快樂。——希伯来书 11:25。

然而，在这一切良好资历之中，他仍不足以胜任神所召他的工作。于是，神便带他到米甸去，把他送进另一个学堂，让他吞下失望与被弃绝、默默无闻与孤独、未实现的梦想与渴望这等苦菜。在早先，他是出于自己的志向愿意与神的子民同列；但这一章人生却是被迫上演的。

我们从出埃及记的记载中得知，他生命的最后一段充满复杂的参与与重大的服事。虽然出埃及的出路读来惊心动魄并提供了深刻的见解，但我们中大多数人不能诚实地认同那位大能的摩西与他与神的动态同工。相反，许多人发现自己正处在他生命中那无大事的四十年中段。虽然代表这四十年的经文只有数十节，但我们假定那是彻底的训练，刻印了极大的忍耐、灵魂的探求，或许还有一点沮丧。

对我们来说，那段时期代表着周遭干渴的时光似乎结出不了比显明我们干瘪、结壳之心更有成果的东西——被以往失败与罪的后果所干瘪与消耗。就在这些时候，我们的信心可能会有滑坡，并非因为我们责怪神我们的处境，而是我们可能开始把生命看作徒然，每一天都和前一天一样。也许我们开始在无异象的迟钝中徘徊——在属灵沮丧的迷雾里挣扎，寻求鼓励与提醒，表明神没有忘记我们。有时，甚至感觉我们的祷告拍在天花板上弹回，嘲弄地笑着对我们说我们在神国中的用途已尽。在长久的试探和试炼中，我们会感到被弃；甚至会想象神转而反对我们。我们仰望天问：“主啊，为什么？”我们永远不会经历到主耶稣所受的被弃和被撇之程度，但当我们在自己狭小的领域经历这些时，似乎耗尽了我们一切属灵的力量与活力。我们想……如果主要我们经历这样的四十年，我们的人生就没有时间把所学转化为结果了。但神的时机是完美的。因此，我们不宜过于关心服事学堂的长短，而要彻底熟悉来自米甸的信息。当一些人领受了米甸的苦涩打击并退居讥讽的旁观者时，我们必须抖去旷野的尘土，明白地起来认识……

神的目的

神为我们生命的每一处细节都有目的。祂可能把我们安置在艰难的位置上，为要在我们里面锻造新的职分。正是在米甸，摩西认识到自己的骄傲、自信、信心的缺乏和自己手所参与的极大愚妄。在他的米甸里，他独自一人，但并非孤立无援；许多其他的圣徒也曾与他同在。雅各的儿子和波提乏的妻子把另一个充满活力的仆人送到那里——约瑟。忌妒的王的暴怒把一位多才的年轻弹琴者送到那里。甚至一位年老且愚昧、不肯受教的王也发现自己在旷野里吃草如牛，直到他悔改他的骄傲。

纵观历史的篇章，无数圣徒体会到“山谷越黑暗，我越学会祷告”。当他们满带丰盛的热情来到新的一天门槛时，很快便在变形的改变中被剥去一切，最后只手持神的杖出来。他们曾经快言快语、急于行动而迟于聆听的日子已不复存在。在米甸，学生学会把焦点从“我要为神做大事”转向“主啊，你要我做什么？”

他战兢惊恐，问主说：主阿，你要我作甚麼事？主說：起來，下到城裡去，必有人告訴你當作的事。——使徒行传 9:6。新到米甸的人有很多答案，但大多数都涉及一人独角戏，把自己当作主角。毕业生默然而庄重地走出来，因为他们历尽了那艰苦的过程，把肉体与灵分开，这过程是借着……

神的熬炼

银子虽在窑中被炼，金子在炉中被试，惟耶和华试验人心。——箴言 17:3。当摩西经过米甸的门口时，神摆在他眼前的第一幕是在井旁的不义。当时米甸的祭司有七个女儿…——出埃及记 2:16，正在被一群放荡的牧人赶走。但摩西在埃及接受的训练是全方位的埃及富豪制度训练，其中当然包括一切军事专长与世俗的领导技巧。因此，当他上前帮助这些无助的牧女时，他完全有能力这样做。米甸祭司的这些女儿感激摩西的帮助，便回去告诉她们的父亲说：…有一个埃及人救我们脱离牧人的手，也替我们打水，把羊喂了。——出埃及记 2:19。听了这个故事，他们的父亲流利勒（利乌）深受感动，就为摩西设摆筵宴，给他一个差事并把女儿给他作妻子……都写在一节经文里。——参见出埃及记 2:21。

你们知道，外邦人的治理主张在他们中间作主。并且他们的尊贵人在他们身上有权柄。——马可福音 10:42。虽然摩西为公义而奋勇可敬，但他的取向仅是外邦人的。这在鸡舍中建立等级秩序也许行得通，但在领导神的子民时注定要失败。只是你们中间为首的，必须作你们的用人；谁愿为首的，必作众人的仆人。——马可福音 10:43-44。

这种教义对埃及和摩西来说都是陌生的。许多良善有才的人可以用外邦式的权柄成功经营生意，但这在他们的家庭中很少奏效，在教会里更是徒劳。因此，神几乎在一夜之间把祂所拣选的器皿从贵族移到无产者（工人阶级）。后来他得了一个受训他的民众所厌恶的差事——…因为放羊的人在埃及人为可憎。——创世记 46:34。这熬炼的窑不仅是要教我们一个非常需要的功课，还是要引导我们进入……

神的供应

谦和的人必要以公平教训他，谦和的人必要指教他的道。——诗篇 25:9。神绝不会把我们弃置在旷野的后边；相反，祂为我们量身准备生命处境，使我们进入祂的丰满。若我们抵挡以愤怒为怀的诱惑，神就能够教导我们祂的道。但对摩西来说，情势呈现得让他最不怀疑的是没有发生神圣的指引。

发生……？似乎什么也没有发生。数周融为数月，数月为数年，数年为数十年，而那有恩赐的摩西仍旧是没能出众的牧羊人。我们极难应付的一件事就是“等候”。几乎每个基督徒都要面对长久的苦难，而我们被告知要…要以为不寻常，倒要以为有喜乐；因为你们是与基督一同受苦，叫你们到了将来得荣耀的时候，也可以欢喜快乐。——彼得前书 4:12。但我们不应以我们软弱的感官来判断神的方式，因为在此期间，等候的奇妙作为正在为我们预备……

神的提拔

三十八、三十九、……四十年。现在你来，我要差你去见法老，使你把我的百姓以色列人从埃及领出来。——出埃及记 3:10。

也许神钟意数字四十，但更可能的是，这是摩西走到放下自我的那个地点所需的时日。他的自尊已被彻底熄灭，他卑微地问：我是誰，竟能去见法老，将以色列人从埃及领出来呢？——出埃及记 3:11。

摩西的资格并不比四十年前差，但他的妄自尊大在旷野烈日之下已消散。他在粗犷的牧场与顽梗的羊群中所得的经历使他明白这是几乎不可能的壮举。但任何一个蒙召并不在于独立于……

神的应许

我却必与你同在；这就可作你得以差遣的证据。你既把百姓从埃及领出来，就要在这山事奉神。——出埃及记 3:12。

并不是说摩西已经达成完全，因为我们见到摩西在下一章就惹动耶和华发怒——耶和华向摩西发烈怒…——出埃及记 4:14。随后不久他又成为神刀剑所对准的对象——到了路上在客店的时候，耶和华遇见他，要杀他。——出埃及记 4:24。即便如此，虽然他的器皿仍是泥器，祂已经用火煅造他，使他为主的服事预备好，而且对我们而言，神不会因我们的任性而收回祂的应许。因此，那位自有永有者——参见出埃及记 3:14，把带领祂子民的伟大与永恒任务放在人类肩头上。但这项差遣不在没有……的情况下施行。

神的能力

摩西在旷野时光的真实磨练是什么？我们注意到他在到来之前轻率地愿意挥刀，但在离开时，他手中仅拿着杖。以刀曾使他胜了一个埃及人，但以杖他胜过了埃及的整个势力。神的杖在旷野使水涌出。正是神的杖，当软弱的手举起时，在亚玛力那里得了胜。什么是神的杖？在他到米甸之前，他几乎不知其存在。四十年后几乎不存在没有它的场景。

这杖就是拯救的神能。它是神的智慧，神的真理，神的见证，但更甚于这些的是神的管教。没有它，人就不接受也不察觉神的爱；没有它，人就与神没有连接。主所爱的，他必管教，又鞭打他所收的每一个儿子。你们若忍受管教，神待你们如同待儿子；父亲不管教儿子，便是私生子了。——希伯来书 12:6-8。

这同一个摩西，曾经愿意用外邦人的辖制（作王权）管轄神的子民，如今却为他们恳求，阻止神的怒气毁灭他们。那些曾指责摩西把他们带出去要杀他们、甚至一度要用石头打死他的人，如今成了他心中与情感的中心，尽管他们是他不能进入应许之地的原因。这就是基督的爱。但除非在神的杖下，在旷野的后边，在埃及的地牢中，在亞杜蘭的洞穴中，在阿拉伯的狭困中，与在被神命定让许多子民去的沉寂孤独中学到这一点，否则哪能学成呢，直到他们学会…学我的样式；因为我心里柔和谦卑，你们当负我的轭，学我的样式，就必得着心灵的安息。——马太福音 11:29。诚然，那正是摩西赢得那位圣经学者称作世上最温柔之人的品格之处。世上再没有比受苦的学堂更相反的地方来学这个了。

因此我们也当在此常存，好使我们…晓得他，并得知他复活的大能，并晓得与他同受苦的交通，使我们在生命的死上模成他的样式。——腓立比书 3:10。
